tables.grain: one 1099 summary row per contact per report tax year
tables.description: Per-contact 1099 box amounts for a US tax year, exploded from the report's Contacts array: what the org paid each reportable vendor, bucketed into IRS form boxes, plus the identity fields (name, address, TIN) that would print on the form. Amounts are ANNUAL AGGREGATES DERIVED FROM PAYMENTS — never add them to payment- or bill-level cash metrics or the same dollars count twice. Identity fields are a point-in-time snapshot of the contact's W-9 data and are heavily PII.
gotchas: Box amounts are yearly aggregates DERIVED from the same payments in xero_payments/bills — never combine the two tables in one metric or dollars double-count.
Amounts are recomputed live per fetch, not frozen filings: a past year's numbers move when bookkeeping changes. Date any quoted figure with the parent report's updated_date_utc.
Box numbering carries no stable meaning across years (2020 moved nonemployee compensation from MISC box 7 to NEC box 1) and Box12 does not exist in the payload at all.
Availability is optional (tenninetynine scope + US org). An empty table is 'not available', never 'no reportable vendors' — degrade explicitly.

examples.question: Top 1099 vendors for 2025 by total reported amount
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(business_name, legal_name, name) AS vendor,
       COALESCE(box1,0)+COALESCE(box2,0)+COALESCE(box3,0)+COALESCE(box4,0)+COALESCE(box5,0)+COALESCE(box6,0)+COALESCE(box7,0)+COALESCE(box8,0)+COALESCE(box9,0)+COALESCE(box10,0)+COALESCE(box11,0)+COALESCE(box13,0)+COALESCE(box14,0) AS total_reported
FROM xero_1099_contacts
WHERE report_year = 2025
ORDER BY total_reported DESC
LIMIT 25

examples.question: Which 1099 contacts are missing a tax ID before filing?
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(legal_name, name) AS vendor, federal_tax_classification
FROM xero_1099_contacts
WHERE report_year = 2025
  AND (tax_id IS NULL OR tax_id = '')
ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one 1099 report header per requested tax year
tables.description: Header of the US 1099 report (GET /Reports/TenNinetyNine), fetched once per reportYear the scan iterates. The interesting data is the per-contact box amounts exploded into xero_1099_contacts; this table anchors the year partition and records when Xero last recomputed the report. The report is a LIVE recomputation over the org's payments and 1099 rules, not a frozen filing — re-fetching a past year after bookkeeping changes returns different numbers.
gotchas: Availability is optional twice over: the connection needs the separately granted accounting.reports.tenninetynine.read scope AND the org must be a US org using 1099 tracking. Absence of rows means 'not available', not 'no 1099 activity' — answers must degrade explicitly.

Box amounts are recomputed live from current bookkeeping, not frozen filings: fetching 2023 today can differ from what was actually filed in January 2024. Say which snapshot a number comes from (updated_date_utc).
The scan fans out over the reportYear query parameter (one request per year), not over a parent id — there is no pagination and no If-Modified-Since on this op.

columns.name: report_title

columns.name: report_date

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: When Xero last recomputed the report. If this moves for a past year, that year's box amounts have changed since you last read them — re-sync the child rows.

columns.name: contacts

tables.grain: one chart-of-accounts entry per AccountID
tables.description: The org's chart of accounts — the dimension every financial number in the connector eventually joins to. Class (ASSET/LIABILITY/EQUITY vs REVENUE/EXPENSE) is the read-only, authoritative statement split; Type is the granular behavior (BANK, DIRECTCOSTS, OVERHEADS…); SystemAccount marks the control accounts Xero manages itself (DEBTORS = AR control, CREDITORS = AP control, GST = tax control). Archived and deleted accounts remain referenced by historical journal lines, so this dimension must never be pre-filtered to ACTIVE inside a historical join.
gotchas: Class, not Type, decides statement membership: type = 'REVENUE' misses SALES and OTHERINCOME accounts; class = 'REVENUE' catches them all. This single confusion is the most common wrong-P&L cause in Xero data.
Archived/deleted accounts still carry history. Inner-joining a status = 'ACTIVE' filtered dimension into journal lines silently deletes old activity from totals.
SystemAccount is empty string OR null for normal accounts — filter with NULLIF(system_account, '') IS NULL, not system_account IS NULL alone.
BankAccountNumber, BankAccountType and CurrencyCode are only meaningful when type = 'BANK'; Description is absent for bank accounts. Column presence encodes account kind.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable account identifier and the row key — the durable join target for journal lines, budget lines and every document line's AccountCode lookup.

columns.name: code
columns.description: Customer-defined alphanumeric code (max 10, e.g. '200' or 'SALES'). Editable and re-usable over time — join by account_id, present by code. Some system accounts have no code at all.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Current display name (max 150). Historical journal lines carry the name as at posting — after renames the two differ; this one is 'now'.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Granular account behavior. Use for operational slices (BANK accounts, DIRECTCOSTS vs OVERHEADS cost split); do NOT use for statement membership — SALES, REVENUE and OTHERINCOME are distinct Types inside one Class, and filtering type = 'REVENUE' silently drops sales accounts.
columns.enums: BANK; CURRENT; CURRLIAB; DEPRECIATN; DIRECTCOSTS; EQUITY; EXPENSE; FIXED; INVENTORY; LIABILITY; NONCURRENT; OTHERINCOME; OVERHEADS; PREPAYMENT; REVENUE; SALES; TERMLIAB; PAYG

columns.name: bank_account_number
columns.description: The org's own bank account number — populated only when type = 'BANK'. Sensitive financial identifier: display masked, never use in URL parameters.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ACTIVE accounts are usable today; ARCHIVED/DELETED ones persist on history. Filter status for 'what can we post to now' questions only — historical aggregates must keep all statuses or old balances vanish.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text purpose of the account (max 4000); valid for all types except bank accounts.

columns.name: bank_account_type
columns.description: Sub-kind of a BANK account — CREDITCARD spend behaves as liability-side cash, PAYPAL as a clearing wallet. Non-bank accounts return NONE or empty string; treat both as 'not a bank account'.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: Currency of a bank account (bank accounts only; other accounts follow the org's base currency). Join xero_currencies for the display name. The spec's enum is the ISO-4217 set; the extracted list is truncated at HRK — treat values beyond it as valid ISO codes.
columns.enums: AED; AFN; ALL; AMD; ANG; AOA; ARS; AUD; AWG; AZN; BAM; BBD; BDT; BGN; BHD; BIF; BMD; BND; BOB; BRL; BSD; BTN; BWP; BYN; BYR; BZD; CAD; CDF; CHF; CLF; CLP; CNY; COP; CRC; CUC; CUP; CVE; CZK; DJF; DKK; DOP; DZD; EEK; EGP; ERN; ETB; EUR; FJD; FKP; GBP; GEL; GHS; GIP; GMD; GNF; GTQ; GYD; HKD; HNL; HRK

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: The account's DEFAULT tax rate (join to xero_tax_rates). Lines can override it — tax analysis of actual activity reads the line's tax_type, not this default.

columns.name: enable_payments_to_account
columns.description: Whether payments may be applied directly to this account — how non-bank clearing accounts show up inside xero_payments.account_id.

columns.name: show_in_expense_claims
columns.description: Whether the account is offered for expense-claim receipt coding — a UI availability flag, not evidence any claims exist.

columns.name: class
columns.description: Read-only statement classification and THE split for financial statements: REVENUE + EXPENSE classes form the P&L, ASSET + LIABILITY + EQUITY form the balance sheet. Every P&L query in this connector filters on this column — not on type.

columns.description: Set when Xero itself manages the account: DEBTORS is the AR control, CREDITORS the AP control, GST the tax control, RETAINEDEARNINGS the rollup. Non-system accounts return empty string or null — treat both as 'not system'. Exclude control accounts when analyzing discretionary spend, or AR/AP movements masquerade as activity.

tables.grain: one fixed-asset settings record per organisation (unkeyed API singleton)
tables.description: Per-organisation fixed-asset configuration: register numbering, the date asset depreciation started in Xero, the date depreciation was last run, and the default disposal gain/loss accounts. last_depreciation_date is the freshness bound for every book value in xero_assets — accumulated depreciation and accounting_book_value are computed through that date, not today. opt_in_for_tax records the organisation's tax-depreciation election, but this connector revision exposes no tax book values, so tax-basis questions cannot be answered from staging.
gotchas: Unkeyed singleton: the primary key is minted (singleton_id) and each sync overwrites the row in place — there is no history of settings changes, so last_depreciation_date only describes CURRENT staleness, never past run cadence.

The three disposal accounts are defaults, not postings: individual disposals can be redirected in the UI. Actual posted gains and losses live in journal lines (ledger_config) against whatever account was used.
asset_number_sequence is text and is the next number to issue, not a count of assets; deleted drafts consume numbers, so deriving register size from it (or from max(asset_number)) overcounts.

columns.name: singleton_id
columns.api: synthetic:constant key ('settings') minted because GET /Settings returns one unkeyed record per organisation
columns.description: Constant synthetic row key for the per-organisation singleton; the platform's tenant scoping makes the row unique. Exists only so the table has a declared grain key.

columns.name: asset_number_prefix
columns.description: Prefix Xero stamps onto new asset_number values ('FA-' by default). Strip it before sorting register numbers numerically.

columns.name: asset_number_sequence
columns.description: The NEXT sequence number Xero will issue, stored as text. A high-water mark, not a count of assets — deleted drafts consume numbers, so arithmetic on it misestimates register size.

columns.name: asset_start_date
columns.description: The date depreciation calculations started on registered fixed assets in Xero. Assets acquired earlier were migrated with an opening balance in prior_accum_depreciation_amount — expect no depreciation journals before this date.

columns.name: last_depreciation_date
columns.description: Through-date of the most recent depreciation run — the freshness bound for accounting_book_value and both accumulated-depreciation fields on every asset. If it lags today, book values are stale by exactly that gap; state the as-of date rather than presenting them as current.

columns.name: default_gain_on_disposal_account_id
columns.description: GL account that ordinary disposal GAINS (recovery above book value, capped at original cost) default-post to; join xero_accounts for code and name. A default — individual disposals can be redirected in the UI.

columns.name: default_loss_on_disposal_account_id
columns.description: GL account disposal LOSSES default-post to — the loss twin of the gain account. A disposal hits one or the other (plus possibly the capital-gain account), never both gain and loss.

columns.name: default_capital_gain_on_disposal_account_id
columns.description: GL account for the capital-gain slice (proceeds above original cost) on profitable disposals. Distinct from the ordinary gain account — conflating them mislabels the P&L line the gain lands on.

columns.name: opt_in_for_tax
columns.description: Whether the organisation opted into Xero's tax depreciation calculation. Even when true, this connector revision carries no tax-book values (no taxValues object) — the flag records the election, not data availability.

joins.note: Default posting account for ordinary disposal gains.
Default posting account for disposal losses.
Default posting account for the capital-gain slice of profitable disposals.

examples.question: How fresh are this organisation's asset book values?
examples.sql:
SELECT last_depreciation_date,
       CURRENT_DATE - last_depreciation_date AS days_since_last_depreciation_run
FROM xero_asset_settings

examples.question: Which GL accounts do asset disposals default to?
examples.sql:
SELECT g.code AS gain_account, l.code AS loss_account, c.code AS capital_gain_account
FROM xero_asset_settings s
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts g ON g.account_id = s.default_gain_on_disposal_account_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts l ON l.account_id = s.default_loss_on_disposal_account_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts c ON c.account_id = s.default_capital_gain_on_disposal_account_id

tables.grain: one asset type (depreciation class) per assetTypeId
tables.description: Depreciation classes that categorise fixed assets and — critically — carry the three GL account mappings that turn depreciation into ledger truth: the fixed-asset cost account, the accumulated-depreciation contra account, and the depreciation-expense P&L account. The embedded BookDepreciationSetting here is only the DEFAULT copied onto an asset at registration; each asset keeps its own overridable copy on xero_assets, so depreciation analytics read the asset's columns, not these defaults. locks marks types with posted accumulated depreciation that Xero refuses to delete; unlocked unused types can hard-delete and vanish between scans.
gotchas: The bookDepreciationSetting on a type is only the default seeded at registration; assets keep their own overridable copy. Grouping depreciation behaviour by the type's default method mislabels any overridden asset — use xero_assets' own depreciation columns.

Types with locks = 0 can be hard-deleted in Xero and drop out of the API without tombstones; only a full identity rescan notices. An asset_type_id remembered from an old export may legitimately resolve to nothing.

Three GL accounts, three roles: fixed_asset (balance-sheet cost), accumulated_depreciation (balance-sheet contra), depreciation_expense (P&L). Joining the expense account into a balance-sheet question — or vice versa — produces plausible-looking wrong numbers.

columns.name: asset_type_id
columns.description: Xero's UUID for the asset type; the classification key xero_assets.asset_type_id points at.

columns.name: asset_type_name
columns.description: Name of the depreciation class ('Motor Vehicles', 'Office Equipment') and the natural label for register breakdowns. Editable — group by asset_type_id when identity over time matters.

columns.name: fixed_asset_account_id
columns.description: GL account holding these assets' capitalised COST on the balance sheet; join to xero_accounts. The debit side of registration — not where depreciation expense goes.

columns.name: depreciation_expense_account_id
columns.description: P&L account each depreciation run debits for assets of this type. 'Depreciation expense by class' resolves through this mapping into journal lines (ledger_config), not from register snapshots.

columns.name: accumulated_depreciation_account_id
columns.description: Contra-asset balance-sheet account credited by depreciation runs; cost account plus this equals net book value in the GL. Same run as the expense account, different financial statement — confusing the two misstates both.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_method
columns.description: Depreciation method handed to NEW assets of this type as a default. The asset's own depreciation_method is what actually runs — reporting the register from this column mislabels overridden assets.
columns.enums: NoDepreciation; StraightLine; DiminishingValue100; DiminishingValue150; DiminishingValue200; FullDepreciation

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_averaging_method
columns.description: Default first/last-period proration (whole-month vs daily) seeded onto new assets of this type; the operative value is xero_assets.averaging_method.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_rate
columns.description: Default annual rate (decimal fraction, 0.05 = 5%) offered at registration when the calculation method is 'Rate'. A ratio and only a default — the operative rate is the asset's own depreciation_rate.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_effective_life_years
columns.description: Default life in years for 'Life'-method assets of this type; the asset's own effective_life_years wins once registered.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_calculation_method
columns.description: Which default input this type hands to new assets: 'Rate' (default_depreciation_rate), 'Life' (default_effective_life_years) or 'None' for methods needing neither.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciable_object_id
columns.description: Xero's internal identifier for the object this default setting binds to (the asset type itself). Depreciation-engine plumbing, not an analytical join key.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciable_object_type
columns.description: Type discriminator for default_depreciable_object_id; engine plumbing.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_book_effective_date_of_change_id
columns.description: Identifier of the effective-dated change record if the type's default setting was amended; evidence of a policy change whose history stays inside Xero.

columns.name: locks
columns.description: Nonzero when assets of this type carry accumulated depreciation, which deletion-locks the type in Xero. Zero means deletable — such types can hard-delete and disappear from a later scan without a tombstone.

joins.note: Balance-sheet account carrying capitalised cost for assets of this type.
Contra-asset account accumulating depreciation credits.
P&L account for depreciation expense — the bridge from the register to journal-based expense reporting.

examples.question: Net book value and lifetime depreciation by asset type, with the GL cost account
examples.sql:
SELECT t.asset_type_name, acc.code AS fixed_asset_account_code,
       SUM(a.accounting_book_value) AS net_book_value,
       SUM(COALESCE(a.prior_accum_depreciation_amount, 0) + COALESCE(a.current_accum_depreciation_amount, 0)) AS lifetime_depreciation
FROM xero_asset_types t
JOIN xero_assets a ON a.asset_type_id = t.asset_type_id AND a.asset_status = 'Registered'
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts acc ON acc.account_id = t.fixed_asset_account_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 3 DESC

examples.question: Which depreciation classes default to straight-line vs diminishing value?
examples.sql:
SELECT book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_method, COUNT(*) AS asset_types,
       string_agg(asset_type_name, ', ' ORDER BY asset_type_name) AS types
FROM xero_asset_types
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one fixed-asset register entry per assetId (Draft, Registered or Disposed)
tables.description: The fixed-asset register: every capitalised asset Xero tracks, with its acquisition cost, its own depreciation policy (flattened from assets:BookDepreciationSetting), Xero-computed depreciation state (flattened from assets:BookDepreciationDetail) and the current accounting net book value. This is the register view, not the ledger: statutory depreciation expense and accumulated-depreciation postings live in journals against the asset type's GL accounts (ledger_config domain). Every book-value and accumulated-depreciation figure is computed only through the organisation's last depreciation run (xero_asset_settings.last_depreciation_date) and is a last-value-over-time snapshot, never a flow. Net-book-value questions filter asset_status = 'Registered': Draft rows have no GL existence yet and Disposed rows carry frozen history.
tables.additivityAxis: time
gotchas: GET /Assets serves exactly one status per call (required uppercase status query param: DRAFT/REGISTERED/DISPOSED), so the ingester runs three scans and staging holds every status. Stored asset_status is mixed-case ('Registered') — filter with the stored casing, and filter it always: Draft rows have no GL existence and Disposed rows carry frozen book values.

Every book-value and accumulated-depreciation field is computed only through xero_asset_settings.last_depreciation_date, not through today. An org that has not run depreciation for months silently overstates net book value — report the as-of date with the number.

current_accum_depreciation_amount is the current financial year only and resets at year end; lifetime accumulated depreciation is prior + current. Dated depreciation-expense-in-period questions are better answered from journals (ledger_config) via the asset type's expense account — this table is register state, not dated postings.

Disposal economics are split across three fields: disposal_price (proceeds), current_capital_gain (proceeds above original cost) and current_gain_loss (lower of proceeds or cost, minus book value). current_capital_gain + current_gain_loss legitimately reconstructs total proceeds-minus-book-value — but adding disposal_price to either slice double-counts the proceeds.

No object in the Assets API carries a modified watermark (no UpdatedDateUTC): syncs are full rescans, and hard-deleted draft assets simply vanish — a missing asset_id is a deletion, not data loss. The businessUse*/privateUse* splits and initial_deduction_percentage populate for New Zealand organisations only.

columns.name: asset_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the asset and the row key; stable across renames, status transitions and disposal.

columns.name: asset_name
columns.description: Human-readable label shown in Xero's register and the natural display column. Editable at any time and not unique — asset_number is the stable human reference, asset_id the join key.

columns.name: asset_type_id
columns.description: Classifies the asset into its depreciation profile and, through xero_asset_types, the GL account trio (cost, accumulated depreciation, expense). Optional in the API, so Draft rows can be null; a Registered asset always has one.

columns.name: asset_number
columns.description: Unique human-facing register reference, auto-issued as the settings prefix plus sequence (e.g. FA-0104) unless a custom number was typed at registration. Deleted drafts still consume sequence numbers, so gaps are normal and are not missing data.

columns.name: purchase_date
columns.description: Acquisition date and the axis for capex-by-period questions. Not necessarily when depreciation begins — depreciation_start_date can trail it (delivered vs placed in service), so asset-age and remaining-life math should anchor on depreciation_start_date.

columns.name: purchase_price
columns.description: Historical acquisition cost in the organisation's base currency (the Assets API is base-currency only). This is capex at purchase, never current worth — current worth is accounting_book_value. When cost_limit is set below it, only cost_limit depreciates.

columns.name: disposal_date
columns.description: Date the asset was sold, scrapped or written off; null unless asset_status = 'Disposed'. 'Disposals in period' filters this date — filtering purchase_date instead silently reports acquisitions.

columns.name: disposal_price
columns.description: Sale proceeds at disposal (0 for scrapped assets), base currency. The outcome is decomposed separately into current_capital_gain (proceeds above original cost) and current_gain_loss (vs remaining book value) — adding disposal_price to either double-counts the proceeds.

columns.name: asset_status
columns.description: Lifecycle gate for every aggregate: Draft exists only in the register (no GL impact yet), Registered is live and depreciating, Disposed is history with frozen figures. Net-book-value and depreciation totals filter 'Registered'; capex totals usually exclude only 'Draft'. Stored values are mixed-case — the API's status query filter uses uppercase DRAFT/REGISTERED/DISPOSED, but SQL against staging matches 'Registered'.

columns.name: warranty_expiry_date
columns.description: Warranty end date for maintenance and replacement planning. Spec-typed as a free string in YYYY-MM-DD form rather than a date field; staged as date. Null means unrecorded, not in or out of warranty.

columns.name: serial_number
columns.description: Manufacturer serial recorded for physical identification, insurance and audit trails. Free text, not enforced unique — never a join key.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_method
columns.description: The asset's OWN depreciation method, seeded from the type default at registration but overridable per asset — report from this column, not the type's default. NoDepreciation holds book value flat; FullDepreciation expenses the whole cost immediately; the DiminishingValue variants encode the declining-balance multiplier (100/150/200% of the straight-line rate).
columns.enums: NoDepreciation; StraightLine; DiminishingValue100; DiminishingValue150; DiminishingValue200; FullDepreciation

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_averaging_method
columns.description: How first and last depreciation periods are prorated: FullMonth books a whole month regardless of the in-month day, ActualDays prorates daily. Explains small differences when reconciling recomputed depreciation to Xero's own figures.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_rate
columns.description: Annual depreciation rate as a decimal fraction (0.05 = 5% per year), operative only when depreciation_calculation_method = 'Rate'. A ratio: never summed, never a currency amount.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_effective_life_years
columns.description: Asset life in whole years, operative only when depreciation_calculation_method = 'Life'. Exactly one of this and depreciation_rate drives the calculation — reading the inoperative one misexplains the expense.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciation_calculation_method
columns.description: Selector for WHICH input drives depreciation: 'Rate' uses depreciation_rate, 'Life' uses effective_life_years, 'None' means neither applies (NoDepreciation / FullDepreciation methods). Read the operative field, not both.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciable_object_id
columns.description: Xero's internal identifier for the depreciable object this setting binds to (the asset itself here). Depreciation-engine plumbing — analytical joins use asset_id.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_depreciable_object_type
columns.description: Type discriminator for depreciable_object_id (which object class the setting attaches to). Engine plumbing, not an analytical dimension.

columns.name: book_depreciation_setting_book_effective_date_of_change_id
columns.description: Identifier of the effective-dated change record created when the depreciation setting was amended mid-life. Evidence that policy changed — the history itself is not exposed by this API.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_depreciation_start_date
columns.description: Date book depreciation began — can trail purchase_date (delivered vs placed in service) and can also precede xero_asset_settings.asset_start_date for assets migrated into Xero, whose pre-Xero depreciation arrives as an opening balance in prior_accum_depreciation_amount. The anchor for asset age and remaining-life projections; using purchase_date instead overstates elapsed depreciation for assets placed in service late.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_cost_limit
columns.description: Optional cap on the depreciable base: when set below purchase_price, Xero depreciates only this amount and the remainder never expenses. Null means the full cost depreciates. Future-depreciation projections that ignore it overstate expense.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_residual_value
columns.description: Salvage floor depreciation stops at. Fully-depreciated assets with a residual still show a nonzero accounting_book_value — 'book value = 0' is the wrong test for fully depreciated.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_prior_accum_depreciation_amount
columns.description: Depreciation accumulated in financial years BEFORE the current one, including any opening balance migrated into Xero. Lifetime accumulated depreciation = this + current_accum_depreciation_amount; either alone understates.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_current_accum_depreciation_amount
columns.description: Depreciation booked in the CURRENT financial year only, through the last depreciation run — effectively depreciation expense YTD for the asset, and it resets to zero at financial year end. Not lifetime accumulation; add prior_accum_depreciation_amount for that.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_current_capital_gain
columns.description: On disposal: sell price minus original purchase price when sold at a profit over cost — the capital-gain slice, posted to the capital-gain disposal account. Zero or null for undisposed assets and loss-making disposals.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_current_gain_loss
columns.description: On disposal: the lower of sell price or purchase price, minus book value at disposal — the ordinary gain/loss-on-disposal slice that hits P&L. current_capital_gain and current_gain_loss together decompose the proceeds-vs-book outcome; summing either with disposal_price double-counts.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_business_use_capital_gain
columns.description: New Zealand organisations only: the business-use share of the disposal capital gain (NZ splits mixed-use assets). Null outside NZ — a jurisdictional null, not missing data.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_business_use_current_gain_loss
columns.description: New Zealand only: disposal gain or loss attributable to the asset's business-use portion. Pair with private_use_current_gain_loss to reconstruct the full outcome of a mixed-use disposal.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_private_use_capital_gain
columns.description: New Zealand only: the private (non-business) share of the disposal capital gain, typically treated differently for tax than the business share. Null outside NZ.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_private_use_current_gain_loss
columns.description: New Zealand only: disposal gain or loss on the private-use portion. Excluding it understates the economic result of mixed-use disposals; folding it into deductible P&L overstates the business result.

columns.name: book_depreciation_detail_initial_deduction_percentage
columns.description: New Zealand only: the Investment Boost immediate-deduction percentage claimed on the asset. A rate, never summed; null outside NZ or when no boost was claimed.

columns.name: can_rollback
columns.description: True when Xero can roll this asset's depreciation back individually (no 'legacy' journal entries and no lock period in the way). An operational capability flag — irrelevant to totals, but a hint that figures could still be restated.

columns.name: accounting_book_value
columns.description: Current net book value on the ACCOUNTING book: depreciable cost less accumulated depreciation, computed through the last depreciation run — THE answer to 'what are our assets worth on the books'. Last-value-over-time: only the latest row per asset counts, and totals filter asset_status = 'Registered' (Draft is unposted, Disposed is frozen history). This spec revision exposes no tax-book counterpart (no taxValues object), so book value here is accounting basis only.

columns.name: is_delete_enabled_for_date
columns.description: Whether Xero would currently allow this asset to be deleted (a server-computed UI affordance, mainly true for Drafts). Deletion is hard: a deleted asset disappears from the API rather than gaining a status, so absence from a fresh scan is the only tombstone.

joins.note: Depreciation class plus the GL account trio (cost, accumulated depreciation, expense). asset_type_id can be null on Draft rows created without a type.

joins.on: xero_assets.asset_id IS NOT NULL AND xero_asset_settings.singleton_id = 'settings'
joins.note: Effectively a cross join to the per-organisation singleton (platform tenant scoping makes it exactly 1 row, so every asset row matches it): last_depreciation_date bounds every book-value figure on this table.

examples.question: Current net book value of the asset register by asset type
examples.sql:
SELECT t.asset_type_name, SUM(a.accounting_book_value) AS net_book_value
FROM xero_assets a
JOIN xero_asset_types t ON t.asset_type_id = a.asset_type_id
WHERE a.asset_status = 'Registered'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Assets disposed this year and the gain or loss booked
examples.sql:
SELECT asset_name, asset_number, disposal_date, disposal_price,
       book_depreciation_detail_current_gain_loss AS gain_loss_vs_book,
       book_depreciation_detail_current_capital_gain AS capital_gain_over_cost
FROM xero_assets
WHERE asset_status = 'Disposed'
  AND disposal_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
ORDER BY disposal_date

examples.question: Capex (assets capitalised) by quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', purchase_date) AS quarter, SUM(purchase_price) AS capex
FROM xero_assets
WHERE asset_status <> 'Draft'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one attachment on one parent record, keyed by parent endpoint + parent id + attachment id
tables.description: Single cross-parent catalog of file attachments across every attachment-capable accounting endpoint (Invoices, CreditNotes, BankTransactions, BankTransfers, Contacts, Accounts, ManualJournals, Receipts, PurchaseOrders, Quotes, RepeatingInvoices...), fetched by per-record fan-out. Rows are file METADATA — the binary lives behind another rate-budgeted call. Because the fan-out burns one request per parent against a hard rate budget, coverage is sampled/limited: a parent with no rows here is 'not scanned or none', never provably 'none'.
gotchas: Fan-out cost: one API call per parent record against Xero's 60/min and capped daily budget, so the ingester limits coverage. A parent without rows is NOT proven attachment-free — state the coverage caveat in any 'documents missing paperwork' answer.
parent_id without parent_endpoint is a trap: UUIDs from different endpoints share the column, and an unfiltered join happily matches an invoice's id against a receipt scan's parent.
url is session-gated xero.com content — surfacing it as a clickable public link in an answer hands users a login wall, and fetching the binary spends more of the same rate budget.

columns.name: parent_endpoint
columns.api: synthetic:the {Endpoint} segment of the fan-out path — which Xero collection the parent record lives in (e.g. 'Invoices', 'Receipts', 'BankTransactions')
columns.description: Namespace half of the polymorphic parent key. parent_id is meaningless without it: the same table mixes invoices, receipts, journals and contacts, so every query filters or groups by parent_endpoint before joining parent_id anywhere.

columns.name: parent_id
columns.api: synthetic:the {Guid} segment of the fan-out path — the parent record's vendor UUID
columns.description: UUID of the record the file is attached to; join it to the endpoint's staging table (xero_invoices.invoice_id when parent_endpoint = 'Invoices', and so on).

columns.name: attachment_id
columns.description: Xero's unique id for this attachment instance; the tie-breaking key when one parent carries several files.

columns.name: file_name
columns.description: Original filename as uploaded. The only human-meaningful label — but user-typed, so 'scan001.pdf' tells you nothing; do not classify documents from names alone.

columns.name: url
columns.description: Link to the file on xero.com. It requires an authenticated Xero session and API fetches of the content are separately rate-budgeted — this is not a public, shareable download link.

columns.name: mime_type
columns.description: Declared content type (application/pdf, image/png...). Set at upload and more trustworthy than the file_name extension for typing documents.

columns.name: content_length
columns.description: File size in bytes. Safe to SUM for storage estimates at this table's grain — each row is a distinct uploaded copy.

columns.name: include_online
columns.description: True when the file is exposed on the customer-facing online invoice. Only meaningful for invoice-family parents; elsewhere it is noise.

joins.note: Polymorphic parent: repeat this pattern per endpoint/table pair (Receipts to xero_receipts.receipt_id, BankTransactions to xero_bank_transactions.bank_transaction_id, ...).

examples.question: Which invoices carry the most attachment storage?
examples.sql:
SELECT parent_id AS invoice_id, COUNT(*) AS files, SUM(content_length) AS total_bytes
FROM xero_attachments
WHERE parent_endpoint = 'Invoices'
GROUP BY parent_id
ORDER BY total_bytes DESC
LIMIT 20

examples.question: Which authorised bills have no attached source document (subject to attachment-scan coverage)?
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_id, i.invoice_number
FROM xero_invoices i
LEFT JOIN xero_attachments a
  ON a.parent_endpoint = 'Invoices' AND a.parent_id = i.invoice_id
WHERE i.type = 'ACCPAY' AND i.status = 'AUTHORISED' AND a.attachment_id IS NULL

tables.grain: one tracking category/option assignment on one bank transaction line item
tables.description: Tracking category and option assignments stamped on bank transaction lines — Xero's department/region/cost-centre dimensions applied to directly-coded cash. One row per assignment, at most two per line (one per active tracking category). This is the join path for 'spend by department' over spend/receive money; monetary amounts deliberately stay on the line table so this table never carries money that could double.
gotchas: A line with two tracking categories yields two rows here: joining lines to this table and summing line_amount across BOTH categories doubles the money. Constrain to one tracking_category_id per aggregate.
name/option are labels frozen at write time; after a rename, old rows keep the old label. Group by the ids and join the tracking dimension tables for current, consistent labels.

columns.name: bank_transaction_id
columns.description: Bank transaction whose line carries this assignment; lets department/region cuts of direct cash skip a hop when line detail is not needed.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of the parent line in accounting:BankTransaction.LineItems
columns.description: Zero-based position of the parent line in the bank transaction's LineItems array — pairs with bank_transaction_id to reach xero_bank_transaction_line_items.

columns.name: tracking_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position in accounting:LineItem.Tracking (Xero allows at most two entries per line)
columns.description: Zero-based position within the line's Tracking array; Xero permits at most two entries, one per active tracking category, so values are 0 or 1.

columns.name: tracking_category_id
columns.description: The tracking category (e.g. Department, Region) this assignment belongs to — join xero_tracking_categories. Aggregate WITHIN one category at a time or line amounts double across categories.

columns.name: tracking_option_id
columns.description: The chosen option under that category — join xero_tracking_options for governed, rename-proof labels.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Tracking category name as frozen at write time. Renames only reach rows written afterwards — group by tracking_category_id and label from xero_tracking_categories for consistent series.

columns.name: option
columns.description: Option label as frozen at write time; same rename caveat as name — filter by tracking_option_id when history must stay consistent.

joins.note: The line whose amount this assignment classifies; the money stays there.
For status/type/date filters without touching the line table.
The governed category dimension (max 2 active per org).
The governed option dimension with current labels.

examples.question: Directly-coded spend by department (a tracking category) this year, excluding tax
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name AS department,
       SUM(l.line_amount - CASE WHEN t.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(l.tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) AS spend_ex_tax
FROM xero_bank_transaction_line_item_tracking tr
JOIN xero_bank_transaction_line_items l
  ON l.bank_transaction_id = tr.bank_transaction_id AND l.line_index = tr.line_index
JOIN xero_bank_transactions t ON t.bank_transaction_id = tr.bank_transaction_id
JOIN xero_tracking_categories c ON c.tracking_category_id = tr.tracking_category_id
JOIN xero_tracking_options o ON o.tracking_option_id = tr.tracking_option_id
WHERE t.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND t.type = 'SPEND'
  AND t.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  AND c.name = 'Department'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY spend_ex_tax DESC

tables.grain: one GL coding line per bank transaction, keyed by its zero-based position in the LineItems array
tables.description: GL coding detail of each bank transaction: how one cash movement was split across accounts, tax rates, items and (via the tracking child table) departments and regions. 'What did we spend directly-coded cash on' resolves here — but only after joining the parent for direction (type), lifecycle (status) and tax treatment (line_amount_types), none of which exist at line level. Line amounts are unsigned and inherit the parent's currency.
gotchas: line_amount changes meaning with the parent's line_amount_types: Inclusive lines carry tax inside line_amount, Exclusive lines on top. Summing raw line_amount across mixed parents double-counts tax — deflate with tax_amount on Inclusive parents.
Lines carry no direction and no lifecycle. Join the parent and filter its status and type, or deleted/voided rows and shadow-document legs (transfer/prepayment/overpayment) pollute spend-by-account.
account_id can be null on code-entered rows; join on account_code to xero_accounts.code as fallback or coded spend silently drops lines.

columns.name: bank_transaction_id
columns.description: Owning bank transaction. A line means nothing alone: direction, status, date, currency and tax treatment all live on the parent — join it before aggregating anything.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of this line in accounting:BankTransaction.LineItems, preserving Xero's presentation order
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in the parent's LineItems array. Completes the primary key and preserves order even if Xero ever omits or regenerates line_item_id.

columns.name: line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the line. Some edit paths regenerate it, so treat it as an opaque handle — (bank_transaction_id, line_index) is the durable key across syncs.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text narrative of what the money was for — usually the only human explanation on directly-coded cash and the richest signal for classifying spend.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Optional unit count; bank transaction lines frequently omit it because LineAmount is entered directly. Guard for null before dividing or multiplying with it.

columns.name: unit_amount
columns.description: Optional per-unit price in the parent's currency (4dp requested). A price, not a total — never sum it; line_amount is the authoritative line value.

columns.name: item_code
columns.description: User-defined code of the inventory/service Item when the line was coded to one; join xero_items on its code column. This is the mutable code, not the immutable ItemID.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: Chart-of-accounts CODE the line posts to. Some rows carry only this and not account_id — spend-by-account queries that ignore the code fallback silently drop lines.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: AccountID the line posts to — the durable join to xero_accounts and the 'where did the money go' dimension for direct cash coding. Fall back to account_code when null.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate code applied to the line — join xero_tax_rates.tax_type for the rate's name and percentage. Filter here for GST/VAT-exempt analysis instead of inferring from amounts.

columns.name: tax_amount
columns.description: Tax on this line in the parent's currency (auto-calculated unless overridden). With Inclusive line_amount_types it sits INSIDE line_amount; with Exclusive it is on top — the deflation term for ex-tax analysis.

columns.name: line_amount
columns.description: The line's value in the parent's currency, and a chameleon: it excludes tax when the parent is Exclusive but INCLUDES it when Inclusive. Ex-tax spend = line_amount - CASE WHEN parent Inclusive THEN tax_amount ELSE 0 END. Unsigned — direction comes from the parent's type.

joins.note: Mandatory before aggregation: the parent carries type (direction), status (lifecycle), date, currency and line_amount_types (tax treatment).
The GL account coded; when account_id is null join xero_accounts.code = account_code as fallback.
Code-based (ItemCode is the join key Xero exposes on lines, not ItemID); null for the majority of cash-coded lines.
Resolves the tax code to name and effective rate.
0-2 tracking assignments per line; aggregate within one category or line amounts double.

examples.question: Directly-coded spend by GL account this year, excluding tax
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(a.code, l.account_code) AS account_code,
       MIN(a.name) AS account_name,
       SUM(l.line_amount - CASE WHEN t.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(l.tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) AS spend_ex_tax
FROM xero_bank_transaction_line_items l
JOIN xero_bank_transactions t ON t.bank_transaction_id = l.bank_transaction_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a
  ON a.account_id = l.account_id
  OR (l.account_id IS NULL AND a.code = l.account_code)
WHERE t.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND t.type = 'SPEND'
  AND t.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY spend_ex_tax DESC

examples.question: Largest directly-coded cash payments this quarter, with their narrative
examples.sql:
SELECT t.date,
       l.description,
       l.line_amount,
       a.name AS gl_account
FROM xero_bank_transaction_line_items l
JOIN xero_bank_transactions t ON t.bank_transaction_id = l.bank_transaction_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
WHERE t.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND t.type = 'SPEND'
  AND t.date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
ORDER BY l.line_amount DESC
LIMIT 25

tables.grain: one money-in or money-out movement on one Xero bank account per BankTransactionID
tables.description: The spend-and-receive money ledger of every Xero bank account: cash coded straight to GL accounts rather than applied to an invoice or bill. Only type SPEND and RECEIVE rows are first-class cash here — the RECEIVE-/SPEND-TRANSFER, -PREPAYMENT and -OVERPAYMENT types are bank-side shadows of records whose accounting truth lives in xero_bank_transfers, xero_prepayments and xero_overpayments, and every transfer contributes TWO rows (one leg per account). Invoice and bill payments never appear here at all (they are xero_payments), so this table is not the complete bank feed; the reconcilable per-account cash truth is journal lines on BANK-class accounts. Amounts are unsigned and in currency_code — direction lives entirely in type.
gotchas: Type is the double-count minefield: *-TRANSFER rows restate xero_bank_transfers (twice — one leg per account), *-PREPAYMENT rows restate xero_prepayments, *-OVERPAYMENT rows restate xero_overpayments. Any income/expense figure built here must restrict to type IN ('SPEND','RECEIVE'); any union with those tables must dedupe via prepayment_id/overpayment_id or the transfer leg ids.

This is NOT the full bank feed: money applied to invoices and bills arrives as xero_payments and never appears here. Per-account total cash movement only reconciles against journal lines on BANK-class accounts (xero_journal_lines x xero_accounts).
Amounts are unsigned; direction is type. SUM(total) over mixed types is meaningless — sign with CASE WHEN type LIKE 'RECEIVE%' THEN total ELSE -total END.
DELETED and VOIDED rows keep flowing from the API and stay in staging; filter status = 'AUTHORISED' in every aggregate or reversed transactions resurrect.
Monetary fields are in currency_code, not the org's base currency. Multiply by COALESCE(currency_rate, 1) before summing across accounts held in different currencies.

columns.name: bank_transaction_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for this money movement and the row key; also the target of xero_bank_transfers' from/to leg pointers.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Direction plus provenance in one vocabulary. SPEND and RECEIVE are directly coded cash; RECEIVE-TRANSFER/SPEND-TRANSFER are the two legs every bank transfer mints (one per account); the -PREPAYMENT/-OVERPAYMENT types are bank-side shadows of prepayment and overpayment documents. Income/expense analysis must restrict to SPEND and RECEIVE — the shadow types restate money that already lives in xero_bank_transfers, xero_prepayments or xero_overpayments, and summing across all types double-counts it.
columns.enums: RECEIVE; RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT; RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT; SPEND; SPEND-OVERPAYMENT; SPEND-PREPAYMENT; RECEIVE-TRANSFER; SPEND-TRANSFER

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: Who the money was received from or paid to, when the bookkeeper coded one — join to xero_contacts. Frequently null on feed-coded rows; null means 'no counterparty recorded', not 'no counterparty'.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized counterparty display name captured with the transaction. Prefer joining xero_contacts via contact_id for the governed dimension — merged contacts keep only the survivor current there.

columns.name: bank_account_account_id
columns.description: The Xero BANK account the cash moved through — join to xero_accounts. Per-account cash analyses group by this, and it is why one transfer lands as two rows (one per account).

columns.name: bank_account_code
columns.description: User-assigned chart-of-accounts code of the bank account, denormalized for display. Codes are editable — the durable join is bank_account_id.

columns.name: bank_account_name
columns.description: Bank account display name as returned with the transaction; convenient for labels, but rename-proof reporting joins xero_accounts on bank_account_id.

columns.name: is_reconciled
columns.description: True once the row is matched against an imported bank statement line. Unreconciled AUTHORISED rows are provisional bookkeeping — not less real, just unverified against the bank; reconciliation-status questions read this, never status.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Business date of the cash movement (YYYY-MM-DD, not when it was keyed in) — the axis for every cash-flow time series. Use updated_date_utc only for sync watermarks, never for business timing.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference. Per the spec it is only supported for plain SPEND and RECEIVE transactions — it cannot be set directly on transfer/prepayment/overpayment shadow rows, whose narrative lives on the source document (a transfer's Reference sits on xero_bank_transfers and propagates to its legs). Never use presence/absence of a reference to classify row types; type is the classifier.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency (Xero's CurrencyCode enum, ~170 values — not enumerated here) of every monetary field on this row. Summing totals across rows with different currency_code produces a number in no currency; convert via currency_rate first.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Exchange rate to the organisation's base currency at the transaction date; populated for non-base-currency bank accounts (user-defined or XE.com day rate otherwise). Base-currency reporting multiplies monetary fields by this, COALESCEd to 1 for base-currency rows. A rate, never summable.

columns.name: url
columns.description: Deep link to the source document in a connected app (rendered as 'Go to App Name' in Xero); a provenance breadcrumb, not analytical data.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED rows are live; DELETED and VOIDED rows keep being returned by the API and keep landing in staging. Every aggregate filters status = 'AUTHORISED' or reversed history re-inflates cash totals.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Declares whether LINE-level amounts include tax (Inclusive), exclude it (Exclusive) or carry none (NoTax). Header sub_total/total_tax/total are already normalized regardless; line-level analysis must consult this or tax double-counts on Inclusive documents.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Transaction total excluding tax, in currency_code, normalized by Xero regardless of line_amount_types — the safe ex-tax measure when you do not need line detail.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Tax on the whole transaction in currency_code; sub_total + total_tax = total. The header-level tax truth even when Inclusive lines bury tax inside line_amount.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive value of the movement in currency_code, always positive — direction lives in type, not the sign. Net cash flow requires CASE on type before summing; raw SUM(total) over mixed types is meaningless.

columns.name: prepayment_id
columns.description: Non-null exactly on RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT/SPEND-PREPAYMENT rows: the Prepayment document this row is the bank-side shadow of. Join xero_prepayments — and count the money in one table, never both.

columns.name: overpayment_id
columns.description: Non-null exactly on RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT/SPEND-OVERPAYMENT rows: the Overpayment document this row shadows. Join xero_overpayments — the credit's allocations live there, the cash movement lives here; sum one side only.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Xero's last-modified audit stamp and the incremental-sync watermark. Meaningless for business timing — an edit bumps it years after date; never use it in cash-flow series.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when at least one attachment (receipt scan, source doc) exists. The ingester uses it to gate per-transaction attachment fan-out (org_meta's xero_attachments) under Xero's 60-calls/min budget.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-time validation marker (e.g. ERROR/WARNING) echoed on batch upsert responses; effectively always null on read scans. Never encode business logic on it — status is the lifecycle field.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Array of write-rejection messages the API echoes on failed upserts; empty on read scans. Kept verbatim for mechanical completeness — analysts should never filter on it.

columns.name: contact
columns.description: BankTransaction.Contact as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: See LineItems Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: bank_account
columns.description: BankTransaction.BankAccount as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: The bank account the cash moved through; xero_accounts.type/class = BANK rows only.
Counterparty when recorded; often null on feed-coded spend/receive rows.
Only for RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT/SPEND-PREPAYMENT shadows — the document side of the same money.
Only for RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT/SPEND-OVERPAYMENT shadows — the document side of the same money.
Resolves a *-TRANSFER leg to its transfer instruction; each transfer matches exactly two transaction rows (one per account), so this join is many legs to one transfer.
GL coding detail; join here for spend-by-account or tracking cuts.

examples.question: Net directly-coded cash flow by month over the last 12 months
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'RECEIVE' THEN total ELSE -total END) AS net_direct_cash
FROM xero_bank_transactions
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND type IN ('SPEND', 'RECEIVE')
  AND date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '12 months'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Which bank accounts have unreconciled transactions, and how much value is sitting unmatched?
examples.sql:
SELECT a.name AS bank_account,
       COUNT(*) AS unreconciled_count,
       SUM(t.total) AS unreconciled_value
FROM xero_bank_transactions t
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = t.bank_account_account_id
WHERE t.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND t.is_reconciled = false
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unreconciled_value DESC

examples.question: Gross cash in and out per bank account this year, excluding internal transfers
examples.sql:
SELECT a.name AS bank_account,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.type LIKE 'RECEIVE%' THEN t.total ELSE 0 END) AS cash_in,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.type LIKE 'SPEND%' THEN t.total ELSE 0 END) AS cash_out
FROM xero_bank_transactions t
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = t.bank_account_account_id
WHERE t.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND t.type NOT LIKE '%-TRANSFER'
  AND t.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY cash_out DESC

tables.grain: one instruction moving funds between two bank accounts of the same organisation per BankTransferID
tables.description: Movements of funds between two of the organisation's own bank accounts. Each row is the transfer instruction; Xero simultaneously mints a SPEND-TRANSFER bank transaction in the source account and a RECEIVE-TRANSFER in the destination (from_bank_transaction_id / to_bank_transaction_id point at them), so the money in this table always appears twice more in xero_bank_transactions. Transfers relocate cash — they are never income, expense, or a change in total cash, and any flow metric that fails to exclude their legs invents money.
gotchas: Every transfer already exists twice in xero_bank_transactions (SPEND-TRANSFER and RECEIVE-TRANSFER legs, linked by from/to_bank_transaction_id). Counting transfers alongside bank transactions without excluding those legs counts internal moves as both spend AND income.
Transfers change WHERE cash sits, not how much exists: they belong in no revenue, expense or net-cash-flow figure, only in per-account balance movement.

The default GET omits DELETED transfers — the scan must pass includeDeleted=true, and analyses must still filter status = 'AUTHORISED'. With no UpdatedDateUTC on the record, deletion never bumps a watermark; only full rescans catch it.

For cross-currency transfers, amount alone does not tell you what each account saw — read each leg's total (in its own account's currency) via the leg joins; currency_rate records the conversion Xero applied.

columns.name: bank_transfer_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the transfer instruction; each such instruction also mints exactly two rows in xero_bank_transactions.

columns.name: from_bank_account_account_id
columns.description: Source bank account the money left — join xero_accounts; the SPEND-TRANSFER leg lands in this account.

columns.name: from_bank_account_code
columns.description: Chart code of the source bank account, denormalized for display; codes are editable, so durable joins use from_bank_account_id.

columns.name: from_bank_account_name
columns.description: Display name of the source bank account as returned with the transfer; label convenience only — rename-proof reporting joins xero_accounts.

columns.name: to_bank_account_account_id
columns.description: Destination bank account the money entered — join xero_accounts; the RECEIVE-TRANSFER leg lands in this account.

columns.name: to_bank_account_code
columns.description: Chart code of the destination bank account, denormalized for display; the durable join is to_bank_account_id.

columns.name: to_bank_account_name
columns.description: Display name of the destination bank account as returned with the transfer; prefer the id join to xero_accounts for governed labels.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The transferred amount as entered on the instruction. Internal movement, NEVER income or expense — excluding this money from cash in/out is the whole point of this table. For cross-currency transfers, each account's local-currency truth is its leg's total in xero_bank_transactions.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Business date the transfer is recorded on (YYYY-MM-DD, carried by both legs) — the axis for movement-over-time questions; not the settlement date at the real-world bank.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Read-only rate Xero recorded for cross-currency transfers; null/1 for same-currency moves. A rate, never summable — convert before aggregating mixed-currency transfer volumes.

columns.name: from_bank_transaction_id
columns.description: Points at the SPEND-TRANSFER bank transaction minted in the source account — the join that proves a bank transaction row is a transfer leg rather than real spend.

columns.name: to_bank_transaction_id
columns.description: Points at the RECEIVE-TRANSFER bank transaction minted in the destination account — with from_bank_transaction_id, the pair to exclude from income/expense analysis.

columns.name: from_is_reconciled
columns.description: Whether the source-account leg has been matched to an imported statement line; 'transfer in flight' checks read both reconciliation flags.

columns.name: to_is_reconciled
columns.description: Whether the destination-account leg has been matched to an imported statement line; false here with from_is_reconciled true is the classic in-transit signature.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference for the transfer — the spec's plural ('Reference for the transactions') covers the two leg transactions the transfer mints. Narrative only, no lifecycle or matching semantics.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when the transfer carries attachments; gates org_meta's per-parent attachment fan-out under Xero's 60-calls/min rate budget.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: Creation audit stamp — the only timestamp BankTransfer exposes, so it doubles as the append watermark. A later deletion bumps nothing; only full rescans with includeDeleted=true catch it.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED is live; DELETED transfers are only returned when the scan passes includeDeleted=true, and must be filtered from every total or reversed internal moves count as real.

columns.name: from_tracking
columns.description: Up to two tracking category/option references applied to the source side, verbatim as [{TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}]. Rarely used; unnest with jsonb_array_elements when a category cut of transfers is genuinely needed.

columns.name: to_tracking
columns.description: Up to two tracking category/option references applied to the destination side, same shape and caveats as from_tracking; the two sides may legitimately differ.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Array of write-rejection messages echoed on failed upserts; empty on read scans and kept only for mechanical completeness — never filter on it.

joins.note: Source bank account dimension.
Destination bank account dimension (second alias of xero_accounts).
The SPEND-TRANSFER leg; its total is the source account's own-currency amount.
The RECEIVE-TRANSFER leg; its total is the destination account's own-currency amount.

examples.question: How much cash moved between our own bank accounts each month this year, in base currency?
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', bt.date) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS transfers,
       SUM(src.total * COALESCE(src.currency_rate, 1)) AS amount_moved_base
FROM xero_bank_transfers bt
JOIN xero_bank_transactions src ON src.bank_transaction_id = bt.from_bank_transaction_id
WHERE bt.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND bt.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Which transfers have an unreconciled leg (possibly still in transit)?
examples.sql:
SELECT bt.date,
       fa.name AS from_account,
       ta.name AS to_account,
       bt.amount,
       bt.from_is_reconciled,
       bt.to_is_reconciled
FROM xero_bank_transfers bt
JOIN xero_accounts fa ON fa.account_id = bt.from_bank_account_account_id
JOIN xero_accounts ta ON ta.account_id = bt.to_bank_account_account_id
WHERE bt.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND (bt.from_is_reconciled = false OR bt.to_is_reconciled = false)
ORDER BY bt.date DESC

tables.grain: one batch payment header per BatchPaymentID, grouping member payments into a single bank movement
tables.description: Header for a group of bill payments (PAYBATCH) or invoice collections (RECBATCH) that hit the bank as one consolidated transaction. The members are ordinary rows in xero_payments carrying this batch_payment_id, and total_amount equals the sum of those members — so a metric that aggregates both tables counts the same cash twice. This table answers 'what single movements will the bank statement show' and carries the bank-file reference fields; per-document settlement detail always comes from the member payments.
gotchas: This table and xero_payments describe the SAME cash at two grains: total_amount is the sum of member payments. Never add the two tables in one metric.
DELETED batches keep returning from the API (deletion is UI-only); filter status = 'AUTHORISED' on every aggregate.

GET /BatchPayments has no page parameter — the scan is a full-window pull with If-Modified-Since incrementals. The op does accept where and order params, but ordering cannot substitute for pagination on large windows.
reference/particulars/code (NZ), details (non-NZ) and narrative (UK) are region-exclusive: for any single org most of them are null. Their absence is regional, not missing data.

columns.name: batch_payment_id
columns.description: Xero's read-only identifier for the batch and the row key; the value member payments carry in xero_payments.batch_payment_id.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Direction of the whole batch: PAYBATCH pays supplier bills, RECBATCH collects customer invoices. Filter it on every batched-cash question — mixing types nets disbursements against receipts into a meaningless figure.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED is live; DELETED batches (removed in the Xero UI — the API cannot delete them) keep returning with their members intact. Filter status = 'AUTHORISED' everywhere or deleted batches inflate cash movement.

columns.name: account_account_id
columns.description: The bank account the single consolidated movement hits, from the embedded Account stub. Join xero_accounts for code/name; the batch appears on this account's statement as ONE line.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date the batch is paid or collected — the business axis for batched cash flow. Member payments carry their own dates which normally match but are independently editable.

columns.name: date_string
columns.description: String twin of date as returned by the API. Redundant — read date.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Header-level amount slot whose spec text is copied verbatim from Payment.Amount (a documented spec quirk) — it is a write-side field, not the reconciled batch figure. Report batched cash from total_amount, the read-only sum Xero computes from the member payments; never let this column and total_amount both feed a metric.

columns.name: total_amount
columns.description: Read-only sum of the member payments, computed by Xero. Equals SUM(xero_payments.amount) over AUTHORISED members with this batch_payment_id; any metric that adds both this and the member rows has double-counted the cash.

columns.name: is_reconciled
columns.description: Whole-batch reconciliation state against the bank feed: the batch lands on the statement as one line, and this flag says whether that line has been matched. Member payments carry their own is_reconciled in xero_payments — read the level you are actually asking about; do not treat this header flag as a per-payment guarantee.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: (NZ orgs only) Optional reference shown with the batch on the bank reconciliation Find & Match screen and possibly the imported bank statement. Region-specific: null outside NZ.

columns.name: particulars
columns.description: (NZ orgs only) Bank 'particulars' code accompanying the batch on statements and bank rec. Null outside NZ.

columns.name: code
columns.description: (NZ orgs only) Bank 'code' reference accompanying the batch. Null outside NZ; not an account code — do not join it to anything.

columns.name: details
columns.description: (Non-NZ orgs) Reference sent to the org's bank with the batch transaction, max 18 chars. Free text for statement matching.

columns.name: narrative
columns.description: (UK orgs only) Statement-line text shown in Xero only, max 18 chars. Null outside the UK.

columns.name: payments
columns.description: Verbatim member-payment stubs exactly as the BatchPayments endpoint returned them, kept for payload-level reconciliation. The queryable membership edge is xero_payments.batch_payment_id — always use that join; these stubs are partial and go stale.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit watermark for incremental sync (paired with the op's If-Modified-Since parameter). Record-change time, not cash time — bucket cash on date.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation messages retained verbatim for ingestion debugging; empty on healthy reads.

joins.note: Member payments; SUM(members.amount) over AUTHORISED rows reconciles to total_amount.
The bank account carrying the consolidated movement.

examples.question: Supplier disbursements made via batch payments, by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS disbursed
FROM xero_batch_payments
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED' AND type = 'PAYBATCH'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Do any batches disagree with the sum of their member payments?
examples.sql:
SELECT b.batch_payment_id, b.total_amount, SUM(p.amount) AS member_sum
FROM xero_batch_payments b
JOIN xero_payments p ON p.batch_payment_id = b.batch_payment_id AND p.status = 'AUTHORISED'
WHERE b.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING b.total_amount <> SUM(p.amount)

tables.grain: one branding theme per BrandingThemeID
tables.description: The org's document templates (logo, layout) referenced by invoices, credit notes, quotes and repeating templates via branding_theme_id. A small unpaged config set. Analytically useful because many orgs use themes to separate trading names or brands — making this an accidental business-unit dimension.
gotchas: Documents with branding_theme_id NULL use the default theme (sort_order = 0) implicitly — a per-theme revenue split must COALESCE nulls onto the default theme or it under-reports the main brand.
Themes hard-delete: no status, no watermark. Disappearance is detected by full identity rescan; joins from historical documents to a deleted theme need LEFT JOIN.

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the theme and the row key; documents reference it via their branding_theme_id.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name of the theme — often a trading name or brand, which is exactly why grouping documents by theme can approximate business units.

columns.name: logo_url
columns.description: Location of the logo image used by the theme; presentation only.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Always INVOICE per the spec; carried for fidelity, filter on nothing.

columns.name: sort_order
columns.description: Ranked order of themes; 0 marks the org's DEFAULT theme — documents with a null branding_theme_id implicitly use it.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: Creation audit stamp. There is no update watermark — the set is small and fully rescanned each sync.

examples.question: Billed revenue by branding theme (brand/trading name)
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(bt.name, dflt.name, '(unknown theme)') AS theme,
       SUM(i.sub_total * COALESCE(i.currency_rate, 1)) AS billed_net
FROM xero_invoices i
LEFT JOIN xero_branding_themes bt ON bt.branding_theme_id = i.branding_theme_id
LEFT JOIN xero_branding_themes dflt ON i.branding_theme_id IS NULL AND dflt.sort_order = 0
WHERE i.type = 'ACCREC' AND i.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY billed_net DESC

tables.grain: one budgeted period amount per (budget, account, period)
tables.description: The numbers of the planning layer: one row per month bucket ('2019-08') per budgeted account per budget. Modeled as last_value_over_time on the period axis because for balance-sheet accounts the figure is a TARGET BALANCE — summing targets across months double-counts. P&L-account rows are genuinely monthly flows and may be summed across periods, but only after checking the joined account's class; the safe default is to compare period-to-period. Rows arrive via the per-budget fan-out swept over DateFrom/DateTo windows.
tables.additivityAxis: period
gotchas: last_value_over_time on period: balance-sheet account rows are targets — summing them across months manufactures fictional balances. Sum across periods only for accounts whose class is REVENUE or EXPENSE.

Budget amounts are unsigned-positive; ledger actuals for revenue are negative (credits). Variance = budget.amount - (-SUM(net_amount)) for revenue accounts — skip the sign flip and every revenue line looks catastrophically under budget.
The API returns only the DateFrom/DateTo window requested (default roughly the current fiscal year); missing months mean the sweep has not covered them, not that the budget is zero.

columns.name: budget_id
columns.description: Owning budget — inherited from the fan-out; always predicate on ONE budget_id or overlapping OVERALL and TRACKING plans double-count.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: Budgeted account — inherited from the parent budget line; the join to actuals in xero_journal_lines.

columns.name: budget_balances
columns.description: Zero-based position in the line's BudgetBalances array — provenance anchor for the exploded container; chronological within the fetched window, but key on period, not on this.

columns.name: period
columns.description: Month bucket the amount applies to, as 'YYYY-MM' text (e.g. '2019-08'). Align to actuals with to_char(journal_date, 'YYYY-MM') or cast with to_date(period || '-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD').

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The budgeted value for the period — empirically the monetary figure, despite the spec's miscopied 'LineItem Quantity' description. Budget amounts are positive for both revenue and expense plans; flip the sign of REVENUE-class actuals (or ABS them) before computing variance.

columns.name: unit_amount
columns.description: The spec labels this 'Budgeted amount'; in practice it mirrors amount for monetary budgets. Prefer amount for variance math and treat divergence between the two as a signal to inspect the tenant's payload.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Footnotes the budget owner attached to this period's figure — context for anomalous months, not data.

joins.note: Composite parent key — both columns required.
Type decides whether this is the org plan or a tracking slice.
Class tells you whether amount is a monthly flow (P&L) or a target balance (balance sheet).

examples.question: Budget vs actual by month for expense accounts, overall budget, this year
examples.sql:
SELECT bb.period, a.code, a.name,
       bb.amount AS budgeted,
       COALESCE(SUM(l.net_amount), 0) AS actual,
       bb.amount - COALESCE(SUM(l.net_amount), 0) AS remaining
FROM xero_budget_balances bb
JOIN xero_budgets b ON b.budget_id = bb.budget_id AND b.type = 'OVERALL'
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = bb.account_id AND a.class = 'EXPENSE'
LEFT JOIN xero_journals j ON to_char(j.journal_date, 'YYYY-MM') = bb.period
LEFT JOIN xero_journal_lines l ON l.journal_id = j.journal_id AND l.account_id = bb.account_id
WHERE bb.period >= to_char(date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE), 'YYYY-MM')
GROUP BY bb.period, bb.account_id, a.code, a.name, bb.amount
ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Total revenue plan vs actual this year (sign-corrected)
examples.sql:
WITH plan AS (
  SELECT SUM(bb.amount) AS budgeted_revenue
  FROM xero_budget_balances bb
  JOIN xero_budgets b ON b.budget_id = bb.budget_id AND b.type = 'OVERALL'
  JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = bb.account_id AND a.class = 'REVENUE'
  WHERE bb.period >= to_char(date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE), 'YYYY-MM')
), actual AS (
  SELECT -SUM(l.net_amount) AS actual_revenue
  FROM xero_journal_lines l
  JOIN xero_journals j ON j.journal_id = l.journal_id
  JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id AND a.class = 'REVENUE'
  WHERE j.journal_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
)
SELECT plan.budgeted_revenue, COALESCE(actual.actual_revenue, 0) AS actual_revenue
FROM plan CROSS JOIN actual

tables.grain: one budgeted account per (budget, account)
tables.description: The membership bridge between a budget and the chart of accounts: one row per account the budget plans, with the period amounts hanging off xero_budget_balances. Carries no measures itself — its job is to say WHICH accounts a budget covers, and to anchor the (budget, account) key the balances repeat.
gotchas: No measures here — a budget total computed by counting or joining only this table is empty by construction; the amounts are in xero_budget_balances.

columns.name: budget_id
columns.description: Owning budget — inherited key from the fan-out parent.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: The budgeted general ledger account — the join that lets budget balances meet actual journal lines account-by-account.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: The account's code at fetch time — convenience denorm; account_id is the durable identity.

columns.name: budget_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the budget's BudgetLines array — provenance anchor for the exploded container; Xero's statement-order listing of the budgeted accounts.

joins.note: Type (OVERALL vs TRACKING) changes what the plan covers.
Class decides whether the budgeted figures are period flows (P&L) or targets (balance sheet).
The per-period amounts for this budgeted account.

examples.question: Which P&L accounts does the overall budget actually plan?
examples.sql:
SELECT a.code, a.name, a.class
FROM xero_budget_lines bl
JOIN xero_budgets b ON b.budget_id = bl.budget_id AND b.type = 'OVERALL'
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = bl.account_id
WHERE a.class IN ('REVENUE', 'EXPENSE')
ORDER BY a.class, a.code

tables.grain: one tracking category/option pair scoping a budget per (budget, tracking category)
tables.description: The scope declaration of a TRACKING budget: which tracking option (e.g. Region = East) the budget's numbers apply to, up to two pairs per budget mirroring the two-category limit. Empty for OVERALL budgets.
