To compare a tracking budget against actuals, actuals must be filtered through xero_journal_line_tracking to the SAME option pairs — comparing it to unfiltered actuals understates performance against plan.
gotchas: A tracking budget's variance is only meaningful against actuals filtered to the SAME option pair(s) through xero_journal_line_tracking — untracked ledger lines belong to no tracking budget at all.

columns.name: budget_id
columns.description: The tracking budget being scoped — inherited key.

columns.name: tracking
columns.description: Zero-based position in the budget's Tracking array (0 or 1) — provenance anchor for the exploded container.

columns.name: tracking_category_id
columns.description: The dimension the budget slices on — join to xero_tracking_categories.

columns.name: tracking_option_id
columns.description: The specific option the budget covers — the value actuals must be filtered to via xero_journal_line_tracking for a like-for-like variance.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Category name at fetch time — display; ids are the join.

columns.name: option
columns.description: Option label at fetch time — display; group and filter by tracking_option_id.

joins.note: Only TRACKING budgets have rows here.
Current dimension name/status.
Current option name/status.

examples.question: Which segment does each tracking budget plan?
examples.sql:
SELECT b.description AS budget, t.name AS category, t.option AS segment
FROM xero_budget_tracking t
JOIN xero_budgets b ON b.budget_id = t.budget_id
ORDER BY b.description, t.tracking

tables.grain: one budget definition per BudgetID
tables.description: The org's planning layer: the OVERALL budget covers the whole org, while TRACKING budgets re-plan the same org sliced to specific tracking option pairs (see xero_budget_tracking). Budgets are definitions only — the numbers live in xero_budget_lines/xero_budget_balances fetched per budget. Because a tracking budget overlaps the overall one, budget-vs-actual must pick exactly ONE BudgetID per question; summing across budgets counts the same plan twice.
gotchas: A TRACKING budget is a re-slice of the same plan space as OVERALL: SUM over all budgets is meaningless. Resolve the question to one budget_id first.

The budgets LIST returns definitions only — lines and balances require the per-BudgetID fetch with a DateFrom/DateTo window. A budget with no rows in xero_budget_balances may simply not have been swept for that period yet.

columns.name: budget_id
columns.description: Xero's budget identifier and the row key; the fan-out parameter for the per-budget line fetch.

columns.name: type
columns.description: OVERALL is the org-wide plan (exactly one, named 'Overall Budget' in Xero); TRACKING budgets re-plan a tracking slice. Org-level budget-vs-actual uses OVERALL; segment-level uses the matching TRACKING budget — mixing them double-counts the plan.

columns.name: description
columns.description: The budget's display name as entered in Xero — the only human handle for choosing among multiple tracking budgets.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last edit to the budget — the client-side watermark (the list op has no If-Modified-Since); a change here triggers re-fetching the budget's lines and balances.

joins.note: One row per budgeted account; arrives via the GET /Budgets/{BudgetID} fan-out.
Populated only for type = 'TRACKING' — defines which segment the budget plans.

examples.question: What budgets exist and what kind are they?
examples.sql:
SELECT b.budget_id, b.type, b.description, b.updated_date_utc
FROM xero_budgets b
ORDER BY b.type, b.description

tables.grain: one authorized app-to-tenant connection per connection id
tables.description: The authorization roster from the identity API: one row per Xero tenant the user has currently consented to share with Albert. tenant_id is the xero-tenant-id every accounting call is scoped by and the join to xero_organisations. This table defines the sync universe — a tenant that vanishes from it has revoked access, and its staged data freezes at the last successful sync rather than being deleted.
gotchas: A tenant missing from this table has revoked access: its staged data is frozen at the last sync, not deleted. Reporting stale tenants as current is the classic multi-tenant error — check connection presence before trusting recency.
tenantType PRACTICE rows carry no accounting data and no organisation profile; inner joins to xero_organisations drop them and unfiltered counts inflate the org universe.
updated_date_utc moves on reconnection events only — never use it to reason about when the org's DATA last changed.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Identifier of the authorization itself (the spec field is literally 'id'). A disconnect/reconnect can mint a new connection_id while tenant_id stays constant — track tenants by tenant_id, not by this.

columns.name: connection_tenant_id
columns.description: The Xero tenant UUID — the xero-tenant-id header value scoping every API call, and the join key to xero_organisations.organisation_id (equal for ORGANISATION tenants). This, not connection_id, is the durable identity of the org.

columns.name: auth_event_id
columns.description: Shared by every connection granted on the same consent screen — the batch key for multi-org authorizations, and the /Connections filter parameter for 'what did that consent just add'.

columns.name: tenant_type
columns.description: ORGANISATION or PRACTICE (documented informally, not a closed spec enum). Only ORGANISATION tenants have accounting data behind them — PRACTICE rows have no xero_organisations profile and no documents, so unfiltered tenant counts overstate the reporting universe.

columns.name: tenant_name
columns.description: Display name captured at authorization time. It can drift from xero_organisations.name after a rename — prefer the organisation profile's name for labels when a profile row exists.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When the user first connected this tenant to the app. Data earlier than this exists via backfill, not live capture — useful when judging watermark gaps.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Most recent (re)connection time; differs from created_date_utc when the user disconnected and later reconnected. It is consent recency — NOT a data-change watermark for anything inside the org.

joins.note: ORGANISATION tenants only — PRACTICE connections have no organisation profile, so LEFT JOIN when counting connections.

examples.question: Which tenants are currently authorized, and when were they last (re)connected?
examples.sql:
SELECT tenant_name, tenant_type, created_date_utc, updated_date_utc
FROM xero_connections
ORDER BY updated_date_utc DESC

examples.question: Which authorized tenants have no organisation profile (practices)?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.tenant_name, c.tenant_type
FROM xero_connections c
LEFT JOIN xero_organisations o ON o.organisation_id = c.connection_tenant_id
WHERE o.organisation_id IS NULL

tables.grain: one address per contact per address type (POBOX or STREET)
tables.description: Typed address slots exploded from the contact record. Xero stores at most one address per type: POBOX is the postal/billing address that prints on documents, STREET is the physical/delivery address — geographic questions must pick the type that matches their intent. Xero pads responses with empty stubs, so a row proves the slot exists, not that an address does.
gotchas: Empty stubs are routine: Xero returns address entries with every component blank. Count 'contacts with an address' via NULLIF on line1/city, never via row existence.

POBOX vs STREET is billing vs physical. Shipping-territory analysis on POBOX rows (or billing analysis on STREET rows) answers a different question than the one asked — and only one of the two slots may exist for any contact.
country is free text, not ISO: the same nation appears under several spellings, and blank does not mean the org's home country — it means nobody typed one.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: Owning contact; with address_type forms the key because Xero returns a fixed-type set rather than an open list.

columns.name: address_type
columns.description: Which fixed slot this row fills. POBOX is the postal/billing address Xero prints on invoices; STREET is the physical/delivery location. 'Where do we bill' and 'where do we ship' are different filters on this column — defaulting to whichever type happens to exist quietly mixes the two.

columns.name: address_line1
columns.description: First street line, and the usual emptiness test for the whole slot — Xero returns fully blank stubs, so 'has an address' means a non-empty line1 or city, not the existence of a row.

columns.name: address_line2
columns.description: Second street line (suite, unit, floor). Free text, frequently blank; concatenate non-empty lines 1-4 in order to reconstruct the printed block.

columns.name: address_line3
columns.description: Third street line; overflow from users who type whole addresses into the line fields rather than the structured city/region columns — check here before declaring city empty.

columns.name: address_line4
columns.description: Fourth and last street line; rarely used, but part of the printed block when present.

columns.name: city
columns.description: City/town as typed by users — unvalidated free text, so expect casing and spelling variants; normalize before grouping.

columns.name: region
columns.description: State/province/county as free text ('CA', 'California', 'Calif.' all occur). Useful for coarse geography only after normalization.

columns.name: postal_code
columns.description: Postcode/ZIP as typed. Fine-grained enough to identify a household in some countries (UK), so treated as PII despite its analytical appeal for territory mapping.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country as free text (letters only, max 50) — NOT ISO codes. 'UK', 'United Kingdom' and 'Great Britain' fragment the same country across group-bys; map to ISO before any country-level rollup, and treat empty string as unknown, not domestic.

columns.name: attention_to
columns.description: The 'Attention:' person line printed above the address block — a personal name, hence PII, and occasionally the only place a real human is named on an organisation contact.

joins.note: Join to reach lifecycle and customer/supplier flags; geographic rollups should exclude ARCHIVED parents.

examples.question: Active customers by billing country
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(a.country, ''), '(none recorded)') AS country,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.contact_id) AS customers
FROM xero_contact_addresses a
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = a.contact_id
WHERE a.address_type = 'POBOX'
  AND c.is_customer AND c.contact_status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY customers DESC

tables.grain: one current AR/AP balance snapshot per contact, as of the latest sync
tables.description: Xero's own answer to 'what does this contact owe us, and what do we owe them, right now': outstanding and overdue amounts for accounts receivable (their unpaid sales invoices) and accounts payable (your unpaid bills to them). Amounts are RAW document-currency sums that Xero explicitly does not convert to the base currency, so cross-contact totals are only meaningful in single-currency books. This is a snapshot that each sync overwrites — use it for 'top debtors today', and use invoices or journals for aging, history, or base-currency totals.
tables.additivityAxis: time — each sync overwrites the snapshot; only the latest as-of value is valid, and summing a contact's balance across refresh points double-counts
gotchas: Amounts are explicitly NOT converted to base currency. Any SUM across contacts in a multi-currency org adds dollars to euros; group or annotate by xero_contacts.default_currency, and treat even a single contact's figure as suspect if they trade in multiple currencies.

Snapshot semantics: the table holds only the latest as-of values. There is no history here — trend questions ('is our AR growing?') need invoice/journal data, and summing this table across syncs or dates double-counts.

Overdue is contained in Outstanding. outstanding + overdue is a meaningless number that looks plausible enough to ship — the correct decomposition is (outstanding - overdue) not-yet-due plus (overdue) late.
Cross-check against SUM(amount_due) of open AUTHORISED invoices per contact: persistent mismatches indicate scan lag on one of the two tables, and the invoice-side figure is the auditable one.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: The contact this snapshot belongs to; one row per contact, refreshed in place by every scan.

columns.name: accounts_receivable_outstanding
columns.description: What the contact currently owes you across unpaid sales invoices — in RAW document currencies, unconverted to base. For a contact invoiced in several currencies this is a sum across currencies and therefore not a real number; reconcile against open ACCREC invoices in xero_invoices when precision matters.

columns.name: accounts_receivable_overdue
columns.description: The past-due PORTION of accounts_receivable_outstanding — a subset, not an increment. Adding outstanding and overdue double-counts every late invoice; 'not yet due' is outstanding minus overdue.

columns.name: accounts_payable_outstanding
columns.description: What you currently owe the contact across unpaid bills, in raw document currencies. The supplier-side mirror of AR outstanding, with the identical multi-currency trap.

columns.name: accounts_payable_overdue
columns.description: The past-due portion of accounts_payable_outstanding — again a subset. This is the 'we are paying suppliers late' signal, not an addition to the amount owed.

joins.note: Always bring the parent's default_currency into results as the (imperfect) currency frame, and filter contact_status='ACTIVE' for live exposure lists.

examples.question: Top 10 debtors by overdue receivables right now
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, c.default_currency, b.accounts_receivable_overdue
FROM xero_contact_balances b
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = b.contact_id
WHERE c.contact_status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND b.accounts_receivable_overdue > 0
ORDER BY b.accounts_receivable_overdue DESC
LIMIT 10

examples.question: Suppliers we currently owe money to, largest exposure first
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, c.default_currency,
       b.accounts_payable_outstanding,
       b.accounts_payable_overdue
FROM xero_contact_balances b
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = b.contact_id
WHERE c.contact_status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND b.accounts_payable_outstanding > 0
ORDER BY b.accounts_payable_outstanding DESC

tables.grain: one CIS deduction profile per contact (UK Construction Industry Scheme orgs only)
tables.description: Per-contact UK Construction Industry Scheme configuration, fetched by fan-out per contact: whether the contact is a CIS subcontractor and the deduction rate Xero withholds from their payments. Only UK construction orgs have this data at all — for everyone else the endpoint returns nothing, and absence of a row means 'not applicable', never 'not a subcontractor'. The rate is applied at payment time; the actual deducted amounts live on documents, not here.
gotchas: Jurisdiction gate: only UK orgs under the Construction Industry Scheme return data. Treat missing rows as not-applicable — reporting 'no subcontractors' for a NZ org from this table is a category error.
rate is only returned when cis_enabled is true, so null rate is expected on disabled rows and alarming on enabled ones — the latter signals a partial fan-out worth re-running.
This is a per-contact fan-out endpoint under the shared rate budget (60 calls/min, daily caps). Availability is optional: scan plans should gate it on the org being UK-based before spending budget.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: The contact this CIS profile configures, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: cis_enabled
columns.description: Marks the contact as a CIS subcontractor for a UK construction org. Only meaningful where rows exist at all: a missing row in a non-UK org is jurisdictional absence, not false, so left-join semantics matter when flagging subcontractors.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: CIS deduction percentage withheld from the subcontractor's payments (read-only; Xero omits it entirely when cis_enabled is false, so null on a disabled row is normal). A RATE — apply it, never sum or average it across contacts.

joins.note: Left-join from contacts: most contacts legitimately have no row, even in UK orgs.

examples.question: Which subcontractors are CIS-enabled and at what deduction rate?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, s.rate
FROM xero_contact_cis_settings s
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = s.contact_id
WHERE s.cis_enabled
ORDER BY s.rate DESC, c.name

examples.question: CIS-enabled subcontractors whose deduction rate is missing (partial fan-out check)
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, s.contact_id
FROM xero_contact_cis_settings s
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = s.contact_id
WHERE s.cis_enabled AND s.rate IS NULL
ORDER BY c.name

tables.grain: one membership edge per (contact group, contact) pair
tables.description: The many-to-many bridge between contacts and their groups, exploded from the per-group fan-out fetch — the list endpoint never includes members. Membership is CURRENT-STATE only: Xero silently removes archived and merged contacts from groups and keeps no history, so segment membership cannot be reconstructed for the past. Contacts can belong to many groups at once, which makes every join through this table a deliberate one-to-many fan-out.
gotchas: Members only arrive from the per-group fetch (GET /ContactGroups/{ContactGroupID}); the list endpoint returns groups with no Contacts array. An empty members table alongside populated groups means the fan-out has not run, not that groups are empty.

A contact can sit in many groups, so revenue or counts joined through memberships overlap across segments. That is segmentation semantics, not a bug — but summing segments to a total double-counts multi-group contacts.
Xero silently strips archived and merged contacts out of groups, with no event and no history: segment counts shrink without explanation, and past membership is unrecoverable from the API.

Fan-out calls share the 60/min rate budget. Cardinality is small (few groups per org), so the scan planner should still fetch all groups' members every sync — staleness here corrupts segment answers quietly.

columns.name: contact_group_id
columns.description: The group side of the edge, inherited from the fan-out parent.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: The contact side of the edge, from the membership stub Xero nests in the group response. Join xero_contacts for everything beyond identity — the stub carries only id and name.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Denormalized name captured at fan-out time; it lags renames. xero_contacts.name is current truth — this copy exists to make the edge readable without a join and to reconcile stale fan-outs.

joins.note: Resolves the segment label.
Resolves the full contact. Xero removes archived and merged contacts from groups, but staging lags the per-group fan-out — still filter the parent's contact_status='ACTIVE' rather than assuming it.
The segment-revenue path. Contacts in multiple groups duplicate their invoices across segments — segment figures overlap by design and must never be summed to a company total.

examples.question: Which contacts are in the VIP group?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, c.email_address
FROM xero_contact_group_members m
JOIN xero_contact_groups g ON g.contact_group_id = m.contact_group_id
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = m.contact_id
WHERE g.name = 'VIP'
ORDER BY c.name

examples.question: Sales revenue (ex-tax, base currency) by contact-group segment this year (segments overlap; do not total)
examples.sql:
SELECT g.name AS segment,
       SUM(i.sub_total * COALESCE(i.currency_rate, 1)) AS revenue_base_ex_tax
FROM xero_contact_group_members m
JOIN xero_contact_groups g ON g.contact_group_id = m.contact_group_id
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.contact_id = m.contact_id
WHERE i.type = 'ACCREC'
  AND i.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
  AND i.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY g.contact_group_id, g.name
ORDER BY revenue_base_ex_tax DESC

tables.grain: one contact group per ContactGroupID
tables.description: User-curated contact segments ('VIP', 'Wholesale', 'North region') — the cheapest segmentation dimension Xero offers, maintained by hand in the org. The list endpoint returns only ACTIVE groups and omits members entirely; membership arrives via the per-group fan-out into xero_contact_group_members. No modified watermark exists, so the ingester rescans the (small) set every sync and detects deletions as vanished ids.
gotchas: Deleted groups never arrive marked DELETED — they simply stop appearing. Rely on the platform's identity-diff tombstones, not on the status column, to reason about removals.
No UpdatedDateUTC and no paging: this is a full-rescan-every-sync endpoint. Cheap because orgs keep few groups, but it means staleness here is bounded by scan cadence, not watermark correctness.

columns.name: contact_group_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the group and the fan-out parameter that fetches its members.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The segment label as the org typed it. This is business vocabulary, not system vocabulary — surface it verbatim in answers, and expect renames to change history-free (there is no audit trail).

columns.name: status
columns.description: Declares ACTIVE/DELETED, but list GETs return only ACTIVE groups — DELETED ones vanish from responses rather than arriving flagged. Expect only ACTIVE in staging; a group's deletion shows up as its id disappearing on identity diff, at which point the platform tombstones the row.

columns.name: contacts
columns.description: The ContactID and Name of Contacts in a contact group. Returned on GETs when the ContactGroupID is supplied in the URL. Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_contact_group_members (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: The membership edge; a group with zero member rows may be genuinely empty or awaiting its fan-out fetch.

examples.question: Contact groups by size
examples.sql:
SELECT g.name, COUNT(m.contact_id) AS member_count
FROM xero_contact_groups g
LEFT JOIN xero_contact_group_members m
  ON m.contact_group_id = g.contact_group_id
GROUP BY g.contact_group_id, g.name
ORDER BY member_count DESC

tables.grain: one additional contact person per contact per array position
tables.description: The ADDITIONAL people attached to a contact — the primary person lives on xero_contacts (first_name/last_name/email_address), so a complete people-extract is that record UNION these rows. Xero assigns contact persons no identifier, so rows are keyed by array position, which survives only until someone edits the list. The analytical payload is include_in_emails: it decides who is CC'd on emailed invoices and statements.
gotchas: No vendor id: rows are keyed by array position, and any edit to the person list reshuffles ordinals. A changed ordinal is the same human — do not diff this table across syncs to detect 'new people'.
The primary person is absent by design — they live on the parent contact record. Extracts that read only this table systematically miss the most important person on every account.
Xero only allows a small number of additional people per contact, so an apparently sparse table is normal, not a sync failure.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: Owning contact. Half of the key, because Xero gives contact persons no id of their own.

columns.name: person_ordinal
columns.description: Zero-based position in the ContactPersons array — stable only until the list is edited, when Xero silently reshuffles it. Treat (contact_id, person_ordinal) as a current-state key; never build slowly-changing person history on it.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Given name of this additional person — NOT the primary contact person, who lives on xero_contacts.first_name.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Family name of this additional person; frequently blank because users enter display names into first_name alone.

columns.name: email_address
columns.description: This person's email — a first-class identity hint for cross-system entity resolution, and the address Xero actually mails when include_in_emails is true.

columns.name: include_in_emails
columns.description: Whether Xero CCs this person on emailed documents (invoices, statements). 'Who receives our invoices' = the contact's primary email UNION rows here where this is true — filtering on it is what separates recipients from mere directory entries.

joins.note: Filter the parent's contact_status='ACTIVE' before building recipient or outreach lists.

examples.question: Everyone who receives emailed invoices for active contacts
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name AS contact, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.email_address
FROM xero_contact_persons p
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = p.contact_id
WHERE p.include_in_emails AND c.contact_status = 'ACTIVE'
ORDER BY c.name, p.person_ordinal

tables.grain: one phone entry per contact per phone type
tables.description: Typed phone slots exploded from the contact record: DEFAULT (what the Xero UI displays), DDI (direct dial), MOBILE, FAX and OFFICE. Xero returns the full slot set padded with blanks, so presence of a row is meaningless — the analytical unit is a non-empty phone_number. A dialable number is the concatenation of country code, area code and number, each optional and inconsistently filled.
gotchas: All five slots commonly arrive as empty stubs — a row is not a phone number. Filter phone_number <> '' before counting anything.

The full dialable number is split across three columns that users fill inconsistently; comparing raw phone_number values across contacts misses matches that differ only in where the area code was typed.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: Owning contact; with phone_type forms the key over Xero's fixed slot set.

columns.name: phone_type
columns.description: Which fixed slot this is: DEFAULT is the number Xero surfaces in its UI, DDI is a direct-dial line, plus MOBILE, FAX and OFFICE. Pick MOBILE for SMS-reachability questions and DEFAULT for 'the' phone number — scanning all types per contact double-counts people.

columns.name: phone_number
columns.description: The local subscriber number, without country or area code. Empty string means the slot is an unused placeholder — every count of 'contacts with a phone' must filter phone_number <> ''.

columns.name: phone_area_code
columns.description: Area/city dialing component, stored separately from the number and often omitted even when the number is present — reconstruct dialable strings defensively.

columns.name: phone_country_code
columns.description: International dialing prefix (e.g. 44, 64), free text with or without a plus sign. Its absence does NOT mean domestic — most users simply skip it, so it is a poor proxy for contact geography; prefer address country.

joins.note: Join for lifecycle filtering; outreach lists should require the parent's contact_status='ACTIVE'.

examples.question: How many active contacts have a mobile number on file?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.contact_id) AS contacts_with_mobile
FROM xero_contact_phones p
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = p.contact_id
WHERE p.phone_type = 'MOBILE'
  AND p.phone_number <> ''
  AND c.contact_status = 'ACTIVE'

tables.grain: one Xero contact record per ContactID, including ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, GDPRREQUEST and merged-away records
tables.description: The master directory behind every money table: customers, suppliers and everyone in between share this single namespace, distinguished only by the derived is_customer/is_supplier evidence flags. Rows persist through archiving and merging — the scan pages and passes includeArchived=true, so merge losers arrive as ARCHIVED shells whose merged_to_contact_id points at the survivor — which means entity-level analysis must filter contact_status and collapse merges or it overcounts. Almost everything here beyond identity and lifecycle is DEFAULT configuration (tax types, account codes, currency, payment terms, tracking) that seeds NEW documents and proves nothing about historical ones; the document tables carry their own values. Fan-out detail lives in the child tables: xero_contact_persons, xero_contact_addresses, xero_contact_phones, xero_contact_balances, xero_contact_group_members and xero_contact_cis_settings.
gotchas: Merges leave two rows for one entity: the survivor plus an ARCHIVED loser with merged_to_contact_id set. contact_status='ACTIVE' filters losers out of live counts; all-history entity analysis must instead collapse with COALESCE(merged_to_contact_id, contact_id).

is_customer/is_supplier are derived from posted AR/AP invoices, not declarations: quote-only prospects and PO-only vendors show false on both, the flags never revert, and a single contact can be both at once.
Staging retains what Xero hides: the scan uses includeArchived=true, so ARCHIVED and GDPRREQUEST rows are present and every directory metric needs an explicit contact_status filter.

Every default column (tax types, account codes, currency, terms, discount, tracking, branding) is applied at document creation and freely overridden — joining defaults onto historical documents to 'recompute' anything produces confident wrong numbers.

merged_to_contact_id only arrives on paged or by-id fetches; sales_default_line_amount_type and purchases_default_line_amount_type additionally arrive under summaryOnly. The scan plan pages, so all three are populated — but an ad-hoc unpaged, non-summary pull will null them and look like data loss.
updated_date_utc is last-modified, not created: Xero has no contact creation date, so cohort questions ('new customers in March') must be answered from first invoice dates, never from this column.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the contact and the join target of every document table — invoices, credit notes, payments, bank transactions and purchase orders all carry it. Survives renames and archiving; after a merge the losing id remains on this shell row while documents move to the survivor, so group by COALESCE(merged_to_contact_id, contact_id) when counting business entities across full history.

columns.name: merged_to_contact_id
columns.description: Non-null marks this row as the losing side of a contact merge, pointing at the surviving contact that now owns the relationship and its documents. Xero archives the loser at merge time, so these rows also carry contact_status='ARCHIVED'. Only populated on paged or by-id fetches — the scan plan pages, so it is reliable in staging. Counting contacts without collapsing through this column overstates how many customers or suppliers exist.

columns.name: contact_number
columns.description: Shown as 'Contact Code' in the Xero UI but writable only through the API — which makes it the strongest cross-system identity hint on the record, because integrations (POS, CRM, ecommerce) park their own ids here. Try matching on this before resorting to fuzzy name matching. Distinct from account_number, which users edit freely.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: A user-maintained reference editable in both the UI and API. Weaker than contact_number as an identity hint precisely because humans repurpose it — expect blanks, duplicates and recycled values; never assume uniqueness.

columns.name: contact_status
columns.description: Directory lifecycle gate. The scan passes includeArchived=true, so ARCHIVED rows — including every merge loser — persist in staging even though Xero's UI and default API responses hide them; any live-directory count must filter ACTIVE. GDPRREQUEST marks a contact under a GDPR erasure request: exclude it from outreach, enrichment or any surfaced PII immediately, and treat its identity fields as scheduled for removal rather than durable.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name of the organisation or person and the label every report surfaces. It is renamed in place with no history, and archived rows can carry names later reused by live ones — so it is neither stable over time nor safe as a match key. Key on contact_id and join to name last. For sole traders and individuals this IS a personal name — treat as PII.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Given name of the PRIMARY person on the contact record. Additional people live in xero_contact_persons — a person-level extract that reads only this column misses everyone after the first.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Family name of the primary person on the contact record; blank for organisation-only contacts. Pairs with first_name, not with name, which may hold the company instead.

columns.name: company_number
columns.description: Company registration number (Companies House / ASIC style) — a public-registry identifier, not a tax number. The best hook for firmographic enrichment and legal-entity dedupe when populated, which is rarely.

columns.name: email_address
columns.description: Primary email on the record. Invoice emailing also fans out to xero_contact_persons rows with include_in_emails=true, so 'who receives our invoices' is this column UNION that table — neither alone is complete. Xero does not accept umlauts in this field, so accented names may be spelled differently here than in other systems when matching on email.

columns.name: bank_account_details
columns.description: Free-text bank account number Xero uses to prefill payments to this contact. Sensitive financial PII that has no place in analytical output; it is also unvalidated by Xero — declared, not verified.

columns.name: tax_number
columns.description: ABN (AU), GST number (NZ), VAT number (UK) or Tax ID (US/global) — the label shifts with the org's regional edition but the column is one namespace. When tax_number_type is SSN or ITIN this is an individual's tax identifier and maximally sensitive. Formatting is free-text; normalize (strip spaces/dashes) before using it as a match key.

columns.name: tax_number_type
columns.description: Regional qualifier for tax_number; the values the spec declares (SSN, EIN, ITIN, ATIN) are all US identifiers, so expect it mostly null outside US orgs. SSN or ITIN means the adjacent tax_number identifies a person, not a company, and inherits that sensitivity.

columns.name: accounts_receivable_tax_type
columns.description: Contact-level default TaxType applied to new SALES lines for this contact at document-creation time only. Historical lines carry their own TaxType — never recompute tax by joining this backwards onto documents. Joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

columns.name: accounts_payable_tax_type
columns.description: Default TaxType for new PURCHASE (bill) lines from this contact. Same caveat as the AR twin: creation-time default, not document truth. Joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

columns.name: is_supplier
columns.description: Derived, read-only evidence flag: true once ANY accounts-payable invoice (bill) has ever been raised against the contact. It is history, not declaration — a vendor you have only sent purchase orders to stays false, and the flag never reverts. Not exclusive with is_customer; both true is common and legitimate.

columns.name: is_customer
columns.description: Derived, read-only evidence flag: true once ANY accounts-receivable invoice has ever been raised for the contact. Prospects with only quotes show false, so 'customer list' by this flag means invoiced-at-least-once, not CRM-customer. Never reverts, never set by users.

columns.name: sales_default_line_amount_type
columns.description: Default LineAmountTypes proposed on new sales documents for this contact (whether line amounts include tax). Config only — every document stores its own LineAmountTypes, which is what tax math must read. Only returned when summaryOnly or paging is used or on by-id fetches; the paged scan keeps it populated.

columns.name: purchases_default_line_amount_type
columns.description: Default LineAmountTypes for new purchase documents from this contact. Same contract as the sales twin: creation-time default, present only under summaryOnly, paged or by-id fetches, never a substitute for the document's own value.

columns.name: default_currency
columns.description: ISO 4217 code Xero PROPOSES for new documents to this contact — not a guarantee that the contact's documents are in it, since each document carries its own CurrencyCode. Use it for directory-level currency mix and as the reading frame for xero_contact_balances, whose amounts are raw and unconverted. The spec's CurrencyCode enum is very long; join ledger_config's xero_currencies for the codes this org actually subscribes to.

columns.name: xero_network_key
columns.description: Xero-to-Xero network invitation key enabling e-invoicing between two Xero orgs. Operational plumbing with no analytical meaning; retained for lossless staging and as weak evidence the counterparty also runs Xero.

columns.name: sales_default_account_code
columns.description: Default revenue account CODE — Xero account codes are org-editable text, not AccountID uuids — proposed on new sales lines for this contact. Lines store their own AccountCode, so this explains coding behaviour, never actual postings. Joins xero_accounts.code.

columns.name: purchases_default_account_code
columns.description: Default expense account CODE proposed on new purchase lines from this contact. Same contract as the sales twin: a creation-time default keyed by code, joined via xero_accounts.code, never a source of historical postings.

columns.name: sales_tracking_categories
columns.description: Default tracking category/option pairs (TrackingCategoryName + TrackingOptionName entries) proposed on new SALES lines for this contact, verbatim from the API. Real dimensional analysis lives on document line tracking joined to ledger_config's xero_tracking_categories — attributing revenue to a tracking option from this default is wrong whenever users override at entry time, which is exactly when tracking is interesting. Carries the contact-default tracking assignments verbatim: each element is a SalesTrackingCategory pair (TrackingCategoryName, TrackingOptionName) applied to new sales documents for this contact.

columns.name: purchases_tracking_categories
columns.description: Default tracking category/option pairs proposed on new PURCHASE lines from this contact, verbatim from the API. Same warning as the sales twin: a default, not what actually landed on any line. Same SalesTrackingCategory pair shape as the sales default, applied to new purchase documents.

columns.name: tracking_category_name
columns.description: Flattened convenience mirror of the category name inside the Sales/PurchasesTrackingCategories defaults — a write-side echo, redundant with the jsonb columns and silent about which side (sales or purchases) it came from. Prefer the jsonb defaults for config questions and line-level tracking for real analysis.

columns.name: tracking_category_option
columns.description: Flattened mirror of the tracking OPTION inside the contact's default tracking assignment, with the same ambiguity as tracking_category_name. Never treat it as a per-document dimension value.

columns.name: payment_terms
columns.description: Default terms Xero uses to compute DueDate on NEW documents, shaped {Bills:{Day,Type},Sales:{Day,Type}} — Bills governs what you owe this contact (purchases), Sales governs what they owe you. Type is one of DAYSAFTERBILLDATE, DAYSAFTERBILLMONTH, OFCURRENTMONTH, OFFOLLOWINGMONTH (the org-owned PaymentTerm/Bill objects) and Day is the day count or day-of-month that Type interprets. Defaults only: the binding due date is each document's own DueDate. Filter like (payment_terms #>> '{Bills,Day}')::int = 30.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Xero's last-modified stamp and the incremental watermark for the contact scan. It is NOT a creation date — Xero exposes none for contacts — so 'new customers this month' cannot come from here; derive first-seen from the earliest document date instead. Bulk imports and API integrations bump it in clusters, so distributions over this column describe sync behaviour, not business activity.

columns.name: contact_groups
columns.description: Inline membership stubs (ContactGroupID + Name entries) exactly as Xero returns them on the contact. The queryable membership edge is xero_contact_group_members, built from the per-group fan-out — join there. Keep this only to reconcile the two sides when fan-out lag is suspected; parsing it in analytical SQL is a smell.

columns.name: website
columns.description: Read-only website URL — a handy firmographic-enrichment hint and nothing more. No lifecycle or financial meaning.

columns.name: branding_theme_branding_theme_id
columns.description: The invoice branding theme this contact defaults to, lifted one hop from the nested BrandingTheme stub. Join xero_branding_themes for the theme's name; when a document carries its own BrandingThemeID, the document wins — this is only the default.

columns.name: batch_payments
columns.description: Bank prefill block (account number and name, plus NZ-only particulars/code/reference) Xero injects when this contact is included in a batch payment. Contains bank account PII — treat exactly like bank_account_details and keep out of query results. Executed batches themselves live in payments_credits' xero_batch_payments; this is just per-contact configuration. Carries the full BatchPaymentDetails payload (bank account number/name, NZ code and reference, batch details) — supplier banking defaults used when this contact joins a batch payment; bank identifiers make this column PII.

columns.name: balances
columns.description: Verbatim raw AR/AP outstanding-and-overdue snapshot block exactly as Xero returned it on this sync — the audit copy behind xero_contact_balances, which is the queryable, typed form and the one analytical SQL should read. Kept verbatim because the snapshot is overwritten in place every scan: when the typed table looks wrong, this payload is the only record of precisely what Xero reported. Amounts inside are raw document-currency sums, never converted to base.

columns.name: discount
columns.description: Default percentage discount pre-filled on new sales lines for this contact (read-only here). It is a RATE: never sum it, never multiply it against historical revenue — realized discounts live on invoice lines, where users freely override this default.

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Inline attachment stubs as Xero happens to return them — not reliably populated on list scans and never a complete inventory. The governed attachment catalog is org_meta's xero_attachments fan-out; use has_attachments to decide which contacts merit that rate-limited call. Counting files from this column undercounts.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: Cheap scan-time signal that at least one file hangs off the contact — the prioritization key for the rate-limited attachments fan-out. True here with no rows yet in xero_attachments means the fan-out simply has not run, not that data is missing.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-path artifact: Xero populates this on responses to failed or partial POSTs, so on read scans it is effectively always empty. Non-empty values in staging mean a write response was replayed into the pipeline — investigate the ingest, do not analyze the content.

columns.name: has_validation_errors
columns.description: Companion flag to validation_errors with the same write-path-only lifecycle. Expect false/null everywhere on read scans; it carries no directory meaning.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Response-status marker from write calls (the OK/ERROR family). Not a contact lifecycle field — that is contact_status — and never meaningful on read scans; staged for losslessness only.

columns.name: addresses
columns.description: Store certain address types for a contact – see address types Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: phones
columns.description: Store certain phone types for a contact – see phone types Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: contact_persons
columns.description: See contact persons Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: branding_theme
columns.description: Contact.BrandingTheme as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: Self-join from merge loser to survivor — the survivor side MUST be aliased (JOIN xero_contacts AS survivor). COALESCE(merged_to_contact_id, contact_id) collapses the pair to one entity.
The revenue-and-spend path. Remember invoices are BOTH sales (Type=ACCREC) and bills (Type=ACCPAY) and include VOIDED/DELETED rows — filter both on every aggregate.
AR default tax code; accounts_payable_tax_type joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type the same way.
Joined on the org-editable account CODE, not account_id; purchases_default_account_code joins identically.
Resolves the proposed document currency; absence means the org base currency applies.
Default invoice branding for this contact; null means the org default theme.

examples.question: How many active customers do we have right now?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_customers
FROM xero_contacts
WHERE contact_status = 'ACTIVE' AND is_customer

examples.question: Which active suppliers default to 30-day bill payment terms?
examples.sql:
SELECT name
FROM xero_contacts
WHERE contact_status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND is_supplier
  AND (payment_terms #>> '{Bills,Day}')::int = 30
  AND payment_terms #>> '{Bills,Type}' = 'DAYSAFTERBILLDATE'
ORDER BY name

examples.question: How many distinct customer entities have we ever invoiced, collapsing merged duplicates?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(merged_to_contact_id, contact_id)) AS customer_entities
FROM xero_contacts
WHERE is_customer

tables.grain: one allocation of one credit note against one invoice, per credit note and array position
tables.description: Application evidence exploded from CreditNote.Allocations: each row spreads part of a credit note's value onto one invoice, reducing that invoice's amount_due without any cash moving. This is the event_link between credit and invoice — revenue impact stays on credit note lines, cash refunds stay in xero_payments. Amounts are in the credit note's currency.
gotchas: No cash moves here: an allocation offsets an invoice against a credit. Cash refunds of credit notes are payment rows in xero_payments — counting allocations as refunds overstates money out.
allocation_position is not stable across syncs (the array renumbers when an allocation is deleted); treat the parent's allocation set as replace-on-rescan, never diff by position.
Amounts are in the credit note's currency, which always matches the target invoice's currency in Xero — but still convert via the parent's currency_rate for base-currency views.
Filter the PARENT's status: allocations under VOIDED/DELETED credit notes describe offsets that no longer stand.

columns.name: credit_note_id
columns.description: Parent credit note being spent; join xero_credit_notes for type, status and currency — an allocation from a VOIDED credit note is history, not a live offset.

columns.name: allocations
columns.description: Zero-based position within the parent's Allocations array (provenance: the array itself — the ordinal is its index). The spec exposes no allocation identifier, so parent id + position forms the row key; positions renumber when allocations are removed, and the ingester replaces the set per parent rescan.

columns.name: allocations_invoice_invoice_id
columns.description: The invoice this slice of credit was applied to; join xero_invoices. The invoice's amount_due already reflects the allocation — subtracting it again double-nets.

columns.name: allocations_amount
columns.description: Amount of credit applied to that invoice, positive, in the CREDIT NOTE's currency. SUM(amount) per credit note reconciles to the parent's applied_amount; per invoice it explains part of amount_credited.

columns.name: allocations_date
columns.description: The date the allocation takes effect — this, not the credit note's issue date, is when the target invoice's balance dropped. Aging and as-of AR reconstructions must use it.

joins.note: Parent credit note; filter its type and status before trusting the allocation.
The invoice whose balance the allocation reduced.

examples.question: How much of each open invoice was settled by credit rather than cash?
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, i.total, SUM(a.allocations_amount) AS settled_by_credit
FROM xero_credit_note_allocations a
JOIN xero_credit_notes cn ON cn.credit_note_id = a.credit_note_id
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.allocations_invoice_invoice_id = a.allocations_invoice_invoice_id
WHERE cn.type = 'ACCRECCREDIT' AND cn.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
  AND i.type = 'ACCREC'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY settled_by_credit DESC

examples.question: Credit applied to customer invoices per month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', a.allocations_date) AS month,
       SUM(a.allocations_amount * COALESCE(cn.currency_rate, 1)) AS credit_applied_base
FROM xero_credit_note_allocations a
JOIN xero_credit_notes cn ON cn.credit_note_id = a.credit_note_id
WHERE cn.type = 'ACCRECCREDIT' AND cn.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one line item on one credit note per LineItemID
tables.description: The contra side of xero_invoice_line_items: what was credited back, per product and GL account. Rows are stored positive but reduce revenue (ACCRECCREDIT parent) or spend (ACCPAYCREDIT parent) — netting against invoice lines requires negation. Direction, status, currency and LineAmountTypes all come from the parent xero_credit_notes row.
gotchas: Amounts are positive but mean MINUS: net product revenue = invoice lines minus these lines (parent type ACCRECCREDIT). Adding them overstates revenue twice over.
Join the parent for status: lines under VOIDED/DELETED credit notes are dead and must be excluded exactly like voided invoices.
line_amount includes tax when the parent is Inclusive — normalize with tax_amount the same way as invoice lines before netting.

columns.name: line_items_line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the credited line and the row key. Like invoice lines, edits that resubmit the line set without LineItemIDs recreate the lines under new ids — line identity is not durable across every edit.

columns.name: credit_note_id
columns.description: Parent credit note key. Join xero_credit_notes for type (ACCRECCREDIT vs ACCPAYCREDIT), status, currency and line_amount_types — without it this row cannot be signed or filtered correctly.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Zero-based position within the parent's LineItems array (provenance: the array itself). Presentation order only; renumbered on edit.

columns.name: line_items_description
columns.description: Free-text description of what is being credited; description-only lines (null amounts) are legal and carry narrative, not value.

columns.name: line_items_quantity
columns.description: Units credited (positive). For units-returned analysis, negate when netting against invoiced quantity.

columns.name: line_items_unit_amount
columns.description: Per-unit price being credited, document currency. A rate — never summed; credited value is line_amount.

columns.name: line_items_line_amount
columns.description: Credited value of the line, stored positive, in document currency. Includes tax only when the PARENT's line_amount_types is Inclusive. Net revenue by product = invoiced line_amount minus credited line_amount, both tax-normalized the same way.

columns.name: line_items_tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate key being reversed on the line; join xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

columns.name: line_items_tax_amount
columns.description: Tax reversed on this line, document currency. Auto-calculated but overridable — trust the stored value over any recomputation.

columns.name: line_items_account_code
columns.description: GL account code the credit posts against — usually the same revenue/expense account the original invoice line hit; join xero_accounts.code.

columns.name: line_items_account_id
columns.description: Immutable GL account id for the credited line; the durable join to xero_accounts.

columns.name: line_items_item_code
columns.description: Catalogue item code being credited; null on free-typed credit lines. Return-rate analysis joining only on item_code misses free-typed credits.

columns.name: line_items_item_item_id
columns.description: Resolved catalogue item id from the embedded Item echo; the durable join to xero_items.

columns.name: line_items_item
columns.description: Verbatim item stub ({Code, Name, ItemID}) as credited at sync time; prefer scalar item_id/item_code for joins.

columns.name: line_items_tracking
columns.description: Up to 2 tracking assignments ({TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}) — credits carry tracking too, and department/region views that ignore credit-note tracking overstate every tracked segment. Expand with jsonb_array_elements; join xero_tracking_options.

columns.name: line_items_discount_rate
columns.description: Carried for shape-compatibility with the shared LineItem schema, but Xero does not support discounts on credit notes — expect null.

columns.name: line_items_discount_amount
columns.description: Carried for shape-compatibility; discounts are unsupported on credit notes — expect null.

columns.name: line_items_repeating_invoice_id
columns.description: Repeating-template lineage carried on the shared line schema; effectively always null on credit notes.

columns.name: line_items_taxability
columns.description: US automated sales tax classification of the credited line; null outside US orgs.

columns.name: line_items_sales_tax_code_id
columns.description: Internal id of the US sales tax code on the line; US orgs only.

columns.name: line_items_tax_breakdown
columns.description: Per-jurisdiction US sales tax components reversed by this line, kept verbatim; tax_amount already totals them.

joins.note: Mandatory: sign direction (type), status, currency and LineAmountTypes live on the parent.
Fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code when account_id is null on older payloads.
Null on free-typed credit lines — use LEFT JOIN.

examples.question: Net revenue by product (invoiced minus credited) this year
examples.sql:
WITH invoiced AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(li.line_items_item_code, '(no item)') AS line_items_item_code,
         SUM((li.line_items_line_amount - CASE WHEN i.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(li.line_items_tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) * COALESCE(i.currency_rate, 1)) AS invoiced
  FROM xero_invoice_line_items li
  JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_id = li.invoice_id
  WHERE i.type = 'ACCREC' AND i.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
    AND i.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  GROUP BY 1
), credited AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(cli.line_items_item_code, '(no item)') AS line_items_item_code,
         SUM((cli.line_items_line_amount - CASE WHEN cn.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(cli.line_items_tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) * COALESCE(cn.currency_rate, 1)) AS credited
  FROM xero_credit_note_line_items cli
  JOIN xero_credit_notes cn ON cn.credit_note_id = cli.credit_note_id
  WHERE cn.type = 'ACCRECCREDIT' AND cn.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
    AND cn.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT line_items_item_code,
       COALESCE(inv.invoiced, 0) AS invoiced,
       COALESCE(cr.credited, 0) AS credited,
       COALESCE(inv.invoiced, 0) - COALESCE(cr.credited, 0) AS net_revenue
FROM invoiced inv
FULL OUTER JOIN credited cr USING (line_items_item_code)
ORDER BY net_revenue DESC

examples.question: Which GL accounts absorb the most customer credits?
examples.sql:
SELECT a.code, a.name,
       SUM((cli.line_items_line_amount - CASE WHEN cn.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(cli.line_items_tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) * COALESCE(cn.currency_rate, 1)) AS credited_base
FROM xero_credit_note_line_items cli
JOIN xero_credit_notes cn ON cn.credit_note_id = cli.credit_note_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.line_items_account_id = cli.line_items_account_id
WHERE cn.type = 'ACCRECCREDIT' AND cn.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY credited_base DESC

tables.grain: one credit note document (customer credit ACCRECCREDIT or supplier credit ACCPAYCREDIT) per CreditNoteID
tables.description: Negative-document header mirroring xero_invoices: ACCRECCREDIT reduces what a customer owes (contra revenue), ACCPAYCREDIT reduces what the org owes a supplier (contra spend). Net revenue = ACCREC invoices minus ACCRECCREDIT credit notes — adding credit note totals to invoice totals inflates instead of nets. Credit is consumed two ways: allocation against invoices (xero_credit_note_allocations) or cash refund (rows in xero_payments); remaining_credit is what is still unconsumed right now.
gotchas: Credit notes are stored as positive amounts but SUBTRACT from the business: net revenue = invoice revenue minus ACCRECCREDIT credit totals. Adding them inflates revenue by exactly the credited amount.
Type mixes directions: ACCPAYCREDIT rows are supplier credits (reduce spend), not customer refunds. Filter type on every question.
VOIDED/DELETED credit notes are still returned and still land here — status filter required, exactly as with invoices.

Allocation is not refund: allocations (xero_credit_note_allocations) offset invoices with no cash movement; refunds appear as payment rows. 'Money refunded to customers' comes from xero_payments, not from this table's totals.

columns.name: credit_note_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the credit note and the row key.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Direction of the credit: ACCRECCREDIT credits a customer (reduces revenue/AR), ACCPAYCREDIT is a supplier crediting the org (reduces spend/AP). Same trap as invoices — any 'credits issued' number without a type filter mixes both directions.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Same lifecycle as invoices: DRAFT/SUBMITTED unapproved, AUTHORISED live, PAID fully consumed, VOIDED/DELETED dead but still returned by the API. Real credit exposure = status IN ('AUTHORISED','PAID'); unapplied exposure adds remaining_credit > 0.
columns.enums: DRAFT; SUBMITTED; DELETED; AUTHORISED; PAID; VOIDED

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The customer being credited (ACCRECCREDIT) or the supplier crediting the org (ACCPAYCREDIT); join xero_contacts.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized contact name at sync time; contacts merge and rename, so the governed name is xero_contacts via contact_id.

columns.name: credit_note_number
columns.description: Human-facing number, auto-generated from org settings for ACCRECCREDIT; supplier credit numbers are keyed by hand. Display only — not unique, not a join key.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Additional free-text reference, ACCRECCREDIT only; null on supplier credits.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Issue date of the credit — the accrual date that reduces revenue/spend in the period. Defaults to the org-timezone current date when omitted at creation.

columns.name: due_date
columns.description: Due date carried on the document; largely ceremonial for credits — credit notes settle by allocation or refund, not by falling due.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Whether the credit note's line amounts include tax (Exclusive/Inclusive/NoTax). Header sub_total/total_tax/total are normalized; line-level sums must respect this flag exactly as on invoices.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency of all monetary fields on this credit note (spec CurrencyCode enum; extraction truncates the full list — treat no subset as exhaustive). Never sum across currencies without converting.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Rate to the org's base currency fixed for this document (XE.com day rate unless overridden); multiply monetary fields by it for base-currency reporting.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Tax-exclusive credit value in document currency. Stored positive — it REDUCES revenue/spend, so netting requires subtraction (or negate when unioning with invoice lines).

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Total tax being reversed by the credit, in document currency.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive credit value (sub_total + total_tax), stored positive in document currency. The full face value — not what has been used; see applied_amount and remaining_credit.

columns.name: remaining_credit
columns.description: Unconsumed credit balance right now (face value minus allocations and refunds). Current-state, not historical. Outstanding customer credit liability = SUM(remaining_credit) WHERE type='ACCRECCREDIT' AND status='AUTHORISED'.

columns.name: applied_amount
columns.description: Amount of this credit already applied against invoices. The per-invoice detail — which invoice, when, how much — is xero_credit_note_allocations; analyze application behaviour there.

columns.name: fully_paid_on_date
columns.description: Date the credit was fully consumed (allocated and/or refunded); null while any remaining_credit exists.

columns.name: cis_deduction
columns.description: UK Construction Industry Scheme deduction reversed by this credit; null outside CIS-enabled UK orgs.

columns.name: cis_rate
columns.description: CIS deduction percentage for the org — a rate, never summed.

columns.name: sent_to_contact
columns.description: Marked-as-sent flag inside Xero; settable only on approved credit notes. Does not prove delivery.

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Template/branding used for the document; join xero_branding_themes.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when files are attached; the files are catalogued in xero_attachments (org_meta).

columns.name: has_errors
columns.description: True when the payload carried validation errors — sync/data-quality signal, not a business state.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Batch-response status indicator accompanying validation messages; ignore for analytics.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp and the incremental-sync watermark; not a business date.

columns.name: updated_date_utc_string
columns.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc; prefer the parsed timestamp column.

columns.name: payments
columns.description: Read-only echo of CASH REFUNDS paid out against this credit note. Authoritative refund rows live in xero_payments with their refund PaymentTypes — a refund is money out the door, distinct from an allocation which merely offsets an invoice.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation error messages carried verbatim ({Message} objects); data-quality triage only.

columns.name: warnings
columns.description: Non-fatal API warning messages ({Message} objects).

columns.name: invoice_addresses
columns.description: FROM/TO addresses used by US automated sales tax to source the credit; tax metadata, not the contact's master addresses.

columns.name: contact
columns.description: CreditNote.Contact as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: See Invoice Line Items Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: allocations
columns.description: See Allocations Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: Customer on ACCRECCREDIT, supplier on ACCPAYCREDIT.
Null when the default theme applies.

examples.question: Customer credits issued by month, netted sign, base currency
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month,
       -SUM(sub_total * COALESCE(currency_rate, 1)) AS revenue_reduction_base
FROM xero_credit_notes
WHERE type = 'ACCRECCREDIT' AND status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Outstanding unapplied customer credit by customer
examples.sql:
SELECT contact_name, currency_code, SUM(remaining_credit) AS unapplied_credit
FROM xero_credit_notes
WHERE type = 'ACCRECCREDIT' AND status = 'AUTHORISED' AND remaining_credit > 0
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY unapplied_credit DESC

tables.grain: one currency per ISO code enabled in the org's subscription
tables.description: Tiny reference list of the currencies the org has ever enabled — the decode table for every CurrencyCode column in the connector. Presence means 'added to the subscription at some point', not 'currently transacting'; currencies cannot be removed once used, so the list only grows. No watermark and no paging: fully re-scanned each sync.
gotchas: This list is 'ever enabled', not 'in use' — deriving multi-currency exposure from it overstates; measure exposure from document tables' CurrencyCode instead.
Base-currency identification does NOT live here: the org's base currency comes from org_meta's xero_organisations; journal lines are already converted to it.

columns.name: code
columns.description: ISO 4217 code and the row key — the value document CurrencyCode columns join on. The spec enum is the full ISO set; the extracted list is truncated at HRK, so treat later codes as valid.
columns.enums: AED; AFN; ALL; AMD; ANG; AOA; ARS; AUD; AWG; AZN; BAM; BBD; BDT; BGN; BHD; BIF; BMD; BND; BOB; BRL; BSD; BTN; BWP; BYN; BYR; BZD; CAD; CDF; CHF; CLF; CLP; CNY; COP; CRC; CUC; CUP; CVE; CZK; DJF; DKK; DOP; DZD; EEK; EGP; ERN; ETB; EUR; FJD; FKP; GBP; GEL; GHS; GIP; GMD; GNF; GTQ; GYD; HKD; HNL; HRK

columns.name: description
columns.description: Display name of the currency ('United States Dollar') — presentation only.

joins.note: Foreign-currency bank accounts in the chart.

examples.question: Which enabled currencies have foreign-currency bank accounts?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.code, c.description, COUNT(a.account_id) AS bank_accounts
FROM xero_currencies c
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.currency_code = c.code AND a.type = 'BANK'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY bank_accounts DESC, c.code

tables.grain: one reimbursement payment applied to one expense claim
tables.description: Reimbursement cash events, exploded from the Payments array embedded in each expense claim. This is their only home in the design: a Payment served by GET /Payments allocates to exactly one invoice, credit note, prepayment or overpayment, and an expense claim is none of those — so these rows reach staging through the claim scan alone, and a 'total cash paid out' built from xero_payments by itself omits employee reimbursements. Amounts are in org base currency (classic claims carry no currency or rate fields). Status DELETED un-pays the claim yet remains in the payload — filter AUTHORISED on every sum.
gotchas: GET /Payments serves only allocations to invoices, credit notes, prepayments and overpayments, so these reimbursements are absent from xero_payments and cash-out analysis built there alone understates payments made. UNION these rows in — and when you do, do not also count the receipts behind the claim, or the same money is counted as both spend and cash.
DELETED payments remain in the payload and un-pay their claim; filter status = 'AUTHORISED' on every aggregate.
Amounts are always org base currency — no conversion needed, and no currency column to group by.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.description: Xero's payment identifier and the row key, globally unique across the org and stable across syncs (unlike line ids, the embedded payment array is never rewritten wholesale). Do not expect the id to resolve in xero_payments — that endpoint serves only payments allocated to invoices, credit notes, prepayments and overpayments.

columns.name: expense_claim_id
columns.description: The claim this reimbursement pays down; joins xero_expense_claims for the employee and due date.

columns.name: payment_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of the payment in ExpenseClaim.Payments
columns.description: Zero-based position within the claim's embedded Payments array; preserves application order when several part-payments settle one claim.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date the reimbursement was paid — the settlement date for cycle-time and monthly cash-out analysis.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Reimbursement amount in org base currency. Part-payments are legal: SUM per claim to compare against the claim's total.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text payment reference (bank memo, batch note); display and matching aid only.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED is a live reimbursement; DELETED is a reversed one that Xero keeps returning — it un-pays the claim (amount_due goes back up) so every cash sum must filter AUTHORISED.

columns.name: payment_type
columns.description: The shared Payment type vocabulary. For rows in this table the type is incidental — membership here already scopes them to expense-claim reimbursements; do not filter this column to find them.
columns.enums: ACCRECPAYMENT; ACCPAYPAYMENT; ARCREDITPAYMENT; APCREDITPAYMENT; AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT; ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT; APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT; APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Modification stamp of the embedded payment record; rows still arrive via the parent claim scan, so this is diagnostic rather than a scan watermark.

joins.note: Claim header for employee (user_id), due date and lifecycle status.

examples.question: Employee reimbursements paid by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS reimbursed
FROM xero_expense_claim_payments
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Which claims were reimbursed late?
examples.sql:
SELECT ec.expense_claim_id, ec.payment_due_date, p.date AS paid_date, p.date - ec.payment_due_date AS days_late
FROM xero_expense_claim_payments p
JOIN xero_expense_claims ec ON ec.expense_claim_id = p.expense_claim_id
WHERE p.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND ec.payment_due_date IS NOT NULL
  AND p.date > ec.payment_due_date
ORDER BY days_late DESC

tables.grain: one attachment of one receipt to one expense claim
tables.description: The authoritative claim-to-receipt mapping, exploded from the Receipts array embedded in each expense claim. Receipt bodies land in xero_receipts from their own endpoint; this table is the wiring that says which receipts were submitted on which claim. A receipt belongs to at most one claim, and DRAFT (not-yet-claimed) receipts have no row here — their absence is workflow state, not data loss.
gotchas: DRAFT receipts are absent by design — a receipt only appears here once submitted on a claim, so this table undercounts captured-but-unclaimed spend. Find those in xero_receipts WHERE status = 'DRAFT'.
Reconciliation: SUM of linked receipts' totals should equal the claim's total; a mismatch usually means a receipt was declined or voided after submission — investigate before trusting either number.

columns.name: expense_claim_id
columns.description: The claim this receipt was submitted on; joins xero_expense_claims for status and reimbursement amounts.

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.description: The receipt submitted on this claim; joins xero_receipts for merchant, employee and totals, and onward to xero_receipt_line_items for GL detail.

columns.name: receipt_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of the receipt in ExpenseClaim.Receipts
columns.description: Zero-based position of the receipt within the claim's embedded array; preserves submission order for display and diffing.

joins.note: Claim header — filter its status here, not on the receipt, when asking about reimbursement state.
Receipt body; effectively one_to_one per receipt since a receipt sits on at most one claim.

examples.question: Receipt count and value per expense claim
examples.sql:
SELECT ecr.expense_claim_id, COUNT(*) AS receipts, SUM(r.total) AS receipt_value
FROM xero_expense_claim_receipts ecr
JOIN xero_receipts r ON r.receipt_id = ecr.receipt_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY receipt_value DESC

tables.grain: one expense claim submitted by one org user for reimbursement
tables.description: The reimbursement wrapper of Xero's classic expense-claims workflow: who is owed money, how much is outstanding, and which accounting period it reports under. The claim itself carries no expense categories — GL and merchant detail live on the receipts (xero_receipts / xero_receipt_line_items) linked via xero_expense_claim_receipts. Amounts are always in the org's base currency (classic claims have no currency fields). VOIDED and DELETED claims are still returned by the API and must be excluded from every liability number.
gotchas: The claim carries no expense categories: GL-account and merchant analysis comes from receipt lines, not from here. The claim only answers who is owed, how much, and for which period.
VOIDED and DELETED claims are still returned by the API — every liability or spend number must exclude them.

This is Xero's LEGACY (classic) expense-claims API. Tenants on the newer Xero Expenses product return an empty ExpenseClaims collection — an empty table means 'uses the new product', not 'employees spend nothing'.
Amounts are org-base-currency only; there is no currency or rate on claims, so sums are safe org-wide without conversion.

columns.name: expense_claim_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the claim and the row key; the join key for its receipts and reimbursement payments.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Reimbursement lifecycle: SUBMITTED awaits approval, AUTHORISED is an approved liability, PAID is settled, VOIDED/DELETED are dead yet still returned by the API. 'What do we owe employees' is status = 'AUTHORISED' — there is no DRAFT at claim level; drafts exist as unclaimed receipts.

columns.name: user_user_id
columns.description: The org user (employee) who submitted the claim and is owed the reimbursement; joins xero_users. The person axis of employee-spend analysis.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Claim value being reimbursed, in org base currency. Reconciles to the sum of its receipts' totals via xero_expense_claim_receipts — differences flag voided or declined receipts.

columns.name: amount_due
columns.description: Outstanding reimbursement liability as at the last sync, not as at any date you choose. Xero overwrites it in place with no history, so 'what did we owe employees at 30 June' cannot be answered from this column — rebuild that from claim totals minus xero_expense_claim_payments dated on or before the cut-off. Live liability also requires excluding VOIDED/DELETED claims, whose amounts linger in the payload.

columns.name: amount_paid
columns.description: Cumulative amount already reimbursed, so that amount_paid + amount_due reconciles to total. Note the spec's own doc string for this field reads 'the amount still to pay' — the identical sentence it gives AmountDue — which is a copy-paste defect in the published OpenAPI, not two fields meaning the same thing; the field name and the arithmetic are the reliable guide. Like amount_due it is overwritten each sync and carries no history.

columns.name: payment_due_date
columns.description: Date the reimbursement is due to the employee. Overdue liability = AUTHORISED claims with amount_due > 0 past this date.

columns.name: reporting_date
columns.description: Accounting date the claim reports under in Xero — the period axis for expense reporting, distinct from when receipts were spent and from when reimbursement happens.

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.description: Write-side convenience identifier of a single associated receipt echoed by the API. Unreliable on reads — the authoritative claim-to-receipt mapping is xero_expense_claim_receipts; never aggregate through this column.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Server-side modification stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (If-Modified-Since); audit metadata, not a business date.

columns.name: receipts
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_expense_claim_receipts (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: payments
columns.description: See Payments Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_expense_claim_payments (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: The claiming employee — first_name/last_name live there; user rows are org logins, not a payroll employee record.
Fan out to receipts for merchant and GL-level detail.
Reimbursement cash events — the only place they exist in the whole API.

examples.question: Outstanding reimbursements by employee
examples.sql:
SELECT u.first_name || ' ' || u.last_name AS employee, SUM(ec.amount_due) AS owed
FROM xero_expense_claims ec
JOIN xero_users u ON u.user_user_id = ec.user_user_id
WHERE ec.status = 'AUTHORISED' AND ec.amount_due > 0
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY owed DESC

examples.question: How long do reimbursements take from reporting to payment?
examples.sql:
SELECT ec.expense_claim_id, MAX(p.date) - ec.reporting_date AS days_to_reimburse
FROM xero_expense_claims ec
JOIN xero_expense_claim_payments p
  ON p.expense_claim_id = ec.expense_claim_id AND p.status = 'AUTHORISED'
WHERE ec.status = 'PAID'
GROUP BY ec.expense_claim_id, ec.reporting_date
ORDER BY days_to_reimburse DESC

tables.grain: one row per attachment of one file to one Xero business record — a file attached to N records yields N rows
tables.description: The bridge that turns the file library into audit evidence: each row attaches one file to one business record, addressed by the polymorphic (object_group, object_id) pair. This is how 'which invoices have no supporting document' and 'what paperwork backs this bank transaction' resolve — filter object_group first, then join object_id to that group's table.
