Rows are gathered by per-file fan-out (one API call per file in xero_files), so the table is availability-optional and can trail the library under the Files API rate budget. Five denormalized fields (file_name, file_size_bytes, file_created_date_utc, association_date_utc, send_with_object) are only returned by the per-object endpoint GET /Associations/{ObjectId} and are NULL under the bulk scan — name/size/created resolve via the xero_files join instead.
gotchas: Five fields (file_name, file_size_bytes, file_created_date_utc, association_date_utc, send_with_object) are only returned by GET /Associations/{ObjectId}; the bulk per-file scan leaves them NULL. Name/size/created resolve via the xero_files join; attachment timing and send-with-document genuinely require a targeted per-object refresh.

object_id is polymorphic: a bare join to xero_invoices silently drops every non-invoice attachment. Filter object_group before every join, and read object_type only alongside object_group — its vocabulary reuses spellings (Prepayment, Receipt, Contact, Account) with family-specific meanings.

An invoice with zero rows here is not necessarily undocumented: direct per-document uploads live in xero_attachments (org_meta), a separate attachment system. Paperwork-completeness audits must consult both before naming offenders.

Populating this table costs one Files API call per file against a hard rate budget (60 calls/min and a daily cap per org), so it can lag xero_files by whole sync windows on large libraries — it is availability 'optional'; degrade explicitly when it is behind rather than reporting zero attachments.

Detaching a file (or deleting the file) removes the association with no tombstone or timestamp; only a full per-file rescan reveals removals, so between syncs this table can claim evidence that has already been detached.

columns.name: file_id
columns.description: UUID of the attached file and one half of the row key. Join to xero_files for name, content type, size and uploader — always populated there, unlike this table's per-object-endpoint denormalized copies.

columns.name: object_id
columns.description: UUID of the business record the file evidences (an InvoiceID, BankTransactionID, ContactID, ... depending on object_group) and the other half of the row key. It is polymorphic: joining it to any table without first filtering object_group silently discards every other group's rows and understates attachment coverage.

columns.name: object_group
columns.description: Coarse family of the attached-to record and the join router: Invoice rows join xero_invoices, BankTransaction rows join xero_bank_transactions, and so on across twelve families. Always constrain it before joining or before counting 'attachments per document' — the table mixes all families at one grain.
columns.enums: Account; BankTransaction; Contact; CreditNote; Invoice; Item; ManualJournal; Overpayment; Payment; Prepayment; Quote; Receipt

columns.name: object_type
columns.description: Finer classification of the target. For Invoice-group rows it distinguishes AccRec (sales invoice) from Accpay (bill) — Xero's ACCREC/ACCPAY split that governs every revenue-vs-spend question, available here without a join. The vocabulary is shared across families: Account-group rows carry account classes (Bank, Equity, Currliab, ...), and spellings like Prepayment, Receipt or Contact recur with family-specific meanings — never interpret it without object_group beside it.
columns.enums: Unknown; Accpay; AccPayCredit; AccPayPayment; AccRec; AccRecCredit; AccRecPayment; Adjustment; ApCreditPayment; ApOverPayment; ApOverPaymentPayment; ApOverPaymentSourcePayment; ApPrepayment; ApPrepaymentPayment; ApPrepaymentSourcePayment; ArCreditPayment; ArOverPayment; ArOverpaymentPayment; ArOverpaymentSourcePayment; ArPrepayment; ArPrepaymentPayment; ArPrepaymentSourcePayment; CashPaid; CashRec; ExpPayment; ManJournal; PurchaseOrder; Receipt; Transfer; Account; Contact; Business; Employee; Person; User; Org; FixedAsset; PayRun; PriceListItem; Bank; Current; Equity; Expense; Fixed; Liability; Prepayment; Revenue; Sales; Overheads; Depreciatn; OtherIncome; DirectCosts; Currliab; Termliab; NonCurrent; SalesQuote

columns.name: send_with_object
columns.description: Whether the file rides along on client-facing sends of its document (e.g. goes out with the emailed invoice). Only GET /Associations/{ObjectId} returns it, so under the bulk per-file scan it is NULL — meaning unknown, not 'no'. Any count of client-visible attachments must exclude NULLs explicitly or it fabricates an answer.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Denormalized copy of the attached file's name that only the per-object endpoint supplies — NULL under the bulk scan. Prefer xero_files.name via file_id: populated for every row and current after renames.

columns.name: size
columns.description: Denormalized byte size of the attached file, per-object-endpoint-only (NULL under the bulk scan). Never a storage measure even when populated: a file attached to three records appears three times — storage questions belong on xero_files.size_bytes.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When the underlying FILE was created (its upload moment), not when it was attached — attachment timing is association_date_utc, and confusing the two misstates evidence timelines. Per-object-endpoint-only (NULL under the bulk scan); xero_files.created_date_utc is the always-populated equivalent.

columns.name: association_date_utc
columns.description: The attachment moment (UTC) — the only field anywhere that says when evidence was linked to its record ('was the receipt attached before month-end close?'). Only the per-object endpoint returns it, so bulk-scanned rows hold NULL and timing analyses require a targeted per-object refresh first.

joins.note: Always valid — the only join on this table that needs no object_group filter; source of the file's name, mime type, size and uploader.
Only rows with object_group = 'Invoice' — that group covers both sales invoices and bills; split with object_type ('AccRec' vs 'Accpay').
Only rows with object_group = 'CreditNote'; object_type separates AccRecCredit from AccPayCredit.
Only rows with object_group = 'Quote'.
Only rows with object_group = 'BankTransaction' (object_type CashPaid/CashRec/Transfer and friends).
Only rows with object_group = 'Contact' — e.g. contracts or KYC documents held against a customer or supplier.
Only rows with object_group = 'Item'.
Only rows with object_group = 'ManualJournal' — supporting workings for adjustments.
Only rows with object_group = 'Overpayment'.
Only rows with object_group = 'Payment' — remittance advice and similar.
Only rows with object_group = 'Prepayment'.
Only rows with object_group = 'Receipt' (expense-claim receipts).
Only rows with object_group = 'Account'; here object_type holds the account's class (Bank, Equity, Currliab, ...), not a document type.

examples.question: Which authorised bills of $1,000 or more have no file from the library attached?
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, c.name AS supplier, i.total, i.due_date
FROM xero_invoices i
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = i.contact_id
LEFT JOIN xero_file_associations a
  ON a.object_id = i.invoice_id AND a.object_group = 'Invoice'
WHERE i.type = 'ACCPAY' AND i.status = 'AUTHORISED' AND i.total >= 1000
  AND a.file_id IS NULL
ORDER BY i.total DESC

examples.question: Where do attached files actually get used across Xero?
examples.sql:
SELECT a.object_group, COUNT(*) AS associations, COUNT(DISTINCT a.file_id) AS distinct_files
FROM xero_file_associations a
GROUP BY a.object_group
ORDER BY associations DESC

examples.question: Which sales invoices carry the most supporting documents?
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, COUNT(*) AS attached_files
FROM xero_file_associations a
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_id = a.object_id
WHERE a.object_group = 'Invoice' AND a.object_type = 'AccRec'
GROUP BY i.invoice_id, i.invoice_number
ORDER BY attached_files DESC
LIMIT 20

tables.grain: one row per file stored in the tenant's Xero Files library, Inbox included
tables.description: The tenant's document library: every file uploaded to or emailed into Xero Files, with content metadata and the uploader's identity flattened from the nested files:User object. It carries no money — its analytical job is evidencing OTHER records, which resolves by joining through xero_file_associations. Documents added straight onto a transaction through the accounting Attachments endpoints are served by xero_attachments (org_meta); treat the two populations as complementary evidence sources, never as duplicates of each other. Deletion is physical and unflagged and the Files API accepts no modified-since filter, so rows reflect the latest full sweep of the library and absence is the only deletion signal.
gotchas: This is the Files-library population, not 'everything attached in Xero': documents pushed through the accounting Attachments endpoints live in xero_attachments (org_meta), and the two populations are not guaranteed to coincide. Never declare a record undocumented from one system alone.

created_date_utc is the digitization moment, not the business date — answering 'March receipts' from file dates misdates every late-scanned document. Business timing belongs to the associated accounting record.

Deletion is hard: a file removed from the library simply stops appearing, with no status or tombstone in the API. Only a full identity sweep (the API offers no modified-since filter) reveals removals, so this table can transiently overstate the library between syncs.
The uploader's 'Name' field carries an email address (documented Files API quirk) — it is staged as uploaded_by_email. Reports that label it as a person's name look broken to users.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Immutable UUID of the file and the row key; xero_file_associations.file_id points here. Names repeat freely — the same PDF uploaded twice is two distinct ids — so dedupe and join on this, never on name.

columns.name: folder_id
columns.description: UUID of the containing folder — every file lives in exactly one. The workflow test is joining xero_folders and checking is_inbox: Inbox membership separates filed documents from paperwork still awaiting attention.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display label with extension, as uploaded or emailed in and possibly renamed later. Cosmetic only: not unique, not stable, and its extension can disagree with mime_type — identity is file_id and content classification is mime_type.

columns.name: mime_type
columns.description: Content type recorded at upload (application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg, ...) and the practical way to slice documents — scans and receipts vs spreadsheets. It is recorded metadata, not a verified property of the bytes: the spec documents example values, not a content-check, so treat generic entries like application/octet-stream as classification gaps and expect occasional disagreement with the extension in name.

columns.name: size
columns.description: Storage footprint in bytes. Safe to SUM — each row is one stored object — which makes this, not the per-attachment copy in xero_file_associations.file_size_bytes, the source for storage questions; that copy repeats once per record the file is attached to.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When the file entered Xero (upload or email-in moment, UTC) — NOT the business date of the paper it depicts: a March receipt scanned in July is a July row here. 'What did we digitize last month' uses this; expense or revenue timing never does — that lives on the accounting document the file is associated to.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Metadata-change stamp (rename, move between folders) and this table's watermark field — but the Files API accepts no modified-since or where filter, so it powers local delta detection after a full sweep rather than server-side incremental pulls.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: The uploader's Xero user UUID — files:User.Id reached through the FileObject.User ref; the spec labels it only 'Xero identifier'. In practice it matches the org's Xero login identity, so a LEFT JOIN to xero_users.user_id decorates uploads with directory detail — but treat non-matches (departed users; the cross-API identity is observed behavior, not a spec guarantee) as expected, never as broken data.

columns.name: user_name
columns.description: The uploader's EMAIL ADDRESS, delivered in a source field literally called Name — the spec documents the trap: 'Key is Name, but returns Email address of user who created the file'. Present it as an email and never as a display label; the human-readable label is uploaded_by_full_name.

columns.name: user_first_name
columns.description: Uploader's given name, for attributing uploads to people in review workflows. Personal data — mask outside audit contexts and prefer uploaded_by_full_name for display rather than concatenating the parts.

columns.name: user_last_name
columns.description: Uploader's family name; personal data. Kept for matching against HR or directory records — for display use uploaded_by_full_name, which Xero has already assembled.

columns.name: user_full_name
columns.description: Uploader's assembled display name, ready-made for 'who uploaded what' reporting. (The published spec's doc-string for this field is a stray copy of LastName's — the value really is the full name.) Personal data.

joins.note: Every file lives in exactly one folder; the joined row's is_inbox flag marks paperwork still awaiting filing.

Best-effort decoration: the Files spec labels User.Id only 'Xero identifier'; matching the accounting Users UUID is observed behavior, not a spec guarantee. Always LEFT JOIN — uploads by users since removed from the org have no directory row.

examples.question: What was uploaded into Xero Files last month, and by whom?
examples.sql:
SELECT f.name, f.mime_type, f.user_full_name, f.created_date_utc
FROM xero_files f
WHERE f.created_date_utc >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE) - interval '1 month'
  AND f.created_date_utc < date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
ORDER BY f.created_date_utc DESC

examples.question: How much storage does each folder hold?
examples.sql:
SELECT fo.name AS folder, COUNT(*) AS files, ROUND(SUM(f.size) / 1048576.0, 1) AS megabytes
FROM xero_files f
JOIN xero_folders fo ON fo.folder_id = f.folder_id
GROUP BY fo.folder_id, fo.name
ORDER BY megabytes DESC

tables.grain: one row per folder in the tenant's Xero Files library, including the system Inbox
tables.description: The flat (non-nested) folder structure of the Files library, dominated by one special row: the Inbox, where emailed-in and unfiled documents accumulate until someone files or attaches them. It is the workflow dimension for document hygiene — files whose folder is the Inbox are paperwork awaiting processing. file_count is Xero's own point-in-time tally kept for reconciliation; live counts always come from xero_files.
gotchas: file_count is computed at scan time and goes stale the moment files move or arrive; reconcile against COUNT(*) on xero_files by folder_id before quoting either number.
Exactly one row is the Inbox (is_inbox = TRUE) and only it carries the email-in address — every other row has email NULL. Folders are flat: there is no parent-folder field and nothing to recurse.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Folder UUID and the row key; xero_files.folder_id points here. Stable across renames — group by this and decorate with name, or a rename fragments history.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Folder label as shown in Xero ('Inbox', 'Contracts', ...). Users can rename any folder except the Inbox at any time, so it is presentation, not identity.

columns.name: file_count
columns.description: Xero's count of files sitting in the folder at the moment of the folder sweep. It drifts from reality between syncs — the authoritative live number is COUNT(*) of xero_files per folder_id — and persistent disagreement is a sync-freshness signal, not a data bug. Never sum it across historical snapshots.

columns.name: email
columns.description: The magic email-in address: anything mailed to it lands as a file in the Inbox. Only the Inbox row carries a value — NULL for every other folder. It is a machine-minted org capability address (how users forward supplier bills into Xero), not a person's mailbox, which is why it is deliberately not flagged pii.

columns.name: is_inbox
columns.description: Marks the single system Inbox — undeletable, unrenamable, the landing zone for emailed and unfiled documents. 'Paperwork awaiting processing' means files whose folder has this flag set; treating the Inbox as just another folder turns backlog questions into noise.

examples.question: What is sitting unfiled in the Files inbox right now?
examples.sql:
SELECT f.name, f.mime_type, f.uploaded_by_full_name, f.created_date_utc
FROM xero_files f
JOIN xero_folders fo ON fo.id = f.id
WHERE fo.is_inbox
ORDER BY f.created_date_utc ASC

examples.question: Does Xero's folder tally agree with the files we have synced?
examples.sql:
SELECT fo.name, fo.file_count AS xero_count, COUNT(f.file_id) AS synced_count
FROM xero_folders fo
LEFT JOIN xero_files f ON f.id = fo.id
GROUP BY fo.id, fo.name, fo.file_count
HAVING fo.file_count <> COUNT(f.file_id)

tables.grain: one audit/history event per parent record per array position at sync time
tables.description: Single cross-parent audit trail: who did what, when, to which document (created, approved, voided, edited, emailed, notes), fetched by per-record fan-out from GET /{Endpoint}/{Guid}/History. The source rows have NO id and arrive newest-first, so the key is a minted ordinal that is only stable within one sync — order by date_utc, always. Same hard rate budget as attachments, so coverage is sampled and availability is optional.
gotchas: ordinal is array position at sync time with newest-first ordering — it shifts on every new event and every refresh. Any logic keyed on ordinal across syncs double-counts or misses events; order by date_utc.
Fan-out rate budget (shared with attachments): coverage is sampled, availability optional — absence of history rows never proves nothing happened to the document.
user_name is a free-text display name ('System Generated' included); joining actors to xero_users by exact string misses renamed users and practice staff — match fuzzily and expect unmatched rows.
The scope follows the PARENT endpoint (transactions.read for documents, contacts.read for Contacts) — a partial-scope connection yields history for some endpoints and silently none for others.

columns.name: parent_endpoint
columns.api: synthetic:the {Endpoint} segment of the fan-out path — which Xero collection the parent record lives in (e.g. 'Invoices', 'Payments', 'Contacts')
columns.description: Namespace half of the polymorphic parent key; the trail mixes every history-capable endpoint in one table, so filter it before joining or counting anything.

columns.name: parent_id
columns.api: synthetic:the {Guid} segment of the fan-out path — the parent record's vendor UUID
columns.description: UUID of the document/contact whose audit trail this event belongs to; join to the endpoint's staging table under the parent_endpoint filter.

columns.name: ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position in the HistoryRecords array at sync time (Xero returns newest first)
columns.description: Minted tie-breaker, NOT a stable event id: new events prepend, so yesterday's ordinal 0 is today's 1, and every refresh reassigns positions (replace-per-parent). Use date_utc for ordering and never persist references to ordinal.

columns.name: details
columns.description: Human-readable event prose ('INV-0042 sent to Acme.', note bodies). Free text intended for display — pattern-match it for context, never parse amounts or dates out of it.

columns.name: changes
columns.description: Short event-type label ('Created', 'Approved', 'Voided', 'Edited', 'Note'...). The OpenAPI's own description of this field is a copy-paste artifact ('Name of branding theme') — ignore it. The vocabulary is uncontrolled, so hunt event types with ILIKE patterns rather than strict equality.

columns.name: user
columns.description: Display name of the actor as free text (source field 'User', renamed because user is a Postgres reserved word; the spec's 'has a value of 0' description is an artifact). 'System Generated' marks automatic events. Not a UserID — resolving to xero_users is fuzzy name matching against first_name/last_name.

columns.name: date_utc
columns.description: UTC timestamp of the event and the only trustworthy ordering key for the trail. An audit stamp, not a business date — bucket into local days via the org's timezone when users expect calendar-day grouping.

joins.note: Polymorphic parent: repeat per endpoint/table pair. History is the only API evidence of WHO voided/approved a document.

examples.question: What is the latest audit event on each invoice?
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (parent_id)
       parent_id AS invoice_id, changes, details, user, date_utc
FROM xero_history_records
WHERE parent_endpoint = 'Invoices'
ORDER BY parent_id, date_utc DESC

examples.question: Who voided invoices in the last 90 days?
examples.sql:
SELECT parent_id AS invoice_id, user, date_utc
FROM xero_history_records
WHERE parent_endpoint = 'Invoices'
  AND changes ILIKE 'void%'
  AND date_utc >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
ORDER BY date_utc DESC

tables.grain: one line item on one invoice or bill per LineItemID
tables.description: The revenue and spend fact at its true grain: what was billed, for which product/service, posted to which GL account, carrying which tracking dimensions. Rows inherit direction (ACCREC vs ACCPAY), status, currency and LineAmountTypes from the parent — this table alone cannot tell a sale from a bill, so every aggregate joins xero_invoices. line_amount is net of discounts, and whether it includes tax depends on the parent's line_amount_types.
gotchas: No aggregate is safe without joining xero_invoices: without WHERE i.type='ACCREC' AND i.status IN ('AUTHORISED','PAID') you are summing bills, drafts and voided documents into 'revenue'.
line_amount includes tax on Inclusive documents. Net revenue across mixed documents = SUM(line_amount - CASE WHEN i.line_amount_types='Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(tax_amount,0) ELSE 0 END).
Tracking is per line, not per invoice, and absence means 'unassigned' — a department breakdown that inner-joins tracking silently drops untracked revenue.
Description-only lines are legal: null quantity/unit_amount/line_amount rows carry narrative. COUNT(*) is not 'number of billed lines' unless you filter them.
Amounts are in the parent document's currency; convert with the parent's currency_rate before cross-currency totals.

columns.name: line_items_line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the line and the row key. Not guaranteed durable: an update that resubmits the invoice's lines without their LineItemIDs deletes and recreates them under new ids, so never diff line history across syncs by this key alone.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Parent document key. The join to xero_invoices is mandatory: type (ACCREC/ACCPAY), status, currency_code, currency_rate and line_amount_types all live there and all change what this row means.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line within the parent's LineItems array (provenance: the array itself — the ordinal is its index). Presentation order for document reconstruction; re-numbered whenever the invoice is edited, so never use it as a stable identity.

columns.name: line_items_description
columns.description: Free-text line description (min 1 char). Xero allows description-only lines with no quantity or amounts — they carry narrative, not value, and must be excluded from unit economics (quantity IS NULL).

columns.name: line_items_quantity
columns.description: Units billed, up to 4dp; null on description-only lines. Only additive within a single item/unit definition — summing quantity across unrelated items adds hours to widgets.

columns.name: line_items_unit_amount
columns.description: Per-unit price in the document's currency BEFORE any discount. A rate: never sum it — billed value is line_amount. Average selling price should be SUM(line_amount)/SUM(quantity), not AVG(unit_amount).

columns.name: line_items_line_amount
columns.description: The line's billed value in document currency, already net of DiscountRate/DiscountAmount. Whether it includes tax depends on the PARENT's line_amount_types: Exclusive → net of tax, Inclusive → gross. Net revenue safely = line_amount - CASE WHEN parent is Inclusive THEN tax_amount ELSE 0 END.

columns.name: line_items_tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate key applied to the line; join xero_tax_rates.tax_type for the rate's name and percentage. Org-specific vocabulary (OUTPUT2, NONE, ...), not a fixed enum.

columns.name: line_items_tax_amount
columns.description: Tax on this line in document currency. Auto-calculated from the rate but manually overridable — recompute from xero_tax_rates and you will disagree with Xero on edited documents; trust this stored value.

columns.name: line_items_account_code
columns.description: User-facing GL account code the line posts to (join xero_accounts.code). Codes are org-editable — prefer account_id for durable joins.

columns.name: line_items_account_id
columns.description: Immutable GL account identifier for the line; the safe join to xero_accounts. Which account a line posts to is what separates product revenue from freight, interest or clearing noise.

columns.name: line_items_item_code
columns.description: User-defined code of the catalogue item behind the line; null on free-typed lines (very common on ACCPAY bills). Product analytics that drops null item_code silently ignores non-catalogue billing.

columns.name: line_items_item_item_id
columns.description: Resolved Xero identifier of the catalogue item (from the embedded Item echo); the durable join to xero_items — item_code can be renamed, this cannot.

columns.name: line_items_item
columns.description: Verbatim item stub as billed at sync time ({Code, Name, ItemID}). Point-in-time snapshot of the item's identity; use scalar item_id/item_code for joins and xero_items for current attributes.

columns.name: line_items_tracking
columns.description: Up to 2 tracking assignments — the org's self-defined analysis dimensions (Region, Department, ...) — as an array of {TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}. Expand with jsonb_array_elements and join xero_tracking_options on TrackingOptionID. Lines with no entry for a category are 'unassigned' and must not be dropped from breakdowns.

columns.name: line_items_discount_rate
columns.description: Percentage discount on the line — supported on ACCREC invoices only (Xero does not discount ACCPAY bills or credit notes). A rate, never summed; the money effect is already inside line_amount.

columns.name: line_items_discount_amount
columns.description: Absolute discount applied (ACCREC invoices and quotes only). line_amount is already net of it — subtracting again undercounts revenue; discount given = SUM(discount_amount) plus rate-based discounts.

columns.name: line_items_repeating_invoice_id
columns.description: Repeating template this line originated from when the parent was generated by a schedule; null on one-off documents.

columns.name: line_items_taxability
columns.description: US automated sales tax classification of the line; null outside US orgs. PART_TAXABLE lines split their base — see tax_breakdown for the jurisdictional detail.

columns.name: line_items_sales_tax_code_id
columns.description: Internal id of the US sales tax code applied to the line; US automated sales tax orgs only.

columns.name: line_items_tax_breakdown
columns.description: Per-jurisdiction US sales tax components (state/county/city/special district) with rate, tax and taxable/non-taxable/exempt bases. Genuinely polymorphic per jurisdiction, kept verbatim; the line's total tax is already in tax_amount — summing components AND tax_amount double-counts.

joins.note: Mandatory: direction (type), status, currency and LineAmountTypes live on the parent.
GL account the line posts to; fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code when account_id is null on older payloads.
Null on free-typed lines — a LEFT JOIN or product analyses lose non-catalogue billing.

examples.question: Net revenue by GL account this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT a.code AS line_items_account_code, a.name AS account_name,
       SUM((li.line_items_line_amount - CASE WHEN i.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(li.line_items_tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) * COALESCE(i.currency_rate, 1)) AS net_revenue_base
FROM xero_invoice_line_items li
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_id = li.invoice_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.line_items_account_id = li.line_items_account_id
WHERE i.type = 'ACCREC' AND i.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
  AND i.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY net_revenue_base DESC

examples.question: Revenue split by the 'Region' tracking category
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(t.value ->> 'Option', 'Unassigned') AS region,
       SUM((li.line_items_line_amount - CASE WHEN i.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN COALESCE(li.line_items_tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) * COALESCE(i.currency_rate, 1)) AS revenue_base
FROM xero_invoice_line_items li
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_id = li.invoice_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(li.line_items_tracking) AS t(value)
       ON t.value ->> 'Name' = 'Region'
WHERE i.type = 'ACCREC' AND i.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY revenue_base DESC

tables.grain: one invoice-reminder settings record per organisation
tables.description: Org-level toggle from GET /InvoiceReminders/Settings: whether Xero's automatic invoice reminder emails are switched on. A single-row config table; the API exposes only the on/off flag, not the per-reminder schedule visible in the Xero UI. Useful context when interpreting collections behaviour — an org with reminders off is chasing debt manually.
gotchas: The API returns only the org-wide on/off flag — the reminder schedule (7/14/21 days etc.) shown in the Xero UI is NOT available, so never claim per-invoice reminder activity from this table.

columns.name: settings_key
columns.api: synthetic:constant 'invoice_reminders' — the endpoint returns a single org-level settings record with no vendor identifier
columns.description: Minted singleton key so the row has a stable identity; always the literal 'invoice_reminders'.

columns.name: enabled
columns.description: True when automatic invoice reminder emails are on for the org. Context for DSO/collections analysis, not a per-invoice fact — Xero does not expose which invoices actually received reminders.

examples.question: Does this org have automatic invoice reminders switched on?
examples.sql: SELECT enabled FROM xero_invoice_reminders WHERE settings_key = 'invoice_reminders'

tables.grain: one invoice document (sales invoice ACCREC or bill ACCPAY) per InvoiceID
tables.description: Document-header fact for BOTH sides of the ledger: one Xero Invoice object is a sales invoice (Type=ACCREC, money owed to the org) or a supplier bill (Type=ACCPAY, money the org owes). Header totals (sub_total/total_tax/total) are normalized and safe to aggregate after filtering type and status; line-level revenue analysis belongs on xero_invoice_line_items. VOIDED and DELETED documents are still returned by the API and still land here — every total must exclude them. Settlement state (amount_due/amount_paid/amount_credited) is current-state only: it reflects now, not any historical point in time.
gotchas: One object, two directions: ACCREC rows are sales, ACCPAY rows are bills. 'Total invoiced' without WHERE type='ACCREC' silently adds supplier bills to revenue.
VOIDED and DELETED documents keep arriving from the API and keep sitting in this table. Every aggregate needs a status filter; status IN ('AUTHORISED','PAID') is the billed-reality set.
amount_due/amount_paid/amount_credited are the balance NOW. Historical AR/AP as-of a past date must be reconstructed from xero_payments and allocations, not from this table.

All monetary columns are in currency_code, not base currency. Cross-currency totals must multiply by currency_rate first — and even then compare against xero_journals, which is the statutory base-currency truth.
invoice_number is not unique (especially ACCPAY) and Xero can renumber drafts; join on invoice_id only.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the document and the row key; stable across edits, payment and voiding. The only safe join key — invoice_number is not unique.

columns.name: type
columns.description: The single most important filter in the Xero connector: ACCREC is a sales invoice (receivable), ACCPAY is a bill you owe (payable). GET /Invoices only ever returns those two — the other six enum values are the credit-note/prepayment/overpayment shapes surfaced by their own endpoints. Any revenue or spend number that does not filter type mixes sales with purchases and is wrong.
columns.enums: ACCPAY; ACCPAYCREDIT; APOVERPAYMENT; APPREPAYMENT; ACCREC; ACCRECCREDIT; AROVERPAYMENT; ARPREPAYMENT

columns.name: status
columns.description: Lifecycle gate for every aggregate. DRAFT/SUBMITTED are unapproved, AUTHORISED is approved and open, PAID is settled; VOIDED and DELETED are dead documents the API keeps returning. Billed revenue = status IN ('AUTHORISED','PAID'); including VOIDED resurrects cancelled sales, including DRAFT counts things that never happened.
columns.enums: DRAFT; SUBMITTED; DELETED; AUTHORISED; PAID; VOIDED

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The customer (ACCREC) or supplier (ACCPAY) on the document; join xero_contacts. The same contact can play both roles on different documents — direction always comes from type, never from the contact.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized contact display name captured with the document. Convenient for grouping, but contacts merge and rename — the governed name lives on xero_contacts via contact_id.

columns.name: invoice_number
columns.description: Human-facing document number (max 255). Auto-generated for ACCREC from org invoice settings; on ACCPAY it is whatever was keyed from the supplier's paper and is neither unique nor reliably present. Display and lookup only — never a join key.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference, ACCREC only (typically the customer's PO number); null on bills.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Issue date (org-timezone business date) — the accrual date that revenue and spend reports bucket on. Not the payment date; cash timing lives in xero_payments.

columns.name: due_date
columns.description: Contractual due date. Overdue receivables = type='ACCREC' AND status='AUTHORISED' AND amount_due > 0 AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Declares whether LineAmount on this document's lines includes tax: Exclusive (net), Inclusive (gross) or NoTax. Header sub_total/total_tax/total are already normalized regardless — but any SUM over raw line amounts that ignores this flag double-counts tax on Inclusive documents.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency of every monetary field on this row and its lines (spec CurrencyCode enum; the extraction truncates the full list, so treat no subset as exhaustive). Summing across currency_code without converting via currency_rate produces a number in no currency at all.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Exchange rate to the organisation's base currency fixed for this document (XE.com day rate unless overridden). Base-currency reporting multiplies monetary fields by this rate; the rate itself is never summed or averaged.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Tax-exclusive document total in document currency, normalized by Xero regardless of line_amount_types — the safest header-grain revenue/spend measure.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Total tax on the document in document currency. Tax collected is a liability, not revenue — keep it out of income numbers.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive total (sub_total + total_tax) in document currency. This is billed value, not cash received — settlement lives in amount_paid/amount_due and xero_payments.

columns.name: total_discount
columns.description: Sum of line-level discounts (ACCREC only). Line and header totals are already net of it — subtracting it again undercounts revenue.

columns.name: amount_due
columns.description: Open balance right now in document currency (total minus payments and credits). Current-state: yesterday's AR cannot be reconstructed from it. AR today = SUM(amount_due) WHERE type='ACCREC' AND status='AUTHORISED'.

columns.name: amount_paid
columns.description: Cash applied to date via payments, in document currency. The row-by-row evidence (with payment status and type) is xero_payments — aggregate collections there, not here.

columns.name: amount_credited
columns.description: Total knocked off this document by credit notes, overpayments and prepayments. Row-level evidence lives in xero_credit_note_allocations and the payments_credits allocation tables.

columns.name: fully_paid_on_date
columns.description: Date the document reached fully paid; only returned on fully paid invoices. Null does not mean unpaid — check amount_due and status.

columns.name: expected_payment_date
columns.description: User-entered cash-forecast date on sales invoices (ACCREC). Frequently absent and never enforced — a planning hint, not a promise.

columns.name: planned_payment_date
columns.description: ACCPAY twin of expected_payment_date: when the org plans to pay the bill. Null on sales invoices.

columns.name: sent_to_contact
columns.description: Whether the document is marked 'sent' inside Xero (settable only after approval). False does not prove the customer never got it — sending outside Xero bypasses the flag.

columns.name: cis_deduction
columns.description: UK Construction Industry Scheme amount withheld on the document; null outside CIS-enabled UK orgs.

columns.name: cis_rate
columns.description: CIS deduction percentage in force for the org — a rate, never summed.

columns.name: is_discounted
columns.description: True when any line carries a discount; the detail (rate/amount per line) is on xero_invoice_line_items.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when files are attached. The files themselves are catalogued in xero_attachments (org_meta) via a rate-limited per-parent fan-out.

columns.name: has_errors
columns.description: True when the payload carried API validation errors — a data-quality signal from write operations, not a business state.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Batch-response status indicator that accompanies validation messages (e.g. OK/WARNING/ERROR). Sync diagnostics only; ignore for analytics.

columns.name: url
columns.description: Link back to the source document in the originating app (shown as 'Go to [appName]' in Xero). Presentation only.

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Invoice template/branding used; join xero_branding_themes. Orgs often use themes to separate trading lines, so it can act as a de-facto business-unit dimension.

columns.name: repeating_invoice_id
columns.description: Template that generated this document when it came from a repeating schedule; null for one-off documents. Join xero_repeating_invoices to measure realized recurring billing.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Xero's last-modified audit stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (If-Modified-Since). Never bucket business metrics by it — that is what date is for.

columns.name: updated_date_utc_string
columns.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc as returned by the API; prefer the parsed timestamp column.

columns.name: payments
columns.description: Read-only echo of payments applied to this document, kept verbatim for reconciliation. Authoritative payment rows — with their own status and payment_type — live in xero_payments; aggregating this echo double-counts against that table and misses deleted-payment context.

columns.name: prepayments
columns.description: Read-only echo of prepayments applied to this document. Authoritative rows live in xero_prepayments / xero_prepayment_allocations (payments_credits).

columns.name: overpayments
columns.description: Read-only echo of overpayments applied to this document. Authoritative rows live in xero_overpayments / xero_overpayment_allocations (payments_credits).

columns.name: credit_notes
columns.description: Read-only echo of credit notes applied to this invoice. The governed rows are xero_credit_notes and the per-application detail is xero_credit_note_allocations — analyze there.

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Attachment stubs occasionally echoed on the document payload. The catalogued attachment inventory is xero_attachments (org_meta); this echo is not a complete list.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation error messages carried verbatim ({Message} objects). Data-quality triage only — rows with errors are still real documents.

columns.name: warnings
columns.description: Non-fatal API warning messages ({Message} objects), the softer counterpart of validation_errors.

columns.name: invoice_addresses
columns.description: FROM/TO physical addresses used by US automated sales tax to source the transaction. Tax metadata on the document — not the contact's master address book (that is xero_contact_addresses).

columns.name: contact
columns.description: Invoice.Contact as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: See LineItems Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: Customer on ACCREC, supplier on ACCPAY — direction comes from xero_invoices.type.
Null when the org's default theme applies implicitly.
Only populated on documents generated from a repeating template.

examples.question: Revenue billed by month this year, in base currency
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month,
       SUM(sub_total * COALESCE(currency_rate, 1)) AS billed_net
FROM xero_invoices
WHERE type = 'ACCREC'
  AND status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'PAID')
  AND date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Current accounts receivable by customer (document currency)
examples.sql:
SELECT contact_name, currency_code, SUM(amount_due) AS open_balance
FROM xero_invoices
WHERE type = 'ACCREC' AND status = 'AUTHORISED' AND amount_due > 0
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY open_balance DESC

examples.question: Overdue bills we still owe suppliers
examples.sql:
SELECT contact_name, invoice_number, due_date, amount_due
FROM xero_invoices
WHERE type = 'ACCPAY' AND status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND amount_due > 0 AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY due_date

tables.grain: one product or service item in the org's catalog, identified by ItemID
tables.description: The product/service dimension and the only inventory-balance surface in the accounting API. Document lines reference items by user-editable code (item_code), not by uuid — so this table joins to facts through `code`. Sales/purchase details are DEFAULTS offered in the Xero UI, not transacted prices; the transacted price is always unit_amount on the document line. is_tracked_as_inventory gates the stock story: only tracked items carry quantity_on_hand and total_cost_pool (average-cost value of stock), and both are point-in-time snapshots as of the last sync — Xero exposes no stock history. Those two balance columns are why this table is typed last_value_over_time rather than reference: every other column is catalog configuration, but stock value and quantity are as-at balances that may be summed across items and never across time. Items hard-delete: rows vanish from the API and are tombstoned only by full identity scans.
tables.additivityAxis: time — quantity_on_hand and total_cost_pool are as-at-last-sync balances overwritten in place, so they may be summed across items but never across syncs, snapshots or periods
gotchas: is_tracked_as_inventory gates quantity_on_hand/total_cost_pool: untracked items carry NULL, not zero. AVG or COALESCE-to-zero over the whole catalog invents stockless service items — restrict inventory math to tracked rows.

quantity_on_hand and total_cost_pool are as-of-last-sync snapshots with no history. Stock-movement or period-comparison questions are unanswerable from this table — say so rather than differencing stale copies.

Items HARD-delete: deleted items simply vanish from GET /Items. Tombstones appear only after a full identity scan, so recently deleted items may linger; document lines keep their item_code text either way.
sales_unit_price / purchase_unit_price are UI defaults, not transacted prices — revenue or spend computed from them is fiction; use line-level unit_amount/line_amount on the documents.
Fact tables reference items by the user-editable `code`. After a rename, historical lines point at a code that no longer exists here — LEFT JOIN and treat misses as catalog drift, not missing data.

columns.name: item_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable item identifier and the row key. Document lines do NOT carry it — they reference item_code — so fact joins go through code, not this uuid.

columns.name: code
columns.description: User-defined item code (max 30 chars) — the de facto foreign key from every invoice, PO and receipt line (item_code). User-editable: a rename silently orphans historical lines, so LEFT JOIN from facts and treat misses as catalog drift.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name (max 50 chars); not unique — code is the identity, name is the label.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Sales-side description. Xero NULLS this when is_sold flips false — a null on a purchase-only item is expected behavior, not data loss.

columns.name: purchase_description
columns.description: Purchase-side description; nulled by Xero when is_purchased flips false, mirroring the sales side.

columns.name: is_sold
columns.description: Whether the item is offered on sales documents (defaults true). Flipping it false also nulls description and the sales_* defaults — filter on it before reading those columns as configuration gaps.

columns.name: is_purchased
columns.description: Whether the item is available on purchase documents (defaults true); false also nulls purchase_description and the purchase_* defaults.

columns.name: is_tracked_as_inventory
columns.description: The gate for the whole inventory story: true only when both the inventory asset account and purchase COGS account are configured. Untracked items (services, untracked goods) have NULL quantity_on_hand and total_cost_pool — NULL means 'not tracked', never 'zero stock'.

columns.name: inventory_asset_account_code
columns.description: GL account (type INVENTORY) holding stock value for tracked items; joins xero_accounts.code. Null on untracked items — its presence is half of what makes an item tracked.

columns.name: sales_details_unit_price
columns.description: Default (list) selling price offered in the UI, up to 4dp. The transacted price is unit_amount on the document line — computing revenue from this column is fiction. A rate: never summed.

columns.name: sales_details_account_code
columns.description: Default revenue account applied when the item lands on a sales line; individual lines can override, so revenue-by-account must come from the lines, not this default.

columns.name: sales_details_tax_type
columns.description: Default sales tax rate key (joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type); the line's tax_type is what actually applied.

columns.name: purchase_details_unit_price
columns.description: Default purchase price, up to 4dp. Compare with total_cost_pool / quantity_on_hand (true average cost) to spot supplier price drift; never summed.

columns.name: purchase_details_account_code
columns.description: Default expense account for purchases of UNTRACKED items; per the spec it does not apply to the purchase details of tracked items, where the inventory asset account takes over.

columns.name: purchase_details_cogs_account_code
columns.description: Cost-of-goods-sold account, applicable only to tracked items' purchase details — required (with the inventory asset account) to make an item tracked. Null on untracked items; the sales-side Purchase structure never populates it.

columns.name: purchase_details_tax_type
columns.description: Default purchase tax rate key (joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type); the transacted rate lives on the document line.

columns.name: quantity_on_hand
columns.description: Units in stock as of the LAST SYNC — a point-in-time snapshot with no history; NULL (not zero) for untracked items. Period-over-period stock movement cannot be derived from this table, and yesterday's value is gone once resynced.

columns.name: total_cost_pool
columns.description: Value of stock on hand under Xero's average-cost method, as of the last sync; NULL for untracked items. Inventory valuation = SUM over tracked items; total_cost_pool / NULLIF(quantity_on_hand, 0) is the average unit cost.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-response validation indicator from batch upserts; not a catalog lifecycle state (items have none — they hard-delete instead). Ignore for analytics.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Server-side modification stamp and the incremental watermark (If-Modified-Since). It moves for any change to the item record, so it timestamps the quantity_on_hand / total_cost_pool snapshot as much as the catalog fields — read it as 'when Xero last touched this row', never as 'when someone edited the catalog'.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-time validation messages retained verbatim for payload fidelity; empty on clean reads, never analytical.

joins.note: Stock-value account for tracked items; sales/purchase default account codes join xero_accounts.code the same way.
Default sales tax rate; purchase_tax_type joins identically.
Committed purchases of this item; the code join breaks silently after item renames.

examples.question: Current inventory valuation (tracked items)
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(total_cost_pool) AS inventory_value
FROM xero_items
WHERE is_tracked_as_inventory

examples.question: Average unit cost vs default purchase price (price drift)
examples.sql:
SELECT code, name,
       ROUND(total_cost_pool / NULLIF(quantity_on_hand, 0), 4) AS avg_unit_cost,
       purchase_details_unit_price
FROM xero_items
WHERE is_tracked_as_inventory AND quantity_on_hand > 0
ORDER BY avg_unit_cost DESC

tables.grain: one tracking category/option pair applied to one journal line (at most two pairs per line)
tables.description: How the org's analysis dimensions (Department, Region…) attach to the statutory ledger: each row pins one journal line to one option of one tracking category. This is the join that turns P&L into P&L-by-department — filter or group ledger lines through it. Lines with no tracking simply have no rows here, so segment reports silently exclude untracked activity unless you LEFT JOIN and bucket the NULLs as 'unassigned'.
gotchas: Untracked lines have zero rows here. An INNER JOIN limits the P&L to tracked activity only — LEFT JOIN from xero_journal_lines and label NULL as 'unassigned' or department totals will not reconcile to the ledger.
Name and option are frozen at posting; after a rename they disagree with the tracking dimension tables. Group by ids, decorate with current names.

The spec types this array as TrackingCategory[], but the wire shape per element is the four TrackingReference fields (both ids plus the two labels) — there is no nested Options list on a journal line.

columns.name: journal_lines_journal_line_id
columns.description: The ledger line this tracking pair is stamped on — inherited key from xero_journal_lines.

columns.name: journal_id
columns.description: Denormalized grandparent key so segment aggregates can reach journal_date with one join instead of two.

columns.name: journal_lines_tracking_categories
columns.description: Zero-based position in the line's TrackingCategories array (0 or 1 — Xero allows at most two pairs per line). Provenance anchor for the exploded container; the meaningful key is (line, category).

columns.name: tracking_category_id
columns.description: Which analysis dimension this pair belongs to (e.g. the 'Region' category) — join to xero_tracking_categories. Stable across renames, unlike name.

columns.name: tracking_option_id
columns.description: The chosen value within the category (e.g. 'East') — join to xero_tracking_options. Group segments by this id, not by the frozen option text.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Category name as embedded in the immutable journal at posting time. If the org renames the category later, this diverges from xero_tracking_categories.name — filter by id and use current names for display.

columns.name: option
columns.description: Option label frozen at posting time; renamed options split history across labels if you group by this string instead of tracking_option_id.

joins.note: The measures (net_amount) live on the line — this table carries none.
Current category name and status.
Current option name; archived options still appear on historical lines.

examples.question: Expenses by Region this quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(o.name, 'unassigned') AS region, SUM(l.net_amount) AS expenses
FROM xero_journal_lines l
JOIN xero_journals j ON j.journal_id = l.journal_id
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id AND a.class = 'EXPENSE'
LEFT JOIN xero_journal_line_tracking t
  ON t.journal_lines_journal_line_id = l.journal_lines_journal_line_id
 AND t.tracking_category_id IN (SELECT tracking_category_id FROM xero_tracking_categories WHERE name = 'Region' AND status = 'ACTIVE')
LEFT JOIN xero_tracking_options o ON o.tracking_option_id = t.tracking_option_id
WHERE j.journal_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one signed debit or credit ledger line per JournalLineID (a globally unique uuid)
tables.description: The atoms of the statutory ledger: balanced debit/credit lines, ALWAYS in the org's base currency regardless of the source document's currency — the one place in Xero where summing across records is currency-safe without conversion. NetAmount is signed (positive = debit, negative = credit) and sums to zero within every journal; P&L, trial-balance and balance-sheet answers are SUM(net_amount) sliced by the joined account's Class from xero_accounts. Inherits the Advanced journals scope gate from the parent scan.
gotchas: Sign convention: credits are negative, and revenue lives on credit lines. Income presented from SUM(net_amount) without flipping the sign reads as a loss; use -SUM(net_amount) for REVENUE-class aggregates.
Statement questions join Class from xero_accounts. Filtering on the line's own account_type drops accounts (SALES vs REVENUE vs OTHERINCOME are all Class REVENUE).
Amounts are ALWAYS base currency — never multiply by a CurrencyRate; the conversion already happened upstream, unlike every document table in the connector.
gross_amount includes tax that also posts separately to tax-control lines; summing it double-counts GST/VAT. Use net_amount for statements and margins.

columns.name: journal_line_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the individual ledger line and the row key.

columns.name: journal_id
columns.description: Parent journal header — inherited key linking the line to its journal_date, source_type and balancing siblings. Every aggregate that needs a date joins through it.

columns.name: journal_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line inside the journal's JournalLines array — the provenance anchor for the exploded container and the statement print order. JournalLineID is the durable key; this preserves how the entry reads on paper.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: The general ledger account the amount posts to — the join to xero_accounts, whose Class (REVENUE/EXPENSE vs ASSET/LIABILITY/EQUITY) decides whether this line is P&L or balance sheet. Group by this, not by the denormalized name.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: The account's customer-defined code as at posting time. Codes can be edited on the account later; for stable grouping prefer account_id and take the current code from xero_accounts.

columns.name: account_type
columns.description: The granular posting-time account type. Useful for slicing (BANK, DIRECTCOSTS, OVERHEADS…) but a trap for statements: SALES, REVENUE and OTHERINCOME are all Class REVENUE — filter statements on the account's Class, not on this.
columns.enums: BANK; CURRENT; CURRLIAB; DEPRECIATN; DIRECTCOSTS; EQUITY; EXPENSE; FIXED; INVENTORY; LIABILITY; NONCURRENT; OTHERINCOME; OVERHEADS; PREPAYMENT; REVENUE; SALES; TERMLIAB; PAYG

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Account name frozen at posting time. Renames afterwards live only in xero_accounts, so grouping by this string splits one account's history across labels — display only.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Narrative carried from the source transaction line; only returned when populated, so expect nulls rather than empty strings.

columns.name: net_amount
columns.description: The signed base-currency movement: positive for a debit, negative for a credit; sums to zero per journal. Revenue therefore aggregates NEGATIVE — present P&L income as -SUM(net_amount) or profit reads as loss.

columns.name: gross_amount
columns.description: NetAmount + TaxAmount. Summing this for spend or revenue double-counts GST/VAT, which also posts to its own tax-control account lines — statements use net_amount.

columns.name: tax_amount
columns.description: Read-only tax portion on this line in base currency. Tax-liability questions belong to the tax-control accounts (SystemAccount GST) — summing this column mixes rate applications with the control postings.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: TaxType code applied to the line — the join key to xero_tax_rates. Null on untaxed lines; codes for deleted/archived rates persist here forever.

columns.name: tax_name
columns.description: Display name of the tax rate as at posting; the current name lives in xero_tax_rates. Join on tax_type, not on this.

joins.note: Provides journal_date (the period axis), source_type and source_id.
Provides Class and SystemAccount. Archived/deleted accounts still appear on historical lines — never filter the account side to ACTIVE when aggregating history.
Null tax_type on untaxed lines; use a LEFT JOIN.
Zero to two tracking pairs per line — the department/region analysis axes.

examples.question: Monthly profit and loss this calendar year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', j.journal_date) AS month,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.class = 'REVENUE' THEN -l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.class = 'EXPENSE' THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS expenses,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.class IN ('REVENUE', 'EXPENSE') THEN -l.net_amount ELSE 0 END) AS net_profit
FROM xero_journal_lines l
JOIN xero_journals j ON j.journal_id = l.journal_id
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
WHERE j.journal_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Trial balance as at 30 June 2026
examples.sql:
SELECT a.code, a.name, a.class, SUM(l.net_amount) AS balance
FROM xero_journal_lines l
JOIN xero_journals j ON j.journal_id = l.journal_id
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
WHERE j.journal_date <= DATE '2026-06-30'
GROUP BY a.account_id, a.code, a.name, a.class
HAVING SUM(l.net_amount) <> 0
ORDER BY a.code

tables.grain: one immutable statutory journal header per posted transaction event (JournalID)
tables.description: The statutory general ledger feed: every posted transaction in Xero — invoices, payments, bank lines, payroll, manual journals — becomes exactly one immutable journal header whose lines are always in the org's base currency. Because the Reports endpoints are scope-refused, this is the ONLY path to P&L, trial-balance and balance-sheet answers. The endpoint sits behind Xero's Advanced-tier accounting.journals.read approval, so availability is optional: when the scope is missing, financial-statement answers must degrade explicitly, never silently substitute invoice totals. Journals are append-only — never edited, never deleted — so CreatedDateUTC is a complete incremental watermark.
gotchas: Availability is gated: accounting.journals.read needs Xero's Advanced-tier approval. When the connection lacks it this table is absent — say the statutory ledger is unavailable rather than approximating P&L from invoices, which misses payroll, depreciation, manual journals and FX.
JournalDate is the accounting period; CreatedDateUTC is when the record was minted. Period reporting buckets on journal_date — bucketing on created_date_utc misplaces back-dated and imported entries.

The scan ingests the default accrual-basis feed. paymentsOnly=true is a separate cash-basis projection of the ledger that is NOT ingested — cash questions belong to payments and bank-transaction tables, not to a re-scan of this one.
SourceID/SourceType is a polymorphic pointer. A blanket join to one document table silently drops every other source type — always predicate the join on source_type.

columns.name: journal_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable journal identifier and the row key; the join key for xero_journal_lines. JournalNumber is the human-facing sequence, this uuid is the machine one.

columns.name: journal_date
columns.description: The accounting date the entry hits the ledger — the axis for every period total. Back-dated postings make this disagree with created_date_utc by design; bucketing periods on the audit stamp misplaces imports and corrections.

columns.name: journal_number
columns.description: Xero's monotonically increasing journal sequence and the offset-pagination cursor (offset = highest number already ingested, 100 journals per call). Gaps are normal — do not use it as a row count or completeness check.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When Xero minted the journal record — the If-Modified-Since watermark. Because journals are immutable this is both created and last-modified; a journal seen once never changes.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference carried over from the source transaction. Useful for display; matching on it is cosmetic — lineage joins go through source_id/source_type.

columns.name: source_id
columns.description: UUID of the originating document — an InvoiceID when source_type is ACCREC/ACCPAY, a ManualJournalID when MANJOURNAL, a BankTransactionID for CASHREC/CASHPAID, and so on. Null for system-generated entries (e.g. conversion balances). Join it per source_type, never blindly to one table.

columns.name: source_type
columns.description: What kind of transaction created this journal — the router for lineage joins and for slicing ledger activity (MANJOURNAL = manual adjustments, PAYSLIP/WAGEPAYABLE/INTEGRATEDPAYROLL* = payroll, TRANSFER = bank transfers, CASHREC/CASHPAID = spend/receive money). ACCREC here means 'journal born from a sales invoice', not the invoice itself.
columns.enums: ACCREC; ACCPAY; ACCRECCREDIT; ACCPAYCREDIT; ACCRECPAYMENT; ACCPAYPAYMENT; ARCREDITPAYMENT; APCREDITPAYMENT; CASHREC; CASHPAID; TRANSFER; ARPREPAYMENT; APPREPAYMENT; AROVERPAYMENT; APOVERPAYMENT; EXPCLAIM; EXPPAYMENT; MANJOURNAL; PAYSLIP; WAGEPAYABLE; INTEGRATEDPAYROLLPE; INTEGRATEDPAYROLLPT; EXTERNALSPENDMONEY; INTEGRATEDPAYROLLPTPAYMENT; INTEGRATEDPAYROLLCN

columns.name: journal_lines
columns.description: See JournalLines Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: Every journal has at least two balanced lines; the measures live there, the header carries none.
Valid ONLY where source_type = 'MANJOURNAL' — source_id is polymorphic.
Valid ONLY where source_type IN ('ACCREC','ACCPAY') — other source types point at other document tables.

examples.question: How many ledger entries does each activity type generate per month?
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', journal_date) AS month, source_type, COUNT(*) AS journals
FROM xero_journals
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC

examples.question: Which journal did a given invoice post to the ledger?
examples.sql:
SELECT j.journal_id, j.journal_number, j.journal_date, j.reference
FROM xero_journals j
WHERE j.source_type IN ('ACCREC', 'ACCPAY')
  AND j.source_id = '297c2dc5-cc47-4afd-8ec8-74990b8761e9'

tables.grain: one billable-expense link from one source purchase line to (at most) one target sales invoice line
tables.description: The rebilling wiring: each row connects a purchase-side line — an ACCPAY bill line or a SPEND bank-transaction line — to the customer it is recoverable from and, once allocated, to the ACCREC invoice line that recharges it. There are NO amounts on this table; cost lives on the source line and recharge revenue on the target line, so every monetary question is a join. The source join is polymorphic on source_transaction_type_code (ACCPAY vs SPEND) — a single unconditional join silently drops half the links. 'Billable expenses not yet recovered' is status = 'APPROVED'.
gotchas: No amounts live here. Recoverable cost = the SOURCE line's line_amount; recharge revenue = the TARGET line's line_amount. Counting rows or expecting an amount column produces nothing.

The source join is polymorphic: ACCPAY links join xero_invoices/xero_invoice_line_items, SPEND links join xero_bank_transactions/xero_bank_transaction_line_items. An unconditional join to either silently drops the other half.

GET /LinkedTransactions supports neither If-Modified-Since nor where, and exposes `page` with no `pageSize` — the page size is whatever Xero chooses and cannot be raised. Status changes therefore surface only on a full rescan, so this table's freshness lags the invoice tables synced beside it; a link can still read APPROVED here after the recharge invoice has been approved.
ONDRAFT means the recharge sits on a DRAFT invoice: pipeline, not revenue. Only BILLED links are actually recovered; treating ONDRAFT as billed overstates recovery.

columns.name: linked_transaction_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the billable-expense link and the row key.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Always BILLABLEEXPENSE today; the spec reserves room for more link kinds. Filtering on it adds nothing yet — but a future value would change this table's meaning, so tolerate unknowns.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Rebilling pipeline state: APPROVED = recoverable cost not yet on any customer invoice; ONDRAFT = sitting on a draft ACCREC invoice (pipeline, not revenue); BILLED = recharged on an approved invoice; DRAFT mirrors an unapproved source document; VOIDED is dead. 'Unrecovered billable expenses' filters APPROVED.

columns.name: source_transaction_id
columns.description: The purchase-side document the cost came from. Polymorphic: an ACCPAY invoice (xero_invoices) when source_transaction_type_code = 'ACCPAY', a spend-money bank transaction (xero_bank_transactions) when 'SPEND'. Branch before joining.

columns.name: source_line_item_id
columns.description: The exact line on the source document carrying the cost — join xero_invoice_line_items.line_item_id or xero_bank_transaction_line_items.line_item_id depending on the type code. This table has no amounts; the source line is where the cost lives.

columns.name: source_transaction_type_code
columns.description: Discriminator for every source-side join: ACCPAY = link created from a supplier bill line; SPEND = from a spend-money bank transaction line. Any query that joins the source without branching on this drops or misattributes links.

columns.name: target_transaction_id
columns.description: The ACCREC invoice recharging the cost to the customer; null until allocation. Joins xero_invoices — the target is receivable-side by construction.

columns.name: target_line_item_id
columns.description: The specific line on the target invoice. Multiple billable expenses may share one target line, so target-side revenue rollups must de-duplicate the recharge amount before summing.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: The customer the expense is recoverable from, set when the cost is marked billable — present even before any target invoice exists. The axis for 'unbilled recoverables by customer'; joins xero_contacts.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Modification stamp on the link record, useful for dating a status transition after the fact. It is not a scan watermark: the list op accepts neither If-Modified-Since nor where, so the ingester full-rescans regardless and this column can never narrow the pull.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-time validation messages retained verbatim for payload fidelity; empty on clean reads and never analytical.

joins.note: Source bill — valid ONLY where source_transaction_type_code = 'ACCPAY'.
Source spend-money — valid ONLY where source_transaction_type_code = 'SPEND'.
Cost line for ACCPAY sources; carries the recoverable amount.
Cost line for SPEND sources; carries the recoverable amount.
Target ACCREC invoice recharging the cost; null until allocated.
Target invoice line; many links can share one target line — de-duplicate before summing its amount.
The customer to be recharged — a receivable-side contact, unlike the supplier on the source bill.

examples.question: Unrecovered billable expense value by customer (bills and spend-money)
examples.sql:
SELECT lt.contact_id, SUM(COALESCE(ili.line_amount, btl.line_amount)) AS unrecovered_cost
FROM xero_linked_transactions lt
LEFT JOIN xero_invoice_line_items ili
  ON lt.source_transaction_type_code = 'ACCPAY' AND ili.line_item_id = lt.source_line_item_id
LEFT JOIN xero_bank_transaction_line_items btl
  ON lt.source_transaction_type_code = 'SPEND' AND btl.line_item_id = lt.source_line_item_id
WHERE lt.status = 'APPROVED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unrecovered_cost DESC

examples.question: Rebilling pipeline: link counts by status
examples.sql:
SELECT status, source_transaction_type_code, COUNT(*) AS links
FROM xero_linked_transactions
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

tables.grain: one tracking category/option pair per (manual journal, line position, tracking category)
tables.description: Tracking pairs attached to manual journal document lines — at most two per line, mirroring the ledger convention. For POSTED journals the same pairs re-materialize on the statutory side in xero_journal_line_tracking; this table exists so drafts can be segmented before posting and so document-side audits reconcile.
gotchas: For POSTED journals these pairs also exist on the statutory side (xero_journal_line_tracking). Segment statements from the statutory table; use this one for drafts — mixing the two double-counts.
Joins to this table are positional on line_ordinal; forgetting the second key column in the join fans every pair across all lines of the document.

columns.name: manual_journal_id
columns.description: The manual journal document these tracking pairs belong to — inherited from the fan-out parent and the first half of the composite positional key. The status filter that decides whether the pair ever reached the statutory ledger lives on this parent (status = 'POSTED'), so segment analysis must join through it, never treat rows here as posted activity on their own.

columns.name: line_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of the parent line in ManualJournal.JournalLines, inherited from xero_manual_journal_lines
columns.description: Which document line the pair sits on — positional, like the parent line's own key.

columns.name: journal_lines_tracking
columns.description: Zero-based position in the line's Tracking array (0 or 1) — provenance anchor for the exploded container.

columns.name: tracking_category_id
columns.description: The analysis dimension being applied — join to xero_tracking_categories.

columns.name: tracking_option_id
columns.description: The chosen option within the category — join to xero_tracking_options; the stable segment key.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Category name as returned on the document; may drift from the dimension table after renames — ids are the truth.

columns.name: option
columns.description: Option label as returned on the document — display only; group by tracking_option_id.

joins.note: Composite positional join — both columns required.
Current dimension name/status.
Current option name/status.

examples.question: Draft manual journals that still lack any tracking on their lines
examples.sql:
SELECT mj.manual_journal_id, mj.narration
FROM xero_manual_journals mj
JOIN xero_manual_journal_lines ml ON ml.manual_journal_id = mj.manual_journal_id AND COALESCE(ml.is_blank, false) = false
LEFT JOIN xero_manual_journal_line_tracking t
  ON t.manual_journal_id = ml.manual_journal_id AND t.line_ordinal = ml.line_ordinal
WHERE mj.status = 'DRAFT'
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING COUNT(t.tracking_category_id) = 0

tables.grain: one entry line per (manual journal, zero-based array position)
tables.description: The debit/credit lines of manual journal documents. LineAmount is signed like the statutory ledger (debits positive, credits negative) but is a DOCUMENT amount whose tax treatment depends on the parent's LineAmountTypes — it is not automatically the statutory net. Use these lines to inspect drafts and per-line tracking before posting; once the parent is POSTED, the audited numbers live in xero_journal_lines. Lines have no vendor id, so the key is the parent id plus array position.
gotchas: These are document lines, not the ledger: summing them alongside xero_journal_lines double-counts every POSTED manual journal. Statements come from journal lines; this table adds drafts and narration.
Always predicate on the parent's status = 'POSTED' for anything that claims to describe the books — draft, deleted and voided documents keep their lines here.
Line identity is positional. If a draft is re-edited and lines reordered, ordinals shift between syncs — do not build history on (manual_journal_id, line_ordinal) for DRAFT documents.

columns.name: manual_journal_id
columns.description: Parent manual journal — inherited key; the status filter that decides whether these lines ever reached the ledger lives on the parent.

columns.name: journal_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the document's JournalLines array — the only stable line identity Xero provides (lines carry no uuid) and the provenance anchor for the exploded container.

columns.name: line_amount
columns.description: Signed document amount: debits positive, credits negative; a balanced journal sums to zero (net of tax handling). Under LineAmountTypes = Inclusive this CONTAINS tax_amount — normalize before comparing across documents; the statutory net is xero_journal_lines.net_amount.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: Customer-defined code of the target account as entered; account_id is the durable join — codes can be re-used after edits.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: The general ledger account the line hits — join to xero_accounts for Class when classifying what an adjustment moved.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Per-line narrative supplementing the parent's narration.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: TaxType code applied to the line — join to xero_tax_rates; drives the calculated tax_amount.

columns.name: tax_amount
columns.description: Tax calculated from tax_type and line_amount. Whether it is inside or on top of line_amount depends on the parent's LineAmountTypes — check before netting.

columns.name: is_blank
columns.description: True for empty spacer rows kept in the document layout. They carry no amounts; exclude them from line counts or averages.

joins.note: Status, date and LineAmountTypes — all three change what the line means.
Class tells you what kind of account the adjustment touched.
LEFT JOIN — tax_type is null on untaxed lines.

examples.question: Largest posted manual adjustments this year by gross debit size
examples.sql:
SELECT mj.manual_journal_id, mj.date, mj.narration, SUM(CASE WHEN ml.line_amount > 0 THEN ml.line_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_debits
FROM xero_manual_journal_lines ml
JOIN xero_manual_journals mj ON mj.manual_journal_id = ml.manual_journal_id
WHERE mj.status = 'POSTED' AND mj.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY total_debits DESC
LIMIT 20

examples.question: Which accounts do manual corrections touch most often?
examples.sql:
SELECT a.code, a.name, COUNT(*) AS lines_touched
FROM xero_manual_journal_lines ml
JOIN xero_manual_journals mj ON mj.manual_journal_id = ml.manual_journal_id AND mj.status = 'POSTED'
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = ml.account_id
WHERE COALESCE(ml.is_blank, false) = false
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY lines_touched DESC
LIMIT 15

tables.grain: one manual journal document per ManualJournalID
tables.description: Hand-keyed ledger adjustments — accruals, corrections, opening balances — as editable documents with a status lifecycle. Only POSTED manual journals reach the general ledger (where they reappear in xero_journals with source_type MANJOURNAL); DRAFT and ARCHIVED are staging states, and DELETED/VOIDED are dead but still returned by the API. This table's unique value over xero_journals is draft visibility, narration, and availability without the Advanced journals scope — it is NOT a second copy of the ledger to sum.
gotchas: POSTED manual journals ALSO exist in xero_journals/xero_journal_lines. Unioning the two line tables double-counts every posted adjustment — use manual journal lines for drafts and narration, journal lines for statements.
DELETED and VOIDED documents keep coming back from the API. Any aggregate that skips the status filter resurrects reversed adjustments.
With line_amount_types = 'Inclusive', line amounts contain tax; comparing them against Exclusive documents without normalizing overstates the inclusive ones.

columns.name: manual_journal_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the manual journal document and the row key; xero_journals.source_id points here when source_type = 'MANJOURNAL'.

columns.name: narration
columns.description: The accountant's required description of why the adjustment exists — the best human signal for classifying corrections vs accruals vs opening balances.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The accounting date the journal posts to (YYYY-MM-DD) — period bucketing uses this, not updated_date_utc.

columns.name: status
