columns.description: Lifecycle state. Only POSTED affects the ledger; DRAFT and ARCHIVED never posted; DELETED (was draft) and VOIDED (was posted) are dead yet still returned. Every total over lines must filter status = 'POSTED' or drafts and voids contaminate it.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Whether line amounts are tax Exclusive, Inclusive, or NoTax. With Inclusive, a line's LineAmount contains its TaxAmount — summing LineAmount across mixed documents double-counts tax; the statutory net lives in xero_journal_lines.

columns.name: url
columns.description: Link back to a source document in an external app (shown as 'Go to [appName]' in Xero) — presence signals the journal was machine-created by an integration.

columns.name: show_on_cash_basis_reports
columns.description: Whether the journal participates in cash-basis reporting (defaults true). Irrelevant to accrual questions; only matters when replicating Xero's cash-basis statements.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when supporting documents are attached — the cheap pre-filter before fanning out to org_meta's per-parent attachments endpoint with its 60/min rate budget.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark (If-Modified-Since). Not the accounting date — see date.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-response marker (e.g. ERROR/WARNING) accompanying validation payloads; carries no accounting meaning on read and is null in normal scans.

columns.name: warnings
columns.description: Verbatim array of API warning messages — populated on write responses, effectively always null in read scans. Kept for payload fidelity; element shape is the spec's ValidationError (Message), not owned by this domain.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Verbatim array of API validation errors — write-time noise, null in read scans; presentation-only.

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Verbatim attachment stubs occasionally embedded in responses. The governed copy of attachment metadata is org_meta's xero_attachments — query that, treat this as raw evidence.

columns.name: journal_lines
columns.description: See JournalLines Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: Lines are only present when the scan pages (page param) or fetches by id — the unpaged list omits them.
The statutory copy: rows there have source_type = 'MANJOURNAL'. Only POSTED manual journals appear.

examples.question: Manual adjustment activity by month, posted only
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS posted_journals
FROM xero_manual_journals
WHERE status = 'POSTED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Draft manual journals waiting to post, oldest first
examples.sql:
SELECT manual_journal_id, date, narration
FROM xero_manual_journals
WHERE status = 'DRAFT'
ORDER BY date

tables.grain: one online-invoice sharing URL per invoice
tables.description: Per-invoice fan-out from GET /Invoices/{InvoiceID}/OnlineInvoice: the public 'view your invoice online' link Xero hosts for sales invoices. Operational/engagement metadata, not a financial fact. Fetched lazily against the fan-out rate budget, so coverage is best-effort — absence of a row means not-yet-fetched at least as often as not-available.
gotchas: Fan-out endpoint under Xero's hard rate budget (60 calls/min, 1k-5k/day per org): rows are backfilled opportunistically, so missing rows usually mean 'not fetched yet', not 'no link exists'.
ACCREC only — requesting the online invoice of an ACCPAY bill is an API error, so the scan plan must filter parents by type before fanning out.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: The sales invoice this sharing URL belongs to (inherited fan-out key); join xero_invoices.

columns.name: online_invoice_url
columns.description: Publicly reachable URL of the hosted invoice. Anyone with the link can view the document — treat as shareable-sensitive even though it is not personal data per se.

joins.note: Only sales invoices (type ACCREC) have online invoices; the endpoint errors for bills.

examples.question: Get the shareable link for invoice INV-0042
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, oi.online_invoice_url
FROM xero_online_invoices oi
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_id = oi.invoice_id
WHERE i.invoice_number = 'INV-0042'

tables.grain: one entitlement action per organisation per action name
tables.description: The org's capability/entitlement matrix from GET /Organisation/Actions: named features (e.g. 'UseMulticurrency', 'Payroll', 'AttachFiles') with an ALLOWED/NOT-ALLOWED verdict driven by plan, region and edition. This is the reference to consult BEFORE declaring a data gap: an empty multicurrency, payroll or attachments footprint under a NOT-ALLOWED action is a plan limitation, not a sync failure.
gotchas: The negative status is hyphenated ('NOT-ALLOWED'); filtering on NOT_ALLOWED returns zero rows and every capability appears granted.
Action names are an open vocabulary with no spec enum — probe with ILIKE when hunting a capability, and expect new names to appear over time.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.api: synthetic:the connected tenant's OrganisationID, minted onto each row from connection context — GET /Organisation/Actions takes no path parameter and the Action payload carries no org id
columns.description: The organisation these entitlements belong to — the connection's single org, inherited as row context (the Action payload itself carries no org id).

columns.name: name
columns.description: Entitlement name, e.g. 'UseMulticurrency', 'Payroll', 'AttachFiles'. Open vocabulary — Xero adds names without notice, so treat values as data and never hard-code an exhaustive list.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Whether the org's plan/region grants the capability. Note the hyphen: the negative value is NOT-ALLOWED, not NOT_ALLOWED — an underscore filter silently matches nothing and makes every feature look enabled.

joins.note: Dozens of action rows per organisation.

examples.question: Is multicurrency enabled for each connected organisation?
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name AS organisation, a.status
FROM xero_organisation_actions a
JOIN xero_organisations o USING (organisation_id)
WHERE a.name = 'UseMulticurrency'

tables.grain: one address per organisation per address type (POBOX, STREET or DELIVERY)
tables.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.Addresses. Xero maintains at most one address per type per org, so (organisation_id, address_type) is the true key. POBOX is the postal/mailing address that documents display; STREET is the physical address. Rows are replaced wholesale with each parent refresh — an address cleared in Xero simply stops appearing.
gotchas: Rows are replace-per-parent: an address deleted in Xero disappears from the array with no tombstone in the payload — absence IS the deletion signal.
country is free text while the org's country_code is ISO — mixing the two in one GROUP BY splits the same country into multiple buckets.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

columns.name: address_type
columns.description: Which slot this row fills. 'The org's address' is ambiguous until you pick one: statements and invoices show the postal (POBOX) address, while STREET is the physical location. Choosing the wrong slot puts the wrong address on generated documents.

columns.name: address_line1
columns.description: First free-text address line (max 500 chars). Lines are display text, not parsed components — do not geocode or split from a single line.

columns.name: address_line2
columns.description: Second free-text address line; frequently blank rather than null.

columns.name: address_line3
columns.description: Third free-text address line; rarely populated.

columns.name: address_line4
columns.description: Fourth free-text address line; rarely populated.

columns.name: city
columns.description: Town/city component (max 255). Free text — normalize casing before grouping.

columns.name: region
columns.description: State/region/county component. Free text, not a controlled state code — 'NSW' and 'New South Wales' both occur.

columns.name: postal_code
columns.description: Postal/ZIP code (max 50). Keep as text: leading zeros are significant in many countries.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country as letters-only free text (max 50) — NOT guaranteed to be an ISO code ('New Zealand', not 'NZ'). For reliable country grouping use xero_organisations.country_code instead.

columns.name: attention_to
columns.description: Person or role the mail is addressed to (max 255). A personal name — treat as PII.

joins.note: At most three rows (one per type) per organisation.

examples.question: What postal address should appear on statements for each organisation?
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name, a.address_line1, a.city, a.postal_code, a.country
FROM xero_organisation_addresses a
JOIN xero_organisations o USING (organisation_id)
WHERE a.address_type = 'POBOX'

tables.grain: one CIS configuration record per organisation
tables.description: UK Construction Industry Scheme posture per org, fetched by fan-out from GET /Organisation/{OrganisationID}/CISSettings: whether the org operates as CIS contractor and/or subcontractor, and the HMRC-verified deduction rate applied to subcontracted labour. Only meaningful for UK-version orgs — for everyone else the endpoint returns nothing, and absence of a row is the expected state, not a gap.
gotchas: UK-only feature: non-UK orgs return no CIS settings, and availability is optional — treat a missing row as 'not a CIS org', never as unknown-due-to-error without checking sync logs.
rate is a whole-number percentage; multiplying labour by rate without /100 overstates deductions 100x.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.description: The organisation whose CIS settings these are — the fan-out path parameter, minted onto the row because the CISOrgSetting payload carries no id of its own.

columns.name: cis_contractor_enabled
columns.description: True when the org files CIS as a contractor — it deducts tax from subcontractor labour, and CIS-labour line items on its bills carry those deductions.

columns.name: cis_sub_contractor_enabled
columns.description: True when the org is itself a CIS subcontractor — customers withhold the deduction from ITS invoices, so cash received legitimately undershoots invoiced totals by the CIS rate.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: CIS deduction percentage as a whole-number percent (20 means 20%), read-only and set by HMRC verification status (30 unverified, 20 standard, 0 gross-payment). Dividing by 100 twice — or not at all — is the classic wrong-CIS-number mistake.

joins.note: At most one CIS settings row per organisation; present only for UK orgs with CIS enabled.

examples.question: Which connected organisations operate under CIS, and at what deduction rate?
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name, c.cis_contractor_enabled, c.cis_sub_contractor_enabled, c.rate
FROM xero_organisation_cis_settings c
JOIN xero_organisations o USING (organisation_id)

tables.grain: one external profile link per organisation per array position
tables.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.ExternalLinks — the org's website and social profiles (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, GooglePlus, Website). Xero exposes no link id, so the key is a minted array ordinal and rows are replaced per parent on refresh. The array is present only once Organisation settings have been edited in Xero; most orgs have zero rows.
gotchas: ordinal is reassigned on every refresh (no source id, replace-per-parent) — deduplicate by (organisation_id, link_type, url), not by ordinal, when comparing across syncs.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

columns.name: ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position in Organisation.ExternalLinks as returned
columns.description: Minted array position — stable only within a single sync because the source has no link id. Never persist references to it across refreshes.

columns.name: link_type
columns.description: Which service the link points at. Values are mixed-case exactly as the enum spells them ('Website', not 'WEBSITE') — filters are case-sensitive.

columns.name: url
columns.description: Public profile/website URL as entered by the org — marketing surface, not verified or normalized.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Optional free-text label for the link; usually null.

joins.note: Zero to a handful of rows per organisation.

examples.question: Which organisations have a website or social presence on file?
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name, l.link_type, l.url
FROM xero_organisation_external_links l
JOIN xero_organisations o USING (organisation_id)
ORDER BY o.name, l.ordinal

tables.grain: one default payment-term rule per organisation per document side (SALES or BILLS)
tables.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.PaymentTerms: the org-level DEFAULT due-date rules for new sales invoices and new bills, one row per side. These are data-entry defaults three levels removed from reality — contact-level terms override them, and every document ultimately carries its own DueDate. Use this table to describe policy ('we invoice net 20'), never to compute lateness.
gotchas: These are DEFAULTS only: contact-level payment terms override them and every invoice carries its own DueDate. Computing overdue/lateness from this table instead of the document's DueDate mislabels invoices wholesale.
day and term_type are one fact in two columns — a net-N reading of an OF*MONTH row shifts every projected due date by weeks.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

columns.name: term_scope
columns.api: synthetic:discriminator for which PaymentTerm branch this row materializes — SALES from accounting:PaymentTerm.Sales, BILLS from accounting:PaymentTerm.Bills
columns.description: Which side of the business the default applies to: SALES governs new receivable invoices you issue, BILLS governs new payables you record. Reading the BILLS row as customer terms inverts the direction of the policy.

columns.name: bills_day
columns.description: Numeric day whose meaning flips with term_type: for DAYSAFTERBILLDATE/DAYSAFTERBILLMONTH it is a day COUNT (net-N), for OFCURRENTMONTH/OFFOLLOWINGMONTH it is a calendar day-of-month (the Nth). 20 can mean 'net 20' or 'the 20th' — never read it without term_type. Projection reads PaymentTerm.Bills.Day for the BILLS row and the identically-shaped PaymentTerm.Sales.Day for the SALES row (term_scope selects the branch).

columns.name: bills_type
columns.description: The due-date formula day plugs into. DAYSAFTERBILLDATE: day days after the document date; DAYSAFTERBILLMONTH: day days after the end of the document's month; OFCURRENTMONTH/OFFOLLOWINGMONTH: due on the day-th of this/next month. Note the spec's branch type is named 'Bill' (a payment-term shape), unrelated to supplier bills. Projection reads PaymentTerm.Bills.Type for the BILLS row and PaymentTerm.Sales.Type for the SALES row (term_scope selects the branch).

joins.note: At most two rows (SALES, BILLS) per organisation; either may be absent when never configured.

examples.question: What default payment terms does each organisation offer on sales invoices?
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name, t.bills_day, t.bills_type
FROM xero_organisation_payment_terms t
JOIN xero_organisations o USING (organisation_id)
WHERE t.term_scope = 'SALES'

tables.grain: one phone entry per organisation per phone type slot
tables.description: Normalized explode of Organisation.Phones, which reuses the accounting API's shared Phone shape (the same object Contacts use, owned by contacts_dir). Xero maintains fixed type slots (DEFAULT, DDI, MOBILE, FAX, OFFICE) with at most one entry per type. A dialable number is the concatenation of country code + area code + number — no single column holds the full number.
gotchas: The number is split across three parts and any part may be an empty string — concat_ws(' ', ...) with NULLIF guards, or 'orgs without phones' counts orgs that merely left one part blank.
Slots for unused types may still arrive with all parts blank; existence of a row does not mean a phone number exists.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.description: Owning organisation; inherited from the parent profile row during the same scan.

columns.name: phone_type
columns.description: Slot key from Xero's fixed phone-type set (DEFAULT, DDI, MOBILE, FAX, OFFICE — the shared Phone schema's enum, which lives in contacts_dir's ground truth). DEFAULT is the primary number to display.

columns.name: phone_number
columns.description: Subscriber-number part only (max 50). Xero often returns empty strings rather than nulls for unused slots — filter blanks before counting 'orgs with a phone on file'.

columns.name: phone_area_code
columns.description: Area-code part (max 10). Keep as text; leading zeros matter.

columns.name: phone_country_code
columns.description: Country-dialling-code part (max 20), without a guaranteed '+' prefix. Concatenate country + area + number for display.

joins.note: At most one row per phone type per organisation.

examples.question: What is each organisation's primary phone number?
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name,
       NULLIF(concat_ws(' ', p.phone_country_code, p.phone_area_code, p.phone_number), '') AS phone
FROM xero_organisation_phones p
JOIN xero_organisations o USING (organisation_id)
WHERE p.phone_type = 'DEFAULT'

tables.grain: one organisation profile per connected Xero tenant
tables.description: The legal-entity master record and the decoder ring for every number in the connector: exactly one row per connected tenant. base_currency is the currency all journal lines and base-converted totals resolve to; financial_year_end_day/month define the fiscal calendar every 'this year' question must respect; version and country_code decide regional semantics (which payroll region exists, what tax_number means). The record carries no UpdatedDateUTC, so the sync refreshes it wholesale and the table is current-state only — settings changes leave no history here. Filter is_demo_company before any cross-org rollup: Xero's demo company ships with realistic invoices that poison portfolio totals.
gotchas: is_demo_company orgs carry realistic sample invoices, payments and contacts; any multi-org aggregate that fails to exclude them reports business that does not exist.
organisation_id equals xero_connections.tenant_id only for ORGANISATION-type tenants — PRACTICE connections have no row here, so inner joins from connections silently drop practices.
There is no update watermark on this record: lock dates, tax settings and defaults change without any timestamp moving. The table is current-state; never reconstruct settings history from it.
default_sales_tax/default_purchases_tax are data-entry defaults, not facts about stored documents — each document's own LineAmountTypes governs its line maths.

columns.name: organisation_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the organisation and the row key. For ORGANISATION-type tenants it is the same UUID presented as the xero-tenant-id header, i.e. it equals xero_connections.tenant_id — that equality is the join between authorization metadata and the profile.

columns.name: api_key
columns.description: Xero-to-Xero network key displayed in org settings. It is an operational credential, not an analytical attribute — never surface it in generated answers; it lands in staging only for settings-snapshot completeness.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name shown inside Xero and the label to use in multi-org answers. Routinely differs from legal_name after rebrands — do not treat the two as interchangeable.

columns.name: legal_name
columns.description: The name Xero prints on reports and statutory-style documents. Prefer it for formal output, name for conversational labels.

columns.name: pays_tax
columns.description: Whether the org is registered with its local tax authority (GST/VAT registered). When false, zero tax amounts across documents are expected behaviour — a 'missing tax' finding on a non-registered org is not a data gap.

columns.name: version
columns.description: Regional edition the org was provisioned on; each *ONRAMP value pairs with the plain region its name prefixes (AUONRAMP with AU, and so on), so group them with their base region for regional analysis. This — not country_code alone — decides how tax_number reads (TFN vs GST vs VAT vs Tax ID), which payroll region can exist, and which tax bases are plausible. Key regional logic off it.
columns.enums: AU; NZ; GLOBAL; UK; US; AUONRAMP; NZONRAMP; GLOBALONRAMP; UKONRAMP; USONRAMP

columns.name: organisation_type
columns.description: One of the record's two identically-enumerated legal-form classifications (the other is organisation_entity_type); the spec documents no precedence between them and in practice they carry the same value. Segment on one column consistently — mixing the two across queries splits cohorts whenever they disagree.
columns.enums: ACCOUNTING_PRACTICE; COMPANY; CHARITY; CLUB_OR_SOCIETY; INDIVIDUAL; LOOK_THROUGH_COMPANY; NOT_FOR_PROFIT; PARTNERSHIP; S_CORPORATION; SELF_MANAGED_SUPERANNUATION_FUND; SOLE_TRADER; SUPERANNUATION_FUND; TRUST; PERSONAL; SINGLEMEMBERLLC; CCORPORATIONLLC; PARTNERSHIPLLC; SCORPORATIONLLC; LLC; NOTLLC; UNSPECIFIED

columns.name: base_currency
columns.description: The currency every journal line and base-converted total resolves to (spec enum CurrencyCode, ISO 4217; the full value list is larger than the extract inlines, so it is deliberately not enumerated here). Documents carry their own CurrencyCode plus a CurrencyRate back to THIS currency — summing raw document amounts across orgs with different base currencies produces a number in no currency at all.

columns.name: country_code
columns.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 home country (spec enum CountryCode, not inlined in full). Use for geographic grouping; use version for behavioural semantics — a GLOBAL-version org can sit in any country.

columns.name: is_demo_company
columns.description: True for Xero's sample company. Its invoices, payments and contacts are fabricated but look real in every downstream table — exclude demo orgs from any aggregate that reaches a human, or the rollup reports revenue that does not exist.

columns.name: organisation_status
columns.description: ACTIVE when the API can address the org. Anything else means the tenant is not currently reachable, so expect stale staging data downstream — not fresh zeros.

columns.name: registration_number
columns.description: Companies-register number, shown for NZ/AU/UK orgs. Public company identifier and the anchor for matching the org to external registries; not personal data.

columns.name: employer_identification_number
columns.description: US EIN, present only when set on US orgs. Business tax identifier — treat as sensitive and keep out of answers unless explicitly requested.

columns.name: tax_number
columns.description: The org's tax-authority identifier. The same field renders as Tax File Number (AU), GST Number (NZ), VAT Number (UK) or Tax ID (US/Global) depending on version — label it accordingly, and treat it as sensitive.

columns.name: financial_year_end_day
columns.description: Day component of fiscal year end (calendar day 0-31). 'This financial year' in any P&L-style question means the year ending on this day/month, not the calendar year — defaulting to Jan-Dec silently misstates YTD for most AU/NZ/UK orgs.

columns.name: financial_year_end_month
columns.description: Month component of fiscal year end (1-12). Pair with financial_year_end_day to derive fiscal periods; AU orgs typically end 30/6, UK 31/3 — never assume December.

columns.name: sales_tax_basis
columns.description: Accounting basis used for tax returns; the enum mixes regional vocabularies (PAYMENTS/INVOICE are NZ-style, CASH/ACCRUAL AU/US, FLATRATE* UK schemes). It changes when tax is reported, not what documents say — do not use it to reinterpret invoice tax fields.
columns.enums: PAYMENTS; INVOICE; NONE; CASH; ACCRUAL; FLATRATECASH; FLATRATEACCRUAL; ACCRUALS

columns.name: sales_tax_period
columns.description: Filing frequency for tax returns, again a regionally-mixed vocabulary. Useful for anticipating filing/lock cadence; never a transformation input for amounts.
columns.enums: MONTHLY; QUARTERLY1; QUARTERLY2; QUARTERLY3; ANNUALLY; ONEMONTHS; TWOMONTHS; SIXMONTHS; 1MONTHLY; 2MONTHLY; 3MONTHLY; 6MONTHLY; QUARTERLY; YEARLY; NONE

columns.name: default_sales_tax
columns.description: Default LineAmountTypes label applied to NEW sales documents ('Tax Exclusive' etc.). A UI default only — every document carries its own LineAmountTypes, which is what governs that document's line maths. Never apply this org default to interpret existing lines.

columns.name: default_purchases_tax
columns.description: Default LineAmountTypes label for new purchase documents. Same warning as default_sales_tax: a default for data entry, not a fact about stored documents.

columns.name: period_lock_date
columns.description: Standard users cannot edit transactions dated on or before this date. Numbers before the lock are closed for reporting; a restatement before the lock implies an adviser-level edit. Null when no lock is set.

columns.name: end_of_year_lock_date
columns.description: The adviser-level year-end lock. Anything before it is effectively published accounts; treat pre-lock movements in staging as re-sync artifacts to investigate, not business changes to report.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When the org was created in Xero. Documents DATED before this are conversion/migration balances from a prior system, not live trading history — a useful tripwire when 'first year' growth looks impossible.

columns.name: timezone
columns.description: Org display timezone (spec enum TimeZone, not inlined in full). Xero business dates (Date, DueDate) are calendar dates unaffected by it; use it only when bucketing UTC audit timestamps (UpdatedDateUTC, history DateUTC) into local days.

columns.name: organisation_entity_type
columns.description: Legal-form classification (company, partnership, trust, sole trader...) — the attribute to segment a portfolio by entity type. Shares its exact vocabulary with organisation_type and normally agrees with it; the spec declares no precedence, so pick one column for segmentation and coalesce to the other only when it is null.
columns.enums: ACCOUNTING_PRACTICE; COMPANY; CHARITY; CLUB_OR_SOCIETY; INDIVIDUAL; LOOK_THROUGH_COMPANY; NOT_FOR_PROFIT; PARTNERSHIP; S_CORPORATION; SELF_MANAGED_SUPERANNUATION_FUND; SOLE_TRADER; SUPERANNUATION_FUND; TRUST; PERSONAL; SINGLEMEMBERLLC; CCORPORATIONLLC; PARTNERSHIPLLC; SCORPORATIONLLC; LLC; NOTLLC; UNSPECIFIED

columns.name: short_code
columns.description: Short identifier used in Xero deep links (Go URLs). Handy for constructing links back into the Xero UI; never a join key.

columns.name: class
columns.description: Subscription plan family. LEDGER and *_CASHBOOK classes are adviser-managed books with reduced feature sets — empty invoicing or payroll tables under those classes are plan limitations, not sync failures. DEMO/TRIAL classes corroborate is_demo_company-style exclusions.
columns.enums: DEMO; TRIAL; STARTER; STANDARD; PREMIUM; PREMIUM_20; PREMIUM_50; PREMIUM_100; LEDGER; GST_CASHBOOK; NON_GST_CASHBOOK; ULTIMATE; LITE; ULTIMATE_10; ULTIMATE_20; ULTIMATE_50; ULTIMATE_100; IGNITE; GROW; COMPREHENSIVE; SIMPLE; BASICLITE; ULTRA

columns.name: edition
columns.description: BUSINESS or PARTNER. PARTNER-edition orgs are sold through accounting partners with restricted functionality — some have no invoicing at all. Check this before diagnosing missing documents as an ingestion bug.

columns.name: line_of_business
columns.description: Free-text industry description typed by the org owner. Uncontrolled vocabulary — group with care and never treat as an enum.

columns.name: addresses
columns.description: Verbatim Addresses array exactly as returned (AddressForOrganisation shape), preserved for payload fidelity. Query xero_organisation_addresses instead — the child table is the normalized surface; both are refreshed in the same scan.

columns.name: phones
columns.description: Verbatim Phones array (shared accounting Phone shape), preserved for payload fidelity. Query xero_organisation_phones for filtering; phone parts here are split across PhoneCountryCode/PhoneAreaCode/PhoneNumber.

columns.name: external_links
columns.description: Verbatim ExternalLinks array (social/website profile links). Present only when the org has updated Organisation settings; the normalized surface is xero_organisation_external_links.

columns.name: payment_terms
columns.description: Verbatim PaymentTerms object ({Bills:{Day,Type}, Sales:{Day,Type}}) — the org-level DEFAULT due-date rules. The queryable form is xero_organisation_payment_terms; neither overrides a document's own DueDate.

joins.note: Authorization metadata for this tenant. Equality holds for ORGANISATION-type tenants; PRACTICE connections have no organisation row.
Dimension row for the base currency (ledger_config). Journal-line amounts are always stated in this currency.

examples.question: Which connected organisations are demo companies that must be excluded from reporting?
examples.sql:
SELECT organisation_id, name
FROM xero_organisations
WHERE is_demo_company

examples.question: What fiscal calendar and base currency does each org report in?
examples.sql:
SELECT name, base_currency, financial_year_end_day, financial_year_end_month, sales_tax_basis
FROM xero_organisations
ORDER BY name

tables.grain: one application of overpayment credit to one invoice, keyed by parent overpayment and array position
tables.description: The settlement edge between an overpayment and the invoices it pays down: each row moves a slice of excess-payment credit onto exactly one invoice on a given date. Like prepayment allocations these are cash-free settlements — the money moved when the overpayment happened, so allocation amounts must never join collections metrics. Rows are exploded from the parent's Allocations array, re-land wholesale when the parent changes, and carry no independent watermark.
gotchas: Allocation amount is settlement without cash: adding it to payment-based collections double-counts money that arrived with the original overpayment.
Rows re-land wholesale with the parent (no independent watermark) and removed allocations just disappear. Reconcile by replacing the set per overpayment_id at each sync.
Direction, currency and voiding live on the PARENT: filter xero_overpayments.type and exclude VOIDED parents before summing, and convert with the parent's currency_rate across currencies.

columns.name: overpayment_overpayment_id
columns.description: Parent overpayment whose credit this row consumes. Populated by the ingester from the parent scan context; provenance is the Allocation shape's source-document echo slot, which the API rarely materializes inline.

columns.name: allocation_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position in the parent Overpayment.Allocations array
columns.description: Array position within the parent payload, minted because older payloads omit AllocationID. Stable only within one parent version — the set is replaced whenever the parent re-syncs; never diff ordinals across syncs.

columns.name: allocation_id
columns.description: Xero's allocation identifier when returned (used for allocation deletes upstream). Not the row key because legacy payloads omit it; prefer it for entity resolution when present.

columns.name: invoice_invoice_id
columns.description: The invoice this slice of credit paid down. Customer-side credit lands on ACCREC invoices, supplier-side on ACCPAY bills; direction comes from the parent overpayment's type. Join xero_invoices for what got settled.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Credit applied to the invoice, in the DOCUMENT currency, up to 4dp. Settlement only — the cash event was the original excess payment. Reduces the invoice's AmountDue and the parent's remaining_credit equally.

columns.name: date
columns.description: When the credit was applied — the settlement date for invoices paid by overpayment credit. Distinct from, and often later than, the parent's own date.

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.description: The spec's delete-acknowledgement flag, seen on delete responses. On reads a removed allocation simply vanishes from the parent's array — detect unwound applications by set comparison across syncs, not by this flag.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-response artefact indicating payload status. Ignore for analytics.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation messages retained verbatim; empty on healthy reads.

joins.note: Parent credit document; carries direction (type), currency and status.
The invoice settled by this application.

examples.question: Invoices paid down by overpayment credit, most recent first
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, a.amount, a.date
FROM xero_overpayment_allocations a
JOIN xero_overpayments op ON op.overpayment_overpayment_id = a.overpayment_overpayment_id AND op.status <> 'VOIDED'
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_invoice_id = a.invoice_invoice_id
ORDER BY a.date DESC
LIMIT 50

examples.question: Overpayment credit applied per month this year (customer side)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', a.date) AS month, SUM(a.amount) AS credit_applied
FROM xero_overpayment_allocations a
JOIN xero_overpayments op ON op.overpayment_overpayment_id = a.overpayment_overpayment_id
WHERE op.type IN ('RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT', 'AROVERPAYMENT') AND op.status <> 'VOIDED'
  AND a.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one overpayment credit document per OverpaymentID
tables.description: Credit created when someone paid MORE than was owed (or paid with nothing owed): Xero books the excess as an overpayment against the contact, to be allocated to invoices or refunded later. Like prepayments it is never revenue — the excess is a liability (customer side) or asset (supplier side) until consumed, and the underlying cash already lives in the bank transaction feed. Direction is carried by type (RECEIVE-*/AR* = customer overpaid you, SPEND-* = you overpaid a supplier); remaining_credit and applied_amount are current-state balances restated every sync.
gotchas: An overpayment is not income — it is someone else's money (customer side) or your money parked with a supplier. Treating totals as revenue or spend misstates both P&L and the balance sheet.
VOIDED overpayments keep returning from the API; exclude them everywhere. type mixes customer and supplier directions in one column — filter it in every aggregate.
remaining_credit/applied_amount are current-state balances overwritten each sync. Historical questions must use xero_overpayment_allocations dates and refund payment rows, not this table alone.
The excess cash itself is a bank transaction (banking domain); rows here are the credit ledger. Counting both as cash movement double-counts.

columns.name: overpayment_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the overpayment and the row key; allocations and refund payments point back to it.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Direction of the credit. RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT/AROVERPAYMENT: a customer paid you too much (you owe it back). SPEND-OVERPAYMENT: you overpaid a supplier. Pick a side in every question — netting the two hides both the liability and the asset. Note the spec lists no AP* alias here; supplier-side rows arrive as SPEND-OVERPAYMENT.

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The counterparty who over- or was over-paid, from the embedded Contact stub. Join xero_contacts for names and merge survivorship.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date the overpayment was created — when the excess cash actually moved. Allocation dates on the child table are when the credit was later consumed.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED still carries credit; PAID means fully applied or refunded; VOIDED is cancelled but still returned by the API. Exclude VOIDED from every total or outstanding credit is overstated.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: How amounts inside line_items relate to tax (Exclusive/Inclusive/NoTax). Overpayment lines are typically NoTax because the excess is pure settlement, but do not assume — the header sub_total/total_tax/total are always normalized regardless.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Verbatim ordered line array, auto-generated when the excess was banked. Kept as payload: document totals answer overpayment questions, and the coding here is mechanical (a receivable/payable suspense line), not analyst-facing. Interpret raw LineAmount only with line_amount_types.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Tax-exclusive total of the overpayment in currency_code — always ex-tax regardless of line_amount_types.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Total tax on the overpayment; normally 0.00 because an overpayment is settlement excess, not a taxable supply. Non-zero values deserve investigation before they enter any tax report.

columns.name: total
columns.description: sub_total + total_tax in currency_code: the full size of the credit when created; never changes as credit is consumed. Lifecycle position comes from applied_amount and remaining_credit.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: Document currency for every monetary column on this row. The extracted spec enum truncates mid-alphabet (ends at HRK) — treat the value set as open ISO-4217 (USD, NZD, SGD and others occur constantly); never validate against the enum list. Summing across currencies without converting via currency_rate is meaningless.
columns.enums: AED; AFN; ALL; AMD; ANG; AOA; ARS; AUD; AWG; AZN; BAM; BBD; BDT; BGN; BHD; BIF; BMD; BND; BOB; BRL; BSD; BTN; BWP; BYN; BYR; BZD; CAD; CDF; CHF; CLF; CLP; CNY; COP; CRC; CUC; CUP; CVE; CZK; DJF; DKK; DOP; DZD; EEK; EGP; ERN; ETB; EUR; FJD; FKP; GBP; GEL; GHS; GIP; GMD; GNF; GTQ; GYD; HKD; HNL; HRK

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Rate to the org's base currency at creation; the XE.com day rate when none was specified. Multiply monetary columns by this for base-currency reporting; null means base currency (treat as 1.0). Never SUM a rate.

columns.name: remaining_credit
columns.description: Unapplied credit RIGHT NOW — a balance restated on every sync, not history. SUM across AUTHORISED rows gives today's outstanding overpayment credit; do not trend it over time from this table, and do not expect total - applied_amount to equal it once cash refunds exist.

columns.name: applied_amount
columns.description: Credit consumed against invoices so far, as a current-state figure. Per-invoice, per-date detail lives in xero_overpayment_allocations — use that for any time-based analysis.

columns.name: allocations
columns.description: Verbatim allocation array for payload-level audit. The analytic surface is xero_overpayment_allocations, exploded one row per application — query that, not this.

columns.name: payments
columns.description: Refund-payment stubs returned inline. Canonical refund rows live in xero_payments with overpayment_id set and payment_type AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT/APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT — use that join.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Optional free-text description of the overpayment. Display and matching material only.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when files are attached; the rows come from org_meta's xero_attachments fan-out (rate-budgeted).

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Attachment stubs if included inline (usually absent on list reads). Governed attachment data lives in xero_attachments.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit watermark for incremental sync; moves when allocations or refunds change, which keeps the child table fresh. Not a business date.

columns.name: updated_date_utc_string
columns.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc. Redundant — read the timestamp column.

joins.note: The counterparty the credit sits with.
Applications of this credit to invoices.
Cash refunds of this credit (payment_type AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT/APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT).

examples.question: Outstanding customer overpayment credit by contact
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, SUM(op.remaining_credit) AS credit_outstanding
FROM xero_overpayments op
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_contact_id = op.contact_contact_id
WHERE op.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND op.type IN ('RECEIVE-OVERPAYMENT', 'AROVERPAYMENT')
GROUP BY 1
HAVING SUM(op.remaining_credit) > 0
ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Of overpayments created this year, how much was refunded vs reapplied?
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(op.applied_amount) AS reapplied_to_invoices,
       SUM(op.total - op.applied_amount - op.remaining_credit) AS refunded_or_other
FROM xero_overpayments op
WHERE op.status <> 'VOIDED'
  AND op.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)

tables.grain: one custom online-payment service configuration per PaymentServiceID
tables.description: Org-level configuration of 'Pay Now' services shown on Xero online invoices — the branded URL a customer clicks to pay. Pure reference data: no amounts, no events. It tells you what payment rails the org OFFERS, not what was used; actual receipts are still xero_payments rows regardless of which service collected them, and the service-to-branding-theme assignment that decides which invoices show which button is not exposed on this read surface.
gotchas: This endpoint needs the separately granted 'paymentservices' scope (a limited-availability Xero scope). Zero rows can mean the connection lacks the scope, not that the org offers no payment services — degrade the answer explicitly.

Configuration only: nothing here links a service to the payments it collected, and the branding-theme assignment that decides which invoices show which button is not on this read surface. Never infer per-invoice payment options or per-service revenue from this table.

columns.name: payment_service_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the configured service and the row key.

columns.name: payment_service_name
columns.description: Display name of the service ('Stripe', 'PayPal', a custom gateway). Free text chosen by the org — do not key provider logic off it.

columns.name: payment_service_url
columns.description: The custom payment URL customers are sent to from online invoices, usually templated with invoice placeholders. Configuration, not evidence a payment happened.

columns.name: pay_now_text
columns.description: Label on the Pay Now button in Xero Online Invoicing; defaults to 'Pay by credit card' when unset. Presentation only.

columns.name: payment_service_type
columns.description: Service kind. The spec declares no enum but states API-created services are always CUSTOM; natively integrated gateways configured in the UI may surface other values — treat as open vocabulary.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation messages retained verbatim; empty on healthy reads.

examples.question: What online payment services does the org offer on its invoices?
examples.sql:
SELECT payment_service_name, payment_service_type, pay_now_text, payment_service_url
FROM xero_payment_services
ORDER BY payment_service_name

tables.grain: one payment or refund applied against exactly one invoice, credit note, prepayment or overpayment
tables.description: Cash application evidence: each row records money moving between a bank/clearing account and exactly one receivable or payable document. A payment is not revenue (that is the invoice line) and not cash in the bank (that is the bank transaction feed) — it is the allocation that connects them. Refunds of credit notes, prepayments and overpayments appear here too, as the six *CREDITPAYMENT/*PREPAYMENTPAYMENT/*OVERPAYMENTPAYMENT PaymentType values (no value literally contains 'REFUND'), so 'payments received' must filter both Status and PaymentType or refunds inflate collections. Batched payments also roll up into xero_batch_payments; count cash from exactly one of the two tables.
gotchas: PaymentType mixes directions and refunds in one vocabulary. 'Cash collected from customers' is status = 'AUTHORISED' AND payment_type = 'ACCRECPAYMENT' — every other combination is a different business event.

Amount is in the document's currency. Summing across currencies without converting via currency_rate produces a number in no currency at all; bank_amount is in the bank account's currency and is the bank-side truth.
A DELETED payment un-pays its invoice: the invoice's AmountDue goes back up, but the payment row remains in the API response. Filter status on every aggregate.
Batched cash is represented twice: each member payment here AND one header in xero_batch_payments whose total_amount equals the sum of its members. Aggregate cash from exactly one of the two tables.

The original receipt of a prepayment/overpayment is a bank transaction, not a payment row. Rows with prepayment_id/overpayment_id set are the REFUNDS — adding them to collections cancels cash that genuinely arrived.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable payment identifier and the row key. Stable across edits; deleting a payment flips status to DELETED rather than removing this row from the API.

columns.name: payment_type
columns.description: What kind of application this is. ACCRECPAYMENT is a customer paying an invoice; ACCPAYPAYMENT is you paying a bill; the six *CREDIT/*OVERPAYMENT/*PREPAYMENT types are refunds of credit documents — money moving in the OPPOSITE direction to the ordinary payment on the same AR/AP side. Collections analysis must whitelist ACCRECPAYMENT: including refund types overstates receipts, and including ACCPAYPAYMENT mixes directions.
columns.enums: ACCRECPAYMENT; ACCPAYPAYMENT; ARCREDITPAYMENT; APCREDITPAYMENT; AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT; ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT; APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT; APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED is a live application; DELETED is a reversed one that Xero keeps returning forever. Every cash total must filter status = 'AUTHORISED' — deleted payments otherwise resurrect settled history and un-paid invoices look paid.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The business date the cash applied — the axis for collections, DSO and cash-timing questions. It is user-keyed and can be backdated into closed periods, so 'cash collected in March' can change after March; use updated_date_utc to detect that drift.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The applied amount in the DOCUMENT's currency, up to 4dp. For foreign-currency invoices this is not what left the bank — see bank_amount for the bank-side figure and currency_rate for the conversion actually used. Summing amount across currencies without converting is a number in no currency.

columns.name: bank_amount
columns.description: What actually moved through the bank account, in the BANK account's currency. Equals amount only when document and bank currencies match. Cash-in-bank questions read bank_amount; document-settlement questions read amount — mixing the two misstates FX differences.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Exchange rate captured when the payment was received; populated only for payments against non-base-currency invoices and credit notes. Multiply amount by this to restate in the org's base currency; null means the document is already base currency — treat as 1.0, never drop the row. A rate, so never SUM it.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text remittance description ('Direct Debit', cheque number). Reconciliation matching material — never a join key and never unique.

columns.name: is_reconciled
columns.description: True once the payment is matched to a bank statement line. An unreconciled AUTHORISED payment is a real application whose cash is not yet confirmed by the bank feed — state which basis (book vs bank-confirmed) a cash answer uses.

columns.name: account_account_id
columns.description: The bank or clearing account the cash touched, from the embedded Account stub. Join xero_accounts for code, name and class; do not assume it is a BANK-class account — clearing and current-asset accounts appear here too.

columns.name: code
columns.description: Code of the account used to make the payment, echoed flat beside the Account stub. Not all accounts carry codes — join on account_id, not on this.

columns.name: invoice_invoice_id
columns.description: Set when this payment settles an invoice. The invoice may be a sale (ACCREC) or a bill (ACCPAY) — direction comes from payment_type or Invoice.Type after the join. Exactly one of invoice_id, credit_note_id, prepayment_id, overpayment_id is non-null per row.

columns.name: invoice_number
columns.description: Human-readable number of the settled invoice, denormalized for display. Numbers are org-editable and not guaranteed unique across drafts — join on invoice_id for correctness.

columns.name: credit_note_credit_note_id
columns.description: Set when this row is a CASH REFUND of a credit note (payment_type ARCREDITPAYMENT/APCREDITPAYMENT). The credit note's non-cash applications to invoices live in xero_credit_note_allocations, not here.

columns.name: credit_note_number
columns.description: Display number of the refunded credit note. Same caveat as invoice_number: join on credit_note_id, not the number.

columns.name: prepayment_prepayment_id
columns.description: Set when this row refunds unapplied prepayment credit back to the counterparty (payment_type ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT). The ORIGINAL prepayment cash arrived as a bank transaction, not as a row here — counting both directions as collections cancels real cash.

columns.name: overpayment_overpayment_id
columns.description: Set when this row refunds overpayment credit (payment_type AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT/APOVERPAYMENTPAYMENT). Overpayment credit consumed against invoices is in xero_overpayment_allocations; only the cash-out refund appears here.

columns.name: batch_payment_id
columns.description: Present iff the payment was created inside a batch; groups member payments into the single bank movement on xero_batch_payments. Null for individually entered payments. This is the join key for batch membership.

columns.name: batch_payment
columns.description: Verbatim embedded stub of the parent batch (id, type, status, totals) exactly as the Payments endpoint returned it, kept for payload-level audit only. Query batch attributes through the batch_payment_id join to xero_batch_payments, where they are typed and current — this stub goes stale when the batch is edited.

columns.name: bank_account_number
columns.description: The supplier's bank account number the payment was sent to, captured on batched bill payments. PII/banking data: expose only in remittance workflows, never in analytic rollups.

columns.name: particulars
columns.description: NZ bank-statement 'particulars' reference travelling with the payment instruction. The spec's own description duplicates BankAccountNumber's text (a documented spec quirk); treat it as a bank reference string and keep it PII-shielded because account fragments appear in the wild.

columns.name: details
columns.description: Remittance text that appears on the supplier's bank statement (non-NZ orgs; 18-char limit at write time). Free text for reconciliation, never a key.

columns.name: has_account
columns.description: API-mechanics flag from the write path (the spec ties it to validation problems on the payload). No analytic meaning — never filter business questions on it.

columns.name: has_validation_errors
columns.description: True when the API attached validation messages to this record on a write response. Ingestion diagnostics only.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-response artefact ('OK'/'ERROR'-style) meaningful only on rows echoed back from a create/update call. Ignore for analytics.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Array of API validation messages, populated on error responses and retained verbatim for ingestion debugging. Empty on healthy reads.

columns.name: warnings
columns.description: Array of API warning messages returned with the record, verbatim. Diagnostics only; carries no business signal.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit watermark driving incremental sync; moves when a payment is edited or deleted. Use date for business time — this timestamp is when the RECORD changed, not when cash moved.

columns.name: updated_date_utc_string
columns.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc returned by the API for convenience. Redundant — always read updated_date_utc.

columns.name: invoice
columns.description: Payment.Invoice as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: credit_note
columns.description: Payment.CreditNote as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: prepayment
columns.description: Payment.Prepayment as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: overpayment
columns.description: Payment.Overpayment as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: account
columns.description: Payment.Account as returned by the pinned OpenAPI. Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: Null for payments applied to credit notes/prepayments/overpayments — exactly one of the four target ids is set per row.
Only for cash refunds of credit notes (payment_type ARCREDITPAYMENT/APCREDITPAYMENT).
Only for cash refunds of prepayment credit.
Only for cash refunds of overpayment credit.
The bank or clearing account the cash touched.
Null unless the payment was created inside a batch.

examples.question: Cash collected from customers by month this year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS collected
FROM xero_payments
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED' AND payment_type = 'ACCRECPAYMENT'
  AND date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Which invoices were paid late?
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, i.due_date, p.date AS paid_date, p.date - i.due_date AS days_late
FROM xero_payments p
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_invoice_id = p.invoice_invoice_id
WHERE p.status = 'AUTHORISED' AND p.payment_type = 'ACCRECPAYMENT' AND p.date > i.due_date
ORDER BY days_late DESC

examples.question: How much credit did we refund to customers this year?
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(amount) AS refunded
FROM xero_payments
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND payment_type IN ('ARCREDITPAYMENT', 'AROVERPAYMENTPAYMENT', 'ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT')
  AND date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)

tables.grain: one deduction type pay item per org
tables.description: The catalogue of deduction pay items (DeductionTypes family of GET /PayItems): what can be withheld from employees, and how each behaves against tax, super and W1. ReducesTax marks pre-tax (salary-packaging-style) deductions; DeductionCategory carries the STP classification for union fees and workplace giving. Retired types persist with current_record = false for historical joins.
gotchas: Pre-tax (reduces_tax) and post-tax deductions are different economic events: netting them together hides that pre-tax deductions lowered PAYG. Split on the flag when analysing withholdings.

columns.name: deduction_type_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable deduction pay item identifier; payslip deduction lines reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Admin-chosen label of the deduction (the spec's doc-string wrongly says 'earnings rate'). Display only; behaviour flags below carry the semantics.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: GL account code the withheld money is posted to (typically a liability until remitted). Join xero_accounts on code.

columns.name: reduces_tax
columns.description: True marks a PRE-TAX deduction that shrinks the PAYG base. The flag that separates salary packaging from ordinary after-tax deductions — effective-tax comparisons that ignore it misread packaged employees as under-taxed.

columns.name: reduces_super
columns.description: True when the deduction also reduces the super guarantee base — rare and usually deliberate. If SGC looks low for some employees, check their deductions for this flag before suspecting error.

columns.name: is_exempt_from_w1
columns.description: Whether amounts on this deduction sit outside BAS label W1. Only matters when reconciling payroll to a lodged BAS, and that is exactly when it matters most: a W1 figure built from gross wages without honouring this flag will not tie to what was reported to the ATO.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the pay item and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. Ticks on configuration edits only — it says nothing about when deductions were actually taken.

columns.name: deduction_category
columns.description: STP classification: UNIONFEES and WORKPLACEGIVING are separately reported to the ATO; NONE is everything else. The filter for charitable-giving and union-fee questions.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: Active flag. Filter true for configuration listings; never filter when joining from historical deduction lines.

joins.note: Join on account CODE.

examples.question: Which deduction types are pre-tax?
examples.sql:
SELECT name, deduction_category
FROM xero_payroll_au_deduction_types
WHERE current_record = true AND reduces_tax = true
ORDER BY name

tables.grain: one earnings rate pay item per org
tables.description: The catalogue of earnings pay items (from the EarningsRates family of GET /PayItems): every kind of pay the org can put on a payslip, with its ATO classification. This dimension is what turns anonymous earnings lines into 'ordinary time vs overtime vs allowance vs ETP' — EarningsType is the classification the whole wage analysis hangs on. Retired items remain (current_record = false) so historical payslip lines keep their labels; never inner-filter them away in joins.
gotchas: current_record = false items still own historical payslip lines. LEFT-join and keep them, or past overtime/allowances silently drop out of classified totals.
rate_per_unit, multiplier and amount are configured DEFAULTS; the money actually paid is on the payslip lines. Multiplying this table's rates by timesheet hours reconstructs an estimate, not payroll.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable pay item identifier; earnings lines and timesheet lines reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Admin-chosen label ('Ordinary Hours', 'Sat Overtime'). Display only — classification logic must use earnings_type, since orgs name items inconsistently.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: GL expense account code this pay item posts wages to; join xero_accounts on code to tie payroll to the P&L.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: The unit label ('Hours') for RATEPERUNIT items. Tells you what a line's number_of_units means — summing units across items with different unit types is meaningless.

columns.name: is_exempt_from_tax
columns.description: True when payments on this item escape PAYG withholding. Effective-tax-rate analyses must exclude exempt items from the taxable base.

columns.name: is_exempt_from_super
columns.description: True when this pay does not attract superannuation guarantee. Explains why SGC is less than 'rate x total wages' whenever exempt items (some allowances, overtime) are in the mix.

columns.name: is_reportable_as_w1
columns.description: Whether payments on this item count in BAS label W1 (gross wages reported to the ATO). W1 reconciliation must filter on this — total wages and W1 wages legitimately differ.

columns.name: is_qualifying_earnings
columns.description: Whether this item counts as qualifying earnings for the superannuation guarantee calculation base. The precise SG-base flag, distinct from is_exempt_from_super's blunt exclusion.

columns.name: allowance_contributes_to_annual_leave_rate
columns.description: For RATEPERUNIT allowances only: whether the allowance feeds the annual-leave pay rate. Configuration nuance for leave-cost modelling; null/false elsewhere.

columns.name: allowance_contributes_to_overtime_rate
columns.description: For RATEPERUNIT allowances only: whether this allowance is rolled into the base used to compute overtime rates. When true the allowance's cost is already reflected inside a richer overtime rate on the payslip lines, so adding an 'allowance uplift' on top of overtime spend counts it twice.

columns.name: earnings_type
columns.description: The ATO classification of this pay item and the primary split key for all wage analysis: ordinary time vs overtime vs allowances vs bonuses vs termination payments (ETP/Lump sums) vs paid parental leave vs workers comp. Termination-related types distort averages — exclude them from run-rate wage metrics.
columns.enums: FIXED; ORDINARYTIMEEARNINGS; OVERTIMEEARNINGS; ALLOWANCE; LUMPSUMD; EMPLOYMENTTERMINATIONPAYMENT; LUMPSUMA; LUMPSUMB; BONUSESANDCOMMISSIONS; LUMPSUME; LUMPSUMW; DIRECTORSFEES; PAIDPARENTALLEAVE; WORKERSCOMPENSATION

columns.name: rate_type
columns.description: How the item is valued: FIXEDAMOUNT (see amount), MULTIPLE of the employee's ordinary rate (see multiplier), or RATEPERUNIT (see rate_per_unit). Tells you which default column is meaningful; the actual paid value is on the payslip line.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: DEFAULT rate per unit for RATEPERUNIT items (the spec transmits it as a string; staged numeric). Employees and payslip lines can override it — cost calculations must use the line-level rate, not this default.

columns.name: multiplier
columns.description: For MULTIPLE items, the factor applied to the employee's ordinary rate (1.5 = time-and-a-half). A rate parameter — never summed.

columns.name: accrue_leave
columns.description: For MULTIPLE items: whether hours paid on this item also accrue leave. Explains accrual differences between ordinary and overtime hours.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Optional default amount for FIXEDAMOUNT items. A configured default, not money paid — paid amounts live on payslip earnings lines.

columns.name: employment_termination_payment_type
columns.description: For EMPLOYMENTTERMINATIONPAYMENT items: ATO ETP code O (other) or R (redundancy/invalidity-related). Drives ETP tax treatment; only relevant on termination analysis.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the pay item and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. It ticks when someone edits the item's rate or flags — it says nothing about when anyone was paid on it, so never use it as an activity date for the earnings it classifies.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: True for the org's active pay items; false for retired ones kept for history. Filter true when listing configurable items; do NOT filter when joining from payslip lines, or historical wages lose their classification.

columns.name: allowance_type
columns.description: STP allowance classification (CAR, MEALS, TRAVEL...) for ALLOWANCE items; null otherwise. The ATO reporting split for allowance spend.
columns.enums: CAR; TRANSPORT; LAUNDRY; MEALS; TRAVEL; OTHER; TOOLS; TASKS; QUALIFICATIONS

columns.name: allowance_category
columns.description: STP Phase 2 sub-categorisation of OTHER-type allowances (uniform, private vehicle, home office...). Null for non-allowance items.
columns.enums: NONDEDUCTIBLE; UNIFORM; PRIVATEVEHICLE; HOMEOFFICE; TRANSPORT; GENERAL; OTHER

joins.note: Join on account CODE, not account_id — payroll settings store codes.

examples.question: Which active pay items are super-exempt (explaining an SGC shortfall vs headline wages)?
examples.sql:
SELECT name, earnings_type, is_exempt_from_super, is_reportable_as_w1
FROM xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates
WHERE current_record = true AND is_exempt_from_super = true
ORDER BY earnings_type, name

tables.grain: one net-pay disbursement split per employee per position in the employee's BankAccounts array
tables.description: Standing instructions for where an employee's net pay lands: fixed-amount splits plus exactly one remainder account. This is configuration, not money movement — actual paid amounts are on payslips and in the bank feed. Its analytical use is operational (how many employees split pay, disbursement audit), and it is dense with financial PII.
tables.additivityAxis: time — these rows are the standing instruction as it is right now, overwritten in place with no history kept. amount describes one pay period's fixed split, so it may be totalled across employees but never accumulated across pay periods or successive syncs; what actually moved is on payslips.
gotchas: SUM(amount) is not net pay and not cash paid — the remainder split has no amount, so totals from this table understate disbursement by design. Actual paid amounts live on payslips.
This is current configuration only: it overwrites on change and keeps no history of previous bank accounts.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the employee's bank account array. Order matters operationally: fixed-amount splits are taken in order and the remainder account absorbs what is left.

columns.name: statement_text
columns.description: The narration that appears on the employee's bank statement for the pay credit — employer-chosen text like 'Salary'. Cosmetic; no analytical content.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Name on the destination bank account. Financial PII — restrict to payroll-ops use.

columns.name: bsb
columns.description: Bank-State-Branch routing code of the destination account. Keep as text (leading zeros are significant). Financial PII.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: Destination account number, stored exactly as the bank presents it — variable length with significant leading zeros — hence text, never numeric. Its one legitimate analytical use is duplicate detection: two employees sharing a bsb/account_number pair is a payroll-fraud signal worth surfacing as a flagged count, never as the numbers themselves. Financial PII.

columns.name: remainder
columns.description: True on the split that receives whatever net pay is left after fixed-amount splits. Exactly one row per employee should be true; the remainder row's amount is null/meaningless.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Fixed dollars routed to this split each pay (e.g. $100 to savings). A standing instruction, not a payment: summing it gives neither net pay nor cash out, because the remainder split's variable share is not represented here.

joins.note: Join for status filters; terminated employees keep their disbursement rows.

examples.question: How many active employees split their pay across more than one account?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS employees_with_splits
FROM (
  SELECT b.employee_id
  FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_bank_accounts b
  JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id
  WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE'
  GROUP BY b.employee_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) s

tables.grain: one home address per employee (the employee's single declared HomeAddress)
tables.description: The employee's declared residential address, normalised out of the employee record. Its analytical job is state attribution — payroll tax and long-service-leave rules are state-based — but note it is where the employee lives, which is not necessarily where they work. Entirely PII apart from the state/postcode level of aggregation.
gotchas: This is where the employee lives, not where they work. Using it as 'office location' misattributes remote and cross-border workers; it is the right column for state payroll-tax exposure, not for site analysis.
The Region enum only contains Australian states — an overseas resident either has a null region or a least-wrong state; check country before trusting region.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee and the row key — Xero stores exactly one home address per employee, so this is 1:1 with the parent.

columns.name: address_line1
columns.description: Street address line 1 (required by Xero). Full street addresses are PII — aggregate at region/postal_code for analysis.

columns.name: address_line2
columns.description: Second street line (unit, apartment, building) — null for most single-line addresses, so treat null and empty string as the same when reconstructing a display address. Never filter or group on it; it carries no geographic signal that region/postal_code do not carry better. PII like every street-level field here.

columns.name: city
columns.description: Suburb (Xero labels the field City but for AU addresses it holds the suburb). Free text — expect spelling variants; prefer postal_code for geographic grouping.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Australian state/territory code — the load-bearing column of this table, because payroll tax thresholds and long-service-leave rules differ by state. Null or misleading for employees living overseas (the enum only admits AU states).
columns.enums: ACT; NSW; NT; QLD; SA; TAS; VIC; WA

columns.name: postal_code
columns.description: Postcode. Keep as text — AU postcodes have meaningful leading zeros (e.g. 0800 Darwin).

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country of the home address, free text and often blank for domestic addresses — treat blank as Australia, and a populated non-AU value as the flag that region is unreliable.

joins.note: Always join back for status/employment_type filters — the address table alone includes terminated employees' addresses.

examples.question: Active employees by state
examples.sql:
SELECT a.region AS state, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_home_addresses a
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = a.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND e.employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY employees DESC

tables.grain: one current leave balance per employee per leave type
tables.description: The employee's leave balances as reported by Xero at the moment of the last sync — the 'how much annual leave does everyone have' table. It is a snapshot, not a ledger: each ingest replaces the previous balance, and no history of accrual or consumption survives here (leave movements are on payslip leave lines). Units are whatever the leave type says (hours or days), so cross-type sums are only valid within one unit system.
tables.additivityAxis: time — each sync replaces the balance; summing successive snapshots (or stale copies) double-counts leave
gotchas: This is a current-state snapshot (last_value_over_time): it cannot answer 'leave balance at 30 June' for past dates — historical balances require payslip leave-accrual lines from the processing domain.
Units vary by leave type via type_of_units; summing hours-based and days-based balances together produces a unitless number that will be quoted as hours anyway.
Leave liability in dollars needs three joins: this balance, the employee's ordinary rate (pay template), and the payout flag (template leave line) — balance alone is not a liability.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan); half of the row key.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type this balance belongs to (resolves to PayItems leave types in the payroll config domain); the other half of the row key.

columns.name: leave_name
columns.description: Display name of the leave type, denormalised onto the balance by Xero. It is the only human-readable handle inside this domain, so 'annual leave' questions inevitably pattern-match on it — but it is admin-editable free text, and ILIKE '%annual%' also catches 'Annual Leave Loading' and cashed-out variants, quietly inflating the balance. Key and group on leave_type_id, use this only as a label, and resolve the real leave type through the payroll config domain whenever the number matters.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: The leave available right now, in the leave type's units. Negative values are legitimate (leave taken in advance). This is the number leave-liability estimates start from — multiplied by the employee's rate, and only for leave types that pay out.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: The unit the balance is denominated in, as declared by the leave type (typically Hours). Never aggregate balances across rows with different units — 152 hours plus 5 days is not 157 of anything.

joins.note: Filter status='ACTIVE' — terminated employees' final balances linger and inflate liability.

The template line supplies payout treatment — needed to decide if a balance is a monetary liability. One balance can match several template lines (the template is keyed by array position, not by leave type), so this join fans out and inflates any SUM of number_of_units: use EXISTS or collapse the template side first.

examples.question: Total annual leave hours outstanding for active employees
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(lb.number_of_units) AS annual_leave_hours
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances lb
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = lb.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND e.employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND lb.type_of_units ILIKE 'hours'
  AND lb.leave_name ILIKE '%annual%' AND lb.leave_name NOT ILIKE '%loading%'

examples.question: Employees with more than 4 weeks (152 hours) of annual leave accrued
examples.sql:
SELECT lb.employee_id, lb.number_of_units AS hours_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances lb
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = lb.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND e.employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND lb.type_of_units ILIKE 'hours'
  AND lb.leave_name ILIKE '%annual%' AND lb.leave_name NOT ILIKE '%loading%'
  AND lb.number_of_units > 152
ORDER BY hours_accrued DESC

tables.grain: one super fund membership per SuperMembershipID (an employee's enrolment in one fund)
tables.description: The bridge between employees and superannuation funds: each row is one employee's membership of one fund, with the member number the fund knows them by. Pay-template and payslip super lines reference the membership, not the fund — so fund-level contribution questions route through this table.
gotchas: Employees can hold multiple memberships (old and new funds). 'Which fund is each employee in' needs the membership the active pay-template SGC line points at, not an arbitrary row from this table.

columns.name: super_membership_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this employee-fund enrolment and the row key; what super lines point at.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited from the parent scan). One employee can hold several memberships — e.g. after changing funds — so employee-level rollups must expect >1 row.

columns.name: super_fund_id
columns.description: The destination fund; joins xero_payroll_au_super_funds for name, type (REGULATED vs SMSF) and USI.

columns.name: employee_number
columns.description: The member number the FUND assigned to the employee — not the employer's payroll number. Personal financial identifier; keep out of general answers.

joins.note: Many memberships (across employees) per fund.
Filter parent status for current-workforce fund distribution.

examples.question: Active employees per super fund
examples.sql:
SELECT f.name AS fund, COUNT(DISTINCT m.employee_id) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships m
JOIN xero_payroll_au_super_funds f ON f.super_fund_id = m.super_fund_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = m.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY employees DESC

tables.grain: one tax declaration per employee
tables.description: The employee's TFN declaration and PAYG withholding settings: residency, tax scale, threshold claim, study-loan flags and withholding variations. This drives how much tax each payslip withholds; it is settings, not amounts — actual tax withheld is on payslip tax lines. Contains the Tax File Number, the most sensitive datum in the connector: pii, never to be surfaced.
gotchas: tax_file_number is TFN-Rule-protected data: it may be used for integrity checks but must never appear in query output, even partially masked.

Study-debt analysis on mixed STP1/STP2 data fails, but NOT by double-counting — these are booleans and OR-ing them cannot inflate a count. The real trap is three-valued logic: has_loan_or_student_debt is NULL on records never upgraded to STP2, and the legacy per-loan flags are NULL on records that were, so `WHERE has_help_debt OR has_loan_or_student_debt` silently drops every row whose tested flag is NULL and UNDERCOUNTS. Wrap each flag in COALESCE(flag, false), and read the consolidated flag where the parent employee's is_stp2_qualified is true, the legacy flags where it is false.
These are withholding settings, not amounts: actual tax withheld is on payslip tax lines in the payroll processing domain.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee and row key (1:1 with the parent). The OpenAPI doc-string for this field is a copy-paste error ('Address line 1...'); it is the employee identifier.

columns.name: employment_basis
columns.description: Full-time/part-time/casual basis as declared to the ATO. This is the declared basis for tax, and can drift from reality — FTE analysis should prefer the pay template's ordinary hours; CASUAL here plus leave accruals on payslips is a compliance smell worth surfacing, not hiding.
columns.enums: FULLTIME; PARTTIME; CASUAL; LABOURHIRE; SUPERINCOMESTREAM; NONEMPLOYEE

columns.name: tfn_exemption_type
columns.description: Why no TFN is quoted: NOTQUOTED (top-rate withholding applies), PENDING (28-day grace), PENSIONER, UNDER18. Null when a real TFN exists — so 'employees without a TFN' is tfn_exemption_type IS NOT NULL, not tax_file_number checks.

columns.name: tax_file_number
columns.description: The employee's Tax File Number. Maximum-sensitivity PII with legal handling obligations (TFN Rule) — exists in staging for payroll integrity checks only; never select it into an answer.

columns.name: abn
columns.description: Australian Business Number, populated (and mandatory) only when the employee's income type is NONEMPLOYEE — i.e. this row belongs to a contractor-style payee. A populated ABN is a strong 'not an employee' signal.

columns.name: australian_resident_for_tax_purposes
