columns.description: Tax residency as declared. Tax residency is not citizenship or visa status; pair with residency_status, which carries the three-way STP2 vocabulary.

columns.name: residency_status
columns.description: STP2 residency basis for withholding: AUSTRALIANRESIDENT, FOREIGNRESIDENT (no tax-free threshold, so withholding starts at the first dollar), WORKINGHOLIDAYMAKER (its own concessional ATO schedule, valid only for a registered WHM employer). Drives which tax table applies and is the first field to check for 'why is this person's tax different'. The rates behind each basis are legislated and change by financial year — never hardcode a percentage into a projection from this column.

columns.name: tax_scale_type
columns.description: Which ATO tax scale applies: REGULAR for most; special scales for entertainers, horticulturists/shearers, seniors/pensioners, working holiday makers and foreign residents. Non-REGULAR values explain 'unusual' withholding — check here before flagging a payroll error.
columns.enums: REGULAR; ACTORSARTISTSENTERTAINERS; HORTICULTURISTORSHEARER; SENIORORPENSIONER; WORKINGHOLIDAYMAKER; FOREIGN

columns.name: work_condition
columns.description: Sub-condition for the entertainer tax scale (promotional work, fewer than three performances a week, or none). Only meaningful when tax_scale_type = ACTORSARTISTSENTERTAINERS.

columns.name: senior_marital_status
columns.description: Marital status used by the senior/pensioner tax scale to pick the offset threshold. Only meaningful when tax_scale_type = SENIORORPENSIONER; ignore it elsewhere.

columns.name: tax_free_threshold_claimed
columns.description: Whether the employee claims the tax-free threshold with this employer. An employee can only validly claim it with one employer at a time; false usually means this is a second job, which explains higher withholding.

columns.name: tax_offset_estimated_amount
columns.description: Employee-estimated annual tax offset in whole dollars, used to reduce per-pay withholding. An estimate declared by the employee — not an entitlement and not an amount withheld.

columns.name: has_help_debt
columns.description: Legacy HECS/HELP debt flag from the pre-STP2 declaration. Under STP2 the consolidated has_loan_or_student_debt supersedes the individual loan flags — test the consolidated flag first and fall back to these for older records.

columns.name: has_sfss_debt
columns.description: Legacy Student Financial Supplement Scheme debt flag — a closed loan scheme, so on current data it survives only on long-tenured employees and is a poor proxy for study debt generally. Superseded by has_loan_or_student_debt on STP2-updated records; combining the two is safe only after COALESCE, because a raw NULL makes the whole OR predicate NULL and the row vanishes from the count.

columns.name: has_trade_support_loan_debt
columns.description: Legacy Trade Support Loan flag, likewise folded into has_loan_or_student_debt under STP2.

columns.name: upward_variation_tax_withholding_amount
columns.description: Extra dollars the employee asked to have withheld each pay run, in whole dollars. Additional to scale withholding — explains payslips whose tax looks 'too high'.

columns.name: eligible_to_receive_leave_loading
columns.description: Whether the employee gets leave loading (typically 17.5% on top of annual leave). Affects withholding calculation and leave cost projections — an employee with this true costs more per leave hour than their rate suggests.

columns.name: approved_withholding_variation_percentage
columns.description: ATO-approved downward withholding variation (0-100). When set, scale-based withholding is overridden — the definitive explanation for an employee whose tax percentage looks wrong.

columns.name: has_student_startup_loan
columns.description: Student Start-up Loan flag; one of the loan types consolidated into has_loan_or_student_debt under STP2.

columns.name: has_loan_or_student_debt
columns.description: STP2 consolidated flag: true when the employee has any HELP/HECS, VSL, FS, SSL or TSL debt. The authoritative study-debt indicator on STP2-updated records — use this, not an OR over the legacy flags, or you double-count.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified stamp of the declaration itself. Declarations change rarely; a recent stamp usually marks the STP2 migration touch, not a new TFN declaration.

columns.name: include_leave_loading_in_qualifying_earnings
columns.description: Whether leave loading counts as ordinary-time earnings for Superannuation Guarantee purposes. Changes the SGC base — super-cost projections that ignore it understate liability for leave-loading-eligible staff.

joins.note: Join for status and income_type; a NONEMPLOYEE payee's declaration carries an ABN instead of meaningful scale fields.

examples.question: How many active employees claim the tax-free threshold?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS claiming_threshold
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_tax_declarations t
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND t.tax_free_threshold_claimed = true

examples.question: Active employees on a non-standard tax scale
examples.sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, t.tax_scale_type, t.residency_status
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_tax_declarations t
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND t.tax_scale_type <> 'REGULAR'

tables.grain: one AU payroll employee per EmployeeID
tables.description: The worker dimension for Australian payroll: one row per person (or contractor) the organisation pays through Xero Payroll AU. Every payslip, leave balance, super membership and pay-template line hangs off this spine. Terminated employees are returned forever with Status=TERMINATED, so 'headcount' is a filtered question, never COUNT(*). Payroll is region-exclusive — a tenant runs AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two — so never union this with xero_payroll_uk_employees / xero_payroll_nz_employees; at most one of the three families has rows.
gotchas: Status=TERMINATED employees are returned forever. COUNT(*) is 'everyone ever paid', not headcount — filter status='ACTIVE' for current workforce, or use start/termination dates for as-at-date headcount.
employment_type=CONTRACTOR and income_type IN ('NONEMPLOYEE','LABOURHIRE') rows are payees, not employees. Headcount, tenure and leave questions must exclude them or the numbers inflate.

GET /Employees (list) returns a summary record; the nested families (PayTemplate, OpeningBalances, TaxDeclaration, SuperMemberships, LeaveBalances, BankAccounts) are only complete on the per-employee fetch. Every child table in this domain is filled by that fan-out — one call per employee against the same 60-calls-per-minute, 1k-5k-per-day org budget as the rest of the connector — so on a large or freshly connected org the children lag this root. A missing child row means 'not fetched yet', never 'this employee has none'; check the parent row exists before reporting an absence as zero.

Payroll is region-exclusive: never UNION this with the UK/NZ employee tables; a tenant has at most one region populated, and the field vocabularies (v1 PascalCase here, v2 camelCase there) do not line up.

The record carries exactly one StartDate/TerminationDate pair, so it can represent only one employment episode. A rehired person either has their termination cleared (the earlier episode disappears entirely) or is re-entered under a new EmployeeID (two rows, one human). Turnover rates, average tenure and 'first hired' dates computed from this table alone are therefore wrong in both directions for any org that re-hires — state the limitation rather than quoting the number.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable employee identifier and the row key. Every child table in this domain and every AU payslip carries it.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Legal first name as declared for payroll and STP reporting. Personal data — mask outside HR-scoped analysis.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Family name as reported to the ATO in STP submissions. Xero does not deduplicate humans: a rehired person, or someone who is also an accounting Contact, appears as separate records carrying the same name — so matching people on first_name/last_name across tables manufactures false merges. Join on employee_id. Personal data; mask outside HR-scoped analysis.

columns.name: middle_names
columns.description: Middle name(s), frequently null. Do not use name fields for identity matching across systems — use employee_id.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Salutation (Mr/Ms/Dr...), free text. Presentation only — never a gender or seniority signal.

columns.name: date_of_birth
columns.description: Employee date of birth (required by Xero for tax-scale determination). Sensitive personal data; use only for age-banded workforce analysis with masking.

columns.name: gender
columns.description: Declared gender code: N (not stated), M, F, I (indeterminate/intersex). A four-value administrative code for ATO reporting — treat N as 'unknown', not a category of interest.

columns.name: email
columns.description: Employee's email address (often personal, not corporate). PII; also unreliable as a join key — employees change addresses.

columns.name: phone
columns.description: Landline or primary contact number exactly as the payroll admin typed it — no format normalisation, no country-code convention, and very often a duplicate of mobile. It exists for payroll contact, not analysis: it is not a reliable dedupe key and a populated value is no evidence the number is current. PII.

columns.name: mobile
columns.description: Mobile number, the channel Xero Me payslip notifications use, so it is the contact field most likely to be maintained when phone has gone stale. Still unvalidated free text — a populated mobile is not proof the employee is enrolled in self-service, and counting non-null values as 'digitally onboarded' overstates adoption. PII.

columns.name: twitter_user_name
columns.description: Employee's Twitter handle, a legacy vanity field almost always null. Carried for completeness; no analytical use.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Employment start date — the opening of the employment episode. Tenure = start_date to COALESCE(termination_date, today). Null for some contractor-style records; exclude nulls from tenure math rather than defaulting to an epoch.

columns.name: termination_date
columns.description: The end of the employment episode; null while employed. Headcount-as-at-date questions must test start_date <= d AND (termination_date IS NULL OR termination_date >= d) — filtering only on status gives today's answer for every historical date.

columns.name: termination_reason
columns.description: ATO STP2 cessation code: V voluntary, I ill health, D deceased, R redundancy, F dismissal, C contract cessation, T transfer. Attrition analysis should split V (resignation-like) from employer-initiated R/F — lumping them together hides the story. It is an STP Phase 2 code, so expect it null on employees terminated before the org's STP2 upgrade even though termination_date is set; a null is 'not stated', never 'voluntary'.
columns.enums: V; I; D; R; F; C; T

columns.name: status
columns.description: ACTIVE or TERMINATED. Terminated employees are returned by the API forever — every current-workforce aggregate must filter status = 'ACTIVE' or the answer counts ghosts. For point-in-time headcount use the date columns instead; status only reflects now.

columns.name: job_title
columns.description: Free-text job title. Uncontrolled vocabulary — do not GROUP BY it and present the result as an org structure without normalisation.

columns.name: classification
columns.description: Award/agreement classification (e.g. a modern-award level), free text set by the payroll admin. Useful for award-compliance slicing when populated; often blank.

columns.name: employee_group_name
columns.description: The employee's tracking-option under the org's employee-group tracking category — Xero's mechanism for splitting payroll expense by department/team. This is the join-by-name bridge to xero_payroll_au_settings.tracking_categories and to xero_tracking_options; it is how per-department payroll cost questions resolve. Name, not id — renames break history.

columns.name: is_authorised_to_approve_leave
columns.description: Grant of the Xero Me permission to approve other employees' leave requests. It is an access right, not a reporting line — payroll admins and office managers routinely hold it with no direct reports — so counting approvers as managers inflates the management layer and understates span of control.

columns.name: is_authorised_to_approve_timesheets
columns.description: Grant of the Xero Me permission to approve submitted timesheets. Independent of the leave-approval grant — an employee may hold either, both or neither — so a 'who can approve anything' question must test both flags rather than assuming they are set together, and neither implies a reporting relationship.

columns.name: ordinary_earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate that defines this employee's ordinary hours (the basis for leave accrual and SGC ordinary-time earnings). Resolves against the pay-items earnings rates owned by the payroll config domain.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The pay calendar (weekly/fortnightly/monthly cycle) this employee is paid on. Determines which pay runs can contain their payslips; 'per-period' template amounts mean per this calendar's period.

columns.name: income_type
columns.description: STP2 income stream type. SALARYANDWAGES is a normal employee; WORKINGHOLIDAYMAKER changes tax treatment; NONEMPLOYEE and LABOURHIRE are paid through payroll but are not employees — exclude them from headcount and leave-liability questions; CLOSELYHELDPAYEES are family/director payees with relaxed STP timing.

columns.name: employment_type
columns.description: EMPLOYEE or CONTRACTOR. Contractors flow through payroll for super/ABN reasons but are not employees: any 'employees', 'headcount' or 'leave' question must filter EMPLOYEE (and usually income_type) or it silently counts contractors.

columns.name: country_of_residence
columns.description: Two-letter country of residence carried for STP2 reporting of foreign residents and working holiday makers. Almost always AU, and it changes no withholding by itself — the tax consequence lives in the tax declaration (residency_status/tax_scale_type), so never infer a tax treatment from this column. The value list published in the spec is alphabetically truncated (it stops at DJ), so treat the enums string as illustrative, not as a validation whitelist that would reject real countries.
columns.enums: AF; AX; AL; DZ; AS; AD; AO; AI; AQ; AG; AR; AM; AW; AU; AT; AZ; BS; BH; BD; BB; BY; BE; BZ; BJ; BM; BT; BO; BA; BW; BV; BR; IO; BN; BG; BF; BI; KH; CM; CA; CV; KY; CF; TD; CL; CN; CX; CC; CO; KM; CG; CD; CK; CR; CI; HR; CU; CY; CZ; DK; DJ

columns.name: is_stp2_qualified
columns.description: Whether the employee record has been upgraded for STP Phase 2 compliance. A data-migration flag: false means STP2 fields (income_type, termination_reason codes, disaggregated tax flags) may be missing or stale — it does not mean the employee is unpayable.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Server-side last-modified stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (paired with If-Modified-Since). An audit timestamp — never a proxy for hire, termination or pay events.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation messages echoed on the record, kept verbatim for debugging failed writes. Presentation-only payload; never filter or aggregate on it.

columns.name: home_address
columns.description: Verbatim HomeAddress payload from the per-employee fetch — the source the ingester rebuilds and diffs xero_payroll_au_employee_home_addresses from. Query the normalized address table, not this blob: jsonb ->> extraction returns NULL silently on a key typo, and the state/postcode analysis columns live there. Street-level PII.

columns.name: bank_accounts
columns.description: Verbatim BankAccounts array, preserved because Xero's array order is operationally meaningful: fixed-amount splits are taken in order before the remainder account absorbs what is left, and this blob is the authoritative record of that order behind xero_payroll_au_employee_bank_accounts.line_index. Dense financial PII (BSB, account numbers) — never surface raw.

columns.name: pay_template
columns.description: Verbatim PayTemplate object — all five line families in their original order — from the per-employee fetch; the audit copy the xero_payroll_au_pay_template_* tables are exploded from. Analysis belongs in those tables (they carry the calculation_type branching guidance); this blob exists to preserve line ordering and to reconcile template changes between syncs.

columns.name: opening_balances
columns.description: Verbatim OpeningBalances object — the conversion header plus all six migrated-YTD line arrays — exactly as the per-employee fetch delivered it. The xero_payroll_au_opening_balance* tables are the queryable form; keep this copy for conversion audits, because opening balances change rarely and a diff here pinpoints when a migration correction landed.

columns.name: tax_declaration
columns.description: Verbatim TaxDeclaration payload backing xero_payroll_au_employee_tax_declarations. It contains the Tax File Number in clear text, so treat the entire column as TFN-Rule-protected: never SELECT it into an answer, even for debugging — the normalized table exposes every safe field individually.

columns.name: leave_balances
columns.description: Verbatim LeaveBalances array behind xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances. Snapshot semantics apply to the blob exactly as to the table: it is the balance at last sync, not history — do not mine stale payload copies for a time series; historical balances require payslip leave lines from the processing domain.

columns.name: super_memberships
columns.description: Verbatim SuperMemberships array behind xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships. Carries fund-assigned member numbers (personal financial identifiers) — PII. Use the normalized membership table for joins to funds and super lines; this copy exists for ingest reconciliation.

columns.name: earnings_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_earnings_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: deduction_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_deduction_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: super_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_super_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: reimbursement_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_reimbursement_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: leave_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_pay_template_leave_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Actual pay lives on payslips (payroll processing domain); this table is the who, not the how much.
Tax declaration is fetched per employee; may be absent for never-completed records.
Current leave balances per leave type.
An employee can hold multiple fund memberships over time.

examples.question: Current active employee headcount by employee group
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(employee_group_name, '(no group)') AS employee_group, COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM xero_payroll_au_employees
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND (income_type IS NULL OR income_type NOT IN ('NONEMPLOYEE', 'LABOURHIRE'))
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY headcount DESC

examples.question: Terminations this Australian financial year, by reason
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(termination_reason, '(not stated)') AS termination_reason, COUNT(*) AS terminations
FROM xero_payroll_au_employees
WHERE employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND (income_type IS NULL OR income_type NOT IN ('NONEMPLOYEE', 'LABOURHIRE'))
  AND termination_date >= (CASE WHEN EXTRACT(month FROM CURRENT_DATE) >= 7
       THEN make_date(EXTRACT(year FROM CURRENT_DATE)::int, 7, 1)
       ELSE make_date(EXTRACT(year FROM CURRENT_DATE)::int - 1, 7, 1) END)
  AND termination_date <= CURRENT_DATE
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY terminations DESC

examples.question: Average tenure in years of the current workforce
examples.sql:
SELECT AVG((CURRENT_DATE - start_date) / 365.25) AS avg_tenure_years
FROM xero_payroll_au_employees
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND (income_type IS NULL OR income_type NOT IN ('NONEMPLOYEE', 'LABOURHIRE'))
  AND start_date IS NOT NULL

tables.grain: one leave application per employee per requested leave span
tables.description: Leave requests as employees and admins entered them: one row per application for a span of a leave type, with the payroll processing broken into per-pay-period slices in xero_payroll_au_leave_periods. This is the intent record — whether the leave was actually processed (or rejected) lives on the period statuses, so absence metrics that count applications without checking periods count leave that never happened. Scanned via GET /LeaveApplications/v2, the current revision of the collection; the op exposes no status filter, so requested, scheduled and rejected leave all arrive together and must be separated downstream. A deleted application disappears from the collection outright — there is no cancelled status and no tombstone.
gotchas: The application row has no status; approval state lives on each leave period (SCHEDULED/PROCESSED/REQUESTED/REJECTED). Counting applications as leave taken counts rejected and future leave too.

Rejected leave is not removed: the application survives with its periods marked REJECTED, and nothing on this row says so. Absence, cover and leave-liability numbers read from this table alone count refused requests as time off.
The units of leave are on the periods, not here: date arithmetic on start/end counts weekends and partial days as full leave.

Payroll is region-exclusive — a tenant runs AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two. Zero AU leave rows on a UK/NZ org is the correct answer 'no AU payroll', not a sync failure, and the regions must never be unioned into one absence metric.

columns.name: leave_application_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the application and the row key (the spec doc-string mislabels it as an employee id).

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee taking the leave; join xero_payroll_au_employees. The grouping key for absence-per-person analysis.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: What kind of leave this is; join xero_payroll_au_leave_types for the LeaveCategoryCode (annual vs personal/sick vs long-service...) and paid/unpaid flag. Absence analyses that skip the join conflate paid holidays with unpaid or statutory leave.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Free-text title of the request. Marked PII because employees routinely type health and family details here — mask in shared outputs.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First calendar day of the requested span. Calendar days, not working days: (end_date - start_date) overstates leave consumed — use the periods' NumberOfUnits for actual units.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last calendar day of the requested span (inclusive). Overlap tests against a window need the usual start <= window_end AND end >= window_start pattern.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text reason for the leave. PII for the same reason as title — medical and personal circumstances live here; never surface it in aggregates.

columns.name: pay_out_type
columns.description: DEFAULT is leave taken as absence; CASHED_OUT converts balance to money with the employee still at work. Absence and headcount-coverage analyses must exclude CASHED_OUT applications.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark for leave. It moves when the request is approved, rejected or edited, so it is a processing timestamp, not a lodgement date — the record carries no 'applied on' field, and using this as one dates old leave to whenever it was last touched.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on every read. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful copy of the record, and a non-null value here means a write was replayed, not that the business record is invalid.

joins.note: Employee identity and attributes.
Leave category, units and paid/unpaid flags.
The quantified, statused slices — where 'how much leave' answers actually live.

examples.question: Employees on leave during the last week of December 2025
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT la.employee_id
FROM xero_payroll_au_leave_applications la
JOIN xero_payroll_au_leave_periods lp ON lp.leave_application_id = la.leave_application_id
WHERE la.pay_out_type = 'DEFAULT'
  AND lp.leave_period_status IN ('SCHEDULED', 'PROCESSED')
  AND la.start_date <= '2025-12-31' AND la.end_date >= '2025-12-25'

examples.question: Leave applications by leave category and month of leave start (the record carries no lodgement date)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', la.start_date) AS month, lt.leave_category_code, COUNT(*) AS applications
FROM xero_payroll_au_leave_applications la
JOIN xero_payroll_au_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = la.leave_type_id
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

tables.grain: one leave period per leave application per pay period it spans
tables.description: The payroll slicing of a leave application: Xero splits each request into one row per pay period it touches, each carrying the units of leave falling in that period and a processing status. This is where leave becomes quantified and real — PROCESSED rows have hit a posted payslip, SCHEDULED are approved future slices, REQUESTED await approval, REJECTED never happened. Every 'leave taken' number is a filtered SUM over this table.
gotchas: Summing number_of_units without a status filter counts rejected and not-yet-approved leave as taken. State the status set explicitly in every query.
Units follow the leave type's unit of measure — summing across leave types mixes hours with days for orgs that track differently. Group by or convert via xero_payroll_au_leave_types.type_of_units.
A single application fans out across many periods: joining applications to periods and then counting applications without DISTINCT multiplies the count by period fan-out.

columns.name: leave_application_id
columns.description: Parent application key, inherited on explode; the path to employee, leave type and pay-out type.

columns.name: leave_periods
columns.description: Zero-based position of this period in the application's LeavePeriods array; periods have no id of their own. Periods are also uniquely addressed by their pay-period dates within an application, but the ordinal is the stable key.

columns.name: leave_periods_pay_period_start_date
columns.description: Start of the pay period this slice of leave falls into — aligns with a pay run's period dates, which is how leave joins back to the run that paid it.

columns.name: leave_periods_pay_period_end_date
columns.description: End of the pay period for this slice. The natural time axis for leave trend analysis, since it is when the leave hits payroll.

columns.name: leave_periods_number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave (in the leave type's TypeOfUnits, usually hours) consumed in this pay period. The additive leave measure — but only after filtering leave_period_status, or requested and rejected leave pollutes the total.

columns.name: leave_periods_leave_period_status
columns.description: Lifecycle of this slice: REQUESTED (awaiting approval), SCHEDULED (approved, future), PROCESSED (paid on a posted run), REJECTED (never happened). 'Leave taken to date' = PROCESSED only; 'committed leave' = PROCESSED + SCHEDULED; REJECTED must always be excluded.

joins.note: Employee, leave type and CASHED_OUT flag live on the parent.

Date-based bridge to the run that processed the slice. Period end dates repeat across calendars, so on the date alone this fans out many-to-many — additionally constrain to the employee's calendar via the run's payroll_calendar_id to make it effectively many-to-one.

examples.question: Leave hours actually taken per employee per quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT la.employee_id, date_trunc('quarter', lp.leave_periods_pay_period_end_date) AS quarter,
       SUM(lp.leave_periods_number_of_units) AS leave_units_taken
FROM xero_payroll_au_leave_periods lp
JOIN xero_payroll_au_leave_applications la ON la.leave_application_id = lp.leave_application_id
WHERE lp.leave_periods_leave_period_status = 'PROCESSED' AND la.pay_out_type = 'DEFAULT'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Approved future leave scheduled over the next 90 days
examples.sql:
SELECT la.employee_id, SUM(lp.leave_periods_number_of_units) AS scheduled_units
FROM xero_payroll_au_leave_periods lp
JOIN xero_payroll_au_leave_applications la ON la.leave_application_id = lp.leave_application_id
WHERE lp.leave_periods_leave_period_status = 'SCHEDULED'
  AND lp.leave_periods_pay_period_end_date <= CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '90 days'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one leave type pay item per org
tables.description: The catalogue of leave types (LeaveTypes family of GET /PayItems): each org-defined leave entitlement with its accrual quantum, unit of measure, statutory category and pay behaviour. LeaveCategoryCode is the cross-org normalizer — org-specific names like 'RDO bank' map onto statutory categories (ANNUALLEAVE, PERSONALSICKCARERSLEAVE, LONGSERVICELEAVE...). Joined from leave applications and payslip leave-accrual lines.
gotchas: Org-specific names hide statutory meaning: two orgs' 'Personal Leave' and 'Sick Leave' are the same PERSONALSICKCARERSLEAVE category. Always aggregate on leave_category_code, not name.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable leave type identifier; applications and accrual lines reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Admin-chosen label (the spec's doc-string wrongly says 'earnings rate'). Display only — categorize via leave_category_code.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: The unit leave is tracked in (usually Hours). Governs what every NumberOfUnits on periods and accrual lines means — mixing types with different units in one SUM is a unit error.

columns.name: normal_entitlement
columns.description: Units a full-time employee is entitled to per year (e.g. 152 hours annual leave). A policy parameter for expected-accrual modelling; actual accruals are on the payslip accrual lines.

columns.name: leave_loading_rate
columns.description: Extra percentage paid on top of ordinary earnings when this leave is taken (typically 17.5 for loaded annual leave). Explains why leave pay exceeds base rate x units; null/zero when no loading applies.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the leave type and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. An entitlement or loading edit refreshes it — not evidence any leave was accrued or taken.

columns.name: is_paid_leave
columns.description: Whether taking this leave generates pay. Unpaid leave types produce absence without wages — absence cost models must branch on this.

columns.name: show_on_payslip
columns.description: Whether this leave type's balance is printed on employee payslips. A presentation setting with no bearing on accrual or entitlement — a false here means employees cannot see the balance, not that the type stopped accruing, so never read it as 'inactive'.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: Active flag. Filter true for configuration listings; keep false rows joinable from historical leave.

columns.name: leave_category_code
columns.description: Statutory classification (STP Phase 2) of the leave type — the canonical split for absence analysis and the only safe way to compare leave across orgs whose custom names differ.
columns.enums: ANNUALLEAVE; LONGSERVICELEAVE; PERSONALSICKCARERSLEAVE; ROSTEREDDAYOFF; TIMEOFFINLIEU; COMPASSIONATEANDBEREAVEMENTLEAVE; STUDYLEAVE; FAMILYANDDOMESTICVIOLENCELEAVE; SPECIALPAIDLEAVE; COMMUNITYSERVICELEAVE; JURYDUTYLEAVE; DEFENCERESERVELEAVE

columns.name: sgc_exempt
columns.description: True when pay for this leave is exempt from the superannuation guarantee. Another contributor to SGC-vs-wages gaps.

columns.name: is_qualifying_earnings
columns.description: Whether pay for this leave counts inside the superannuation-guarantee earnings base. It is the precise counterpart to the blunt sgc_exempt flag and the two can disagree, so an 'SGC vs wages' ratio computed without checking both is the usual reason a perfectly correct super figure looks like an underpayment.

joins.note: Applications reference the type; category and units flow from here.

examples.question: Active leave types with their annual entitlement and loading
examples.sql:
SELECT name, leave_category_code, normal_entitlement, type_of_units, leave_loading_rate, is_paid_leave
FROM xero_payroll_au_leave_types
WHERE current_record = true
ORDER BY leave_category_code

tables.grain: one migrated YTD deduction amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.DeductionLines array
tables.description: Year-to-date deduction totals migrated at conversion, one row per deduction type. Amount is the meaningful field in this context; the shared DeductionLine shape's other fields are carried but typically null. Conversion-year only.
gotchas: Conversion-year only: include in YTD deduction totals solely for the payroll year containing the opening balance date.

Only deduction_type_id and amount are meaningful here — calculation_type/percentage/number_of_units are shape carry-overs from the shared DeductionLine object and are typically null; branching on them as if this were a pay template misclassifies migrated amounts.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance deduction array; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: deduction_type_id
columns.description: The deduction pay item the migrated YTD amount sits under — the axis conversion-year reconciliation matches on: pair it with the same DeductionTypeID on Xero payslip deduction lines, or the year's total silently splits across two rows for one deduction.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: YTD dollars deducted in the prior system as at the opening balance date. Conversion-year only.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: Inherited from the shared DeductionLine shape. A migrated deduction is a completed total, so no calculation basis is recorded and this is normally null. Critically, a stray PRETAX/POSTTAX value here does NOT tell you the tax treatment of the migrated dollars — the pre-tax/post-tax split of pre-conversion deductions is not carried across, so do not use this column to adjust migrated taxable income.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Percentage slot on the shared shape. Migrated deductions arrive as dollar totals, so this is null even for employees whose current deduction is percentage-based — its emptiness says nothing about how the deduction was configured before conversion.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Unit slot on the shared shape, unused for migrated totals. Null here means 'not recorded at migration', not zero units — never coalesce it to 0 and multiply.

joins.note: The header carries the as-at date.

examples.question: Migrated YTD deductions per employee
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, SUM(amount) AS migrated_ytd_deductions
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_deduction_lines
GROUP BY 1

examples.question: Migrated deductions by type with their conversion as-at date
examples.sql:
SELECT dl.deduction_type_id, ob.opening_balance_date, SUM(dl.amount) AS migrated_amount
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_deduction_lines dl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_opening_balances ob ON ob.employee_id = dl.employee_id
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY migrated_amount DESC

tables.grain: one migrated YTD earnings amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.EarningsLines array
tables.description: Year-to-date earnings brought over from the previous payroll system at conversion, one row per earnings rate. In this context Xero populates the rate id and the YTD amount; the other EarningsLine fields are carried for shape-fidelity but are typically null. These amounts predate every Xero payslip — they are the missing left-hand side of conversion-year YTD reconciliations.
gotchas: These amounts are additive only within the conversion payroll year: 'total earnings FY24' must include them if (and only if) the opening balance date falls in FY24.
Opening balances only exist for migrated employees — their absence is normal, not missing data.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance earnings array; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate the migrated YTD amount belongs to — reconciliation must match it to the same rate on Xero payslips.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: YTD dollars earned under this rate in the prior system as at the opening balance date. Belongs only to the conversion payroll year — adding it to later years fabricates earnings.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: Inherited from the shared EarningsLine shape. An opening balance records money the previous system already calculated, so there is no live calculation basis and this is normally null; where a migration tool did populate it, it describes how the OLD system derived the figure, never how Xero will pay this employee. Branching on it as if this were a pay template misreads settled history as a standing instruction.

columns.name: annual_salary
columns.description: The shared shape carries an annual-salary slot, but an opening balance states what was already paid, not a forward rate, so expect null. Even when populated it is the salary in force at conversion — historical context only; the current salary is on the pay-template earnings line.

columns.name: number_of_units_per_week
columns.description: Contracted weekly units on the shared shape. Opening balances migrate dollar totals, not work schedules, so this is effectively always null — do not try to reconstruct pre-conversion FTE or hours from it.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Per-unit rate slot on the shared shape. Migrated YTD figures arrive as totals with no rate decomposition, so this is null; an implied historical rate would need units this table does not carry, and inventing one from amount alone is guesswork.

columns.name: normal_number_of_units
columns.description: Ordinary-units basis used by MULTIPLE-type rates on the shared shape; meaningless for a settled total and null in practice. Its emptiness is not evidence that no overtime or penalty rates were paid before conversion.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Unit count from the shared shape. Opening balances migrate dollars, never hours, so hours-worked questions about the pre-conversion period cannot be answered from this domain at all — say the data does not exist rather than returning null as zero hours.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: The FIXEDAMOUNT-rate slot on the shared shape; null for migrated balances, because every migrated dollar lands in amount regardless of how the previous system classified it. Never add it to amount hoping for a fuller total — you would be adding an empty column to a complete one.

joins.note: The header carries the as-at date that scopes these amounts.

examples.question: Migrated YTD gross earnings per employee at conversion
examples.sql:
SELECT ol.employee_id, SUM(ol.amount) AS migrated_ytd_earnings
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_earnings_lines ol
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY migrated_ytd_earnings DESC

examples.question: Migrated earnings scoped to their conversion as-at date
examples.sql:
SELECT ob.opening_balance_date, ol.employee_id, ol.earnings_rate_id, ol.amount
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_earnings_lines ol
JOIN xero_payroll_au_opening_balances ob ON ob.employee_id = ol.employee_id
ORDER BY ob.opening_balance_date, ol.employee_id

tables.grain: one migrated leave-balance amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.LeaveLines array
tables.description: Leave balances carried over from the previous system at conversion: leave type plus units. These seed the running balances that xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances now reports — they are the historical starting point, not the current balance.
tables.additivityAxis: the conversion instant — unlike its money-valued sibling tables this is a leave STOCK frozen at the header's opening_balance_date, not a flow. It totals across employees within one leave type, but it must never be added to current balances (xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances already has this seed baked in) nor to post-conversion accruals, and units differ by leave type so cross-type sums are invalid as well.
gotchas: This is the balance at conversion, frozen forever. Reporting it as current leave balance understates or overstates everyone hired or accruing since migration.

This table has no unit column: number_of_units is denominated in whatever the leave type declares (hours vs days). Summing across leave types without resolving type_of_units via the leave type (or the matching leave_balances row) adds hours to days.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance leave array; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type whose balance was carried over — the join to the matching xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances row and to the leave type's unit declaration in the payroll config domain. Without resolving it, number_of_units has no unit.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave (hours or days per the leave type) held at conversion. A historical seed value — for today's balance use xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances, never this.

joins.note: Seed balance vs current balance for the same employee and leave type. Many-to-one, not one-to-one: this table is keyed by array position, so a leave type appearing twice in the migrated array matches the single balance row twice and silently duplicates it. Collapse this side to one row per (employee_id, leave_type_id) before subtracting or summing.
The header carries the opening_balance_date these seed balances are frozen at — without it the units have no as-at date.

examples.question: Total leave units carried into Xero at conversion, by leave type
examples.sql:
SELECT leave_type_id, SUM(number_of_units) AS migrated_units
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_leave_lines
GROUP BY 1

examples.question: Leave accrued since conversion (current balance minus migrated seed)
examples.sql:
SELECT lb.employee_id, lb.leave_name,
       lb.number_of_units - ob.number_of_units AS units_accrued_since_conversion
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_leave_lines ob
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances lb
  ON lb.employee_id = ob.employee_id AND lb.leave_type_id = ob.leave_type_id
ORDER BY units_accrued_since_conversion DESC

tables.grain: one migrated YTD paid-leave earnings amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.PaidLeaveEarningsLines array
tables.description: STP2 disaggregation of migrated YTD earnings: leave actually paid in the prior system, split by leave type, with the leave-loading portions split by Super Guarantee treatment. Exists so conversion-year STP reporting can categorise paid leave correctly; only present on STP2-migrated employees.
gotchas: amount is a categorisation of earnings already counted in the migrated earnings lines — never add the two tables together for 'total migrated pay'.

Rows exist only for STP2-migrated employees, and the leave-loading split columns only for annual-leave-category types — absence means 'not disaggregated', not 'no leave paid pre-conversion'; check the parent employee's is_stp2_qualified before reading empty as zero.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the paid-leave earnings array; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type under which the migrated paid-leave dollars are categorised for STP2. The loading-split columns only populate when this resolves to an annual-leave-category type in the payroll config domain — check the category before reading their nulls as zero loading.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: YTD dollars of this leave type paid in the prior system. Already contained within the migrated earnings totals for STP purposes — adding it on top of opening-balance earnings lines double-counts leave pay.

columns.name: sgc_applied_leave_loading_amount
columns.description: Migrated leave loading that WAS subject to Super Guarantee, only for annual-leave-category types. Splitting loading by SGC treatment is what makes conversion-year super reconciliation possible.

columns.name: sgc_exempted_leave_loading_amount
columns.description: Migrated leave loading exempt from Super Guarantee, only for annual-leave-category types. Its presence explains why migrated super is lower than a flat SGC-rate estimate over gross.

columns.name: reset_stp_categorisation
columns.description: Write-side control flag to reset STP categorisation for the leave type (annual-leave categories only). Ingested for fidelity; carries no analytical signal.

joins.note: The header carries the as-at date.

examples.question: Migrated paid-leave dollars by leave type
examples.sql:
SELECT leave_type_id, SUM(amount) AS migrated_paid_leave
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_paid_leave_lines
GROUP BY 1

examples.question: Migrated leave loading split by Super Guarantee treatment
examples.sql:
SELECT leave_type_id,
       SUM(sgc_applied_leave_loading_amount) AS loading_subject_to_sgc,
       SUM(sgc_exempted_leave_loading_amount) AS loading_exempt_from_sgc
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_paid_leave_lines
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY loading_subject_to_sgc DESC NULLS LAST

tables.grain: one migrated YTD reimbursement amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.ReimbursementLines array
tables.description: Year-to-date reimbursements migrated at conversion, one row per reimbursement type. Reimbursements are outside gross wages, so these rarely matter beyond completeness of conversion-year payment summaries.
gotchas: Reimbursements are tax-free repayments, not remuneration; including them in migrated gross-earnings reconciliation overstates wages.

Conversion-year only, like every opening-balance table: these amounts belong solely to the payroll year containing the header's opening_balance_date, and absence of rows means the employee simply had no migrated reimbursements — not missing data.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance reimbursement array; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: reimbursement_type_id
columns.description: The reimbursement pay item the migrated YTD amount belongs to; resolve against the payroll config domain's reimbursement types for the name, and match on this id (not the free-text description) when reconciling against payslip reimbursement lines.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: YTD dollars reimbursed in the prior system as at the opening balance date. Not wages — keep out of gross-pay reconciliations.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text narration inherited from the shared shape, usually null because migration tools carry totals per reimbursement type without the original wording. Reconcile against payslip reimbursement lines on reimbursement_type_id — matching on this text loses every row where the narration was dropped or reworded at conversion.

columns.name: expense_account
columns.description: Expense-code slot on the shared shape. Migrated reimbursements were already expensed in the previous system, so nothing posts to a Xero account and this is null — pre-conversion reimbursement spend cannot be attributed to a GL account from this table, and a report that groups by it will show everything under one empty bucket.

joins.note: The header carries the as-at date.

examples.question: Employees with migrated reimbursement history
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT employee_id
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_reimbursement_lines
WHERE amount IS NOT NULL AND amount <> 0

examples.question: Migrated YTD reimbursements per employee with conversion date
examples.sql:
SELECT rl.employee_id, ob.opening_balance_date, SUM(rl.amount) AS migrated_reimbursements
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_reimbursement_lines rl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_opening_balances ob ON ob.employee_id = rl.employee_id
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY migrated_reimbursements DESC

tables.grain: one migrated YTD superannuation amount per employee per position in the employee's OpeningBalances.SuperLines array
tables.description: Year-to-date super contributions migrated at conversion, one row per membership/contribution type. Amount and contribution_type are the meaningful fields; remaining shared SuperLine fields are carried but typically null. Conversion-year only.
gotchas: Conversion-year only: add these to payslip super lines solely for the financial year containing the header's opening_balance_date. Carrying them into a later year inflates that year's super by an entire pre-conversion history that was never accrued in Xero.

contribution_type still matters on migrated data: SGC and SALARYSACRIFICE both count toward the employee's concessional cap, but only SGC-plus-EMPLOYERADDITIONAL is employer expense — collapsing the types turns a cap-reconciliation number into a cost number (or vice versa).

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the opening-balance super array; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: super_membership_id
columns.description: Which of the employee's fund memberships received the migrated contributions — the join through xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships to the fund. Can be null on old conversions; treat null as 'fund unknown at migration', not as a broken join.

columns.name: contribution_type
columns.description: Which contribution stream the YTD amount belongs to — SGC vs salary sacrifice vs voluntary matters for concessional-cap reconciliation.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: YTD super dollars accrued in the prior system as at the opening balance date. Conversion-year only.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: Inherited from the shared SuperLine shape. The migrated figure is a settled contribution total, so no basis is recorded and this is normally null; the basis actually in force (STATUTORY / PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS / FIXEDAMOUNT) lives on the pay-template super line, and reading it from here would describe the previous system, not Xero.

columns.name: minimum_monthly_earnings
columns.description: Earnings-floor slot on the shared shape, irrelevant once a contribution has been made and null here. Do not read a null as proof no earnings threshold was applied before conversion — the migrated amount is the only evidence of what was actually contributed.

columns.name: expense_account_code
columns.description: GL expense-code slot on the shared shape. Migrated balances raise no Xero journal — they are opening figures, not postings — so this is null, and pre-conversion super expense cannot be split by account or department from this table.

columns.name: liability_account_code
columns.description: GL liability-code slot on the shared shape, null for the same reason as expense_account_code. Any super owed at conversion sits in the org's opening balance sheet, not against a code recorded here, so do not reconcile the super payable account to this table.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Contribution-percentage slot on the shared shape; null for migrated totals. Dividing amount by migrated earnings yields an average across the whole pre-conversion period, not the rate in force at any point — do not present it as the employee's super rate.

joins.note: The header carries the as-at date.

examples.question: Migrated YTD super by contribution type
examples.sql:
SELECT contribution_type, SUM(amount) AS migrated_ytd_super
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_super_lines
GROUP BY 1

examples.question: Per-employee migrated super with its conversion as-at date
examples.sql:
SELECT sl.employee_id, ob.opening_balance_date, SUM(sl.amount) AS migrated_super
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balance_super_lines sl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_opening_balances ob ON ob.employee_id = sl.employee_id
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY migrated_super DESC

tables.grain: one opening-balance header per employee
tables.description: Conversion-time header for an employee migrated into Xero mid-payroll-year: the as-at date and the year-to-date PAYG tax brought across. The per-category YTD amounts live in the opening-balance line tables. These rows exist only for employees who were migrated with history; their absence means the employee's Xero payslips are the complete record. It is not pure reference data: tax is the migrated PAYG measure, additive across employees inside the conversion year and meaningless outside it.
gotchas: Opening balances belong to exactly one payroll year — the Australian financial year containing opening_balance_date. Include them in that year's YTD and omit them from every other: folding them into a later year inflates it by an entire pre-conversion history that was never paid in Xero, and leaving them out of the conversion year understates it by the same amount.
tax is a string in the source; casting failures ('' or non-numeric) should be treated as 'no migrated tax', not zero-with-confidence.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee and row key (at most one opening-balance set per employee).

columns.name: opening_balance_date
columns.description: The as-at date of the migrated YTD figures — the boundary between 'paid in the old system' and 'paid in Xero'. YTD reconstructions for the conversion year must add opening balances to Xero payslips only up to this year, and never for later years.

columns.name: tax
columns.description: YTD PAYG tax withheld in the old system at conversion. The API delivers it as a string — cast to numeric before arithmetic, and expect blanks rather than zeros for employees without migrated tax.

joins.note: Only employees migrated mid-year have a row here.

examples.question: Which employees were migrated into Xero with prior-system YTD balances?
examples.sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, ob.opening_balance_date,
       CASE WHEN ob.tax ~ '^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$' THEN ob.tax::numeric END AS migrated_ytd_tax
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balances ob
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = ob.employee_id
ORDER BY ob.opening_balance_date

examples.question: Total PAYG tax carried in from the previous payroll system, by conversion date
examples.sql:
SELECT ob.opening_balance_date,
       COUNT(*) AS employees_migrated,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ob.tax ~ '^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$' THEN ob.tax::numeric END) AS migrated_ytd_payg
FROM xero_payroll_au_opening_balances ob
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one pay run, keyed by PayRunID — one processing of one payroll calendar over one pay period
tables.description: The header of every AU payroll processing event: each row is one run of one payroll calendar over one period, carrying org-level totals (Wages, Deductions, Tax, Super, Reimbursement, NetPay) that Xero computes by summing the run's payslips. DRAFT runs are visible work-in-progress that will change or vanish; only POSTED runs are payroll that actually happened. The embedded payslip roster (PayslipSummary array) is exploded to xero_payroll_au_payslips via the per-payslip fan-out and also kept verbatim here as payslip_summaries. All amounts are AUD — AU payroll has no multi-currency dimension. Deletion is a disappearance rather than a tombstone: PayRunStatus carries only DRAFT and POSTED, so a run deleted in Xero simply stops being returned.
gotchas: DRAFT runs are returned alongside POSTED ones and their totals still move. Every payroll cost, PAYG, super or headcount figure must filter pay_run_status = 'POSTED', or in-flight drafts book provisional, still-changing totals as real payroll. (A run posts in place under the same PayRunID, so the failure mode is inclusion of unfinished numbers, not duplication.)
Header Wages/Deductions/Tax/Super/Reimbursement/NetPay are already the sum of the run's payslips, which are in turn sums of their line families. Summing two grains in one query double-counts.
PaymentDate (cash) and the period dates (accrual) can land in different months. 'Payroll paid in July' and 'payroll cost of July' are different questions — pick the axis deliberately.

NetPay is not employer cost. Employer cost is wages plus the employer-funded share of super (SGC and EMPLOYERADDITIONAL); tax and deductions are withheld out of wages, and adding them to wages counts them twice.
Payroll is region-exclusive: an org has AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two. Empty AU tables on a UK/NZ tenant mean 'no AU payroll', not 'sync failure' — never union across regions.

A deleted run leaves no trace: PayRunStatus has no VOIDED or DELETED value, so a run removed in Xero stops being returned and an incremental UpdatedDateUTC sync can never observe its removal. Until a full identity scan reconciles disappearances, a deleted draft keeps answering questions from staging.

columns.name: pay_run_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable pay run identifier and the row key; the parent key for every payslip in the run.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The payroll calendar this run was generated from (the spec's doc-string mislabels it 'pay run'). It determines the run's frequency — join xero_payroll_au_payroll_calendars for WEEKLY/MONTHLY etc. Comparing costs across calendars of different frequencies without normalizing to a common period is a classic wrong answer.

columns.name: pay_run_period_start_date
columns.description: First day of the period the employees are being paid FOR. Use with the end date for accrual-style period attribution; not the day money moved.

columns.name: pay_run_period_end_date
columns.description: Last day of the period worked. The natural axis for 'payroll cost of period X' questions; a run's payment can land in a later calendar month than its period.

columns.name: pay_run_status
columns.description: DRAFT is an unposted work-in-progress whose totals still move; POSTED is committed payroll. Every cost, tax, super or headcount figure must filter POSTED — a draft's totals are provisional and may never post at those numbers, so including them books payroll that has not happened.

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: The day employees are actually paid. Cash-timing questions (PAYG remitted, wages paid in month X) group by this; period-cost questions use the period dates. The two conventions split a run across months whenever payment falls after period end.

columns.name: payslip_message
columns.description: Free-text note printed on every payslip in the run. Presentation only; never a filter for analysis.

columns.name: wages
columns.description: Total gross wages for the run — the sum of its payslips' Wages, which already includes ordinary, leave and timesheet earnings. Do not add payslip or earnings-line sums on top of this; pick one grain.

columns.name: deductions
columns.description: Total employee deductions withheld in the run, stored as a positive magnitude that is subtracted from gross on the way to net pay. It is money withheld from employees, not an extra employer cost.

columns.name: tax
columns.description: Total PAYG withholding for the run, a positive magnitude withheld from employees and owed to the ATO. It is part of gross wages, not a cost on top of them.

columns.name: super
columns.description: Total superannuation for the run across all contribution types. Employer-funded SGC is a cost ON TOP of wages, but this total also folds in salary-sacrifice and employee contributions that came out of gross — for a clean employer-cost split use xero_payroll_au_payslip_superannuation_lines filtered by contribution_type.

columns.name: reimbursement
columns.description: Total expense reimbursements paid through payroll. Not wages, not taxed, not super-bearing — exclude from remuneration analyses but include in cash-out.

columns.name: net_pay
columns.description: What actually lands in employees' bank accounts: wages minus deductions, PAYG tax and employee-funded super (salary-sacrifice and member contributions, which sit on the superannuation lines rather than in Deductions), plus reimbursements. It is NOT the employer's payroll cost (that is wages plus employer super) — mixing the two understates cost by the withholdings.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Xero's last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark. A run edited after posting refreshes this — not evidence of a new pay event.

columns.name: payslips
columns.description: The run's embedded per-employee summary roster, kept verbatim in the order the API returns it. Retained because it arrives atomically with the run (the full payslip table needs one fan-out call per payslip, which can lag) and because EmployeeGroup exists nowhere else in the payload. Prefer xero_payroll_au_payslips for analysis; this is the audit copy and the ingester's linkage record.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on reads. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful record.

joins.note: Gives the run its frequency (WEEKLY, MONTHLY...). Normalize before comparing costs across calendars.
Header totals already sum the payslips — after this join, aggregate one side only.

examples.question: Gross wages, super and net pay by month this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(wages) AS gross_wages,
       SUM(super) AS super,
       SUM(net_pay) AS net_paid
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_runs
WHERE pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: PAYG withheld per quarter (cash timing, for BAS reconciliation)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', payment_date) AS quarter, SUM(tax) AS payg_withheld
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_runs
WHERE pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one standing deduction instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.DeductionLines array
tables.description: Recurring deductions configured on the employee's pay template — union fees, child support, salary-packaging and the like — with their calculation basis. Template configuration only: the money actually deducted each pay is on payslip deduction lines. PRETAX vs POSTTAX matters: pre-tax deductions reduce taxable income, post-tax do not.
tables.additivityAxis: time — a standing instruction snapshot, overwritten on change. amount totals across employees to a per-period deduction bill but must never be accumulated across pay periods; percentage is a rate and is never summed at all. Amounts actually deducted are payslip deduction lines.
gotchas: Template deductions are standing instructions — actual deducted amounts (and one-off deductions added in a pay run) are only on payslip deduction lines.
amount and percentage are mutually exclusive by calculation_type; averaging or summing across both populates a metric from two different unit systems.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the template's deduction lines; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: deduction_type_id
columns.description: The deduction pay item applied. The type (in the payroll config domain) carries the name and whether it reduces super or W1 — this line only carries the employee-specific quantum.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: FIXEDAMOUNT uses amount; PRETAX/POSTTAX are percentage-based and use percentage. Branch on this before reading the numerics — and remember PRETAX shrinks taxable income while POSTTAX does not, which changes any net-pay modelling.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Fixed deduction per pay period, populated for FIXEDAMOUNT lines. Per-period money — annualise via the employee's payroll calendar before comparing across employees.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Percentage of earnings deducted, for PRETAX/POSTTAX lines. A rate: never summed, and meaningless without the earnings base on the eventual payslip.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units for unit-based deduction setups; rarely populated on templates. Treat null as 'not unit-based', not zero.

joins.note: Filter parent status for current-workforce questions.

examples.question: Active employees with a recurring post-tax deduction
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT e.employee_id
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_deduction_lines d
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = d.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND d.calculation_type = 'POSTTAX'

examples.question: Total fixed deductions per pay period by deduction type (active employees)
examples.sql:
SELECT d.deduction_type_id, COUNT(DISTINCT d.employee_id) AS employees, SUM(d.amount) AS per_period_total
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_deduction_lines d
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = d.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND d.calculation_type = 'FIXEDAMOUNT'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY per_period_total DESC

tables.grain: one standing earnings instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.EarningsLines array
tables.description: The employee's recurring earnings setup: which earnings rates apply and how they are calculated (annual salary, entered rate, or the rate's own default). This is the template copied onto each new payslip — expected pay, not actual pay. Actual earnings are payslip earnings lines in the payroll processing domain; use this table for salary-book, FTE and pay-structure questions, not for cost incurred.
tables.additivityAxis: time — the template is current state, overwritten whenever pay is restructured, with no history retained. annual_salary and the per-period amounts sum legitimately ACROSS employees (that is the salary book) but must never be accumulated across pay periods or successive syncs; what was actually paid each period is on payslip earnings lines.
gotchas: This is the template, not the payslip: expected pay, before any pay-run edits, unpaid leave or one-off changes. 'What did we pay' must come from payslip earnings lines, never from here.
The numeric columns are calculation_type-dependent: summing amount, fixed_amount and annual_salary together mixes per-period and per-year money and produces a number with no meaning.
Per-period columns are per the employee's payroll calendar; normalise via the calendar (weekly vs monthly) before comparing employees or annualising.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the pay template's earnings lines; with employee_id it forms the row key because one earnings rate can appear on multiple lines.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate (pay item) this line applies — ordinary hours, overtime, allowances. Resolves against the payroll config domain's earnings rates; the rate, not this line, carries the name and STP category.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: Decides which numeric columns on this row are authoritative: ANNUALSALARY uses annual_salary + number_of_units_per_week; ENTEREARNINGSRATE uses rate_per_unit x number_of_units; USEEARNINGSRATE takes the rate's own default. Reading the wrong column for the type yields nulls or nonsense — always branch on this first.

columns.name: annual_salary
columns.description: Annual salary in AUD, populated only when calculation_type = ANNUALSALARY. The salary-book column: SUM over active employees' ANNUALSALARY lines is the org's committed base salary bill (excluding super and on-costs).

columns.name: number_of_units_per_week
columns.description: Contracted units (hours) per week for salaried lines — the numerator for FTE (divide by the org's full-time week, commonly 38). Null on rate-based lines.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Dollar rate per unit for ENTEREARNINGSRATE lines — an hourly rate, never a total. Never SUM this column; multiply by units first.

columns.name: normal_number_of_units
columns.description: Base ordinary units used when the earnings rate is a multiple of another rate (RateType MULTIPLE, e.g. overtime at 1.5x). Only meaningful for those rates.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Per-period template amount where the line is expressed as a flat amount. Per pay period of the employee's calendar — comparing employees on different calendars without normalising to annual mixes weekly against monthly numbers.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Template units per pay period for rate-based lines (hours per period, not per week). Pairs with rate_per_unit or the rate's default rate.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Per-period amount used only when the underlying earnings rate's RateType is FIXEDAMOUNT (e.g. a flat allowance). Distinct from amount; check both when hunting a template's flat components.

joins.note: Always filter the parent to status='ACTIVE' for salary-book questions — templates of terminated employees persist.

examples.question: Total committed annual base salary of active employees
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(l.annual_salary) AS annual_salary_book
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = l.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND e.employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND (e.income_type IS NULL OR e.income_type NOT IN ('NONEMPLOYEE', 'LABOURHIRE'))
  AND l.calculation_type = 'ANNUALSALARY'

examples.question: Approximate FTE by employee group (38-hour week)
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(e.employee_group_name, '(no group)') AS employee_group,
       ROUND(SUM(l.number_of_units_per_week) / 38.0, 2) AS fte
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = l.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND e.employment_type = 'EMPLOYEE'
  AND (e.income_type IS NULL OR e.income_type NOT IN ('NONEMPLOYEE', 'LABOURHIRE'))
  AND l.calculation_type = 'ANNUALSALARY'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY fte DESC

tables.grain: one standing leave-accrual instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.LeaveLines array
tables.description: How each leave type accrues for this employee: the calculation method, annual entitlement units, termination payout treatment and whether the accrual counts as qualifying earnings for super guarantee. This is entitlement configuration — accrued balances live in xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances and leave actually taken is on payslip leave lines.
tables.additivityAxis: time — current accrual configuration, overwritten when entitlements change. annual_number_of_units is a per-year entitlement and number_of_units a per-period accrual rate, so neither may be accumulated over time; the running balance those rules produce lives in xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances.
gotchas: Leave liability questions need entitlement (here), balance (leave_balances) and payout treatment (entitlement_final_pay_payout_type) together — balances for NOTPAIDOUT leave types are not a financial liability.
annual_number_of_units is per year while number_of_units is per pay period; adding or comparing them without the calendar produces absurd entitlements.

Joining this table to leave balances on (employee_id, leave_type_id) is not the 1:1 match it looks like — the row key here is array position, so one leave type configured on two template lines duplicates the balance row and doubles any liability total. Use EXISTS (as the example below does) or collapse this side first.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the template's leave lines; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type accruing (annual, personal, long service...). Names and unit types live on the leave types in the payroll config domain; this id is also the join to the employee's balance rows.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: How the accrual is computed: BASEDONORDINARYEARNINGS accrues proportionally to hours worked; FIXEDAMOUNTEACHPERIOD adds a constant; ENTERRATEINPAYTEMPLATE uses this line's units; NOCALCULATIONREQUIRED means no automatic accrual (e.g. unpaid leave). Determines which unit columns below mean anything.

columns.name: entitlement_final_pay_payout_type
columns.description: Whether the accrued balance pays out on termination (PAIDOUT) or lapses (NOTPAIDOUT). The switch that decides if this leave type belongs in the leave-liability provision — NOTPAIDOUT balances are an operational fact, not a monetary liability.

columns.name: employment_termination_payment_type
columns.description: ETP classification if the payout forms an Employment Termination Payment: O (other/ordinary) or R (redundancy-related, concessionally taxed). Only meaningful when the payout routes through an ETP.

columns.name: include_superannuation_guarantee_contribution
columns.description: Whether pay for this leave attracts super guarantee contributions (the spec doc-string 'amount of leave line' is wrong — this is a boolean SGC switch). Affects the super cost of every hour of this leave taken.

columns.name: is_qualifying_earnings
columns.description: Whether this leave line counts as qualifying (ordinary-time) earnings for superannuation guarantee calculations. Together with the SGC flag it decides the super base — misreading either understates SGC liability.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Per-period accrual units when the calculation type takes units from this template line. Units are hours or days per the leave type — check before aggregating.

columns.name: annual_number_of_units
columns.description: Hours of leave accrued per year — the annual entitlement (152 = 4 weeks at 38h). The right column for 'how much leave does each person earn per year'.

columns.name: full_time_number_of_units_per_period
columns.description: Full-time-equivalent ordinary units per period used to pro-rata BASEDONORDINARYEARNINGS accruals for part-timers. A scaling basis, not an accrual amount.

joins.note: Entitlement config vs current balance for the same employee and leave type. This table is keyed by (employee_id, line_index) and NOT by leave type, so nothing prevents a leave type appearing on two template lines; when it does the balance row is duplicated and any SUM(number_of_units) over the join doubles. Use EXISTS, or reduce this side to one line per (employee_id, leave_type_id), before aggregating balances.
Filter parent status; terminated employees keep template rows.

examples.question: Annual leave entitlement (hours per year) for active employees
examples.sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, ll.annual_number_of_units AS annual_leave_hours
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_leave_lines ll
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = ll.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND ll.annual_number_of_units IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY annual_leave_hours DESC

examples.question: Which leave balances are a real monetary liability (pay out on termination)?
examples.sql:
SELECT lb.employee_id, lb.leave_name, lb.type_of_units, lb.number_of_units
FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_leave_balances lb
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = lb.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_leave_lines ll
    WHERE ll.employee_id = lb.employee_id
      AND ll.leave_type_id = lb.leave_type_id
      AND ll.entitlement_final_pay_payout_type = 'PAIDOUT'
  )
ORDER BY lb.number_of_units DESC

tables.grain: one standing reimbursement instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.ReimbursementLines array
tables.description: Recurring reimbursements on the employee's pay template (e.g. a fixed phone allowance repaid through payroll). Reimbursements are not earnings: they are tax-free repayments of employee outlay and are excluded from gross wages, PAYG and super. Template only — actual reimbursed amounts are on payslip reimbursement lines.
tables.additivityAxis: time — the standing reimbursement instruction as it is now, with no history. amount is per pay period: total it across employees for a per-period figure, but reaching an annual number requires multiplying through the employee's payroll calendar, never summing rows over time.
