gotchas: Reimbursements are excluded from gross wages, tax and super — any 'total pay' figure that includes them overstates remuneration; any expense analysis that ignores them understates cost recovery through payroll.

Template rows persist after termination and amount is per the employee's pay calendar: 'recurring reimbursement spend' must filter the parent to status='ACTIVE' and normalise per-period amounts through the calendar before annualising, or it counts departed staff and mixes weekly with monthly money.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the template's reimbursement lines; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: reimbursement_type_id
columns.description: The reimbursement pay item applied; the type (payroll config domain) names it and fixes its default expense account.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Recurring reimbursement per pay period. Not wages: exclude from any gross-pay, PAYG or super base calculation, or those bases inflate.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text line description (max 50 chars) shown on the payslip. Display only.

columns.name: expense_account
columns.description: Expense account code the reimbursement posts against (visible as a code once a pay run posts). Joins xero_accounts on code for P&L attribution.

joins.note: Filter parent status for current-workforce questions.

examples.question: Active employees with recurring reimbursements and their per-period amounts
examples.sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, r.description, r.amount
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_reimbursement_lines r
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = r.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE'
ORDER BY r.amount DESC

examples.question: Per-period recurring reimbursements by destination expense account
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(r.expense_account, '(type default)') AS expense_account, SUM(r.amount) AS per_period_total
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_reimbursement_lines r
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = r.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY per_period_total DESC

tables.grain: one standing superannuation instruction per employee per position in the employee's PayTemplate.SuperLines array
tables.description: Recurring super contributions configured per employee: the statutory SGC line plus any salary-sacrifice, employer-additional or employee-voluntary lines, each pointing at a super membership and the GL accounts it posts to. Configuration, not contributions — amounts actually accrued each pay are on payslip super lines. The contribution_type split is the compliance axis: SGC is the employer's legal obligation; SALARYSACRIFICE reduces the employee's taxable income.
tables.additivityAxis: time — the contribution setup as it stands now, overwritten on change. amount describes one pay period's fixed contribution and may be totalled across employees but never across periods; percentage and minimum_monthly_earnings are rates/thresholds and are never summed at all. Accrued super is on payslip super lines.
gotchas: STATUTORY lines have no percentage in the data — the SGC rate is legislated per financial year. Projecting super cost from this table requires supplying the current rate externally; actual accrued super is on payslip super lines.
SALARYSACRIFICE is part of the employee's package, not an extra employer cost; counting it alongside SGC as 'employer super expense' overstates on-costs.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee (inherited key from the parent scan).

columns.name: line_index
columns.description: Ordinal within the template's super lines; forms the key with employee_id.

columns.name: super_membership_id
columns.description: Which of the employee's fund memberships this contribution pays into — the join to xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships and from there to the fund. Null on STATUTORY lines created before a membership was set.

columns.name: contribution_type
columns.description: SGC is the compulsory employer guarantee; SALARYSACRIFICE is employee pre-tax money (reduces their taxable income and counts toward their concessional cap); EMPLOYERADDITIONAL is employer money above SGC; EMPLOYEE is post-tax voluntary. Employer super EXPENSE above salary is SGC + EMPLOYERADDITIONAL only — SALARYSACRIFICE and EMPLOYEE are the employee's own money that the employer merely remits, so folding them into 'employer super cost' overstates on-costs.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: STATUTORY applies the legislated SGC rate to ordinary-time earnings; PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS uses percentage; FIXEDAMOUNT uses amount. STATUTORY lines carry no rate here — the rate is legislated and changes by financial year, so do not hardcode it in projections.

columns.name: minimum_monthly_earnings
columns.description: Monthly earnings floor below which this super line does not apply — a legacy of the (since-abolished) $450/month SGC threshold. Non-zero values on current data are stale config worth flagging, not applying.

columns.name: expense_account_code
columns.description: GL account code the super expense posts to (joins xero_accounts on code, not id). Where payroll meets the P&L — super cost by department resolves through this account plus tracking.

columns.name: liability_account_code
columns.description: GL account code for the accrued super payable until remitted to the fund. The balance on this account is super owed, not super cost.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Contribution percentage for PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS lines. A rate — never summed; null on STATUTORY and FIXEDAMOUNT lines.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Fixed contribution per pay period for FIXEDAMOUNT lines. Per-period money on the employee's calendar; annualise before comparing.

joins.note: Resolves to the destination fund via the membership.

Code-based join (payroll stores codes, not AccountIDs); codes are org-editable, so joins can dangle after a chart-of-accounts recode. liability_account_code joins the same way for the accrued-super side.
Every question below filters the parent — terminated employees keep their super template lines, so an unfiltered count of SGC arrangements includes people who left.

examples.question: Active employees with voluntary super arrangements beyond the statutory guarantee
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT e.employee_id, s.contribution_type
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_super_lines s
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = s.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND s.contribution_type <> 'SGC'

examples.question: Salary-sacrifice super arrangements for active employees, with their basis
examples.sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, s.calculation_type,
       s.percentage AS pct_of_earnings, s.amount AS fixed_per_period
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_template_super_lines s
JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = s.employee_id
WHERE e.status = 'ACTIVE' AND s.contribution_type = 'SALARYSACRIFICE'
ORDER BY e.employee_id

tables.grain: one pay schedule, keyed by PayrollCalendarID — an org can define several calendars of the same frequency, so calendar_type is not a key
tables.description: The org's pay schedules: each row defines a frequency (WEEKLY, FORTNIGHTLY, MONTHLY...) that pay runs are generated from and employees are assigned to. Small reference set. StartDate and PaymentDate describe the UPCOMING period and roll forward every time a run posts — they are 'next period' pointers, not history; historical periods live on the pay runs themselves.
gotchas: start_date/payment_date are rolling 'next period' values that mutate after every posted run — snapshotting or grouping history by them attributes all past payroll to the upcoming period.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable calendar identifier; pay runs and employees reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Admin-chosen label ('Weekly Wages', 'Monthly Salaries'). Display only — frequency logic must use calendar_type, names lie.

columns.name: calendar_type
columns.description: The pay frequency. The normalization key for comparing costs across calendars: a WEEKLY calendar posts ~4.33 runs per month, so per-run comparisons across types are meaningless without annualizing.
columns.enums: WEEKLY; FORTNIGHTLY; FOURWEEKLY; MONTHLY; TWICEMONTHLY; QUARTERLY

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Start of the UPCOMING (next unposted) pay period — a rolling pointer, not the calendar's creation date and not history. Never use it to date past payroll.

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: When the upcoming period will be paid; rolls forward like start_date. Useful for 'when is the next pay day', useless for history.

columns.name: reference_date
columns.description: The anchor date from which the period sequence was originally generated. Fixed at setup; explains period boundary alignment.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified stamp; ticks every time the rolling dates advance, so expect it to churn with each posted run.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on every read. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful copy of the record, and a non-null value here means a write was replayed, not that the business record is invalid.

joins.note: All history lives on the runs; the calendar only knows the next period.

examples.question: Which pay calendars exist and when is each next pay day?
examples.sql:
SELECT name, calendar_type, start_date AS next_period_start, payment_date AS next_pay_day
FROM xero_payroll_au_payroll_calendars
ORDER BY payment_date

tables.grain: one deduction line per payslip per position in the payslip's DeductionLines array
tables.description: Employee-side deductions withheld on a payslip (union fees, workplace giving, purchase plans...), exploded from Payslip.DeductionLines. Amounts are positive magnitudes subtracted from gross on the way to net pay — money the employer holds and remits elsewhere, never an employer cost. Join xero_payroll_au_deduction_types for the deduction's name and its pre-tax/W1 treatment.
gotchas: Deductions are employee money in transit, not employer expense. Adding them to wages when computing payroll cost double-counts, because they are already inside gross wages.
Pre-tax deductions (deduction type ReducesTax = true) shrink the PAYG base: comparing tax across employees without accounting for salary-packaging deductions misreads effective tax rates.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip the deduction was withheld on, inherited on explode. It repeats across the payslip's deduction lines, and the two things every deduction total needs — the employee and the run's POSTED status — are both reached through it (payslip -> run), so no aggregate here is trustworthy until that two-hop join is made.

columns.name: deduction_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's DeductionLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: deduction_type_id
columns.description: Which deduction pay item this is; join xero_payroll_au_deduction_types for name, ReducesTax and category. Without the join, 'deductions by kind' is unanswerable — the line carries no label.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: Whether the line was computed as a fixed amount or as a percentage of earnings. It governs whether amount or percentage is the configured driver — amount is always the resulting dollars, so measures should read amount whatever this says. The spec publishes no value list here: discover the values present in the tenant rather than hard-coding literals.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Dollars withheld on this line, positive. Subtract from gross — never add to employer cost, and never sign-flip twice when reconciling to net pay.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: The configured percentage for percentage-calculated lines (null for fixed). A parameter, not a measure — averaging or summing it is meaningless.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units behind a unit-priced deduction — rare, since most deductions are a flat dollar figure or a percentage — and null otherwise. These are not hours worked and must never feed a labour-hours measure; amount is the only money on the line.

joins.note: Then to the run for the POSTED filter.
Name, DeductionCategory and pre-tax flags. Keep historical (current_record = false) types joinable.

examples.question: Total withheld by deduction type this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT dt.name AS deduction, SUM(dl.amount) AS withheld
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_deduction_lines dl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_deduction_types dt ON dt.deduction_type_id = dl.deduction_type_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = dl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Employees with workplace-giving deductions last quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT p.employee_id
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_deduction_lines dl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_deduction_types dt ON dt.deduction_type_id = dl.deduction_type_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = dl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND dt.deduction_category = 'WORKPLACEGIVING'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '3 months'
  AND r.payment_date < date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)

tables.grain: one earnings line per payslip per position in the payslip's EarningsLines array
tables.description: The wage detail of a payslip: one row per earnings rate applied (ordinary time, overtime, allowances, bonuses...), exploded from Payslip.EarningsLines. This is the table for 'overtime spend', 'allowance cost by type' or hourly-vs-salary splits — join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates for the rate's EarningsType classification. Salaried employees typically show a single ANNUALSALARY-calculated line; hourly staff show units x rate. Timesheet-generated and leave-generated earnings live in sibling tables, so this table alone understates gross wages.
gotchas: This table is only one of three wage sources on a payslip — LeaveEarningsLines and TimesheetEarningsLines are siblings. 'Gross wages' from this table alone undercounts anyone who took leave or is timesheet-paid; use payslip.wages for the total.

The dollar value lives in different columns depending on how the line was calculated: fixed lines carry amount, rate lines are rate_per_unit x number_of_units, and salary-calculated lines carry neither. Their period value is NOT annual_salary and cannot be reconstructed here without the calendar's periods-per-year, so SUM(amount) is not gross earnings and no expression over annual_salary is either — for a salaried population take wages from xero_payroll_au_payslips.
annual_salary repeats the full yearly salary on every payslip; any aggregate over it must take MAX/AVG per employee, never SUM.
Lines under DRAFT runs are provisional — always propagate the POSTED filter down through the payslip -> run join.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited on explode. Run status and pay dates are two joins away (payslip -> run).

columns.name: earnings_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's EarningsLines array, minted at explode time to preserve presentation order; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Which pay item produced this line. Join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates for EarningsType (ORDINARYTIMEEARNINGS vs OVERTIMEEARNINGS vs ALLOWANCE...) — the line itself does not say what kind of earnings it is.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: How the line's amount was computed — from the employee's standard rate, a rate typed onto the payslip, or an annual salary. It decides which of annual_salary / rate_per_unit x number_of_units / amount is the operative value, so reading the wrong one yields nulls or nonsense. The spec publishes no value list for this field: discover the values present in the tenant instead of hard-coding literals into a filter.

columns.name: annual_salary
columns.description: The annual salary standing behind a salary-calculated line — a yearly rate of pay stamped onto a per-period row, never the money paid this period. SUM across payslips multiplies one salary by the number of runs; even AVG is only meaningful after collapsing to one row per employee. To turn it into a period cost you would need the calendar's periods-per-year, which is exactly the guess that produces wrong numbers — read the paid figure from xero_payroll_au_payslips.wages instead.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: The per-unit (usually hourly) rate actually applied on this line. A rate, not an amount — never SUM it; the line's cost is rate x units.

columns.name: normal_number_of_units
columns.description: The employee's standard units for the period (their normal hours), as opposed to the units actually paid. Compare with number_of_units to spot over/under-standard periods; do not use it as hours worked.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units (typically hours) paid on this line. The correct 'hours paid' measure at payslip grain; for hours as entered day-by-day use the timesheet tables instead.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The line's dollar value where the calculation is a fixed amount rather than rate x units. For fixed and rate-based lines the cost is COALESCE(amount, rate_per_unit * number_of_units); salary-calculated lines can populate neither, and dividing annual_salary by a guessed pay frequency is how analysts invent numbers — take the salaried portion from xero_payroll_au_payslips.wages instead. SUM(amount) on its own silently drops every rate-based and salaried line.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_au_pay_runs for the POSTED filter and pay dates.
Classifies the line (EarningsType, allowance type, W1/tax/super exemptions). Do not filter the rate table's current_record here or historical lines lose their labels.

examples.question: Overtime cost by month this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(COALESCE(el.amount, el.rate_per_unit * el.number_of_units)) AS overtime_cost
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_earnings_lines el
JOIN xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates er ON er.earnings_rate_id = el.earnings_rate_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = el.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
  AND er.earnings_type = 'OVERTIMEEARNINGS'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Allowances paid by allowance type, last quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT er.allowance_type, SUM(COALESCE(el.amount, el.rate_per_unit * el.number_of_units)) AS allowances_paid
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_earnings_lines el
JOIN xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates er ON er.earnings_rate_id = el.earnings_rate_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = el.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND er.earnings_type = 'ALLOWANCE'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '3 months'
  AND r.payment_date < date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one leave accrual line per payslip per position in the payslip's LeaveAccrualLines array
tables.description: Leave EARNED in the period: each row records units of a leave type accrued on one payslip, exploded from Payslip.LeaveAccrualLines. This is the flow side of leave — accruals in, leave-earnings out — not a balance. Xero does not expose a per-payslip leave balance here; balances live on the employee record in the payroll employees domain, and summing accruals alone reconstructs only the credit side.
gotchas: Accrual is not balance and not leave taken. Leave taken lives in leave-earnings lines and PROCESSED leave periods; balances live on the employee record. Summing this table answers only 'how much leave was EARNED'.
Units are in the leave type's TypeOfUnits (usually hours). Mixing leave types that accrue in different units into one SUM produces a number in no unit at all.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip that granted this accrual, inherited on explode. One payslip accrues several leave types, so the column repeats; it is also the only thing that dates the accrual, because the line carries no period of its own — 'leave accrued in Q3' is a filter on the run behind this payslip, never on anything in this table.

columns.name: leave_accrual_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's LeaveAccrualLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: leave_accrual_lines_leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type being accrued; join xero_payroll_au_leave_types for name and LeaveCategoryCode (annual vs personal vs long service...). Accrual analysis without the join lumps incompatible entitlements together.

columns.name: leave_accrual_lines_number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave accrued on this payslip — a per-period increment, NOT the employee's balance. Sum over POSTED runs for leave earned in a window; treating any single value as a balance is wrong by construction.

columns.name: leave_accrual_lines_auto_calculate
columns.description: True when Xero computed the accrual from the leave type's entitlement settings; false when it was manually entered on the payslip. Manual overrides are where accrual anomalies hide — segment on this before declaring an entitlement misconfigured.

joins.note: Then to the run for the POSTED filter and period attribution.
Leave category, units-of-measure and paid/unpaid flags.

examples.question: Annual leave hours accrued per employee this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, SUM(lal.leave_accrual_lines_number_of_units) AS annual_leave_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_leave_accrual_lines lal
JOIN xero_payroll_au_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_accrual_lines_leave_type_id = lal.leave_accrual_lines_leave_type_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = lal.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
  AND lt.leave_category_code = 'ANNUALLEAVE'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Manually overridden leave accruals in the last quarter (entitlement misconfiguration hunt)
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, lt.name AS leave_type, SUM(lal.leave_accrual_lines_number_of_units) AS units_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_leave_accrual_lines lal
JOIN xero_payroll_au_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_accrual_lines_leave_type_id = lal.leave_accrual_lines_leave_type_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = lal.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND lal.leave_accrual_lines_auto_calculate = false
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '3 months'
  AND r.payment_date < date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC

tables.grain: one leave earnings line per payslip per position in the payslip's LeaveEarningsLines array
tables.description: Wages paid for leave taken (or cashed out) in the period, exploded from Payslip.LeaveEarningsLines. Each row prices leave units at an earnings rate; PayOutType distinguishes leave actually taken from balances cashed out, which behave differently for leave-liability and for headline 'time off' questions. These amounts are already inside the payslip's Wages total.
gotchas: This table does not name the leave TYPE (annual vs sick...) — it prices leave at an earnings rate. Leave-type splits come from xero_payroll_au_leave_applications/xero_payroll_au_payslip_leave_accrual_lines, not from here.
CASHED_OUT lines pay money without absence: counting them as time off overstates absence, and excluding them from wage cost understates payroll. Split on pay_out_type explicitly.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip whose leave pay this line prices, inherited on explode. Many rows share it, so a payslip measure (wages, net_pay) joined against this table is repeated once per leave line — collapse to one row per payslip before mixing the two grains. It is also the only route to the pay period, since the line itself carries no date.

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's LeaveEarningsLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines_earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate the leave was paid at. Join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates; note leave paid at a loading-inflated rate still points at the base rate item.

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines_rate_per_unit
columns.description: The rate this leave was priced at on the payslip. A rate, not money — never SUM it; the line's value is rate_per_unit * number_of_units. Do not assume it already carries the leave type's LeaveLoadingRate: whether loading is folded into this rate or paid as its own earnings line is an org configuration choice, so reconcile leave cost against the payslip's Wages rather than asserting either.

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines_number_of_units
columns.description: Leave units (typically hours) paid on this line. Summing across POSTED runs gives leave hours PAID — which is leave consumed only for DEFAULT rows, not CASHED_OUT ones.

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines_pay_out_type
columns.description: DEFAULT is leave taken as time off; CASHED_OUT converts balance to money with no absence. 'Days off taken' must exclude CASHED_OUT; 'leave balance drawdown' includes both. Ignoring this flag inflates absence metrics at every cash-out event.

joins.note: Then to the run for POSTED status and pay dates.
Rate metadata; the leave type itself is on the accrual lines / leave application, not here.

examples.question: Cost of leave paid per month, split leave taken vs cashed out
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       lel.leave_earnings_lines_pay_out_type,
       SUM(lel.leave_earnings_lines_rate_per_unit * lel.leave_earnings_lines_number_of_units) AS leave_pay
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_leave_earnings_lines lel
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = lel.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Leave hours actually paid as time off per employee this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, SUM(lel.leave_earnings_lines_number_of_units) AS leave_hours_paid
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_leave_earnings_lines lel
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = lel.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND lel.leave_earnings_lines_pay_out_type = 'DEFAULT'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one reimbursement line per payslip per position in the payslip's ReimbursementLines array
tables.description: Expense money returned to employees through payroll, exploded from Payslip.ReimbursementLines. Reimbursements ride the payslip but are not remuneration: no PAYG, no super, excluded from W1. They belong in cash-out and expense analyses, never in wage-cost or average-pay figures.
gotchas: Reimbursements are inside NetPay but outside Wages: including them in average-salary or per-hour cost metrics inflates pay; excluding them from 'cash paid to employees' understates the bank movement.
Payroll reimbursements can double up with the same expense claimed through Xero expense claims/bills — reconcile by expense account before adding payroll reimbursements to total T&E.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip that carried this reimbursement, inherited on explode. It repeats per line, and the payslip's own reimbursements column already totals these rows — join through it for the run's POSTED filter and pay date, but never add the two grains together.

columns.name: reimbursement_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's ReimbursementLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: reimbursement_type_id
columns.description: Which reimbursement pay item this is; join xero_payroll_au_reimbursement_types for the name and its expense account.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text note on the line ('parking, client visit'). Useful for eyeballing, unreliable for classification — the type id is the categorical field.

columns.name: expense_account
columns.description: GL account code the reimbursement expense posts to. Join xero_accounts on its code (not account_id) to land these in the P&L alongside other expenses.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Dollars reimbursed on this line. Already inside payslip.reimbursements and pay_run.reimbursement — sum one grain only, and keep it out of wage-cost measures.

joins.note: Then to the run for POSTED status.
Type name and default expense account.
Join is on the account CODE, not account_id.

examples.question: Reimbursements paid through payroll by type, this year
examples.sql:
SELECT rt.name AS reimbursement_type, SUM(rl.amount) AS paid
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_reimbursement_lines rl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_reimbursement_types rt ON rt.reimbursement_type_id = rl.reimbursement_type_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = rl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Monthly cash reimbursed to employees via payroll (to reconcile against payslip totals)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(rl.amount) AS reimbursed
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_reimbursement_lines rl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = rl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one superannuation line per payslip per position in the payslip's SuperannuationLines array
tables.description: The superannuation detail of a payslip, exploded from Payslip.SuperannuationLines: each row is one contribution instruction, pairing a super fund membership with a contribution type. The same membership and type can appear on more than one line, which is why the row key is the array ordinal rather than that pairing. ContributionType is the load-bearing split — SGC and EMPLOYERADDITIONAL are employer-funded cost on top of wages, while SALARYSACRIFICE and EMPLOYEE come out of the employee's gross. Every 'super liability', 'SGC compliance' or 'employer cost' number starts by filtering this column; the payslip's Super total mixes all four.
gotchas: ContributionType decides whose money it is: SGC + EMPLOYERADDITIONAL are employer cost, SALARYSACRIFICE + EMPLOYEE are the employee's own. Any super figure that skips this split is wrong for at least one audience.
SGC accrues at pay time but is remitted quarterly: 'super paid' by payment_date_for_this_period and 'super accrued' by the run's payment_date legitimately disagree within a quarter.
Salary sacrifice reduces taxable wages AND appears here: adding sacrifice super back to gross wages when comparing pay levels double-counts the sacrificed dollars.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip the contribution was calculated on, inherited on explode. It repeats once per fund-and-contribution-type line, so joining payslips here fans the payslip's Super total out across its own components; the employee identity and the run's POSTED status both arrive only through this key.

columns.name: superannuation_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's SuperannuationLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_super_membership_id
columns.description: The employee's super fund membership this contribution goes to (memberships live on the employee record in the payroll employees domain). Group by it to see per-fund flows; one employee can contribute to multiple lines in one payslip.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_contribution_type
columns.description: The single most important filter in AU super analysis. SGC is the statutory employer guarantee; EMPLOYERADDITIONAL is voluntary employer cost; SALARYSACRIFICE is employee remuneration redirected pre-tax; EMPLOYEE is post-tax employee money. 'Employer super cost' = SGC + EMPLOYERADDITIONAL only — adding the other two overstates cost with the employees' own money.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_calculation_type
columns.description: How the amount was derived: STATUTORY follows the SG rate rules, PERCENTAGEOFEARNINGS uses the percentage column, FIXEDAMOUNT is a set dollar figure. Explains why percentage or amount is null on some rows.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_minimum_monthly_earnings
columns.description: The monthly earnings floor configured for this contribution, echoed from the employee's super setup onto the line. A threshold parameter, not money: SUM or AVG over it means nothing. Its real use is explaining a zero or absent contribution in a light month — check this before reporting an SG underpayment.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_expense_account_code
columns.description: GL account code the super EXPENSE posts to (employer-funded lines). Join xero_accounts on code to tie payroll super to the P&L.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_liability_account_code
columns.description: GL account code the unpaid-super LIABILITY sits in until remitted to the fund. Balance-sheet reconciliation of super payable joins here on code.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_payment_date_for_this_period
columns.description: The scheduled date for remitting this contribution to the fund — the axis for super CASH-OUT timing, distinct from the payslip's pay date. Accrued-vs-paid super gaps come from confusing the two.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_percentage
columns.description: The contribution percentage for percentage/statutory lines (e.g. the SG rate). A rate — never SUM; use it to sanity-check amount against wages.

columns.name: superannuation_lines_amount
columns.description: Dollars of super on this line for this period. Additive across POSTED payslips, but only meaningful after splitting by contribution_type — a raw SUM mixes employer cost with employee savings.

joins.note: Then to the run for POSTED status and pay/period dates.
Join on account CODE. Same pattern for expense_account_code.

examples.question: SGC (statutory employer super) accrued by quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', r.payment_date) AS quarter, SUM(sl.superannuation_lines_amount) AS sgc_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_superannuation_lines sl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = sl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND sl.superannuation_lines_contribution_type = 'SGC'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Employer vs employee super contributions per employee this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id,
       SUM(sl.superannuation_lines_amount) FILTER (WHERE sl.superannuation_lines_contribution_type IN ('SGC', 'EMPLOYERADDITIONAL')) AS employer_funded,
       SUM(sl.superannuation_lines_amount) FILTER (WHERE sl.superannuation_lines_contribution_type IN ('SALARYSACRIFICE', 'EMPLOYEE')) AS employee_funded
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_superannuation_lines sl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = sl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY employer_funded DESC

tables.grain: one PAYG tax line per payslip per position in the payslip's TaxLines array
tables.description: PAYG withholding detail per payslip, exploded from Payslip.TaxLines. Most payslips carry one automatic PAYG line; extra or overridden lines appear for ETPs and schedule-based manual tax (ManualTaxType names which schedule). Amounts are withheld from the employee and owed to the ATO — a liability in transit, not an employer expense. This is the reconciliation table for W2/BAS PAYG figures.
gotchas: PAYG withheld is employee money in transit to the ATO — inside gross wages, not on top. Adding tax to wages when computing employer cost double-counts it.
ETP and schedule-manual lines (manual_tax_type set) do not follow normal marginal rates: excluding them from effective-tax-rate analyses avoids branding terminations as anomalies.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip the PAYG was withheld on, inherited on explode. Usually one tax line per payslip, but never assume it: ETP and manual-schedule payslips add more, so treat this as a repeating foreign key and de-duplicate before combining it with payslip-level measures.

columns.name: tax_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's TaxLines array; kept as the key for uniformity with the sibling line tables even though tax lines also carry their own id.

columns.name: tax_lines_payslip_tax_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the tax line — the only payslip line family with a native id. Stable across re-fetches; use it for change tracking rather than the ordinal.

columns.name: tax_lines_amount
columns.description: PAYG dollars withheld on this line. Sums (over POSTED runs) to the payslip's Tax and the run's Tax — reconcile at one grain only.

columns.name: tax_lines_tax_type_name
columns.description: Human label of the withholding type ('PAYG'). A display string, not a stable enum — filter on manual_tax_type for schedule logic.

columns.name: tax_lines_description
columns.description: Free-text explanation of the withholding as printed on the payslip. Presentation only and org-authored, so it is not a classification: parsing it for 'ETP' or 'HELP' instead of reading manual_tax_type produces a rule that breaks the first time an admin retypes the wording.

columns.name: tax_lines_manual_tax_type
columns.description: Set only when someone overrode automatic PAYG with a manual schedule amount (ETP, Schedule 4/5 variants). Null means Xero calculated the tax. Manually-taxed payslips are exactly where withholding anomalies concentrate — segment on this before flagging outliers.
columns.enums: PAYGMANUAL; ETPOMANUAL; ETPRMANUAL; SCHEDULE5MANUAL; SCHEDULE5STSLMANUAL; SCHEDULE4MANUAL

columns.name: tax_lines_liability_account
columns.description: GL account code holding the PAYG payable until remitted; populated for posted runs. Join xero_accounts on code for balance-sheet reconciliation.

joins.note: Then to the run for POSTED status and payment_date (the BAS timing axis).
Join on account CODE, not account_id.

examples.question: PAYG withheld per month, automatic vs manually-taxed
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       (tl.tax_lines_manual_tax_type IS NOT NULL) AS manually_taxed,
       SUM(tl.tax_lines_amount) AS payg_withheld
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_tax_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = tl.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Does line-level PAYG reconcile to the run headers this year?
examples.sql:
SELECT r.pay_run_id, r.tax AS header_tax, SUM(tl.tax_lines_amount) AS line_tax
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.pay_run_id = r.pay_run_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslip_tax_lines tl ON tl.payslip_id = p.payslip_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING ABS(r.tax - SUM(tl.tax_lines_amount)) > 0.01

tables.grain: one timesheet-generated earnings line per payslip per position in the payslip's TimesheetEarningsLines array
tables.description: Earnings lines that Xero generated from approved timesheets when the pay run was created, exploded from Payslip.TimesheetEarningsLines (same EarningsLine shape as the manual earnings table). Kept separate because it answers a different question: how much of the wage bill was driven by timesheets versus standing pay templates. Employees paid purely on salary never appear here.
gotchas: These lines are already inside payslip.wages and pay_run.wages — they are a breakdown, not an addition. Adding them to the manual earnings table AND the payslip total triple-counts.

Hours here are hours PAID from timesheets after approval and posting; xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines holds hours ENTERED (any status). Reconciling the two without matching on run period and APPROVED/PROCESSED status produces phantom gaps.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip this timesheet-derived line belongs to, inherited on explode. It is NOT unique here — a payslip normally has several timesheet lines — so joining payslips to this table repeats every payslip-level total once per line. Aggregate the lines first, then join, never the reverse.

columns.name: timesheet_earnings_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the payslip's TimesheetEarningsLines array, minted at explode time; the source line has no id of its own.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate the timesheet hours were paid at; join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates to classify. The rate here comes from the timesheet line's rate selection, not necessarily the employee's default.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: How the amount was computed; for timesheet-generated lines this is effectively rate x units, which is why amount is usually null here and the cost has to be multiplied out. The spec publishes no value list for this field — discover the values present in the tenant rather than hard-coding literals.

columns.name: annual_salary
columns.description: The employee's annual salary, rarely populated on a timesheet-generated line since these are priced from hours. When present it is a yearly rate of pay sitting on a per-period row: never SUM it, and never treat it as this line's cost.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: The rate the timesheet units were paid at, which is the earnings rate's rate as resolved for this employee — not necessarily the pay item's default. A rate, not money: never SUM it, and never average it across lines as 'average hourly rate' without weighting by number_of_units.

columns.name: normal_number_of_units
columns.description: The employee's standard units for the period, carried onto the line as a reference point — it is what they would normally be paid, not what the timesheet recorded. Use it only as the denominator when measuring over- or under-standard periods; using it as hours worked reports a contract, not a timesheet.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Timesheet hours actually paid on this line. This is 'paid hours'; the raw entered-by-day hours (including unapproved) live in xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Fixed dollar value when the line is not rate x units; usually null here. Line cost = COALESCE(amount, rate_per_unit * number_of_units).

joins.note: Then to the run for POSTED status and dates.
Rate classification (overtime vs ordinary etc.).

examples.question: Share of gross wages driven by timesheets, by month
examples.sql:
WITH ts AS (
  SELECT p.pay_run_id,
         SUM(COALESCE(tel.amount, tel.rate_per_unit * tel.number_of_units)) AS timesheet_wages
  FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines tel
  JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = tel.payslip_id
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(COALESCE(ts.timesheet_wages, 0)) AS timesheet_wages,
       SUM(r.wages) AS gross_wages,
       ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(ts.timesheet_wages, 0)) / NULLIF(SUM(r.wages), 0) * 100, 1) AS timesheet_share_pct
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r
LEFT JOIN ts ON ts.pay_run_id = r.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Timesheet hours paid per employee last month
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, SUM(tel.number_of_units) AS timesheet_hours_paid
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines tel
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.payslip_id = tel.payslip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 month'
  AND r.payment_date < date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one payslip per employee per pay run
tables.description: The employee-level slice of a pay run: each row is one employee's pay for one run, with totals (Wages, Deductions, Tax, Super, Reimbursements, NetPay) that Xero derives from the typed line families exploded into the xero_payroll_au_payslip_* tables. Rows are fetched one-by-one via GET /Payslip/{PayslipID} using the ids from the parent run's roster. A payslip has no status of its own — it is as real as its run, so every aggregate must join xero_payroll_au_pay_runs and filter POSTED.
gotchas: A payslip carries no status: one under a DRAFT run is provisional and will change. Join the run and filter pay_run_status = 'POSTED' on every aggregate.
Wages/Deductions/Tax/Super/Reimbursements/NetPay already total the line families in the xero_payroll_au_payslip_* tables. Sum this table OR a line table, never both in one measure.

Super mixes employer-funded (SGC, EMPLOYERADDITIONAL) with employee-funded (SALARYSACRIFICE, EMPLOYEE) contributions. 'Employer payroll cost' that adds the whole Super column overstates cost whenever staff salary-sacrifice.

pay_run_id is inherited from the parent scan, not present on the raw Payslip payload — a row re-fetched outside the run scan cannot re-derive it, which is why the ingester preserves the roster linkage.

Payslip detail arrives via one API call per payslip under the payroll rate budget (60 calls/min, capped daily per org), so this table and its line children can lag the run header for a just-posted run. A header-vs-lines mismatch confined to the newest run is usually ingestion lag, not a data error.

A payslip means 'this person was in this run', which is not headcount. Someone on unpaid leave or with a zero-value run still gets a payslip, a mid-period joiner or leaver appears in whichever run paid them rather than the periods they worked, and a weekly calendar gives the same person four or five payslips a month. COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id) is 'people paid in the window' — say that, do not call it headcount, and never divide wages by it to get 'average salary' without annualising.

Payslips under a DRAFT run are provisional in existence, not just in value: removing an employee from a draft run deletes the payslip outright, so the id vanishes from the roster and stops resolving with no tombstone left behind.

columns.name: payslip_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable payslip identifier, the row key, and the fan-out parameter that fetched this row.

columns.name: pay_run_id
columns.description: Inherited from the parent run whose roster listed this payslip — the Payslip payload itself does not carry it. The only path to run status and pay dates, so effectively mandatory in every query.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee being paid; join xero_payroll_au_employees for current identity, employment dates and classifications. Group by this, not by name — names duplicate.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Employee first name as printed on the payslip — a point-in-time copy that goes stale after a name change. Display only; identity lives in employee_id.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Employee last name as printed on the payslip; same point-in-time caveat as first_name. Two employees can share a full name — never join or group on it.

columns.name: payslips_employee_group
columns.description: The employee-group (tracking) name carried from the pay run's embedded summary roster — the full Payslip payload omits it. The AU-payroll way orgs encode department/cost-centre; null when the org does not group employees.

columns.name: wages
columns.description: The payslip's gross wages: the sum of its earnings, leave-earnings and timesheet-earnings lines. Adding line-table sums on top of this double-counts.

columns.name: deductions
columns.description: Total withheld from this employee via deduction lines, as a positive magnitude. Withheld from gross — not an employer cost.

columns.name: tax
columns.description: PAYG withheld from this employee this run (sum of tax lines), a positive magnitude inside gross. Per-employee annual PAYG = sum over POSTED runs only.

columns.name: super
columns.description: Total super on the payslip across all contribution types — SGC, employer-additional, salary-sacrifice and employee contributions all mixed together. Any 'employer super cost' or 'SGC liability' number must instead come from the superannuation lines filtered by contribution_type.

columns.name: reimbursements
columns.description: Expense money returned to the employee through this payslip. Not remuneration: exclude from wage, tax and super analyses.

columns.name: net_pay
columns.description: Take-home pay: wages minus deductions, tax and employee-funded super (salary-sacrifice/member contributions, carried on the superannuation lines, not in Deductions), plus reimbursements. Use for 'what did we transfer to employees'; never for employer cost.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the payslip record; drives re-fetching an edited payslip. Not a payment date — pay dates live on the run.

columns.name: earnings_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_earnings_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: timesheet_earnings_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: deduction_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_deduction_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: reimbursement_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_payslip_reimbursement_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Mandatory in practice: run status (POSTED filter), payment date and period dates all live on the run.
Current employee identity and attributes; payslip names are stale point-in-time copies.

examples.question: Top 10 employees by gross wages this financial year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, SUM(p.wages) AS gross_wages
FROM xero_payroll_au_payslips p
JOIN xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED' AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months') + INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY gross_wages DESC LIMIT 10

examples.question: Employees paid per pay run over the last 6 months
examples.sql:
SELECT r.payment_date, r.pay_run_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.employee_id) AS employees_paid
FROM xero_payroll_au_pay_runs r
JOIN xero_payroll_au_payslips p ON p.pay_run_id = r.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'POSTED'
  AND r.payment_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one reimbursement type pay item per org
tables.description: The catalogue of reimbursement pay items (ReimbursementTypes family of GET /PayItems): the categories of expense money an org repays through payroll, each mapped to a GL expense account. A small reference dimension joined from payslip reimbursement lines; retired types persist with current_record = false.
gotchas: Reimbursement types map to EXPENSE accounts, not wage accounts — routing them into wage-cost aggregates misstates both payroll and T&E.

columns.name: reimbursement_type_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable reimbursement pay item identifier; payslip reimbursement lines reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Admin-chosen label ('Travel reimbursement'; the spec's doc-string wrongly says 'earnings rate'). The only categorical handle this small dimension offers.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: Default GL expense account code for this reimbursement type; join xero_accounts on code. Payslip lines can override it via their own expense_account.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp on the reimbursement pay item and the incremental sync watermark for the PayItems scan. Configuration recency only — it says nothing about when money was reimbursed.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: Active flag for the pay item. Filter true when listing what the org can currently reimburse; never filter it inside a join from historical reimbursement lines, or retired types drop their rows and reimbursement spend silently shrinks in older periods.

joins.note: Join on account CODE.

examples.question: Active reimbursement types and their expense accounts
examples.sql:
SELECT name, account_code
FROM xero_payroll_au_reimbursement_types
WHERE current_record = true
ORDER BY name

tables.grain: one payroll settings record per organisation (the endpoint returns exactly one)
tables.description: Org-wide AU payroll configuration: the payroll year's day count, STP Phase 2 enablement, and which tracking categories classify employees and timesheets. Singleton per tenant. The GL account wiring inside Settings is normalised into xero_payroll_au_settings_accounts.
gotchas: Singleton: any join that multiplies through this table must treat it as one row, and the tracking category ids inside the jsonb are the only bridge from payroll employee groups to the org's tracking dimensions.

tracking_categories is an untyped object in the spec, so every path into it is a guess that fails silently — jsonb ->> on an absent key returns NULL, which reads as 'no tracking category configured' when it actually means the path is wrong. Inspect jsonb_object_keys first and report an unresolved path as unknown, never as absent configuration.

days_in_payroll_year is org-configured, not a constant. Annualising or de-annualising pay-template amounts with a hardcoded 365 (or 260 working days) will disagree with Xero's own arithmetic on every org that has changed it.

columns.name: settings_scope
columns.api: synthetic:constant 'AU_PAYROLL' — GET /Settings returns exactly one record per tenant, which has no vendor id
columns.description: Minted singleton key so the row has a stable identity across syncs.

columns.name: days_in_payroll_year
columns.description: Number of days in the org's payroll year, as configured in Xero. The divisor for deriving per-period amounts from annual salaries — use this value, not a hardcoded 365, when replicating Xero's salary-per-period maths.

columns.name: employees_are_stp2
columns.description: Whether the org has been enabled for STP Phase 2 employee editing. False means STP2-only fields across the employee tables (income types, disaggregated flags) may be systematically absent — an ingestion-wide data-quality signal, not an employee attribute.

columns.name: tracking_categories
columns.description: Which tracking category classifies employee groups and which classifies timesheets. Kept verbatim because the spec types this as a bare object and declares no keys at all: the EmployeeGroups / TimesheetCategories shape is a runtime observation, not a contract, so probe with jsonb_object_keys before hardcoding a path — a wrong key returns NULL silently instead of erroring, and that NULL reads as 'no tracking configured' when it means 'wrong key'. Resolve the ids inside against xero_tracking_categories to name the dimensions, then match employee_group_name to that category's options.

columns.name: accounts
columns.description: Verbatim Settings.Accounts array — the payroll control-account wiring exactly as returned, normalized into xero_payroll_au_settings_accounts. Query that table for the role filters (WAGESEXPENSE, PAYGLIABILITY, ...); this copy exists so a re-wire of the payroll GL accounts is diffable between syncs.

joins.note: The accounts table is the exploded Settings.Accounts array of this singleton and carries the same minted settings_scope key. Written as a real key equality: the previous literal-only predicate named no column of the child table, which Postgres executes as an unconstrained cross join.

examples.question: Which tracking category drives employee-group reporting?
examples.sql:
SELECT jsonb_object_keys(tracking_categories) AS configured_slot,
       tracking_categories -> 'EmployeeGroups' ->> 'TrackingCategoryID' AS employee_group_tracking_category_id,
       tracking_categories AS raw_payload
FROM xero_payroll_au_settings

examples.question: Payroll year length and STP Phase 2 readiness for this org
examples.sql:
SELECT days_in_payroll_year, employees_are_stp2
FROM xero_payroll_au_settings

tables.grain: one payroll control-account wiring entry per settings singleton per AccountID + Type in Settings.Accounts
tables.description: The GL accounts AU payroll posts to — the wiring between payroll and the general ledger: wages expense, wages payable, PAYG liability, super expense and super liability. The payroll-specific Type values are the roles; join to xero_accounts for the full chart-of-accounts context. This is where 'which GL account holds unpaid super' resolves.
gotchas: This lists only the handful of control accounts payroll is wired to — it is not the chart of accounts. Payroll costs by department resolve through journals on these accounts plus tracking, not through this table alone.

The grain is (settings_scope, account_id, type), not account_id: the same GL account can serve more than one payroll role. COUNT(*) counts wiring entries, not distinct accounts — use COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) for the latter.

columns.name: settings_scope
columns.api: synthetic:constant 'AU_PAYROLL' — parent key inherited from the singleton GET /Settings record, which carries no vendor id
columns.description: Parent key copied down from xero_payroll_au_settings so this explode table joins to its header on a real column instead of a bare literal. Constant within a tenant, and deliberately so: the value is uninteresting, but without it the header-to-lines join degenerates into a cross join that would multiply rows the moment a second scope ever appeared.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: GL account identifier — the same UUID as xero_accounts.account_id, making the cross-domain join exact. Part of the key, not the whole key: the same account can be wired to more than one payroll role.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Account type including the payroll-specific roles (PAYGLIABILITY, PAYG, SUPERANNUATIONEXPENSE, SUPERANNUATIONLIABILITY, WAGESEXPENSE, WAGESPAYABLELIABILITY) alongside standard ledger types. The payroll roles are the reason this table exists — filter on them to find where each payroll obligation posts. Key member: one GL account may carry several roles, so (settings_scope, account_id, type) is the grain.
columns.enums: BANK; CURRENT; CURRLIAB; DEPRECIATN; DIRECTCOSTS; EQUITY; EXPENSE; FIXED; INVENTORY; LIABILITY; NONCURRENT; OTHERINCOME; OVERHEADS; PREPAYMENT; REVENUE; SALES; TERMLIAB; PAYGLIABILITY; PAYG; SUPERANNUATIONEXPENSE; SUPERANNUATIONLIABILITY; WAGESEXPENSE; WAGESPAYABLELIABILITY

columns.name: code
columns.description: Customer-defined account code — the value payroll template lines store in their *account_code columns, so this is the hop that turns codes back into account ids.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Human label of the wired GL account, echoed from the chart of accounts at sync time. Use it to sanity-check the wiring in a report; for anything durable resolve account_id against xero_accounts, because admins rename accounts and this echo goes stale between syncs.

joins.note: Same underlying GL account; xero_accounts adds class, reporting codes and status. Many-to-one because one GL account can appear here under multiple payroll roles — joining without collapsing on account_id double-counts that account.

examples.question: Which GL accounts do wages, PAYG and super post to?
examples.sql:
SELECT type, code, name
FROM xero_payroll_au_settings_accounts
ORDER BY type

tables.grain: one regulated super fund product per ABN + USI
tables.description: Reference catalogue of APRA-regulated super fund products, fetched by looking up the ABN/USI of funds the organisation uses. It exists to give regulated funds their official product name and to validate USIs — it is industry reference data, not tenant data, and carries no amounts.
gotchas: Availability optional: rows exist only for products looked up via the funds' ABN/USI during ingestion — this is not a complete national product registry, and SMSFs never appear here.

columns.name: abn
columns.description: ABN of the entity offering the product and half the row key. One ABN typically fronts many USIs, so it never identifies a product on its own — never join funds to products on ABN alone or you fan a fund out across every product that ABN offers. Text, because an ABN is an 11-digit identifier rather than a quantity and can arrive spaced or unspaced.

columns.name: usi
columns.description: Unique Superannuation Identifier of the product; the other half of the key and the join back to xero_payroll_au_super_funds.usi.

columns.name: spin
columns.description: Superannuation Product Identification Number — the pre-SuperStream product identifier the spec explicitly marks deprecated in favour of USI. Populated only on legacy products and never on newly registered ones, so a null here says nothing about whether the product is valid or current. Resolve identity through usi; fall back to spin only when matching historical records that predate USIs.

columns.name: product_name
columns.description: The official registered product name — the label to prefer over the admin-typed fund name when presenting regulated funds.

joins.note: Several org fund records could reference the same product.

examples.question: Official product names of the regulated funds the org uses
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name, f.name AS name_in_xero
FROM xero_payroll_au_super_fund_products p
JOIN xero_payroll_au_super_funds f ON f.usi = p.usi
ORDER BY p.product_name

tables.grain: one superannuation fund per SuperFundID registered in the organisation's payroll
tables.description: The organisation's registry of destination super funds: APRA-regulated funds (identified by USI) and self-managed funds (SMSF, identified by ABN plus their own bank details). The two types populate disjoint field sets — treat Type as a schema switch. Employees connect here via super memberships; contribution amounts never live on this table.
gotchas: REGULATED and SMSF rows have disjoint populated columns; an aggregate over bank-detail columns silently covers only SMSFs, and one over usi only regulated funds.
spin is deprecated — legacy rows may carry SPIN with no USI; resolve product identity via USI first, SPIN only as a last-resort legacy match.

This is a registry of fund RECORDS, not of distinct funds. The same physical fund can be registered more than once (a re-entry, or one record per employer number), giving several SuperFundIDs that share a USI — so 'how many funds do we pay into' is COUNT(DISTINCT usi) for regulated funds; COUNT(*) overstates it and splits that fund's members across rows.

Rows persist after the last employee leaves a fund. A fund appearing here is not evidence anyone contributes to it — confirm through xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships joined to active employees before reporting fund usage or negotiating on member counts.

columns.name: super_fund_id
columns.description: Xero's fund identifier and the row key; what super memberships reference.

columns.name: type
columns.description: REGULATED (APRA fund, identified by USI) or SMSF (self-managed, identified by ABN with its own BSB/account for direct payment). This decides which columns are populated — querying usi on an SMSF or bank details on a regulated fund returns nulls by design.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Fund display name. For REGULATED funds prefer the product name resolved via USI from xero_payroll_au_super_fund_products — this field is whatever the payroll admin typed.

columns.name: abn
columns.description: Australian Business Number — the spec documents it as the ABN of the self-managed super fund, i.e. the SMSF's primary identifier (SMSFs have no USI). Identify REGULATED funds by usi, not this column. Keep as text; ABNs are 11 digits and not arithmetic.

columns.name: bsb
columns.description: Bank-State-Branch routing code used to pay contributions directly to a self-managed fund. Text, because BSBs carry meaningful leading zeros and a hyphen convention that numeric storage destroys. Populated only where type = 'SMSF' — null on a regulated fund is correct, not a gap, since APRA funds are paid via SuperStream against the USI. Sensitive financial data.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: Destination account number for direct payment to a self-managed fund, stored as the bank presents it and never as a number. SMSF-only, so a COUNT of non-null values here counts SMSFs rather than funds with valid payment details. Sensitive financial data — never surface the value itself.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Name the SMSF's bank account is held in — typically the fund's trustee, who in a single-member SMSF is the employee themselves. That makes this fund-level column capable of leaking an individual's identity, so treat it as personal data even though the table is not employee-grained. SMSF-only. Sensitive; never join it into employee-level output.

columns.name: electronic_service_address
columns.description: The SMSF's SuperStream electronic service address (ESA) for receiving contribution messages. SMSF-only, operational plumbing.

columns.name: employer_number
columns.description: The employer number some funds assign to this organisation — identifies the EMPLOYER to the fund, not any employee.

columns.name: spin
columns.description: Legacy Superannuation Product Identification Number, deprecated in favour of USI. Present only on funds created long ago; never join on it when a USI exists.

columns.name: usi
columns.description: Unique Superannuation Identifier of the regulated fund product — the canonical join to xero_payroll_au_super_fund_products and the identifier SuperStream payments route on. Null for SMSFs.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified stamp and incremental watermark for the fund registry scan.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation messages echoed on the record, verbatim for debugging. Presentation-only.

joins.note: Fund to member enrolments.
REGULATED funds only — SMSFs have no USI and no product row.

examples.question: How many distinct funds does the org actually pay into, by type?
examples.sql:
SELECT f.type,
       COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(f.usi, f.super_fund_id)) AS distinct_funds,
       COUNT(*) AS fund_records
FROM xero_payroll_au_super_funds f
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM xero_payroll_au_employee_super_memberships m
  JOIN xero_payroll_au_employees e ON e.employee_id = m.employee_id
  WHERE m.super_fund_id = f.super_fund_id AND e.status = 'ACTIVE'
)
GROUP BY 1

examples.question: Self-managed funds registered in payroll (SMSFs carry their own compliance obligations)
examples.sql:
SELECT super_fund_id, name, abn, electronic_service_address
FROM xero_payroll_au_super_funds
WHERE type = 'SMSF'
ORDER BY name

tables.grain: one timesheet line per timesheet per position in its TimesheetLines array — a line pairs one earnings rate with one optional tracking option, but the same pairing can legitimately appear twice, so the ordinal is what makes the key
tables.description: The per-rate detail of a timesheet: each line books hours against one earnings rate, optionally tagged to a tracking option for cost-centre attribution. NumberOfUnits is NOT a scalar — it is an ARRAY with one element per day of the timesheet period, in day order starting at the timesheet's StartDate, stored here as jsonb. Daily and per-line hour analysis expands the array; the parent timesheet's Hours column is the pre-summed shortcut.
gotchas: NumberOfUnits is an array of per-day values, not a total. Any query that does not expand the jsonb (jsonb_array_elements_text(...)::numeric) or use the parent's hours column is wrong — casting the array itself to numeric errors, and grabbing element 0 reports only the first day.
Line hours inherit the parent's status: summing lines without joining the timesheet and filtering APPROVED/PROCESSED books draft and rejected hours as worked.

The daily array is aligned to the TIMESHEET period, so element index i maps to start_date + i days; aggregating across timesheets by index without converting to real dates misaligns weeks that start on different days.

columns.name: timesheet_id
columns.description: Parent timesheet key, inherited on explode; status, employee and period dates live on the parent.

columns.name: timesheet_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this line in the timesheet's TimesheetLines array, minted at explode time; lines have no id of their own.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate these hours will be paid at (ordinary vs overtime vs allowance); join xero_payroll_au_earnings_rates. The split key for overtime-hours analysis at entry time.

columns.name: tracking_item_id
columns.description: Despite the name, this is a tracking OPTION id (from the tracking category the org designated for timesheets) — join xero_tracking_options.tracking_option_id, not the category table. The cost-centre/department axis for labor hours; null when the org does not track timesheets.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: ARRAY of daily hour values, one element per day of the timesheet period, ordered from the timesheet's StartDate (element 0 = start day, weekends included as 0 or null). Total line hours = SUM over jsonb_array_elements_text(number_of_units)::numeric; day-of-week analysis uses the element index added to start_date. Reading it as a single number, or taking the first element, silently drops most of the hours.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified stamp on the line itself; the parent timesheet's stamp is the sync watermark, this one localizes which line changed.

joins.note: Status filter (APPROVED/PROCESSED), employee and period dates all come from the parent.
Classifies the hours (ordinary/overtime/allowance).
TrackingItemID is an option id despite its name; it belongs to the org's designated timesheet tracking category.

examples.question: Hours by tracking option (cost centre) for processed timesheets last month
examples.sql:
SELECT tl.tracking_item_id,
       SUM(u.value::numeric) AS hours
FROM xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_timesheets t ON t.timesheet_id = tl.timesheet_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(tl.number_of_units) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(value, day_index)
WHERE t.status = 'PROCESSED'
  AND t.start_date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 month'
  AND t.start_date < date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
  AND u.value IS NOT NULL AND u.value <> ''
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Daily hours profile (day of week) for approved timesheets this quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT to_char(t.start_date + (u.day_index::int - 1), 'Dy') AS weekday,
       SUM(u.value::numeric) AS hours
FROM xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_au_timesheets t ON t.timesheet_id = tl.timesheet_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(tl.number_of_units) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(value, day_index)
WHERE t.status IN ('APPROVED', 'PROCESSED')
  AND t.start_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
  AND u.value IS NOT NULL AND u.value <> ''
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY MIN(EXTRACT(isodow FROM t.start_date + (u.day_index::int - 1)))

tables.grain: one timesheet record, keyed by TimesheetID — normally one per employee per period, but employee + period is NOT a key because a refused or superseded submission persists alongside its replacement
tables.description: Hours as entered: one timesheet record per employee per period, with a total Hours figure and per-rate daily detail in xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines. Status is the trust boundary — DRAFT and REQUESTED are unvetted claims, APPROVED is signed off, PROCESSED has been consumed by a posted pay run, REJECTED was refused — and it is also what keeps the grain honest, since a rejected submission and the corrected resubmission both survive for the same employee and period. Hours only become wages when a run picks the timesheet up, at which point they surface as TimesheetEarningsLines on payslips. Deletion is a disappearance, not a status: TimesheetStatus has no DELETED value, so a removed timesheet simply stops being returned and only a full identity scan retires the staged row.
gotchas: Hours entered are not hours paid: only timesheets consumed by a POSTED run become wages (as payslip TimesheetEarningsLines). Comparing entered vs paid without matching status and run period manufactures discrepancies.
hours already sums the lines' daily units — adding line-level sums to the header doubles the count.

REJECTED and DRAFT timesheets sit in the table indefinitely, and a refused submission is not replaced by its resubmission — both rows survive for the same employee and the same period. An unfiltered SUM(hours) therefore double-counts every corrected week on top of counting hours nobody approved.

Payroll is region-exclusive: a tenant runs AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two. Zero rows here on a UK/NZ org means 'no AU payroll', not a broken sync, and AU timesheets must never be unioned with the UK/NZ tables.

columns.name: timesheet_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable timesheet identifier and the row key — the only thing that is actually unique here, since the same employee and period can carry a rejected submission and its replacement.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Whose hours these are; join xero_payroll_au_employees. Do not treat employee + period as unique: a refused submission and its replacement both persist, so 'hours for employee X in week W' must filter status before summing or the rejected copy is added back in.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day of the timesheet period; also the anchor for reading the daily units arrays on the lines (element 0 = this day).

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day of the timesheet period (inclusive). Period length fixes the expected length of each line's daily units array.

columns.name: status
columns.description: The trust filter. DRAFT/REQUESTED hours are unvetted; APPROVED is signed off but unpaid; PROCESSED is in a posted pay run; REJECTED never counts. 'Hours worked' analyses usually mean APPROVED + PROCESSED — including drafts turns typos into labor cost.

columns.name: hours
columns.description: Total hours on the timesheet across all lines and days — Xero's own rollup of the lines' daily units. Use it instead of re-summing the jsonb arrays when the per-rate/per-day split is not needed.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp and the incremental sync watermark for timesheets. It ticks on every status transition (submit, approve, reject) as well as on hour edits, so it dates the last administrative touch, not the work — never use it as the date hours were worked; that is start_date/end_date.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-response diagnostic payload from the API; null on every read. Never analytical — present only so the staging row is a faithful copy of the record, and a non-null value here means a write was replayed, not that the business record is invalid.

columns.name: timesheet_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_au_timesheet_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Employee identity, calendar assignment and ordinary earnings rate.
Per-rate daily detail; the header hours already total the lines.

examples.question: Approved or processed hours per employee per week
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, date_trunc('week', start_date) AS week, SUM(hours) AS hours
FROM xero_payroll_au_timesheets
WHERE status IN ('APPROVED', 'PROCESSED')
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2, 1

examples.question: Timesheets still awaiting approval for closed periods
examples.sql:
SELECT timesheet_id, employee_id, start_date, end_date, hours
FROM xero_payroll_au_timesheets
WHERE status IN ('DRAFT', 'REQUESTED') AND end_date < CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY end_date

tables.grain: one org-level deduction pay item per deduction id
tables.description: The org's catalogue of voluntary deduction types (payroll giving, KiwiSaver voluntary contributions, superannuation top-ups, other) and the liability account each posts to. Definitions only: amounts actually deducted from pay are payslip deduction lines in the pay-run domain.
