Note the category overlap trap: KiwiSaverVoluntaryContributions here is EXTRA voluntary saving — the standard employee KiwiSaver deduction is a statutory deduction, not this.
gotchas: This is a catalogue: no money moved here. Deducted dollars live on payslip lines keyed by this id.
Deleting a deduction type in Xero flips current_record false rather than removing it — counting all rows overstates the org's live deduction offerings.

columns.name: deduction_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the deduction type (lower-cased 'deductionId' in this v2 API); referenced by payslip deduction lines.

columns.name: deduction_name
columns.description: The label the org gave this deduction, shown on payslips and in the pay-run UI. Free text edited in place, so historical payslip lines render under today's name — classify with deduction_category and join on deduction_id. Grouping deductions by name silently merges two types an org renamed to the same string and splits one it renamed mid-year.

columns.name: deduction_category
columns.description: Statutory-reporting bucket. PayrollGiving earns tax credits; KiwiSaverVoluntaryContributions is voluntary top-up saving (NOT the standard 3-10 percent employee contribution); Superannuation is non-KiwiSaver schemes; NzOther is everything else. Classifying deductions in payslip analysis starts here.

columns.name: liability_account_id
columns.description: GL liability account the withheld money accrues to until paid out; joins to xero_accounts.account_id for reconciling payroll liabilities against the ledger.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: True when the deduction type is active. Inactive types persist because historical payslips reference them — filter current_record for 'available deductions' but keep all rows when decoding history.

columns.name: standard_amount
columns.description: Default NZD amount suggested when the deduction is added to a payslip; a default, not what was actually deducted anywhere.

joins.note: Ledger liability account for withheld amounts.

examples.question: Active deduction types by category
examples.sql:
SELECT deduction_category, COUNT(*) AS types
FROM xero_payroll_nz_deductions
WHERE current_record
GROUP BY 1

tables.grain: one org-level earnings rate (pay item) per earnings rate id
tables.description: The org's catalogue of ways people can be paid: ordinary earnings, overtime multipliers, allowances, bonuses, holiday pay and the rest, each with its calculation mechanics (rate-per-unit, multiple-of-ordinary, fixed) and the GL expense account it posts to. Every timesheet line, salary record, pay-template line and payslip earnings line points here — it is the decoding dimension for all NZ earnings analysis. Definitions only; earned dollars live on payslips.
gotchas: WithholdingIncome rates pay schedular contractors through payroll — include them in 'wages' and the employee wage bill absorbs non-employee spend.
For multiplier rates the dollar value depends on each employee's ordinary rate; the catalogue alone cannot price an hour of overtime.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the earnings rate; the foreign key on timesheet lines, salary records and pay-template lines.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name ('Ordinary Hours', 'Time and a Half'...). Names are org-chosen — classify by earnings_type, not by string-matching names.

columns.name: earnings_type
columns.description: Statutory classification of the earning. RegularEarnings is base pay; OvertimeEarnings feeds overtime metrics; HolidayPay is the 8-percent casual payout; WithholdingIncome flags schedular-contractor pay that is NOT employee wages and must be excluded from wage-bill answers; the two Tips values contain parentheses and need exact-string matching.
columns.enums: Allowance; Backpay; Bonus; Commission; DiscretionaryPayments; HolidayPay; LumpSum; OtherEarnings; OtherGrossEarnings; OvertimeEarnings; RegularEarnings; SalarySacrificeForKiwiSaver; Tips(Direct); Tips(Non-Direct); WithholdingIncome

columns.name: rate_type
columns.description: Calculation mechanics: RatePerUnit uses rate_per_unit x units; MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate scales the employee's own ordinary rate by multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate (so the dollar rate differs per employee); FixedAmount pays fixed_amount flat. Exactly one of the three amount columns is meaningful per row.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: Unit label for quantities recorded against this rate (typically Hours). Timesheet units inherit this meaning — summing units across rates with different unit types is meaningless.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: True when the rate is active for new pay; retired rates persist because historical lines reference them.

columns.name: expense_account_id
columns.description: GL expense account this earning posts to — the bridge from payroll to P&L wage-cost lines; joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Default NZD rate per unit, only when rate_type = RatePerUnit; per-employee salary records override it. Null here does not mean unpaid.

columns.name: multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate
columns.description: Multiplier on the employee's ordinary rate (1.5 = time-and-a-half), only when rate_type = MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate. The resulting dollar rate is per-employee — never treat this as a dollar amount.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Flat NZD amount per occurrence, only when rate_type = FixedAmount.

joins.note: P&L account carrying this earning's cost.

examples.question: Overtime rate definitions in force
examples.sql:
SELECT name, rate_type, multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate
FROM xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates
WHERE earnings_type = 'OvertimeEarnings' AND current_record

examples.question: Earnings rates posting to each expense account
examples.sql:
SELECT a.name AS account, COUNT(*) AS rates
FROM xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates er
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = er.expense_account_id
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one wage-destination bank account per employee, keyed by employee and array position
tables.description: The bank accounts an electronically-paid employee's net pay is split into, with the split rule per account: a FixedAmount account takes dollar_amount each pay and the Balance account absorbs the remainder. Highly sensitive PII (account numbers). dollar_amount is a per-pay split INSTRUCTION, not money that has moved — summing it across employees estimates configured splits, not actual payroll cash.
gotchas: dollar_amount is configuration. Actual net pay disbursed lives in pay-run payslips; treating these splits as payments fabricates cash flow.
Full account numbers are PII with fraud risk — expose only under explicit governance, never in ad-hoc answers.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.api: synthetic:EmployeeID path parameter of GET /Employees/{EmployeeID}/PaymentMethods, denormalized onto each exploded bank account (Employee.employeeID is the real-world source; neither BankAccount nor PaymentMethod carries it in the payload)
columns.description: Owning employee, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: bank_accounts
columns.description: Zero-based position in the parent's bankAccounts array (accounts carry no id); provenance is the array itself. Order matters to Xero's split logic — fixed-amount accounts are taken before the Balance account.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Account holder name as it will be written into the NZ bank file, capped by Xero at 32 characters. Frequently an abbreviated or joint-account form of the employee's legal name, so it is not a reliable match back to first_name/last_name and must never be used to reconcile people across systems.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: Bank account number, digits only. Sensitive financial PII — never surface in analytical answers; keep as text to preserve leading zeros.

columns.name: sort_code
columns.description: Six-digit bank/branch code prefixing the account number. Text, not integer — leading zeros are significant.

columns.name: particulars
columns.description: First of NZ banking's three free-text annotation fields (particulars / code / reference) that print on both parties' statements — conventionally the payer or 'Wages'. Set per destination account, so a split-pay employee can see different text against each credit. A label only: it carries no amount, date or identifier the platform can compute from.

columns.name: code
columns.description: Second of the NZ particulars/code/reference statement triplet, conventionally a short payroll or employee code the payer uses to recognise the credit. Org-chosen free text with no referential integrity to anything in Xero — resist the temptation to join or group on it, and never treat a matching code as evidence two rows are the same person.

columns.name: dollar_amount
columns.description: Fixed NZD amount routed to this account each pay when calculation_type is FixedAmount; null/irrelevant for the Balance account. A standing instruction, not a payment record.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Third of the NZ particulars/code/reference triplet — the statement text the employee sees against the credit, often the pay period or 'Salary'. Static configuration reused on every pay, so it does not identify a specific payment and cannot be used to reconcile an individual wage transfer to a pay run.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: FixedAmount takes dollar_amount each pay; Balance receives whatever net pay remains. Exactly one Balance account should exist per employee — more than one indicates misconfiguration worth flagging, not averaging.

joins.note: Parent method should be Electronically when rows exist.

examples.question: Employees splitting pay across multiple accounts
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) AS accounts
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_bank_accounts
GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

tables.grain: one leave request (a dated span of one leave type) per employee
tables.description: Leave events: each row is one employee's request to take a specific leave type over a start/end date span. The per-pay-period splits, unit counts and approval status live in xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_periods — this header has NO units column, so 'days of leave taken' must come from the periods table, never from counting header rows or date arithmetic on the span (which counts weekends and part-days wrongly). The canonical workforce_leave fact is sourced from the periods table for exactly that reason; treating this header as a second source of the same concept counts every request twice at a grain that carries no quantity.
gotchas: No units on this header. SUM anything about leave quantities from the periods table; end_date - start_date counts calendar days including weekends and public holidays.
There is no status on the header either — approval state (Approved/Completed/Estimated) is per period. A request whose periods are all Estimated has not been taken yet.

Per-employee fan-out: one call per employee against Xero's 60-calls-per-minute per-org budget, driven off the employee scan. Leave can therefore lag the employee master, so a request entered in the last few minutes may be missing rather than absent — never report 'nobody booked leave' from a stale subresource without saying when it last synced.

columns.name: leave_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this leave request and the row key (the spec's description mislabels it 'LeaveType' — it is the leave record's own id).

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee taking the leave, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Which kind of leave. Join xero_payroll_nz_leave_types for the name and whether it is paid — 'annual leave taken' without this join silently mixes sick, bereavement and unpaid leave.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text reason entered with the request (max 50 chars). May contain personal detail (medical mentions) — treat as sensitive display text, never a grouping dimension.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First calendar day of the leave span. Calendar span, not units: a Friday-to-Monday request spans 4 days but may consume 2 units — quantity questions go to the periods table.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last calendar day of the leave span, inclusive. Filter leave overlapping window [a,b] with start_date <= b AND end_date >= a.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change to this request; sync watermark, not a business date.

joins.note: Leave for terminated employees remains in history.
Name, paid/unpaid flag and units of the leave type.
The unit-bearing per-pay-period breakdown; use it for any quantity of leave.

examples.question: Who is on leave today?
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, lt.name AS leave_type, l.start_date, l.end_date
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = l.employee_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = l.leave_type_id
WHERE CURRENT_DATE BETWEEN l.start_date AND l.end_date

examples.question: Leave requests per employee this year
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) AS requests
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave
WHERE start_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one current leave balance per employee per leave type
tables.description: Point-in-time leave balances: how many units of each leave type each employee holds as of the last sync. A snapshot, not a ledger — Xero returns only the current value, so there is no balance history and summing across syncs or time double-counts. Balances can be negative (leave taken in advance).
tables.additivityAxis: time
gotchas: last_value_over_time: this is the balance as of the last sync. Never SUM across time or across syncs; trend questions need the payslip-side balances from pay runs, not this table.
NZ annual leave is tracked in weeks and most other leave in hours — a naive SUM(balance) mixes units. Group by type_of_units.

Balances are returned for everyone still in the employee list, including leavers whose final pay has not been processed. An org-level accrued-leave total that does not join xero_payroll_nz_employees and filter the employment window carries balances for people who no longer work there.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee holding the balance, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Leave type of the balance; join xero_payroll_nz_leave_types for accrual rules.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Leave type name denormalized by Xero onto the balance; convenient for display but the id is the join key.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Current balance in type_of_units. Negative means leave taken in advance. Always units, never dollars — the one dollar figure in the leave family is annual_leave_total_amount_paid on xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_types; liability estimates from this column need a pay rate on top.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: Unit of the balance (Hours for most types, Weeks for NZ annual leave entitlement). Summing balances across unit types produces a meaningless number — always group or filter by this.

joins.note: Balances exist only for leave types assigned to the employee.
Accrual schedule and paid/unpaid flag.

examples.question: Accrued leave balance by leave type for current staff, kept in each type's own units
examples.sql:
SELECT lt.name AS leave_type, b.type_of_units, SUM(b.balance) AS total_balance
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_balances b
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = b.leave_type_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id
WHERE e.start_date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (e.end_date IS NULL OR e.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY lt.leave_type_id, lt.name, b.type_of_units
ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Who has taken leave in advance (negative balance)?
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, lt.name AS leave_type, b.balance, b.type_of_units
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_balances b
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = b.leave_type_id
WHERE b.balance < 0
ORDER BY b.balance

tables.grain: one pay-period slice of one leave request, keyed by leave request and array position
tables.description: The quantity-bearing grain of leave: each leave request is split into the pay periods it touches, with units scheduled (number_of_units) and units actually taken (number_of_units_taken) plus the period's approval status. This is THE table for 'how much leave' questions. Statuses matter: Estimated periods are forecasts that a pay run has not confirmed; only Approved/Completed periods represent real leave.
gotchas: Estimated periods are forecasts. Including them in 'leave taken' reports future leave as already consumed; filter period_status IN ('Approved','Completed').
Units are heterogeneous: hours for most types, weeks for some statutory NZ leave. Group by type_of_units or convert explicitly before summing.

The same GET /Employees/{EmployeeID}/LeavePeriods data also exists as a standalone endpoint; this table is built from the Leave fan-out so each slice stays attached to its request — do not ingest both or slices duplicate.

columns.name: leave_id
columns.description: Parent leave request this period slice belongs to.

columns.name: periods
columns.description: Zero-based position of this slice within the parent request's periods array (the slices carry no id of their own); provenance is the periods array itself. Chronological order follows period_start_date, which is the safer sort key.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.api: synthetic:EmployeeID path parameter of GET /Employees/{EmployeeID}/Leave, denormalized onto each exploded period (Employee.employeeID is the real-world source; neither LeavePeriod nor EmployeeLeave carries it in the payload)
columns.description: Employee on leave, denormalized from the fan-out path so leave-by-person queries skip a join.

columns.name: period_start_date
columns.description: Start of the PAY period this slice falls in — the payroll calendar's boundary, not the leave's own start date.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: End of the pay period this slice falls in. Bucket leave into months by this date (or the parent's dates) consistently — mixing conventions splits one request across months twice.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave scheduled in this period, in type_of_units (usually hours, weeks for some statutory types). The planned quantity; compare with number_of_units_taken for realized leave.

columns.name: number_of_units_taken
columns.description: Units actually taken in this period per the processed pay run. 'Leave taken' totals SUM this, filtered to Approved/Completed — using number_of_units counts scheduled-but-cancelled leave.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: Unit for number_of_units (Hours, Days, Weeks as Xero spells them). NZ statutory leave mixes hour- and week-based types — never SUM units across different type_of_units values.

columns.name: type_of_units_taken
columns.description: Unit for number_of_units_taken; normally equals type_of_units but is carried separately by the API — check both before aggregating.

columns.name: period_status
columns.description: Approved = confirmed for a pay run; Completed = paid in a finalized run; Estimated = Xero's forecast split that no pay run has confirmed. Actual-leave metrics must exclude Estimated or future forecast leave inflates history.

joins.note: Header carries the leave type and overall span.
Denormalized person link.

examples.question: Hours of leave taken per employee this year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, SUM(p.number_of_units_taken) AS hours_taken
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_periods p
WHERE p.period_status IN ('Approved','Completed')
  AND p.type_of_units_taken = 'Hours'
  AND p.period_start_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Scheduled vs actually taken leave hours by leave type, excluding unconfirmed forecast periods
examples.sql:
SELECT lt.name AS leave_type,
       SUM(p.number_of_units) FILTER (WHERE p.type_of_units = 'Hours') AS scheduled_hours,
       SUM(p.number_of_units_taken) FILTER (WHERE p.type_of_units_taken = 'Hours') AS taken_hours
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_periods p
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave l ON l.leave_id = p.leave_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = l.leave_type_id
WHERE p.period_status IN ('Approved','Completed')
GROUP BY lt.leave_type_id, lt.name
ORDER BY taken_hours DESC NULLS LAST

tables.grain: one leave-type assignment (with its accrual configuration) per employee per leave type
tables.description: The per-employee accrual contract for each leave type the employee is enrolled in: how it accrues, at what annual quantity, caps, opening balance and NZ-specific holiday-pay flags. This is configuration, not consumption — actual leave taken is in leave periods and current balances in leave balances. The same leave_type_id appears for many employees with DIFFERENT accrual values, which is exactly why this table exists separately from the org-level xero_payroll_nz_leave_types.
gotchas: Per-employee values override the org-level leave type: the same leave_type_id carries different accrual quantities per person. Entitlement reporting reads THIS table, not xero_payroll_nz_leave_types.
annual_leave_total_amount_paid is dollars while every other quantity here is units — mixing them in one SUM is a category error.

opening_balance and annual_leave_total_amount_paid are point-in-time balances sitting in an otherwise configuration table, so the table-level 'reference' additivity does not license them: they may be added across employees for a liability at one moment, never across time or sync runs. Trended leave liability has to come from pay-run payslip balances, not from here.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee this accrual configuration applies to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The org-level leave type being configured for this employee; join xero_payroll_nz_leave_types for its name.

columns.name: schedule_of_accrual
columns.description: How this employee accrues the type. AnnuallyAfter6Months and OnAnniversaryDate grant lump entitlements; PercentageOfGrossEarnings accrues per pay (casual holiday pay); NoAccruals means the type never self-accrues (sick leave granted by statute events). Determines which of the quantity columns below is meaningful.

columns.name: units_accrued_annually
columns.description: Annual accrual quantity in type_of_units_to_accrue; 0 when schedule_of_accrual is NoAccruals. An entitlement rate, not a balance.

columns.name: type_of_units_to_accrue
columns.description: Unit of units_accrued_annually (Hours/Days/Weeks). Comparing entitlements across employees requires equal units first.

columns.name: maximum_to_accrue
columns.description: Cap on accrued units; null means uncapped. Balances at the cap accrue nothing further — relevant when projecting future liability.

columns.name: opening_balance
columns.description: Units granted when the type was first assigned to the employee (migration or enrolment); a one-time seed, already reflected in the current balance — never add it on top.

columns.name: opening_balance_type_of_units
columns.description: Unit of the opening balance; can differ from the accrual unit for annual leave (weeks vs hours).

columns.name: rate_accrued_hourly
columns.description: Documented by Xero as 'not supported in Payroll NZ' — always null/0 for NZ tenants; present only for cross-region schema parity. Never use.

columns.name: percentage_of_gross_earnings
columns.description: For PercentageOfGrossEarnings schedules: the percent of gross accrued per pay (8 percent is the NZ casual holiday-pay standard). Meaningless under other schedules.

columns.name: include_holiday_pay_every_pay
columns.description: Holiday-pay-specific: true means the 8 percent is paid out in every pay run instead of banked — such employees accrue no annual-leave balance, so their zero balance is correct, not missing data.

columns.name: show_annual_leave_in_advance
columns.description: Annual-leave-specific payslip display flag: include leave available in advance in the shown balance. Presentation only — does not change the stored balance.

columns.name: annual_leave_total_amount_paid
columns.description: Annual-leave balance expressed in DOLLARS (NZD), maintained by Xero alongside the unit balance. The one dollar figure in the leave family — use it for leave-liability questions instead of multiplying units by a guessed rate. It is a snapshot overwritten on every sync, not a ledger: add it across employees to value the liability at one instant, never across sync dates or reporting periods, because this table keeps no history to add up.

columns.name: schedule_of_accrual_date
columns.description: The date the employee next/first becomes entitled to the accrual (anniversary-based schedules). A future date means the entitlement has not landed yet.

joins.note: One row per assigned leave type; unassigned org types have no row for the employee.
Org-level name and paid/unpaid flag for the type.

examples.question: Annual leave dollar liability for current staff
examples.sql:
SELECT elt.employee_id, SUM(elt.annual_leave_total_amount_paid) AS annual_leave_liability_nzd
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_types elt
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = elt.employee_id
WHERE elt.annual_leave_total_amount_paid IS NOT NULL
  AND e.start_date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (e.end_date IS NULL OR e.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one historical pay-period opening-balance line per employee, keyed by employee and array position
tables.description: Pre-Xero earnings history typed in at migration so NZ Holidays Act calculations (ordinary weekly pay, average weekly earnings) are correct from the org's first Xero pay run. Each row is one prior pay period's gross earnings with the days paid and unpaid weeks that period contributes to the divisor. It describes the time BEFORE the org used Xero payroll, so it is disjoint from payslip earnings rather than overlapping them: unioning the two does not double count, it silently changes the basis of a 'total earnings' answer from 'calculated and paid through Xero' to 'partly unaudited figures a human keyed in at go-live'. Report the two series separately and label which is which.
gotchas: These are pre-migration earnings a person keyed in, not amounts Xero calculated or paid. Because they cover periods before go-live they do not overlap payslips, so unioning them is not a double count — it is a basis change that imports unaudited figures into a payroll total. Keep the series separate and say which one an answer used.
Per-employee fan-out endpoint: subject to the 60/min rate budget, synced opportunistically; absence of rows means 'nothing entered', not zero earnings.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: balance_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position in the openingBalances array of EmployeeOpeningBalancesObject
columns.description: Minted array position — the source rows carry no identifier of their own. Stable only within one sync; use employee_id + period_end_date for human-facing ordering.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: End date of the historical pay period this line covers. Periods predate the org's first Xero pay run — a line dated after go-live indicates a data-entry error, not a real pay period.

columns.name: days_paid
columns.description: Number of days paid in the period; feeds NZ 'ordinary weekly pay' divisors. Zero with positive gross usually means a lump sum, which distorts averages.

columns.name: unpaid_weeks
columns.description: Whole weeks unpaid within the period; subtracted from the divisor in average-weekly-earnings calculations, so ignoring it understates the true weekly average.

columns.name: gross_earnings
columns.description: Gross earnings for the historical period, NZD. Safe to SUM across periods for a migration-total, but never mix with pay-run payslip earnings — the two series are disjoint in time by construction.

joins.note: Only migrated employees have rows; employees hired after go-live legitimately have none.

examples.question: Migrated gross-earnings history per employee
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, MIN(period_end_date) AS earliest_period, SUM(gross_earnings) AS total_migrated_gross
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_opening_balances
GROUP BY employee_id ORDER BY total_migrated_gross DESC

examples.question: Average weekly earnings implied by the migrated history, for weekly-paid employees
examples.sql:
SELECT b.employee_id,
       SUM(b.gross_earnings)
         / NULLIF(COUNT(*) - SUM(COALESCE(b.unpaid_weeks, 0)), 0) AS implied_avg_weekly_earnings
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_opening_balances b
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_run_calendars c ON c.payroll_calendar_id = e.payroll_calendar_id
WHERE c.calendar_type = 'Weekly'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one earnings template line per employee pay template, keyed by its payTemplateEarningID
tables.description: The employee's standing pay template: the earnings lines Xero pre-loads into each new pay run draft (e.g. 40 ordinary hours at $X, plus a standing allowance). Template lines are defaults, not payments — a pay run can override or remove them, so 'what someone was paid' comes from payslips while 'what someone is set up to be paid' comes from here and from xero_payroll_nz_salary_and_wages.
gotchas: Templates are defaults, not history. Summing template amounts is 'configured pay per period', which diverges from actual pay whenever timesheets, leave or one-off lines apply.
rate_per_unit/number_of_units vs fixed_amount are alternative encodings — adding both double-counts the line.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee the template belongs to; the API also echoes it inside the pay template body, which is the provenance used here.

columns.name: pay_template_earning_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this template line; the stable line key.

columns.name: earning_templates
columns.description: Zero-based position in the template's earningTemplates array, preserving Xero's display order; provenance is the array itself.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Which earnings rate the line applies; join xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates to learn whether the line is RatePerUnit or FixedAmount and which columns below are live.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Default rate per unit for this line, NZD; only meaningful for rate-per-unit earnings. Multiply by number_of_units for the per-period default amount.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Default units per period (the spec's description repeats 'rate per unit' — it is the unit count). Zero units with a set rate means the line waits for timesheet input.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Fixed NZD amount per period for fixed-amount earnings; mutually exclusive with rate x units. Per-period template cost is COALESCE(fixed_amount, rate_per_unit * number_of_units).

columns.name: name
columns.description: Read-only display name of the template line, echoing the earnings rate name at assignment time; the live name is on the joined earnings rate.

joins.note: One template per employee, many lines.
Rate type and expense account for the line.

examples.question: Configured per-period template pay by employee
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, SUM(COALESCE(fixed_amount, rate_per_unit * number_of_units)) AS template_pay_per_period
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_pay_template_earnings
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one payment-method record per employee
tables.description: How the employee is paid: Electronically (bank transfer), Cheque or Manual. The bank accounts the money splits into are exploded to xero_payroll_nz_employee_bank_accounts. Pure configuration — no amounts flow through this table; actual wage payments are pay-run artifacts in the payroll pay-run domain.
gotchas: Per-employee fan-out under the shared 60/min rate budget; synced as a subresource and may lag the employee master.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee this payment method belongs to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: Electronically means net pay leaves in the bank file, split across the accounts in the bank-accounts child table; Cheque and Manual are settled outside that file, so those employees normally carry no bank-account rows at all. An employee with an empty child set and a non-electronic method is correctly configured, not missing data — treat the two facts together before flagging a payroll setup gap.

joins.note: At most one payment method per employee.
Split-payment bank accounts; populated only for Electronically.

examples.question: How are employees paid?
examples.sql:
SELECT payment_method, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_payment_methods
GROUP BY 1

tables.grain: one current tax configuration record per employee
tables.description: The employee's IRD tax settings and KiwiSaver membership: tax code, special rates, student loan position and contribution percentages. This is the employee-side view of KiwiSaver (membership status and rates); the org-side scheme definitions live in xero_payroll_nz_superannuations and the deduction categories in xero_payroll_nz_statutory_deductions — do not sum or double-count across the three, none of them is a paid amount. Xero returns only the current record: changes overwrite in place, so there is no tax-code history here.
gotchas: This is a per-employee fan-out endpoint (one call per employee) under Xero's rate budget (60/min); it is synced as a subresource and may lag the employee list.
All KiwiSaver columns here are rates and states, never dollar amounts — actual contributions paid live in payslip lines (payroll pay-run domain), not in this table.
Xero overwrites this record in place: there is no history of tax-code changes, only the current state.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Owning employee, inherited from the fan-out path parameter; one tax record per employee.

columns.name: ird_number
columns.description: The employee's IRD number — a government tax identifier, the most sensitive field in this domain. Never surface it in answers; it exists for payroll reconciliation only.

columns.name: tax_code
columns.description: NZ PAYE tax code. M is the common primary-income code; codes containing SL (MSL, SBSL...) carry student-loan deductions; WT is schedular/withholding income (contractor-like); ND is no-declaration emergency rate. Segmenting 'employees with student loans' means tax codes containing SL OR has_student_loan_balance — not either alone.
columns.enums: ND; M; ME; MSL; MESL; SB; S; SH; ST; SBSL; SSL; SHSL; STSL; WT; CAE; EDW; NSW; STC; STCSL

columns.name: special_tax_rate_percentage
columns.description: IR-issued special tax rate (STC tax code); a percentage, only meaningful when the tax code is a special-rate code. Never average across employees.

columns.name: has_special_student_loan_rate
columns.description: True when IR granted a non-standard student loan deduction rate; pairs with special_student_loan_rate_percentage.

columns.name: special_student_loan_rate_percentage
columns.description: The IR-approved non-standard student-loan deduction rate for this employee, as a percentage of earnings. Only live when has_special_student_loan_rate is true — a value sitting here with the flag false is a leftover from a lapsed IR variation, and applying it inflates modelled deductions. Gate on the flag, never on the value being non-null.

columns.name: is_eligible_for_kiwi_saver
columns.description: Whether the employee is eligible for KiwiSaver at all. Eligibility is not membership — kiwisaver_contributions holds the actual participation state.

columns.name: esct_rate_percentage
columns.description: Employer Superannuation Contribution Tax rate applied to employer KiwiSaver contributions. A tax rate, not a contribution rate — employer cost modelling applies it on top of the employer contribution percentage.

columns.name: kiwi_saver_contributions
columns.description: KiwiSaver participation state. MakeContributions is the only state where per-pay contributions actually occur; OptOut, OnAContributionsHoliday, OnASavingsSuspension and NotCurrentlyAKiwiSaverMember all mean zero current contributions even though the rate columns may still hold values. Any 'KiwiSaver participation' metric filters this, not the rate columns.

columns.name: kiwi_saver_employee_contribution_rate_percentage
columns.description: Employee's elected contribution rate (3/4/6/8/10 percent typically). A rate, not a dollar amount, and stale for non-contributing members — gate on kiwisaver_contributions = 'MakeContributions' before using.

columns.name: kiwi_saver_employer_contribution_rate_percentage
columns.description: Employer's KiwiSaver contribution rate for this employee, as a percentage of gross. A rate, not a cost: employer on-cost = gross earnings x this rate, and ESCT is then charged on that contribution via esct_rate_percentage. The NZ statutory employer minimum has moved over time and is scheduled to keep rising, so never hard-code a floor or infer non-compliance from a comparison to a remembered number — read the stored rate and the effective date of the answer.

columns.name: kiwi_saver_employer_salary_sacrifice_contribution_rate_percentage
columns.description: Portion of the employer contribution funded by salary sacrifice. Part of, not additional to, the package — adding it on top of the employer rate double-counts.

columns.name: kiwi_saver_opt_out_date
columns.description: Date an opt-out from KiwiSaver took effect; populated alongside kiwisaver_contributions = 'OptOut'. Presence of a date is not a current-state test — someone who opted out and later re-joined keeps the historical date while their state moves to MakeContributions. Read kiwisaver_contributions for participation and use this only to date the event.

columns.name: kiwi_saver_contribution_holiday_end_date
columns.description: When a contributions holiday / savings suspension expires; after this date contributions resume, so 'currently suspended' checks this date as well as the state.

columns.name: has_student_loan_balance
columns.description: True when IR notified a remaining student-loan balance, which caps final deductions. Distinct from having an SL tax code — an employee can carry SL deductions with no balance letter on file.

columns.name: student_loan_balance
columns.description: The balance from the IR letter, in NZD, as at student_loan_as_at. A point-in-time notified figure, not a live balance — it does not decrease as deductions are made.

columns.name: student_loan_as_at
columns.description: Date of the IR student-loan letter that student_loan_balance was copied from.

joins.note: Every employee has at most one current tax record.

examples.question: KiwiSaver participation rate among current staff
examples.sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.kiwi_saver_contributions = 'MakeContributions') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_contributing
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employees e
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employee_tax t ON t.employee_id = e.employee_id
WHERE e.start_date <= CURRENT_DATE AND (e.end_date IS NULL OR e.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)

examples.question: Employees with student loan deductions
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, t.tax_code
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_tax t
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id
WHERE t.tax_code LIKE '%SL%' OR t.has_student_loan_balance

tables.grain: one effective-dated working pattern per employee
tables.description: Header of an employee's regular-week working pattern, effective from a date; the actual hours-per-weekday grid lives in xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_weeks. Patterns are effective-dated like salaries: the pattern in force at date D is the one with the greatest effective_from <= D per employee. Only employees whose salary record uses work_pattern_type RegularWeek have meaningful patterns.
gotchas: The list endpoint returns headers only; hours require the per-pattern detail call (a second fan-out layer) — patterns can be synced while their week grids lag.

columns.name: payee_working_pattern_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the working pattern (spelled payeeWorkingPatternID in the API); the key the working-weeks detail hangs off.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee the pattern belongs to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: effective_from
columns.description: Date the pattern takes effect. Multiple patterns per employee form a history — 'current pattern' is the max effective_from <= today, not the latest row synced.

joins.note: Effective-dated history; employees on DaysAndHours salaries may have none.
The per-weekday hours grid, one row per week of a repeating cycle.

examples.question: Employees whose working pattern actually changed this year (excluding their first-ever pattern)
examples.sql:
SELECT wp.employee_id,
       COUNT(*) AS changes_this_year,
       MAX(wp.effective_from) AS latest_change
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_patterns wp
WHERE wp.effective_from >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_patterns prior
    WHERE prior.employee_id = wp.employee_id
      AND prior.effective_from < wp.effective_from
  )
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one week of a working pattern's repeating cycle, keyed by pattern and array position
tables.description: The hours grid of a working pattern: hours to be worked on each weekday. A pattern can repeat over multiple weeks (alternating rosters), hence one row per week in the cycle. Contracted hours, not hours worked — actuals come from timesheets; comparing this grid with timesheet lines finds overtime and under-utilization.
gotchas: Weekly contracted hours = SUM of the seven day columns PER week_ordinal; summing across the whole pattern for a multi-week roster overstates a single week's hours — divide by the cycle length instead.
Second-layer fan-out (one call per pattern) under the 60/min budget; grids can be temporarily missing for freshly-created patterns.

Patterns are effective-dated history, so joining every week grid an employee has ever had and dividing by the cycle length inflates their weekly hours by the number of superseded patterns. Pick the one pattern in force at the reporting date FIRST, then average its weeks.

columns.name: payee_working_pattern_id
columns.description: Parent working pattern, from the detail record's own id field.

columns.name: working_weeks
columns.description: Zero-based week position in the repeating cycle (weeks carry no id); provenance is the workingWeeks array. Week 0 then week 1 alternate for a two-week roster.

columns.name: effective_from
columns.description: Effective date denormalized from the detail record so the grid is usable without joining back to the header.

columns.name: monday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Monday of this week in the cycle. A zero is a real roster fact, not missing data: it marks a non-working day, which is what NZ's 'otherwise working day' test and every leave-in-days conversion key off. Reading null-vs-zero as the same thing silently turns a rostered day off into an unknown.

columns.name: tuesday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Tuesday of this cycle week. Compare against timesheet lines dated on a Tuesday to separate rostered hours from overtime — and use the pattern that was in force on the work date, since a later pattern does not restate history.

columns.name: wednesday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Wednesday of this cycle week. Part-time staff commonly carry a mid-week zero, which is why weekly totals must sum all seven columns rather than assume five equal working days.

columns.name: thursday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Thursday of this cycle week. Supplies the per-day divisor when leave booked in hours has to be reported as days off, so a wrong value here rescales absence reporting rather than pay.

columns.name: friday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Friday of this cycle week. Nine-day-fortnight rosters put their zero here in one week of a two-week cycle only — the reason annualising must divide by the cycle length instead of reading a single week.

columns.name: saturday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Saturday of this cycle week. Non-zero identifies weekend-rostered staff for penal- and overtime-rate analysis, and decides whether a Saturday public holiday is an otherwise working day for this person — so it changes entitlement, not just scheduling.

columns.name: sunday
columns.description: Contracted hours for the Sunday of this cycle week. Like Saturday it drives public-holiday entitlement: a Sunday public holiday is only paid when Sunday is an otherwise working day for the employee, so a zero here removes an entitlement rather than merely recording a day off.

joins.note: Header carries employee and effective date.

examples.question: Average contracted weekly hours per employee under the pattern currently in force
examples.sql:
WITH current_pattern AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (employee_id) employee_id, payee_working_pattern_id
  FROM xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_patterns
  WHERE effective_from <= CURRENT_DATE
  ORDER BY employee_id, effective_from DESC
)
SELECT cp.employee_id,
       SUM(ww.monday + ww.tuesday + ww.wednesday + ww.thursday
           + ww.friday + ww.saturday + ww.sunday)
       / COUNT(*) AS avg_weekly_hours
FROM current_pattern cp
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_weeks ww ON ww.payee_working_pattern_id = cp.payee_working_pattern_id
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one employee record per person employed under the tenant's NZ payroll
tables.description: The worker master for NZ Payroll v2: identity, home address, employment dates and the payroll calendar the person is paid on. This is heavy-PII reference data — names, DOB, address, contact details — not a fact table. Employment status is inferred, not declared: an employee with a null end_date is current; a populated end_date is a termination effective that day. A tenant has AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two — if this table is empty the org simply doesn't run NZ payroll, and no cross-region union with xero_payroll_au_employees/xero_payroll_uk_employees is ever valid.
gotchas: There is no status flag: 'active employee' is derived from dates (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= as-of date, AND start_date <= as-of date). Counting all rows counts every ex-employee ever paid.
Payroll regions are exclusive per tenant. Never UNION this with AU/UK payroll employee tables; at most one of the three is populated.
created_date_utc is when the record entered Xero, not when the person was hired — orgs that migrated to Xero show created dates clustered on the migration day.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable employee identifier; the join key every per-employee fan-out table (tax, leave, pay templates, salary) hangs off.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Honorific (Mr/Ms/Dr). Presentation only — never use it to infer gender; the gender column exists for that and is itself optional.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Legal first name as entered in payroll. Combine with last_name for display; do not use name pairs as a person key — employee_id is the key and duplicate names are common.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Legal last name as entered in payroll. Display alongside first_name; never a join or grouping key — employee_id is the identity.

columns.name: date_of_birth
columns.description: Employee's date of birth, required by Xero. Sensitive PII: use for age-band analytics only under governance; never expose raw in answers.

columns.name: address_address_line1
columns.description: First line of the employee's home address (flattened from the nested Address object). Home address, not a work location — do not use it to place employees at business sites.

columns.name: address_address_line2
columns.description: Optional continuation of the home address (unit, building, care-of). Usually null, and a populated value is not a second address — line1 and line2 are one address and must be concatenated, never counted or compared independently.

columns.name: address_city
columns.description: City/town of the home address. Xero's docs label both city and suburb as 'Suburb' — city is the required one; treat it as the town/city and suburb as the finer locality.

columns.name: address_suburb
columns.description: Suburb of the home address; optional and often null even when city is set.

columns.name: address_post_code
columns.description: Postcode of the home address. Keep as text — NZ postcodes have leading zeros that integer casting destroys.

columns.name: address_country_name
columns.description: Country of the home address; free text, not an ISO code, and usually null for NZ-resident employees — don't filter on it to find NZ staff.

columns.name: email
columns.description: Employee's email address. This is the payroll contact address, which may differ from any xero_users login email — do not join people on email alone.

columns.name: gender
columns.description: Self-declared gender, only M or F in this API version and optional — null is common. Gender pay-gap analysis must report the null cohort separately, not silently drop it.

columns.name: phone_number
columns.description: Contact number captured for payroll correspondence, stored exactly as typed — no country code or spacing normalisation, so the same person appears as '021 123 4567' in one tenant and '+6421 1234567' in another. Never a matching key across systems; resolve people on employee_id.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Employment start date as at the time the record was requested. Headcount as-of-date D is start_date <= D AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= D) — counting rows without the date window overstates headcount with future starters and leavers.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Employment end date; null while employed. Non-null means terminated (or a scheduled termination) — every 'current headcount' or 'active staff' answer must filter end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURRENT_DATE, or ex-employees inflate the count.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The pay-run calendar this employee is paid on. Join to xero_payroll_nz_pay_run_calendars for frequency (Weekly/Monthly...); employees on different calendars are paid on different cycles, so 'this pay period' is per-calendar, not org-wide.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change to the employee record; the incremental-sync watermark. Not an employment event date — never use it for tenure math.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When the record was created in Xero — a data-entry timestamp that can postdate start_date by years for migrated employees. Tenure comes from start_date, never from this.

columns.name: job_title
columns.description: Free-text job title; uncontrolled vocabulary ('Dev', 'Developer', 'Software Developer' are three values). Group with care or via mapping, not raw equality.

columns.name: engagement_type
columns.description: Xero's classification of the employment agreement behind the role. The spec declares NO value set for this field, so the org's actual strings must be inspected before it is used as a segment — never hard-code labels or assume a fixed vocabulary. Rows whose engagement is fixed-term also carry fixed_term_end_date, and employees engaged casually typically have no working pattern at all, so averaging contracted hours across engagement types without segmenting blends incomparable populations.

columns.name: fixed_term_end_date
columns.description: Contractual end of a fixed-term engagement. It is a plan, not a termination: the actual leaving date is end_date, and the two can differ when a contract ends early or is extended.

joins.note: Pay frequency and period boundaries for this employee.
Tax code, IRD number and KiwiSaver membership settings.

examples.question: Current headcount by engagement type
examples.sql:
SELECT engagement_type, COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employees
WHERE start_date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Employees leaving in the next 60 days
examples.sql:
SELECT first_name, last_name, end_date
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employees
WHERE end_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND CURRENT_DATE + 60
ORDER BY end_date

tables.grain: one org-level leave type per leave type id
tables.description: The org's leave-type catalogue: annual, sick, bereavement, public holidays, unpaid and custom types, with whether they are paid and how their units are expressed. The org-wide definition — per-employee accrual quantities live in xero_payroll_nz_employee_leave_types, and this table's typeOfUnits is the decoding key for all leave-unit aggregation.
gotchas: Sick-leave analysis that groups by name breaks on orgs with renamed or duplicated custom types; group by leave_type_id and label with name.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the leave type; the join key from leave requests, balances and per-employee configurations.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name ('Annual Leave', 'Sick Leave'...). Statutory NZ types have conventional names but custom types are free text — prefer id-based logic.

columns.name: is_paid_leave
columns.description: Whether taking this leave pays the employee. Absence-cost questions must split paid from unpaid — unpaid leave reduces pay rather than costing it, the exact opposite effect on the wage bill.

columns.name: show_on_payslip
columns.description: Payslip display flag for the balance; presentation only, no effect on accrual or payment.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change to the type; sync watermark.

columns.name: is_active
columns.description: True when the type can be used on new leave; the ActiveOnly request parameter filters on this, so the sync must NOT pass it or retired types referenced by history disappear.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: Unit leave of this type is paid in (Hours for most; Weeks for NZ annual leave entitlement under the Holidays Act). The reason a blanket SUM over leave units is wrong.

columns.name: type_of_units_to_accrue
columns.description: Unit the type accrues in; can differ from type_of_units (accrue weeks, take hours) — conversion happens via the employee's working pattern.

joins.note: Leave requests of this type.
Current per-employee balances of this type.

examples.question: Paid vs unpaid leave types
examples.sql:
SELECT is_paid_leave, COUNT(*) AS types
FROM xero_payroll_nz_leave_types
WHERE is_active
GROUP BY 1

tables.grain: one pay-run calendar (pay frequency definition) per payroll calendar id
tables.description: The org's pay cycles: frequency (weekly through annual), the CURRENT period's start/end and the payment date. Every employee is attached to exactly one calendar, and pay runs are generated per calendar per period. The period dates roll forward as runs are posted — they describe the next/current period, not a fixed anchor, so period math for history must come from pay runs themselves.
gotchas: period_start/end describe the CURRENT open period only. Historical period boundaries live on pay runs — reconstructing history by subtracting frequencies from these dates breaks across calendar edits.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the calendar; employees and pay runs reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The org's own label for the pay cycle ('Weekly Wages', 'Monthly Salaries'). Free text that is not kept in step with the cadence, so a calendar still named 'Fortnightly' can legitimately be Monthly after the org changed its cycle — read calendar_type for the frequency and never infer it from this string.

columns.name: calendar_type
columns.description: Pay frequency. Annualizing a per-period amount multiplies by the periods-per-year this implies (Weekly 52, Fortnightly 26, FourWeekly 13, Monthly 12, TwiceMonthly 24, Quarterly 4, Annual 1) — using 26 for FourWeekly is the classic annualization bug.
columns.enums: Weekly; Fortnightly; FourWeekly; Monthly; Annual; Quarterly; TwiceMonthly

columns.name: period_start_date
columns.description: Start of the calendar's current/next open period; rolls forward each posted run. Not the calendar's inception date.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: End of the current/next open period; with period_start_date defines the window timesheets and leave will fall into for the next run.

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: The date wages for the current period hit bank accounts — cash-flow forecasting reads this, and it can fall in a different month than the period it pays for (accrual vs cash timing).

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp; changes every time the period rolls, so it is noisy as a change signal.

joins.note: Employees paid on this cycle.

examples.question: Headcount by pay frequency
examples.sql:
SELECT c.calendar_type, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_nz_employees e
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_run_calendars c ON c.payroll_calendar_id = e.payroll_calendar_id
WHERE e.start_date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (e.end_date IS NULL OR e.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one NZ pay run — a single processing (scheduled, unscheduled, or earlier-year-update) of one payroll calendar period
tables.description: The header record for every time NZ payroll was (or is being) processed, and the ONLY place this domain carries dates and a posting status. totalCost is Xero's own employer-cost figure for the run and totalPay is the net cash that reaches employees; they answer different questions and differ by every withholding and employer-side contribution, so never present one as the other. Draft runs are returned by the API alongside Posted ones and their numbers change until posting, so every payroll total must filter pay_run_status = 'Posted'. NZ payroll runs entirely in NZD: there are no currency or rate columns anywhere in this domain, and none are needed. These tables are populated only for tenants whose payroll region is NZ.
gotchas: GET /PayRuns returns Draft runs. A Draft's totals move until posting, and a discarded Draft disappears from the API entirely (hard delete) — the ingester detects removals by full identity rescan, and every analytical query filters pay_run_status = 'Posted'.

total_cost vs total_pay is the employer-cost vs net-cash split. Reporting total_pay as 'payroll cost' understates spend by PAYE, employee deductions and employer-side contributions; reporting total_cost as 'cash out to staff' overstates it by the same.

Joining to payslips fans the run row out once per employee. SUM(r.total_cost) after that join multiplies the run's cost by its headcount — aggregate run columns from xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs alone, and aggregate employee-level money from the payslip tables alone. Never mix levels in one SUM.
EarlierYearUpdate runs restate a previous tax year. Summing them into the month of their payment_date silently rewrites history in trend charts.
PayRun has no modified-watermark field. Incremental sync re-scans the run list (cheap — a few hundred rows per tenant-year) and relies on payslip lastEdited for detail-level change detection.

Payroll is region-exclusive: a tenant has NZ or AU or UK payroll, never two. For an AU or UK tenant these tables are legitimately empty, which means 'no NZ payroll', not 'no payroll' — answer from xero_payroll_au_* / xero_payroll_uk_* instead, and never UNION the regions into one payroll total.

columns.name: pay_run_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the pay run and the row key; the fan-out parameter for pulling this run's payslips.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The payroll calendar (pay frequency schedule) this run was generated from. Group by it to separate the weekly wage cycle from the monthly salary cycle — mixing calendars in a per-run average produces a meaningless blended figure. The calendar entity itself is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: period_start_date
columns.description: First day of the earnings period this run pays for. Use the period dates for labour-cost accrual questions ('what did March labour cost'), not paymentDate — a run paid on 3 April can cover work done in March.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: Last day of the earnings period. Periods of different calendars overlap freely; do not treat (period_start_date, period_end_date) as unique — unscheduled runs reuse the same period.

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: The day employees are paid — the cash-basis date, and the date that fixes the PAYE filing period with IRD. Cash-flow questions bucket by this; accrual questions bucket by the period dates. The two commonly straddle a month boundary.

columns.name: total_cost
columns.description: Xero's own employer-cost total for the run, in NZD — the authoritative answer to 'what did this payroll cost us', and the figure any payslip-level reconstruction must be reconciled against. Using total_pay instead understates cost by every withholding and every employer-side contribution. The spec does not publish the composition, so do not assume it equals gross + employer taxes + employer super: ESCT may already sit inside the employer superannuation figure rather than on top of it, and that difference is real money. Prefer this column over rebuilding cost from payslip columns.

columns.name: total_pay
columns.description: Net cash paid to employees for the run (after PAYE, deductions and statutory withholdings, plus reimbursements). This is the bank-outflow figure that should reconcile to the wages payment in xero_bank_transactions — it is NOT payroll expense.

columns.name: pay_run_status
columns.description: Draft runs are in-progress and mutable — their totals and payslips change or vanish entirely if the draft is discarded. Every aggregate in this domain must filter to 'Posted' (directly here, via a join from the payslip and line tables) or drafts inflate and destabilise history.

columns.name: pay_run_type
columns.description: Scheduled runs follow the calendar; Unscheduled runs are legitimate off-cycle pay (bonuses, corrections, final pay) and belong in cost totals; EarlierYearUpdate runs restate a prior tax year and will distort period-over-period trend lines if bucketed by their payment_date — exclude or handle them explicitly in time series.

columns.name: calendar_type
columns.description: Pay frequency of the calendar behind this run. Needed to annualise correctly: a Weekly run's totals ×52, a Monthly run's ×12 — averaging per-run amounts across mixed frequencies without this column is the classic wrong answer for 'average pay run size'.
columns.enums: Weekly; Fortnightly; FourWeekly; Monthly; Annual; Quarterly; TwiceMonthly

columns.name: posted_date_time
columns.description: When the run was posted (finalised); null while Draft, which makes it the cheapest test for 'has this run actually been committed'. Audit stamp, not a business date — bucket money by payment_date or the period dates, never by this. Despite the DateTime name the spec types it as a date string, so treat any time-of-day component as unreliable and do not compute sub-day posting latency from it; posted-vs-payment-date lag in whole days is the safe use.

columns.name: pay_slips
columns.description: The payslip array as embedded on the pay run response, verbatim and possibly empty. The spec declares the field on PayRun but guarantees nothing about the list endpoint populating it, so this column is never a reliable population of payslips — xero_payroll_nz_payslips, ingested from GET /PaySlips, is the ONLY analytical payslip surface. Treat this as run-level audit evidence of what the run reported at scan time; aggregating out of it double-counts against the payslip tables and, when the array is sparse, silently undercounts instead. Carries employee names and, inside paymentLines, raw bank-account details — hence pii.

joins.note: Every payslip belongs to exactly one run. total_pay is expected to reconcile to SUM(payslip.total_pay) for a Posted run; total_cost has NO single payslip counterpart (there is no PaySlip.totalCost) and must not be assumed equal to any sum of payslip columns. This join fans out — never SUM run-level columns across it.

examples.question: Monthly employer payroll cost and net wages paid, current runs only
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(total_cost) AS employer_cost,
       SUM(total_pay)  AS net_paid
FROM xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs
WHERE pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Off-cycle (unscheduled) pay runs in the last year and what they cost
examples.sql:
SELECT payment_date, period_start_date, period_end_date, total_cost
FROM xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs
WHERE pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND pay_run_type = 'Unscheduled'
  AND payment_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months'
ORDER BY payment_date DESC

tables.grain: one voluntary/contractual deduction line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.deductionLines)
tables.description: Non-statutory deductions withheld from pay: payroll giving, social club, union fees, employee super top-ups beyond KiwiSaver minima. Rolls up to PaySlip.totalDeductions. Statutory withholdings (student loan, child support, employee KiwiSaver) are NOT here — they live in the statutory-deduction-lines table — so 'everything withheld from staff' must union both families.
gotchas: This family excludes statutory withholdings. Student loan, child support and employee KiwiSaver are in xero_payroll_nz_payslip_statutory_deduction_lines — 'total withheld' requires both.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.deductionLines
columns.description: Minted array position; with pay_slip_id, the row key (deduction lines carry no line id of their own — deductionTypeID is a type reference and can repeat).

columns.name: deduction_type_id
columns.description: The configured deduction type applied — the durable GROUP BY for 'deductions by kind'. The type master (name, category) is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: The deduction's UI label at pay time (the spec's 'earnings rate' wording is copy-paste boilerplate — this names the deduction). Snapshot; renames split history, so group by deduction_type_id.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Dollars withheld by this line in NZD — the additive measure, reducing net pay. Always positive-signed as a deduction; do not negate before summing into 'total withheld'.

columns.name: subject_to_tax
columns.description: Whether the deducted amount is still inside taxable earnings. The spec says only 'identifies if the deduction is subject to tax' and does not name the pre-tax/post-tax convention, so the literal reading — true = the amount remains taxable, i.e. withheld after PAYE and not reducing it; false = withheld before tax and shrinking taxable pay — is an inference, not a documented fact. Verify it against one payslip's employee tax line before labelling a report 'pre-tax vs post-tax': inverting the split makes every reconstructed PAYE figure unreconcilable. Nullable, so three-valued logic applies — NOT subject_to_tax silently drops null rows from both buckets.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: The percentage rate for percentage-based deductions; null for fixed-dollar ones. A rate — never summed, and not a substitute for amount, which is the money actually withheld.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: Voluntary deductions withheld by type this year
examples.sql:
-- Grouped by deduction_type_id so a renamed deduction stays one row.
SELECT l.deduction_type_id,
       MAX(l.display_name) AS label_sample,
       SUM(l.amount) AS withheld
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_deduction_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC

examples.question: Deductions split by the subject_to_tax flag, by month
examples.sql:
-- Reported by the raw flag, not by a 'pre-tax'/'post-tax' label: the spec states only
-- that the flag identifies whether the deduction is subject to tax, and getting that
-- direction backwards inverts the whole split. subject_to_tax is nullable, so the
-- unknown bucket is reported rather than silently dropped from both sides.
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(l.amount) FILTER (WHERE l.subject_to_tax IS TRUE)  AS subject_to_tax,
       SUM(l.amount) FILTER (WHERE l.subject_to_tax IS FALSE) AS not_subject_to_tax,
       SUM(l.amount) FILTER (WHERE l.subject_to_tax IS NULL)  AS flag_unknown,
       SUM(l.amount) AS total_deducted
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_deduction_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one ordinary earnings line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.earningsLines)
tables.description: Ordinary (non-leave, non-timesheet) earnings detail: salary, ordinary hours, allowances, bonuses — one row per earnings rate applied on the payslip. amount is the authoritative paid figure; ratePerUnit × numberOfUnits does not always reproduce it (rounding, average-daily-pay substitution, fixed-amount rates), so aggregate amount and treat rate/units as explanatory. This family alone is NOT gross pay — leave and timesheet earnings live in their sibling tables and the three partition PaySlip.grossEarnings.
gotchas: This table alone is not gross pay: leave earnings and timesheet earnings are sibling families. SUM here understates gross for any employee on leave or paid from timesheets — use PaySlip.grossEarnings for the true total.
amount is authoritative; ratePerUnit × numberOfUnits differs on rounding, fixed-amount rates and average-daily-pay lines. Recomputing pay from rate × units silently loses money.
Lines under Draft pay runs mutate and can disappear; always join payslip → run and filter payRunStatus = 'Posted'.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.earningsLines
columns.description: Minted position of the line in the payslip's earningsLines array; with pay_slip_id it forms the stable row key (earnings_line_id is not guaranteed present on every line).

columns.name: earnings_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this earnings line when assigned. Not the row key here — use (pay_slip_id, line_index).

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The pay-item (earnings rate) this line was paid under — the correct GROUP BY for 'pay by type' questions. The rate entity itself (name, rate type, multiplier) is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain; display_name is the local fallback label.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: UI label of the earnings rate at pay time. Convenient for ad-hoc filters ('%overtime%') but it is a snapshot — renamed rates split into two labels across history, so durable grouping uses earnings_rate_id.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Per-unit pay rate (e.g. hourly rate) for unit-based lines; null/irrelevant for fixed-amount lines. A rate, not a measure: never SUM it — average it weighted by number_of_units if you need a blended rate.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units paid, usually hours. 'Hours worked' analysis sums this — but only across lines of unit-based rates; fixed-amount salary lines carry no meaningful units, and units of different rate types (hours vs days) must not be pooled.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: The flat amount for lines whose earnings rate is of RateType Fixed; null otherwise. Do not add it to amount — amount already reflects it. Its usefulness is diagnostic: distinguishing salaried (fixed) from hourly (rate×units) pay.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: What this line actually paid, in NZD — THE additive measure of the table. Trust it over ratePerUnit × numberOfUnits, which drifts on rounding and average-daily-pay substitutions.

columns.name: is_linked_to_timesheet
columns.description: Spec-documented as false for ordinary earnings lines (timesheet-sourced pay materialises in the timesheetEarningsLines family instead). If you see true here, treat it as a data-quality signal, not a category.

columns.name: is_average_daily_pay_rate
columns.description: True when the Holidays Act average daily pay rate replaced the ordinary rate for this line — the reason rate_per_unit × number_of_units can legitimately disagree with amount.

columns.name: is_system_generated
columns.description: True for lines Xero created automatically (calendar-generated base pay) versus manually added ones. Useful to isolate manual payroll interventions; irrelevant to totals — both kinds are real pay.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs for the mandatory Posted filter and payment/period dates.

examples.question: Gross ordinary pay by earnings rate, last quarter
examples.sql:
-- Grouped by earnings_rate_id, not display_name: a renamed rate would otherwise
-- split into two rows and neither would be the rate's real total.
SELECT l.earnings_rate_id,
       MAX(l.display_name) AS label_sample,
       SUM(l.amount) AS paid
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '3 months'
  AND r.payment_date <  date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC

examples.question: Overtime spend by month
examples.sql:
-- display_name matching is a heuristic: it misses overtime rates named otherwise
-- ('Time and a half', 'Penal rate') and catches anything containing the word. Resolve
-- the real earnings_rate_id set from the NZ payroll settings domain for a reportable
-- number, and note overtime paid from timesheets lands in the timesheet-earnings table.
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(l.amount) AS overtime_paid
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND l.display_name ILIKE '%overtime%'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one employee-side tax line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.employeeTaxLines)
tables.description: Tax withheld FROM the employee — PAYE under the payslip's tax code — one row per tax component, rolling up to PaySlip.totalEmployeeTaxes. The sibling employer-tax table shares the identical TaxLine shape but means money the EMPLOYER owes on top of pay; the two tables must never be unioned into a single 'tax' number without labelling direction.
gotchas: Employee-side only. Adding xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employer_tax_lines produces a number that is neither what employees paid nor what the employer owes — keep directions separate.
Student-loan and child-support withholdings are NOT tax lines; they are statutory deductions. 'Everything remitted to IRD' spans this table plus statutory deductions plus employer taxes.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.employeeTaxLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: tax_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this tax line when the API supplies one. Traceability back to the raw payload, not the row key — the spec marks it optional, and because PaySlip embeds the same TaxLine shape twice, an id seen here can also appear in the employer-tax table; dedupe or union on it and you merge opposite-direction money.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Human label of the tax component (e.g. 'PAYE'). Display text — group by global_tax_type_id for durable analysis.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: NZD withheld from the employee by this component — the additive measure, reducing net pay and remitted to IRD by the payment date's filing period.

columns.name: global_tax_type_id
columns.description: Xero's tax-type code for the component — the stable GROUP BY across payslips and tenants (descriptions vary, this doesn't).

columns.name: manual_adjustment
