columns.description: True when the calculated tax was hand-overridden. Manual PAYE adjustments are the first place to look when withheld tax fails to reconcile with IRD filings.

joins.note: Then to the run: filter payRunStatus = 'Posted', and bucket by payment_date — the date that fixes the IRD filing period.

examples.question: PAYE withheld by month (IRD filing view)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(l.amount) AS paye_withheld
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employee_tax_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Payslips with manually adjusted employee tax
examples.sql:
SELECT p.pay_slip_id, p.employee_id, r.payment_date, l.description, l.amount
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employee_tax_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND l.manual_adjustment
ORDER BY r.payment_date DESC

tables.grain: one employer-side tax line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.employerTaxLines)
tables.description: Tax the EMPLOYER owes on top of pay — in NZ practice, ESCT on employer superannuation contributions — one row per component, rolling up to PaySlip.totalEmployerTaxes. Identical TaxLine shape to the employee-tax table but opposite direction: these amounts never touch the employee's net pay, and they belong in employer-cost analysis (gross + employer taxes + employer super).
gotchas: Employer-side only — these amounts are invisible to employees. Subtracting them from gross fabricates a lower take-home; omitting them from cost understates payroll spend.

ESCT relates to the superannuation lines and is stored apart from them by design. Do NOT assume total employer super cost = contributions + ESCT: ESCT is levied on the contribution in NZ, so if the super lines are already gross of it, adding these amounts double-counts the tax. Settle it by reconciling against xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs.total_cost.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.employerTaxLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: tax_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this tax line when the API supplies one. Traceability back to the raw payload, not the row key — the spec marks it optional, and because PaySlip embeds the same TaxLine shape twice, an id seen here can also appear in the employer-tax table; dedupe or union on it and you merge opposite-direction money.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Human label of the employer tax component (e.g. 'ESCT'). Display text — group by global_tax_type_id for durable analysis.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: NZD the employer owes for this component — an additive employer COST. Never subtract from gross when computing take-home; never merge with employee tax into one 'tax' figure.

columns.name: global_tax_type_id
columns.description: Xero's tax-type code for the employer-side component (ESCT in NZ practice) — the durable GROUP BY, since the free-text description varies by tenant and over time. The same code space is used by the employee tax lines, so grouping on it across both tables merges withholdings with employer costs; always keep the source table as a dimension.

columns.name: manual_adjustment
columns.description: True when the calculated employer tax was hand-overridden — the audit flag when ESCT fails to reconcile with contributions × ESCT rate.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: ESCT (employer tax) by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(l.amount) AS employer_tax
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employer_tax_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Employer super contributions and ESCT this year, reported side by side
examples.sql:
-- Deliberately two columns, not a sum: see this table's ESCT gotcha before adding them.
SELECT SUM(s.amount) AS contributions, SUM(t.employer_tax) AS esct
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslips p
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT pay_slip_id, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_superannuation_lines GROUP BY 1) s ON s.pay_slip_id = p.pay_slip_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT pay_slip_id, SUM(amount) AS employer_tax FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employer_tax_lines GROUP BY 1) t ON t.pay_slip_id = p.pay_slip_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)

tables.grain: one leave accrual line on one payslip — units of one leave type accrued in one pay period (position within PaySlip.leaveAccrualLines)
tables.description: Leave ENTITLEMENT EARNED this pay period, per leave type — the accrual side of leave, with no dollar amounts. Units are whatever the leave type is configured in (NZ annual leave is commonly tracked in weeks or hours, sick leave in days or hours), so units must never be summed across leave types. This table is a period-by-period movement, not a balance: current leave balances live on the employee record in the NZ payroll employees domain, and summing accruals without subtracting leave taken does not produce a balance.
gotchas: Units carry no unit-of-measure on the row. Annual leave in weeks plus sick leave in hours is not a number — always GROUP BY leave_type_id and resolve the unit from the leave-type master.
Accruals are movements, not balances. SUM(accruals) − leave taken ≠ current balance unless you also handle opening balances and adjustments; balances live on the employee record.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.leaveAccrualLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type accruing (annual, sick, alternative holidays…). Mandatory GROUP BY before any unit arithmetic — units are only comparable within one leave type. The type master (name, unit) is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave accrued this period, in the leave type's configured unit (hours, days or weeks — the row does not say which). Additive across periods WITHIN a leave type; meaningless summed across types, and not a balance.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and period dates.

examples.question: Leave units accrued per leave type per employee this year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, l.leave_type_id, SUM(l.number_of_units) AS units_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_accrual_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Payslips where a given leave type accrued nothing (accrual gaps)
examples.sql:
SELECT p.pay_slip_id, p.employee_id, r.payment_date
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslips p
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
LEFT JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_accrual_lines l
  ON l.pay_slip_id = p.pay_slip_id
 AND l.leave_type_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'  -- substitute the leave type UUID under investigation
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND l.pay_slip_id IS NULL
ORDER BY r.payment_date DESC

tables.grain: one leave earnings line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.leaveEarningsLines)
tables.description: Pay for leave TAKEN in the period — annual leave, sick leave, public holidays — one row per leave earnings rate on the payslip. This is the money side of leave; the units-accrued side is xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_accrual_lines and the two must not be conflated. Amounts here are already inside PaySlip.grossEarnings: leave pay is a composition slice of gross, never an addition to it.
gotchas: Leave PAID here vs leave ACCRUED in the accrual-lines table are different phenomena; subtracting one family's units from the other's without matching leave types produces nonsense balances.
Amounts are already inside gross_earnings. gross + leave pay double-counts every dollar of leave.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.leaveEarningsLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: earnings_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this earnings line when the API supplies one. Deliberately NOT the row key: the spec marks it optional, so a null would collapse a payslip's lines together. Use it to trace a row back to the raw payload, and note the same id space is shared with the ordinary and timesheet earnings families — it is unique per line, not per family.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The leave earnings rate paid (annual leave, sick leave, public holiday…). The durable GROUP BY for 'leave cost by type'; the rate master lives in the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: Label of the leave rate at pay time — handy for ad-hoc filters, unstable across renames; group by earnings_rate_id for history.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Rate the leave was paid at. Under the Holidays Act this is the GREATER of ordinary and average rates, so it routinely differs from the employee's base rate — a rate, never summed.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave paid on this line (typically hours). 'Leave taken' in units sums this; but do not mix with accrual-line units, which measure entitlement earned, not taken.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Flat amount when the underlying rate is RateType Fixed; already reflected in amount — never add the two.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Leave pay for this line in NZD — the additive measure, and a slice of (not an addition to) the payslip's gross_earnings.

columns.name: is_linked_to_timesheet
columns.description: Spec-documented false for leave earnings lines; present because the line schema is shared. Not a grouping dimension.

columns.name: is_average_daily_pay_rate
columns.description: True when average daily pay (rather than relevant daily pay) priced this leave — the statutory reason rate × units and amount can disagree.

columns.name: is_system_generated
columns.description: The spec says only that this flags whether the line was system generated; in practice that separates leave Xero raised itself (typically from an approved leave request) from leave keyed straight onto the payslip. Use it to surface hand-entered leave for audit, never to filter totals — both kinds are real leave pay and both are already inside gross_earnings.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: Cost of leave paid by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(l.amount) AS leave_paid
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Share of gross pay that was leave, by employee, this year
examples.sql:
WITH slips AS (
  SELECT p.pay_slip_id, p.employee_id, p.gross_earnings
  FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslips p
  JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
  WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
    AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
), leave AS (
  SELECT pay_slip_id, SUM(amount) AS leave_pay
  FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_earnings_lines
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT s.employee_id,
       SUM(COALESCE(l.leave_pay, 0)) AS leave_pay,
       SUM(COALESCE(l.leave_pay, 0)) / NULLIF(SUM(s.gross_earnings), 0) AS share_of_gross
FROM slips s
LEFT JOIN leave l ON l.pay_slip_id = s.pay_slip_id
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one bank payment split of one payslip's net pay (position within PaySlip.paymentLines)
tables.description: How the payslip's NET pay was distributed to bank accounts — one row per destination account, summing to PaySlip.totalPay. Purely a cash-distribution breakdown: no earnings semantics at all, and the row carries raw bank account details, making this the most PII-sensitive table in the domain. Use it to reconcile payroll against the bank feed and to detect split-pay arrangements.
gotchas: Amounts are NET pay distribution — summing them alongside earnings or deduction families double-counts pay at different stages of the waterfall. They tie to total_pay, nothing else.
Raw bank account fields are on this row. Semantic-layer consumers should aggregate amounts and avoid projecting the account columns unless the question is explicitly about payment routing.
Cheque/Manual payslips may carry no meaningful payment splits — bank-feed reconciliation only holds for paymentMethod = 'Electronically'.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.paymentLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: payment_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this payment split when the API supplies one. Kept for traceability back to the raw payload rather than as the key — the spec marks it optional, and Cheque/Manual payslips can omit the split entirely, so keying on it would drop exactly the rows that make net pay fail to tie out.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: NZD paid into this bank account — sums to the payslip's total_pay (net). This is the figure to match against wage payments in xero_bank_transactions; it is NOT earnings or cost.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: Destination bank account number (NZ format) — raw employee banking PII. Restrict exposure; analytically useful only as an opaque grouping key for split-pay detection.

columns.name: sort_code
columns.description: Bank sort code of the destination account (UK-schema field; for NZ the bank/branch is generally embedded in the account number and this is often null). PII.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Account holder/nickname of the destination account as entered — PII, and a fraud-review signal when it does not resemble the employee's own name.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and the payment date the bank movement should match.

examples.question: Employees splitting net pay across more than one bank account
examples.sql:
-- Counted WITHIN a payslip. Counting distinct accounts per employee across periods
-- would flag anyone who simply changed banks as a split-pay arrangement.
SELECT p.employee_id, l.pay_slip_id, r.payment_date,
       COUNT(*) AS destination_accounts,
       SUM(l.amount) AS net_paid
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_payment_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 months'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY 4 DESC, 3 DESC

examples.question: Expected bank outflow per pay date (to reconcile against the bank feed)
examples.sql:
SELECT r.payment_date, SUM(l.amount) AS expected_outflow
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_payment_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND p.payment_method = 'Electronically'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC

tables.grain: one reimbursement line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.reimbursementLines)
tables.description: Non-taxable repayments of employee out-of-pocket expenses, paid through payroll and rolled up to PaySlip.totalReimbursements. Added to net pay AFTER tax — reimbursements are part of cash paid to employees but are neither earnings nor labour cost; leaving them in average-pay or wage-cost analysis inflates both.
gotchas: Reimbursements are inside total_pay (net cash) but outside gross_earnings. Including them in earnings or labour-cost metrics inflates both; excluding them from bank reconciliation makes net pay not tie out.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.reimbursementLines
columns.description: Minted array position; with pay_slip_id, the row key (reimbursement lines have no line id; reimbursementTypeID can repeat).

columns.name: reimbursement_type_id
columns.description: The configured reimbursement type — durable GROUP BY for 'reimbursements by kind'; the type master is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text note for this specific repayment (e.g. 'Nov mileage'). Human context only — free text is not a reliable grouping key.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Dollars repaid on this line in NZD — the additive measure. Part of cash out (inside total_pay) but excluded from gross earnings and from any wage-cost metric.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Per-unit rate for unit-based reimbursements such as mileage (the spec's 'leave earnings' wording is shared-schema boilerplate). Null for flat repayments; a rate, never summed.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units claimed for unit-based reimbursements (e.g. kilometres). Only meaningful alongside rate_per_unit; summing units across different reimbursement types mixes incompatible measures.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: Reimbursements paid through payroll by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(l.amount) AS reimbursed
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_reimbursement_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Employees with the highest expense repayments this year
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, SUM(l.amount) AS reimbursed
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_reimbursement_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

tables.grain: one statutory deduction line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.statutoryDeductionLines)
tables.description: Withholdings required by law, deducted from the employee's pay and rolled up to PaySlip.totalStatutoryDeductions: student loan repayments, child support, employee KiwiSaver contributions. Legally distinct from voluntary deductions and kept in a separate family by Xero — 'all deductions from pay' is this table plus the deduction-lines table. Amounts reduce net pay but are NOT tax lines, even though most are remitted to IRD.
gotchas: Employee KiwiSaver contributions live HERE — not in the superannuation table (employer side) and not in voluntary deductions. Total KiwiSaver flow is this family's KiwiSaver lines plus the employer super lines; do not also add ESCT from the employer tax lines unless you have confirmed the employer contribution is stated net of it, or the tax is counted twice.
Statutory ≠ tax: these amounts are excluded from totalEmployeeTaxes. A 'PAYE + deductions withheld' remittance view needs employee tax lines AND this table.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.statutoryDeductionLines
columns.description: Minted array position; with pay_slip_id, the row key (statutory lines carry no line id; the type id can repeat).

columns.name: statutory_deduction_type_id
columns.description: Which statutory obligation this is (student loan vs child support vs KiwiSaver employee contribution) — the mandatory GROUP BY; the type master is owned by the NZ payroll settings domain. Note child-support withholdings are sensitive by nature: aggregate, don't expose per-person detail casually.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: NZD actually withheld by this line — the additive measure, reducing net pay. Trust it over fixed_amount, which is the configured figure rather than the applied one.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: The configured flat withholding where the type is fixed-amount; already reflected in amount — comparing the two reveals partial withholdings (e.g. protected net pay limits).

columns.name: manual_adjustment
columns.description: True when the statutory amount was hand-overridden — the first filter when withholdings fail to match IRD deduction notices.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: Statutory withholdings by type by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       l.statutory_deduction_type_id,
       SUM(l.amount) AS withheld
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_statutory_deduction_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Lines where less than the configured fixed amount was withheld
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id, r.payment_date, l.fixed_amount, l.amount
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_statutory_deduction_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND l.fixed_amount IS NOT NULL AND l.amount < l.fixed_amount
ORDER BY r.payment_date DESC

tables.grain: one superannuation line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.superannuationLines)
tables.description: EMPLOYER superannuation contributions per payslip — in NZ practice, employer KiwiSaver — rolling up to PaySlip.totalSuperannuation. This is an employer cost on top of gross pay: the employee's own KiwiSaver contribution is a statutory deduction, and ESCT on these contributions sits in the employer tax lines. Treating these amounts as withheld from the employee misstates both take-home and cost.
gotchas: These are employer-side contributions. The employee's KiwiSaver deduction is in the statutory-deduction family — adding this table to deductions overstates what staff gave up, and omitting it from cost understates what the employer spent.

ESCT is recorded in xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employer_tax_lines, not here — but the spec does not say whether these contribution amounts are gross or net of it. In NZ, ESCT is levied ON the employer contribution, so 'super lines + ESCT' is an upper-bound reading that double-counts if the contribution is already gross. Reconcile against xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs.total_cost before publishing a total employer super cost.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.superannuationLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: superannuation_type_id
columns.description: The configured superannuation/benefit type contributed to — durable GROUP BY; type master owned by the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: Benefit label at pay time (e.g. 'KiwiSaver Employer'). Snapshot — group by superannuation_type_id for durable history.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Employer contribution on this line in NZD — the additive measure of the table. A cost outside the employee's pay: never subtract it from gross when computing take-home. Whether this figure is stated gross of ESCT (with the tax levied out of it) or net of ESCT is NOT settled by the spec, and it decides whether employer tax lines add to this or are already inside it — establish which for the tenant by reconciling super + employer tax against the run's total_cost before reporting a super cost.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Flat contribution when the type is fixed-amount rather than percentage-based; already reflected in amount — never add the two.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Contribution rate for percentage-based types (e.g. 3 for the KiwiSaver employer minimum). A rate — never summed; use it to spot above-minimum employer contributions.

columns.name: manual_adjustment
columns.description: True when someone overrode the calculated contribution. The audit flag for hand-edited super — a spike in manual adjustments is a payroll-process smell.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: Employer KiwiSaver contributions by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month, SUM(l.amount) AS employer_super
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_superannuation_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Employees receiving above-minimum (>3%) employer contributions
examples.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT p.employee_id, l.percentage
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_superannuation_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND l.percentage > 3
ORDER BY l.percentage DESC

tables.grain: one timesheet-sourced earnings line on one payslip (position within PaySlip.timesheetEarningsLines)
tables.description: Earnings generated from approved timesheets — the third and final slice of gross pay alongside ordinary and leave earnings. For hourly workforces this family, not earningsLines, is where most wages appear; 'wages by hours worked' questions sum number_of_units and amount here. Amounts are already inside PaySlip.grossEarnings.
gotchas: For hourly workforces most wages land HERE, not in the ordinary earnings table — summing only earningsLines dramatically understates wages for timesheet-driven tenants.
Amounts are already inside gross_earnings; adding families to the header total double-counts.
Draft-run lines mutate; filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' via the payslip → run join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: The payslip this line was exploded from — the row's only route to a person, a date and a posting status, none of which the line itself carries. Every aggregate must climb it to xero_payroll_nz_payslips and on to xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs; querying this table standalone silently mixes mutable Draft-run lines into the totals.

columns.name: line_index
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based ordinal of the line within payroll_nz:PaySlip.timesheetEarningsLines
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line in its source array, minted because the spec guarantees no line id on every row. With pay_slip_id it is the row key — but it is a storage ordinal, not a business sequence: a Draft run re-edited before posting can reshuffle it, so never publish it, join on it, or read meaning into its order.

columns.name: earnings_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this earnings line when the API supplies one. Deliberately NOT the row key: the spec marks it optional, so a null would collapse a payslip's lines together. Use it to trace a row back to the raw payload, and note the same id space is shared with the ordinary and timesheet earnings families — it is unique per line, not per family.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate the timesheet hours were paid under — ordinary vs overtime vs penal rates. Durable GROUP BY; rate master lives in the NZ payroll settings domain.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: UI label of the earnings rate as it stood when the run was posted. Convenient for exploring what a tenant actually calls its ordinary, overtime and penal rates, but it is a snapshot: renaming a rate splits its history into two labels, and two tenants name the same concept differently. Report on earnings_rate_id and use this only as the display string.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Hourly rate applied to the timesheet units. A rate — weight by number_of_units to blend, never SUM.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Timesheet units paid, ordinarily hours — the closest thing this domain has to 'hours worked' for hourly staff (the source Timesheet objects are not exposed in this domain's operations).

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: The flat amount configured on the line when its earnings rate is of RateType Fixed, per the spec; null for the ordinary rate × units case that dominates this timesheet-sourced family. Already reflected in amount — adding the two inflates wages by every fixed line. Its real use is diagnostic: a populated value here explains why rate_per_unit × number_of_units does not reproduce amount.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Timesheet pay for this line in NZD — the additive measure, already inside the payslip's gross_earnings.

columns.name: is_linked_to_timesheet
columns.description: Whether the line came from a timesheet. The spec's text on this field ('Identifies if the leave earnings is taken from the timesheet. False for leave earnings line') is verbatim boilerplate carried over from the shared line schema and describes the LEAVE family, not this one — so the documented 'false' must not be taken as a statement about timesheet earnings. Expect true here on inspection, but verify before filtering on it; a report that filters this to true will return nothing if the field is unpopulated, which reads as 'no timesheet wages' rather than 'flag absent'.

columns.name: is_average_daily_pay_rate
columns.description: True when the Holidays Act average daily pay rate, rather than the rate on the timesheet, priced this line. It is the legitimate explanation for rate_per_unit × number_of_units disagreeing with amount, so exclude these lines before auditing rate integrity — otherwise a compliant statutory substitution reads as a payroll error.

columns.name: is_system_generated
columns.description: True for lines Xero generated (from timesheets), false for manual edits — the manual-intervention audit flag.

joins.note: Then to the run for the Posted filter and dates.

examples.question: Timesheet hours paid and their cost, by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(l.number_of_units) AS hours_paid,
       SUM(l.amount) AS wages_paid
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Effective blended hourly rate by employee last month
examples.sql:
SELECT p.employee_id,
       SUM(l.amount) / NULLIF(SUM(l.number_of_units), 0) AS blended_hourly_rate
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines l
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_slip_id = l.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 month'
  AND r.payment_date <  date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one payslip — one employee's pay within one pay run
tables.description: The employee-level payroll fact: every totals column here is the roll-up of one typed line family below it. Take-home is expected to reconcile as total_pay = gross_earnings − total_employee_taxes − total_deductions − total_statutory_deductions + total_reimbursements, and employer-side amounts (total_employer_taxes, total_superannuation) sit outside take-home entirely. Validate that identity on a sample payslip before publishing anything built on it — the spec's wording for totalDeductions is loose enough to read as an aggregate, and a tenant where it already contains statutory withholdings would make 'all deductions = both columns' double-count. totalEarnings and grossEarnings are the same number for NZ (the spec says so) — never add them. This row carries NO dates and NO status: join xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs for both, and filter pay_run_status = 'Posted' on every aggregate. TaxSettings and GrossEarningsHistory (single nested objects, not arrays) are flattened onto this row.
gotchas: totalEarnings and grossEarnings are the SAME number for NZ (spec-documented). Selecting both and adding them doubles gross pay; this dictionary standardises on gross_earnings.

total_pay is net cash, not cost. Take-home = gross − employee taxes − deductions − statutory deductions + reimbursements; employer cost is a different waterfall and its authoritative value is xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs.total_cost. Reconstructing cost as gross + total_employer_taxes + total_superannuation is an APPROXIMATION that assumes ESCT sits on top of the employer contribution rather than inside it — tie it back to total_cost for one run before publishing it.
Payslips of Draft runs are returned and mutable, and vanish if the draft is discarded. Every aggregate joins to the run and filters pay_run_status = 'Posted'.

total_deductions is modelled as excluding statutory withholdings — student loan, child support and employee KiwiSaver sit in total_statutory_deductions — so 'all deductions' sums both columns. The spec's wording for totalDeductions is ambiguous enough that this must be validated per tenant: if it already includes statutory amounts, summing both double-counts them.
first_name/last_name are display snapshots; group people by employee_id, and fetch identity from xero_payroll_nz_employees.

One payslip is not one employee-month. An employee picked up by an Unscheduled or EarlierYearUpdate run has two payslips in the same period, so COUNT(*) overstates headcount and AVG(gross_earnings) understates pay per person — count DISTINCT employee_id and sum before dividing.

Empty for AU and UK tenants by design (payroll is region-exclusive). No rows means this tenant does not run NZ payroll, not that it ran no payroll — never union with xero_payroll_au_* / xero_payroll_uk_*.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable payslip identifier and the row key; the parent key of every line-family table in this domain.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee this payslip pays. Join xero_payroll_nz_employees for current name, employment and tax detail — the first/last name carried on this row is a display snapshot, not the employee master.

columns.name: pay_run_id
columns.description: The run this payslip belongs to. Always join through it for payRunStatus, payment_date and period dates — the payslip itself carries no dates of its own besides the audit stamp.

columns.name: last_edited
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change and the incremental-sync watermark for this table and its line children. The spec declares day granularity, so the ingester re-pulls with a one-day overlap to catch same-day edits. Not a business date — never bucket money by it.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Employee first name as printed on the payslip — a point-in-time snapshot that goes stale after a name change. Display only; identity questions resolve via employee_id.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Employee last name snapshot at payslip time. Grouping by name instead of employee_id splits one person across a name change and merges distinct people who share a name.

columns.name: total_earnings
columns.description: Earnings before any deductions. Per the spec this is IDENTICAL to gross_earnings for NZ — the schema is shared with other regions where they differ. Pick one (this dictionary standardises on gross_earnings) and never sum both, which exactly doubles gross pay.

columns.name: gross_earnings
columns.description: Gross pay for the period: the sum of the ordinary, leave and timesheet earnings line families combined. Summing only xero_payroll_nz_payslip_earnings_lines understates gross for anyone paid via timesheets or on leave — the three families partition gross, they don't overlap.

columns.name: total_pay
columns.description: The employee's NET pay — cash to their bank accounts, equal to the sum of this payslip's payment lines. Reconciles as gross_earnings − total_employee_taxes − total_deductions − total_statutory_deductions + total_reimbursements. Presenting this as salary or cost is the domain's most common wrong number.

columns.name: total_employer_taxes
columns.description: Employer-side tax for this payslip (in NZ practice, ESCT on employer superannuation contributions). A cost ON TOP of gross — never subtract it when computing take-home, and never add it to total_employee_taxes as 'tax paid by the employee'.

columns.name: total_employee_taxes
columns.description: Tax withheld from the employee's earnings (PAYE). Deducted from gross on the way to net. 'Total PAYE remitted' questions sum this over Posted runs bucketed by the run's payment_date, which fixes the IRD filing period.

columns.name: total_deductions
columns.description: Voluntary/contractual deductions (the deductionLines family): social club, payroll giving, employee super top-ups and the like. Modelled as EXCLUDING statutory withholdings (student loan, child support, employee KiwiSaver), which are total_statutory_deductions — the spec's wording here ('total amount subtracted to reach total pay') is loose, so confirm the split reconciles before reporting a combined deductions figure. Adding a line-family sum on top of this header double-counts either way.

columns.name: total_reimbursements
columns.description: Non-taxable repayments of out-of-pocket expenses, ADDED to pay after tax. Not earnings: include them in 'cash paid to employees' but exclude them from wage-cost and average-earnings analysis or both go high.

columns.name: total_statutory_deductions
columns.description: Withholdings required by law (statutoryDeductionLines family): student loan, child support, employee KiwiSaver contributions. Modelled as disjoint from total_deductions, so 'all deductions' is the sum of both — but prove the disjointness on a sample payslip first: the spec describes totalDeductions as the total subtracted to reach total pay, and if a tenant populates it that way, adding these columns double-counts every statutory dollar. The line families are the tiebreak.

columns.name: total_superannuation
columns.description: Employer superannuation contributions (KiwiSaver employer side; the spec's 'benefits' wording is generic schema text). An employer cost outside the employee's pay, not money withheld from them — the employee's own KiwiSaver contribution lives in the statutory deduction lines, and confusing the two moves real money between 'what staff gave up' and 'what we spent'. Do not reflexively add total_employer_taxes to this to get super cost: in NZ, ESCT is levied on the employer contribution and may already be netted inside this figure. Reconcile any employer-cost build-up against xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs.total_cost, which is Xero's own answer.

columns.name: bacs_hash
columns.description: BACS Service User Number — a UK payments artefact present because the payslip schema is shared across regions. Effectively always null for NZ tenants; treated as a bank-payment identifier, so flagged pii defensively. Never filter or join on it.

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: How the net pay leaves the org. 'Electronically' payslips fan out into payment lines per bank account; Cheque/Manual payslips may carry no meaningful payment-line split at all. Load-bearing because bank-feed reconciliation is only valid over Electronically payslips — including Cheque/Manual rows makes expected outflow exceed what the bank file actually paid, and excluding them from a 'net pay' total understates wages.

columns.name: tax_settings_period_units
columns.description: Number of tax-period units this payslip's PAYE was computed over, paired with tax_period_type (e.g. 1 + 'weeks' for a weekly run). From the payslip's embedded taxSettings object. Input to the tax calculation, not a measure — never sum.

columns.name: tax_settings_period_type
columns.description: Whether PAYE for this payslip was annualised off weeks or months, pairing with tax_period_units to form the tax period Xero applied. It reflects the tax calculation, not the calendar: read pay frequency from the run's calendar_type instead, because a fortnightly calendar reports here as 2 weeks and grouping headcount by this column collapses distinct calendars together.

columns.name: tax_settings_tax_code
columns.description: The IRD tax code the payslip was taxed under, snapshotted at pay time (the employee master may have changed since). M is the common main-income code; codes ending SL carry student-loan deductions; WT is schedular withholding; ND is the penal no-declaration rate. Distribution questions ('how many on secondary codes') group this.
columns.enums: ND; M; ME; MSL; MESL; SB; S; SH; ST; SBSL; SSL; SHSL; STSL; WT; CAE; EDW; NSW; STC; STCSL

columns.name: tax_settings_special_tax_rate
columns.description: The certificate rate applied when tax_code is STC (special tax code) or WT (withholding). Arrives as a string from the spec — cast (::numeric) before arithmetic, and expect null for every ordinary code.

columns.name: tax_settings_lump_sum_tax_code
columns.description: Tax code applied to any lump-sum (extra pay) amount on this payslip — bonuses and final pay are taxed at extra-pay rates, not the period rate. Null when no lump sum was paid.

columns.name: tax_settings_lump_sum_amount
columns.description: Total lump-sum (extra pay) amount taxed under lump_sum_tax_code. The spec types this as a string, so it lands as text — cast ::numeric to aggregate, and remember it is already INSIDE gross_earnings, not additional to it.

columns.name: gross_earnings_history_days_paid
columns.description: Days the employee worked in the pay period (0-365), from the payslip's grossEarningsHistory object. A Holidays Act input feeding average-daily-pay calculations — use it as a divisor (gross / days_paid), never as an additive headcount-days measure across employees with different calendars.

columns.name: gross_earnings_history_unpaid_weeks
columns.description: Full weeks NOT worked in the pay period (0-52), from grossEarningsHistory. Statutory input to leave-rate averaging (it shrinks the divisor), and a usable signal for unpaid-leave periods — but it is a count of weeks, not an amount.

columns.name: earnings_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered earningsLines array exactly as the API returned it. Kept because xero_payroll_nz_payslip_earnings_lines mints its line_index key from this ordering — when a Draft-run edit reshuffles lines, this payload is the audit trail that explains ordinal drift. Analytics NEVER aggregate out of this jsonb; use the explode table, or amounts get counted twice.

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered leaveEarningsLines array from the API — the payload xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_earnings_lines explodes from and mints line_index against. Ordering/audit evidence only: leave-pay analytics come from the explode table, and these amounts are already inside gross_earnings.

columns.name: timesheet_earnings_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered timesheetEarningsLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines and its line_index ordinals. Audit/ordering evidence only; hourly-wage analytics query the explode table, never this jsonb, or timesheet pay double-counts against gross.

columns.name: deduction_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered deductionLines array — the payload xero_payroll_nz_payslip_deduction_lines explodes from (deduction lines carry no line id, so its line_index key depends on exactly this ordering). Audit evidence only; 'deductions withheld' queries use the explode table plus the statutory family.

columns.name: reimbursement_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered reimbursementLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_reimbursement_lines, whose line_index key is minted from this ordering (reimbursement lines have no id of their own). Audit evidence only; reimbursement analytics use the explode table and stay OUT of wage-cost metrics.

columns.name: leave_accrual_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered leaveAccrualLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_leave_accrual_lines and its minted line_index (accrual lines carry no id). Audit evidence only; accrued-units analysis uses the explode table, always grouped by leave type because units carry no unit-of-measure.

columns.name: superannuation_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered superannuationLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_superannuation_lines, whose line_index key depends on this ordering (super lines have no id). Audit evidence only; employer-KiwiSaver analytics use the explode table and remember these are employer-side costs, not withholdings.

columns.name: payment_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered paymentLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_payment_lines and the ordering evidence behind its minted line_index when paymentLineID is absent. Carries raw destination bank-account numbers and holder names, so it is pii and access-restricted like the explode table. Audit evidence only: bank-reconciliation analytics use the explode table, never this jsonb.

columns.name: employee_tax_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered employeeTaxLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employee_tax_lines and its line_index ordinals (taxLineID is not guaranteed on every line). Audit/ordering evidence only; PAYE analytics query the explode table, or withheld tax double-counts.

columns.name: employer_tax_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered employerTaxLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_employer_tax_lines and its line_index ordinals. Same TaxLine shape as the employee array but opposite-direction money (employer cost, in practice ESCT); the direction lives in which column the line came from, which is exactly why the raw payloads are kept apart. Audit evidence only — analytics use the explode table.

columns.name: statutory_deduction_lines
columns.description: Verbatim ordered statutoryDeductionLines array — source payload for xero_payroll_nz_payslip_statutory_deduction_lines, whose line_index key depends on exactly this ordering (statutory lines carry no line id and the type id can repeat). Audit evidence only; student-loan/child-support/KiwiSaver withholding analytics use the explode table.

columns.name: tax_settings
columns.description: Verbatim taxSettings singleton exactly as the API returned it — the audit source the six flattened tax_* / lump_sum_* / special_tax_rate columns on this row were projected from. Query the flattened columns, not this jsonb; it exists so a disputed PAYE calculation can be traced to the untouched payload.

columns.name: gross_earnings_history
columns.description: Verbatim grossEarningsHistory singleton — the payload behind the flattened days_paid and unpaid_weeks columns. Query the flattened columns; this jsonb is the untouched Holidays Act input kept for audit when an average-daily-pay figure is challenged.

joins.note: Mandatory join for dates and for the payRunStatus = 'Posted' filter — the payslip carries neither.
Employee master (current name, employment dates, tax detail). Names on the payslip row are snapshots.

examples.question: Monthly gross pay, PAYE withheld, and net pay across the payroll
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', r.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(p.gross_earnings) AS gross,
       SUM(p.total_employee_taxes) AS paye,
       SUM(p.total_pay) AS net
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslips p
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Employer cost components per employee over the last 12 months
examples.sql:
-- Components are reported separately: PayRun.total_cost is the only Xero-authored
-- employer-cost figure and it has no per-employee counterpart. Reconcile
-- SUM(gross + employer_taxes + superannuation) for a run against that run's
-- total_cost before presenting the reconstruction as 'all-in cost'.
SELECT p.employee_id,
       SUM(p.gross_earnings)        AS gross,
       SUM(p.total_employer_taxes)  AS employer_taxes,
       SUM(p.total_superannuation)  AS employer_super
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslips p
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Does the payslip-level employer-cost reconstruction tie to each run's total_cost?
examples.sql:
SELECT r.pay_run_id, r.payment_date,
       r.total_cost AS xero_total_cost,
       SUM(p.gross_earnings + p.total_employer_taxes + p.total_superannuation) AS reconstructed,
       r.total_cost - SUM(p.gross_earnings + p.total_employer_taxes + p.total_superannuation) AS variance
FROM xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_payslips p ON p.pay_run_id = r.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING ABS(r.total_cost - SUM(p.gross_earnings + p.total_employer_taxes + p.total_superannuation)) > 0.01
ORDER BY ABS(r.total_cost - SUM(p.gross_earnings + p.total_employer_taxes + p.total_superannuation)) DESC

examples.question: How many employees are on student-loan tax codes right now?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.employee_id) AS employees_with_student_loan_codes
FROM xero_payroll_nz_payslips p
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_pay_runs r ON r.pay_run_id = p.pay_run_id
WHERE r.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND r.payment_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 months'
  AND p.tax_settings_tax_code LIKE '%SL'

tables.grain: one org-level reimbursement type per reimbursement id
tables.description: Catalogue of expense-reimbursement pay items (mileage, tools, phone...) paid through payroll, with GST treatment and calculation mechanics. Reimbursements are repayments of employee outlay, not remuneration: exclude them from earnings, tax and KiwiSaver bases in any wage analysis. Amounts actually reimbursed are payslip reimbursement lines.
gotchas: Reimbursements are not earnings: including them in gross-pay or average-wage calculations inflates remuneration with expense repayments.

columns.name: reimbursement_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the reimbursement type; referenced by payslip reimbursement lines.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name of the reimbursement type as shown on payslips (e.g. 'Mileage', 'Tools'). Free text chosen by the org — group by reimbursement_id, not by name, since names can be edited over time.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: GL account the reimbursement posts to (an expense account, since the business bears the cost); joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: True when the type is active; inactive types persist for historical payslip decoding.

columns.name: reimbursement_category
columns.description: Xero's GST treatment bucket for the item, and the reason a reimbursement is not just an expense line: GSTInclusive means the paid amount already contains GST that can be extracted and claimed, NoGST means there is nothing to claim, and GST is the plain GST-treated category. The spec only points at Xero's 'Reimbursement Categories' documentation rather than defining the arithmetic, so confirm the org's intent before deriving a GST credit from a paid amount — guessing the wrong direction moves the credit by the GST rate.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: FixedAmount uses standard_amount; RatePerUnit uses standard_rate_per_unit x units in standard_type_of_units (mileage at cents/km); Unknown appears on legacy rows and means the mechanics must be read from actual payslip lines.

columns.name: standard_amount
columns.description: Default fixed amount for FixedAmount types. The spec types this field as string — the ingester casts to numeric; non-numeric legacy values become null rather than 0.

columns.name: standard_type_of_units
columns.description: Unit for rate-per-unit reimbursements: Hours or km. km signals mileage — the one reimbursement analysts most often want isolated.

columns.name: standard_rate_per_unit
columns.description: Default NZD rate per unit for RatePerUnit types (e.g. the IR mileage rate).

joins.note: Expense account carrying reimbursed costs.

examples.question: Mileage reimbursement rate on file
examples.sql:
SELECT name, standard_rate_per_unit
FROM xero_payroll_nz_reimbursements
WHERE standard_type_of_units = 'km' AND current_record

tables.grain: one effective-dated salary or wage arrangement per employee, identified by its salaryAndWagesID
tables.description: The employee's base-pay history: each row is a salary/hourly arrangement effective from a date, with status Active (current), Pending (future-dated) or History (superseded). This is the table for 'what is X's salary' and for pay-rise analysis, and it is semi-additive — annual_salary adds up across PEOPLE at one moment to give a wage bill, but adding it across an employee's successive arrangements sums every raise they ever received into the total. Every current-pay query therefore reduces to one row per employee first.
tables.additivityAxis: effective_from — the employee's salary-version timeline; reduce to the arrangement in force at the reporting date before adding annual_salary across employees, and never add an employee's own successive rows
gotchas: One employee has many rows (history). SUM(annual_salary) without status = 'Active' adds every raise the person ever had into the wage bill.

annual_salary is base pay. Employer cost adds KiwiSaver employer contributions (rates in xero_payroll_nz_employee_tax), ACC levies and allowances — quoting it as 'cost of employment' understates truth by several percent.
For Hourly staff annual_salary is an annualization, not a commitment — actual pay follows timesheets.

Do not assume status = 'Active' yields exactly one row per person. An employee set up against more than one earnings arrangement can return several Active rows, and SUM(annual_salary) then counts that employee twice. Reduce to one row per employee (greatest effective_from that is not in the future) before adding salaries — the filter on status alone is not a deduplication.

columns.name: salary_and_wages_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this effective-dated pay record; the row key.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee the arrangement belongs to, inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The ordinary-earnings rate this arrangement pays through (normally the org's Ordinary Hours rate); join xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates for its GL expense account.

columns.name: number_of_units_per_week
columns.description: Standard hours per week. The FTE denominator: FTE = this / 40 (or the org's full-time hours). Averaging salaries without weighting by this overstates part-timers.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Hourly rate, NZD. For payment_type Hourly this is the pay basis; for Salary it is derived from annual_salary and hours. Minimum-wage checks compare this, not annual_salary.

columns.name: number_of_units_per_day
columns.description: Standard hours per working day; used by leave-in-days conversions. Hours-per-week / hours-per-day gives implied days-per-week when days_per_week is null.

columns.name: days_per_week
columns.description: Standard working days per week for the arrangement; can be fractional for alternating patterns.

columns.name: effective_from
columns.description: Date the arrangement takes effect. Point-in-time salary at date D is the row with the greatest effective_from <= D per employee — status alone cannot answer historical questions.

columns.name: annual_salary
columns.description: Annual base salary, NZD. Base pay only: excludes overtime, allowances, bonuses and employer KiwiSaver — 'total compensation' questions need payslip earnings, not this. SUM across employees only after filtering status = 'Active'.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Active is the one current arrangement; Pending is future-dated (a scheduled raise); History is superseded. Payroll-cost baselines filter Active; raise-tracking compares consecutive rows ordered by effective_from.

columns.name: payment_type
columns.description: Salary (annual amount drives pay) vs Hourly (rate x timesheet/pattern hours drives pay). Hourly employees' annual_salary is notional — actual earnings vary with hours worked.

columns.name: work_pattern_type
columns.description: Whether standard time is expressed as DaysAndHours (units-per-day/days-per-week here) or a RegularWeek working pattern (see xero_payroll_nz_employee_working_patterns for the per-day hours).

joins.note: Full effective-dated history per employee; exactly one Active row each.
The ordinary earnings rate and its expense account.

examples.question: Current annual base salary bill
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(sw.annual_salary) AS base_salary_bill
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (employee_id) employee_id, annual_salary
  FROM xero_payroll_nz_salary_and_wages
  WHERE status = 'Active' AND effective_from <= CURRENT_DATE
  ORDER BY employee_id, effective_from DESC
) sw
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = sw.employee_id
WHERE e.start_date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (e.end_date IS NULL OR e.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)

examples.question: Employees with a pay rise in the last 12 months
examples.sql:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT employee_id, effective_from, annual_salary,
         annual_salary - LAG(annual_salary) OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from) AS raise
  FROM xero_payroll_nz_salary_and_wages
  WHERE status IN ('Active','History')
) s
WHERE s.raise > 0 AND s.effective_from >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months'

tables.grain: one payroll posting role (PAYE liability, wages payable, wages expense, payroll bank) per tenant
tables.description: The org's payroll posting map: which GL accounts NZ payroll posts PAYE liabilities, wages payable, wage expense and the payroll bank account to. Rows are payroll ROLES pointing at GL accounts — the role (type) is the key, because nothing stops an org pointing two roles at the same GL account, so account_id alone does not guarantee uniqueness. This is plumbing for reconciling payroll to the ledger — the account master itself is xero_accounts in ledger_config.
gotchas: These are the DEFAULT posting accounts. Individual pay items (earnings rates, deductions, super) override them with their own account ids — total payroll cost in the GL is the union of those accounts, not just WAGESEXPENSE.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: GL account UUID; equals xero_accounts.account_id, which is the join to full account metadata. Not the row key — the same GL account can be assigned to more than one payroll role, so key on type.

columns.name: type
columns.description: The payroll role this account plays and the row key: PAYELIABILITY accrues PAYE owed to IR; WAGESPAYABLE holds net wages until paid; WAGESEXPENSE is the default P&L wage cost; BANK is the account wages are paid from. Reconciliation queries pick the role here, then follow account_id into journals.

columns.name: code
columns.description: The account's short code (3 digits per Xero's payroll docs); matches xero_accounts.code but the UUID is the safe join.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Account display name denormalized from the ledger at read time.

joins.note: Full chart-of-accounts metadata for the mapped account; two roles can point at the same account.

examples.question: Which GL accounts does payroll post to by role?
examples.sql:
SELECT s.type AS payroll_role, a.code, a.name
FROM xero_payroll_nz_settings_accounts s
JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = s.account_id
ORDER BY s.type

tables.grain: one org-level statutory deduction type per id
tables.description: Legally-mandated deduction types the org can process: attachment/earnings orders (court fines, child support, MSD repayments, IR arrears), student loan variants and KiwiSaver. These are employer obligations triggered by government notice, unlike the voluntary types in xero_payroll_nz_deductions. Definitions and GL routing only — deducted amounts are payslip lines.
gotchas: Presence of a ChildSupport or CourtFines row means the org has such a type CONFIGURED, not that any employee is subject to one — subject-employee questions need payslip lines.

KiwiSaver total deductions must combine statutory-category KiwiSaver lines and voluntary KiwiSaverVoluntaryContributions lines exactly once each; taking both catalogues' matches against the same payslip line double-counts.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the statutory deduction type (the API calls it just 'id'; docs describe it as the earnings-order id).

columns.name: name
columns.description: The label the payroll administrator gave the order or statutory item. Free text, so it may carry an IR or court reference — and occasionally identifying detail about the employee subject to the order, which is why it should not be surfaced casually. Group by statutory_deduction_category for anything analytical; the name is a display string only.

columns.name: statutory_deduction_category
columns.description: Legal category driving deduction-priority rules: PriorityOrder/NonPriorityOrder/TableBased govern attachment-order sequencing when net pay can't cover everything; ChildSupport, CourtFines, InlandRevenueArrears, MsdRepayments are specific order kinds; the three StudentLoan variants and KiwiSaver round out the statutory set. KiwiSaver appearing HERE (the standard employee contribution) and in the voluntary deductions catalogue (top-ups) is the classic double-count trap.
columns.enums: PriorityOrder; NonPriorityOrder; TableBased; ChildSupport; CourtFines; InlandRevenueArrears; MsdRepayments; StudentLoan; AdditionalStudentLoan; VoluntaryStudentLoan; KiwiSaver

columns.name: liability_account_id
columns.description: GL liability account holding withheld statutory amounts pending remittance to the Crown agency; joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: True when the type is active for new payslips; inactive rows remain for decoding history.

joins.note: Ledger liability account for withheld statutory amounts.

examples.question: Configured statutory deduction types
examples.sql:
SELECT name, statutory_deduction_category
FROM xero_payroll_nz_statutory_deductions
WHERE current_record
ORDER BY statutory_deduction_category

tables.grain: one org-level superannuation benefit scheme per id
tables.description: Employer superannuation schemes the org contributes to: KiwiSaver, complying funds and other schemes, with the calculation rule (fixed amount vs percentage of taxable earnings), default rates, employer cap and the two GL accounts (expense for the employer cost, liability until remitted). The spec models these records with an object literally named 'Benefit' while the endpoint and envelope are Superannuations, so every column below cites payroll_nz:Benefit.* for a table nothing in the payload calls a benefit — that mismatch is spec naming, not a design error. Scheme definitions only: contributed dollars are payslip superannuation lines.
gotchas: Employer KiwiSaver cost questions have three sources that must not be mixed: scheme defaults here, per-employee rates in xero_payroll_nz_employee_tax, and actual contributed dollars on payslips. Only the last is spend.

Spec object name and endpoint disagree: the records are payroll_nz:Benefit but the operation, envelope and array key are all Superannuations. Anyone mapping staging columns back to spec objects by table name will not find a 'Superannuation' object, and anyone searching the NZ payload for a 'benefits' collection will not find that either — this is the one table in the domain where provenance and payload use different words for the same thing.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the superannuation scheme (field name is just 'id' on the Benefit object).

columns.name: name
columns.description: The org's label for the scheme as it prints on payslips. Editable free text, so historical payslip lines display today's name and a rename rewrites the apparent history — read category for what the scheme actually is and join on superannuation_id.

columns.name: category
columns.description: KiwiSaver (the national scheme), ComplyingFund (KiwiSaver-equivalent registered fund) or Other. Employer-contribution analysis usually wants KiwiSaver + ComplyingFund together since both attract ESCT and satisfy auto-enrolment.

columns.name: liability_account_id
columns.description: GL liability account accruing contributions until remitted to the fund/IRD; joins to xero_accounts.account_id.

columns.name: expense_account_id
columns.description: GL expense account carrying the employer's contribution cost; this is where super shows up in P&L wage-cost questions.

columns.name: calculation_type_nz
columns.description: FixedAmount pays standard_amount per period; PercentageOfTaxableEarnings pays percentage of the employee's taxable earnings. Determines which of standard_amount/percentage is live — the other is noise.

columns.name: standard_amount
columns.description: Default per-period NZD contribution for FixedAmount schemes; a default rate card, not an amount contributed.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Default contribution percentage of taxable earnings for percentage schemes. Per-employee KiwiSaver rates in xero_payroll_nz_employee_tax override this default.

columns.name: company_max
columns.description: Employer contribution cap for the scheme; contributions computed above it are clipped, so modelling employer cost from raw percentages without this cap overstates spend for high earners.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: True when the scheme is active; inactive schemes remain for historical payslip decoding.

joins.note: Employer super cost in the P&L.
Accrued contributions pending remittance.

examples.question: Active super schemes and their default contribution rules
examples.sql:
SELECT name, category, calculation_type_nz,
       CASE calculation_type_nz
         WHEN 'PercentageOfTaxableEarnings' THEN percentage::text || '% of taxable earnings'
         WHEN 'FixedAmount' THEN standard_amount::text || ' NZD per period'
       END AS default_contribution,
       company_max
FROM xero_payroll_nz_superannuations
WHERE current_record
ORDER BY category, name

tables.grain: one day's units against one earnings rate (and optional tracking item) within one timesheet
tables.description: The atomic worked-time fact for NZ payroll: date, earnings rate, optional tracking category option and units (hours). This is the grain for daily-hours, overtime and labour-allocation analysis; roll up to the timesheet for period totals. Status lives on the parent — every aggregate over lines must join the header and filter its status, or draft hours pollute actuals.
gotchas: Lines carry no status: aggregate without joining the parent's status and Draft/Requested hours count as worked.
Units are per earnings rate — total daily hours per person needs SUM across lines, but pricing them needs the rate join first since overtime units are not worth ordinary dollars.

columns.name: timesheet_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the line; the row key.

columns.name: timesheet_id
columns.description: Parent timesheet, inherited during explode; the required route to employee, period and status.

columns.name: timesheet_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position within the parent's timesheetLines array, preserving entry order; provenance is the array itself.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee who worked the units, denormalized from the parent so per-person hour queries skip a join — but status filtering still requires the parent.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The calendar day worked (renamed from 'date' to avoid the SQL keyword). Daily-hours series group on this; it always falls inside the parent's period.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Which earnings rate the units are claimed at. Overtime vs ordinary lives here: join xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates and split on earnings_type before pricing hours.

columns.name: tracking_item_id
columns.description: Tracking option (a xero_tracking_options row) tagging the line to a department/region/job when the org enabled a timesheet tracking category (see xero_payroll_nz_tracking_categories). Null when tracking is off — labour-allocation reports must state the untracked remainder.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units worked, in the earnings rate's type_of_units (hours in practice). SUM freely within one earnings-rate unit type after filtering parent status.

joins.note: Status filter lives on the header — join it for every aggregate.
Ordinary/overtime classification and unit type.
Department/region label for labour allocation; null when untracked.

examples.question: Overtime hours by employee this quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT tl.employee_id, SUM(tl.number_of_units) AS overtime_hours
FROM xero_payroll_nz_timesheet_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_timesheets t ON t.timesheet_id = tl.timesheet_id
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_earnings_rates er ON er.earnings_rate_id = tl.earnings_rate_id
WHERE t.status IN ('Approved','Completed')
  AND er.earnings_type = 'OvertimeEarnings'
  AND tl.date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Hours by tracking option (department), showing the untracked remainder
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(o.name, 'Untracked') AS department, SUM(tl.number_of_units) AS hours
FROM xero_payroll_nz_timesheet_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_timesheets t ON t.timesheet_id = tl.timesheet_id
LEFT JOIN xero_tracking_options o ON o.tracking_option_id = tl.tracking_item_id
WHERE t.status IN ('Approved','Completed')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

tables.grain: one submitted timesheet document, identified by timesheetID — an employee can hold more than one covering the same pay-calendar period when a timesheet is resubmitted
tables.description: Header of an employee's timesheet for one pay-calendar period, with lifecycle status and Xero's own totalHours rollup. The employee+period pair is NOT unique — a resubmission creates a second timesheet over the same window, so only timesheetID is the key and period totals must not blindly sum duplicate windows. Hours-by-day detail is in xero_payroll_nz_timesheet_lines. Status is the truth filter: Draft and Requested timesheets are unconfirmed, Approved is ready for payroll, Completed has been consumed by a posted pay run — 'hours worked' analysis over all statuses counts unapproved and possibly abandoned drafts.
gotchas: Salaried employees usually have no timesheets — absence of rows is not absence of work. Utilization metrics over timesheets describe the timesheet-using workforce only.
Draft/Requested hours are unconfirmed and may never be approved; including them overstates worked hours and labour cost forecasts.

employee_id + start_date is NOT unique. A corrected or resubmitted timesheet lands as an additional row over the same window, so SUM(total_hours) across a period counts those hours twice — reduce to the latest row per employee and period (by updated_date_utc) before aggregating.

columns.name: timesheet_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the timesheet; the parent key of its lines.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: Pay calendar whose period this timesheet covers; start/end dates below are that calendar's period boundaries.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee the hours belong to — carried on the record itself here, unlike the fan-out employee tables.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day of the timesheet's pay period. One timesheet per employee per period — a second one for the same window signals a resubmission, not extra hours.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day of the timesheet's pay period, INCLUSIVE — so a containment test is work_date BETWEEN start_date AND end_date, and a half-open range silently drops the final day of every period. It mirrors the pay calendar's window, not the range of days the employee actually entered hours for.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Lifecycle: Draft (being entered), Requested (awaiting approval), Approved (payable), Completed (paid in a posted run). Worked-hours facts filter Approved+Completed; payroll-pending queues filter Requested.

columns.name: total_hours
columns.description: Xero's rollup of the lines' units. Use EITHER this OR SUM(lines.number_of_units), never both in one measure — joining lines and summing header totals multiplies hours by the line count.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last edit; the incremental sync watermark for timesheets and their lines.

joins.note: Timesheets exist mainly for Hourly-paid employees.
Frequency context for the period.
Per-day, per-earnings-rate hour detail.

examples.question: Approved hours by employee this month, counting each pay period once
examples.sql:
SELECT employee_id, SUM(total_hours) AS hours
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (employee_id, start_date, end_date)
         employee_id, total_hours
  FROM xero_payroll_nz_timesheets
  WHERE status IN ('Approved','Completed')
    AND start_date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
  ORDER BY employee_id, start_date, end_date, updated_date_utc DESC
) t
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Timesheets awaiting approval
examples.sql:
SELECT t.timesheet_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, t.start_date, t.end_date, t.total_hours
FROM xero_payroll_nz_timesheets t
JOIN xero_payroll_nz_employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id
WHERE t.status = 'Requested'
ORDER BY t.start_date

tables.grain: one payroll tracking-category configuration record per tenant
tables.description: Singleton configuration naming which of the org's two accounting tracking categories payroll uses: one to group employees (cost-center reporting of wages) and one to tag timesheet lines (labour allocation). The ids point at xero_tracking_categories in ledger_config; their options are what timesheet_lines.tracking_item_id values belong to. Both ids null means payroll tracking is off and labour-allocation questions are unanswerable from tracking.
gotchas: Exactly one row per tenant. If both ids are null, labour allocation by department cannot be derived from payroll tracking — say so rather than returning an empty breakdown as if departments had zero hours.
