columns.name: settings_key
columns.api: synthetic:constant 'payroll_nz' — the endpoint returns exactly one configuration record per tenant and it has no natural key
columns.description: Minted singleton key so the row has a stable identity across syncs.

columns.name: employee_groups_tracking_category_id
columns.description: The accounting tracking category whose options group EMPLOYEES (e.g. by department) for wage-cost reporting; joins to xero_tracking_categories.tracking_category_id. Null = employee grouping not configured.

columns.name: timesheet_tracking_category_id
columns.description: The accounting tracking category whose options tag TIMESHEET LINES; xero_payroll_nz_timesheet_lines.tracking_item_id values are options of this category. Null = timesheet tracking off, so every tracking_item_id will be null too.

joins.note: Category whose options appear on timesheet lines; a second identical join path exists via employee_groups_tracking_category_id.

examples.question: Which tracking category tags timesheets?
examples.sql:
SELECT tc.name AS timesheet_tracking_category
FROM xero_payroll_nz_tracking_categories p
JOIN xero_tracking_categories tc ON tc.tracking_category_id = p.timesheet_tracking_category_id

tables.grain: one employer benefit (pension) pay item per benefit id
tables.description: Org-level employer benefit definitions — in the UK API these are overwhelmingly employer PENSION schemes (the spec literally describes the fields as 'the employer pension'). Each row defines how the employer contribution is computed (fixed vs percentage of gross, qualifying-earnings basis) and which GL accounts it posts to. This is the catalogue; amounts actually contributed per employee per period are payslip benefit lines in the pay-run domain.
gotchas: Despite the generic name, UK 'Benefits' are employer pension schemes in Xero's model — do not expect private-health or car benefits here.
standard_amount and percentage are alternatives gated by calculation_type; quoting the wrong one gives a default that was never applied.
This is configuration: actual employer contributions per period are payslip benefit lines. Multiplying percentage by current salaries ignores qualifying-earnings banding and opt-outs.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the benefit pay item; payslip benefit lines reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The org's label for the scheme as it appears on payslips (typically the pension provider). The only human-readable way to tell two schemes apart, since category collapses everything to StakeholderPension or Other — but it is free text, so an org running one scheme under two items (different contribution tiers) will show near-identical names that must not be merged.

columns.name: category
columns.description: StakeholderPension marks a pension scheme; Other is the catch-all. Pension-specific analyses (auto-enrolment coverage) should filter StakeholderPension.

columns.name: liability_account_id
columns.description: GL account the accrued contribution liability posts to; join xero_accounts to trace payroll postings into the ledger.

columns.name: expense_account_id
columns.description: GL account the employer contribution expense posts to — where pension cost lands in the P&L.

columns.name: standard_amount
columns.description: Default per-period amount — only meaningful when calculation_type = 'FixedAmount'; ignore it for percentage schemes or you will misquote the default.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Employer contribution as a percentage of gross — only meaningful when calculation_type = 'PercentageOfGross'. A rate: never sum it.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: Selects which of standard_amount / percentage drives the contribution. Read this before quoting either figure.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: FALSE means retired configuration kept for history — filter TRUE for 'what schemes do we run today', keep FALSE rows to decode old payslip lines.

columns.name: subject_to_nic
columns.description: Whether the benefit value attracts National Insurance — changes the true employer cost of the scheme beyond the contribution itself.

columns.name: subject_to_pension
columns.description: Whether the amount counts into pensionable earnings for other pension calculations.

columns.name: subject_to_tax
columns.description: Whether the benefit is taxable on the employee; affects net-pay expectations, not employer cost.

columns.name: is_calculating_on_qualifying_earnings
columns.description: TRUE applies the percentage to the auto-enrolment qualifying-earnings band rather than full gross — the same percentage yields materially less contribution, so cost models must branch on this.

columns.name: show_balance_to_employee
columns.description: Payslip presentation toggle; no analytical meaning.

joins.note: Where employer pension cost lands in the P&L.
The pension-contributions-payable liability account.

examples.question: Active employer pension schemes and their contribution basis
examples.sql:
SELECT name, calculation_type,
       CASE calculation_type WHEN 'FixedAmount' THEN standard_amount ELSE percentage END AS default_value,
       is_calculating_on_qualifying_earnings
FROM xero_payroll_uk_benefits
WHERE current_record AND category = 'StakeholderPension'

tables.grain: one deduction pay item per deductionId
tables.description: Org-level deduction definitions: employee pension contributions, salary sacrifice, student/postgraduate loan items, childcare vouchers, court-order style repayments and other before/after-tax deductions. Rows are the catalogue and calculation rules; amounts actually deducted are payslip deduction lines in the pay-run domain. The subject-to flags decide whether a deduction reduces taxable/NIC-able gross — the essence of salary-sacrifice economics.
gotchas: Employee pension deductions here vs employer pension benefits in xero_payroll_uk_benefits: 'pension contributions' as a single number silently drops one side.
Relief-at-source pensions (is_reduced_by_basic_rate) show the net-of-tax-relief amount on payslips — grossing up by 100/80 is required to state the true contribution.
reduces_super_liability is an AU-region artifact of the shared schema; it never applies to UK payroll.

columns.name: deduction_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the deduction pay item; payslip deduction lines reference it.

columns.name: deduction_name
columns.description: The org-configured label employees see on payslips ('AE Pension', 'Cycle to Work'...). Free text and org-specific: two orgs (or one org over time) can name the same kind of deduction differently, so never classify deductions by parsing this string — deduction_category is the reliable classifier; this column is for display and disambiguating multiple items within one category.

columns.name: deduction_category
columns.description: The functional category. SalarySacrifice and StakeholderPension are pre-tax pension routes; StakeholderPensionPostTax is relief-at-source; StudentLoanDeductions/PostgraduateLoanDeductions are HMRC loans. Categorise payslip deduction lines through this, not by parsing names.
columns.enums: CapitalContributions; ChildCareVoucher; MakingGood; PostgraduateLoanDeductions; PrivateUsePayments; SalarySacrifice; StakeholderPension; StakeholderPensionPostTax; StudentLoanDeductions; UkOther

columns.name: liability_account_id
columns.description: GL account the withheld amount is owed from until paid over; join xero_accounts to reconcile payroll liabilities.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: FALSE = retired configuration. Filter TRUE for today's deduction menu; keep FALSE to decode historical payslips.

columns.name: standard_amount
columns.description: Default per-period amount, meaningful only when calculation_type = 'FixedAmount'.

columns.name: reduces_super_liability
columns.description: Cross-region flag (super = AU pension terminology) exposed by the shared schema; not meaningful for UK deductions — ignore rather than interpret.

columns.name: reduces_tax_liability
columns.description: TRUE means the deduction comes out before tax — the employee's taxable pay shrinks. This flag is why gross pay minus visible deductions does not equal taxable pay.

columns.name: calculation_type
columns.description: FixedAmount uses standard_amount; PercentageOfGross uses percentage. Read before quoting a default.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: Percentage of gross for percentage-type deductions. A rate; never summed.

columns.name: subject_to_nic
columns.description: Whether the deducted amount remains inside NIC-able pay. FALSE on salary sacrifice is exactly where employer NIC savings come from.

columns.name: subject_to_tax
columns.description: Whether the deducted amount remains inside taxable pay; the companion to reduces_tax_liability for classifying pre- vs post-tax deductions.

columns.name: is_reduced_by_basic_rate
columns.description: TRUE for relief-at-source pensions: the employee pays the net-of-basic-rate amount and the provider reclaims the rest — the payslip deduction understates the gross contribution by 20%.

columns.name: apply_to_pension_calculations
columns.description: Whether the deduction feeds into pensionable-pay calculations for other items.

columns.name: is_calculating_on_qualifying_earnings
columns.description: TRUE applies percentage deductions to the auto-enrolment qualifying-earnings band instead of full gross — same percentage, smaller base.

columns.name: is_pension
columns.description: Marks the EMPLOYEE side of pension contributions (the employer side is xero_payroll_uk_benefits). Total pension cost questions must combine both tables, not pick one.

joins.note: The payable account holding withheld amounts until remitted.

examples.question: Active deduction items that reduce NIC-able pay (salary-sacrifice style)
examples.sql:
SELECT deduction_name, deduction_category, calculation_type
FROM xero_payroll_uk_deductions
WHERE current_record AND (subject_to_nic = false OR deduction_category = 'SalarySacrifice')

tables.grain: one attachment-of-earnings order pay item per earnings order id
tables.description: Org-level attachment/earnings-order definitions — court-mandated deductions (child support, court fines, creditor orders) applied to employees' pay. The enum is shared across Xero's regions, so NZ/US values (KiwiSaver, USChildSupport) appear as legal enum members but never occur in UK data. Amounts actually withheld are payslip lines in the pay-run domain; this table exists to classify them.
gotchas: The response array is named statutoryDeductions, not earningsOrders — the envelope and the object name disagree with the payload key by design.
An employee HAVING an order is sensitive personal information (debt, child support) — aggregate; never name individuals unless the user explicitly asks.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the earnings order pay item.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The org's label for this order item as it appears on payslips. Orgs routinely name these after the individual case or the issuing court, so the value can itself identify an employee's debt or child-support arrangement — treat it as sensitive when listing, and classify with statutory_deduction_category rather than by reading this string.

columns.name: statutory_deduction_category
columns.description: The legal category of the order. Only UK-relevant values (ChildSupport, CourtFines, Creditor, PriorityOrder, NonPriorityOrder, TableBased, StudentLoan variants...) occur in UK tenants; KiwiSaver/USChildSupport/MsdRepayments belong to other regions sharing this enum.
columns.enums: AdditionalStudentLoan; ChildSupport; CourtFines; Creditor; FederalLevy; InlandRevenueArrears; KiwiSaver; MsdRepayments; NonPriorityOrder; PriorityOrder; TableBased; StudentLoan; VoluntaryStudentLoan; USChildSupport

columns.name: liability_account_id
columns.description: GL account holding withheld order amounts until remitted to the court/agency; join xero_accounts.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: FALSE = retired configuration; filter TRUE for the active menu, keep FALSE to decode historical payslip lines.

joins.note: The payable account for amounts owed to courts/agencies.

examples.question: What attachment-of-earnings order types are configured?
examples.sql:
SELECT statutory_deduction_category, COUNT(*) AS items
FROM xero_payroll_uk_earnings_orders
WHERE current_record
GROUP BY statutory_deduction_category

tables.grain: one earnings rate pay item per earningsRateID
tables.description: The org's catalogue of ways people earn: regular pay, overtime, bonuses, commission, tips, termination pay and the full family of statutory pay types (SSP, SMP, SPP...). Every earnings line on every payslip and timesheet references one of these, making this the classification dimension for gross-pay composition. rate_type gates which of the three rate fields applies — reading the wrong one produces nonsense rates.
gotchas: rate_per_unit, multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate and fixed_amount are mutually exclusive by rate_type — averaging or comparing them across rows mixes units, multipliers and pounds.

Statutory recovery is type-specific, not prefix-wide: family-related statutory pay (SMP/SPP/SAP/ShPP/bereavement/neonatal) is largely reclaimable from HMRC so counting it at gross overstates net payroll cost, while Statutory Sick Pay is not reclaimable at all so netting it off understates cost. Any 'true wage cost' model must branch per earnings_type, never on the Statutory* prefix.
Rates here are org defaults; the employee-level rate can be overridden in pay templates and salary records.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the earnings rate; referenced by payslip earnings lines, timesheet lines, pay templates and salary records.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name ('Regular Hours', 'Overtime 1.5x'...). Classify by earnings_type, not by parsing names.

columns.name: earnings_type
columns.description: The semantic class of the earning, and the only reliable way to split gross pay into regular, premium and statutory components. The Statutory* family does not behave uniformly: family-related statutory pay (maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental, bereavement, neonatal care) is largely recoverable from HMRC, and more than fully recoverable for small employers, so it costs the business far less than its gross; Statutory SICK Pay is NOT recoverable at all and costs the business every penny. Treating the whole Statutory* prefix as one recoverable bucket gets employer cost wrong in both directions. NonPensionable variants are the same payment excluded from pensionable earnings — they change the pension base, not the gross.
columns.enums: Allowance; BackPay; Bonus; Commission; LumpSum; OtherEarnings; OvertimeEarnings; RegularEarnings; StatutoryAdoptionPay; StatutoryAdoptionPayNonPensionable; StatutoryBereavementPay; StatutoryMaternityPay; StatutoryMaternityPayNonPensionable; StatutoryPaternityPay; StatutoryPaternityPayNonPensionable; StatutoryParentalBereavementPayNonPensionable; StatutorySharedParentalPay; StatutorySharedParentalPayNonPensionable; StatutorySickPay; StatutorySickPayNonPensionable; TipsNonDirect; TipsDirect; TerminationPay; StatutoryNeonatalCarePay; StatutoryNeonatalCarePayNonPensionable; StatutoryBereavementPayNorthernIreland

columns.name: rate_type
columns.description: Gates the rate fields: RatePerUnit reads rate_per_unit, MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate reads multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate (x the employee's ordinary rate), FixedAmount reads fixed_amount. The other two fields are noise for any given row.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: What one unit means (typically Hours). Timesheet and payslip unit counts inherit this meaning — check it before converting units to hours.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: FALSE = retired rate kept for history. Filter TRUE for the active catalogue; retired rates still decode old payslips.

columns.name: expense_account_id
columns.description: GL account this earning's cost posts to; join xero_accounts to reconcile payroll expense lines in the P&L.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Default rate per unit — only when rate_type = 'RatePerUnit', and employees can override it. A rate; never summed.

columns.name: multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate
columns.description: Multiplier of the employee's ordinary rate (1.5 = time-and-a-half) — only when rate_type = 'MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate'. The actual money rate differs per employee.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Default fixed amount — only when rate_type = 'FixedAmount'.

joins.note: Where this earning type's cost lands in the GL.

examples.question: Overtime rates and their multipliers
examples.sql:
SELECT name, multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate
FROM xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates
WHERE current_record AND earnings_type = 'OvertimeEarnings'
  AND rate_type = 'MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate'
ORDER BY multiple_of_ordinary_earnings_rate DESC

tables.grain: one net-pay destination bank account per employee per array position
tables.description: The bank accounts an electronically-paid employee's net pay is sent to. More than one row per employee means the net pay is split across accounts — but the payload carries only the account identity (name, number, sort code) and NO amount or percentage per account, so how the split divides is not derivable here: the count of accounts is the only fact this table supports. Every column is sensitive financial PII (UK sort code + account number); this table exists for completeness and payment-ops questions, not for analytics, and should never be surfaced without an explicit request.
gotchas: Multiple rows per employee are a deliberate net-pay split, not duplicates — deduplicating by employee_id destroys the configuration. Equally, no per-account amount or percentage is returned, so any statement about how much lands in each account is invented; answer 'split across N accounts, proportions not available from Xero'.
Sort code + account number together identify a person's bank account; treat any output containing them as a credential-grade disclosure.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.api: synthetic:EmployeeID path parameter of GET /Employees/{EmployeeID}/PaymentMethods, inherited through parent xero_payroll_uk_employee_payment_methods — neither BankAccount nor PaymentMethod carries an employee field
columns.description: The employee the account belongs to. The BankAccount payload itself carries no employee reference, so the ingester stamps the fan-out path parameter onto each exploded row; equals xero_payroll_uk_employees.employee_id.

columns.name: ordinal
columns.description: Position in the bankAccounts array; the source exposes no account id, and order reflects the configured split order.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Account holder name as it appears in the bank file (max 32 chars). PII.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: UK bank account number (up to 8 digits, digits only). Stored as text — leading zeros are significant and arithmetic on it is never valid. Highly sensitive PII.

columns.name: sort_code
columns.description: 6-digit UK sort code identifying the receiving bank branch. Text, leading zeros significant. Highly sensitive PII.

joins.note: Child of the payment method configuration.

examples.question: Which employees split their net pay across multiple accounts?
examples.sql:
SELECT ba.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, COUNT(*) AS accounts
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_bank_accounts ba
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = ba.employee_id
GROUP BY ba.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

tables.grain: one employment contract episode per employee per array position
tables.description: The authoritative employment-episode history: each row is a contract (full/part-time/zero-hour, employee vs worker status, fixed-term window, optional apprenticeship). This — not the flat start/end dates on the employee row — is what re-hires, FTE mix and contract-type analyses should read. The contract start_date is locked once the employee has been paid, making it the most trustworthy hire date in the domain.
gotchas: One employee can carry several contract rows. Per-employee attributes (contract_type, employment_status) must be taken from the latest episode (max start_date), or a re-hired part-timer double-counts in the FTE mix.

There is no contract end date field — an episode's end is inferred from the next episode's start_date or the employee's end_date. Do not invent one by assuming fixed_term_end_date applies to permanent contracts.
employment_status = Worker rows are inside the employee table but outside most statutory-entitlement populations; statutory pay analyses should usually restrict to Employee.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Parent employee; inherited from the record the contracts array was exploded from.

columns.name: ordinal
columns.description: Stable position in the employee's contracts array; part of the key because public_key is optional.

columns.name: public_key
columns.description: Xero's contract identifier. May be absent on older records — hence the ordinal in the key.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Contract start, locked once the employee has been paid. Use this for hire-date and tenure analysis; the employee row's start_date is a mutable snapshot.

columns.name: employment_status
columns.description: Employee vs Worker is a UK employment-law distinction (workers lack unfair-dismissal and statutory-redundancy rights, and some statutory pay entitlements). Unspecified appears on older data — treat it as unknown, not Employee.

columns.name: contract_type
columns.description: FullTime/PartTime/ZeroHour. Any FTE or average-hours metric must segment on this — averaging zero-hour staff into full-time averages produces a meaningless blended number.

columns.name: is_fixed_term
columns.description: TRUE for fixed-term contracts; pair with fixed_term_end_date for expiry-pipeline questions. Null/false means permanent.

columns.name: fixed_term_end_date
columns.description: When a fixed-term contract expires. Only populated when is_fixed_term — a null here on a permanent contract is expected, not missing data.

columns.name: developmental_role_details_start_date
columns.description: Start of the developmental (apprenticeship) role window within this contract. Apprentices under 25 qualify for NI category H and apprentice National Minimum Wage rates only inside this window.

columns.name: developmental_role_details_end_date
columns.description: End of the developmental role window; after this date the person is an ordinary employee for wage-floor and NIC purposes even if the contract continues.

columns.name: developmental_role_details_developmental_role
columns.description: The role type; the spec supports only 'Apprentice' today, so treat any non-null value as an apprenticeship flag.

columns.name: developmental_role_details_public_key
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the developmental-role sub-record; only needed to correlate edits, never an analysis key.

joins.note: Explode child; an employee can have multiple contract episodes (re-hires, status changes).

examples.question: Contract-type mix of the current workforce
examples.sql:
SELECT c.contract_type, COUNT(*) AS people
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (employee_id) employee_id, contract_type
  FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts
  ORDER BY employee_id, start_date DESC
) c
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = c.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY c.contract_type ORDER BY people DESC

examples.question: Fixed-term contracts expiring in the next 90 days
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, c.fixed_term_end_date
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts c
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = c.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
WHERE c.is_fixed_term AND c.fixed_term_end_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND CURRENT_DATE + 90
ORDER BY c.fixed_term_end_date

tables.grain: one leave request per leaveID
tables.description: Booked leave (holiday, unpaid leave, org-defined types) per employee. Each request spans start_date..end_date but the quantified time off — units per pay period — lives in xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_periods; this table alone cannot tell you how many hours were taken. Statutory family leave and SSP episodes are tracked separately in the statutory leave tables, so 'all absence' questions need both families.
gotchas: Counting rows counts requests, not days or hours — a two-week holiday and a half-day are one row each. Quantity questions must SUM number_of_units from the periods table.

Statutory maternity/paternity/sick leave is NOT here — it lives in xero_payroll_uk_statutory_leave_summaries and xero_payroll_uk_statutory_sick_leaves. 'Total absence' from this table alone misses statutory episodes. Do not fix that with a blind UNION either: a request booked against a leave type flagged is_statutory_leave in xero_payroll_uk_leave_types surfaces in both families, so the combined view has to be de-duplicated on employee plus overlapping dates or the same absence is counted twice.
Leave rows for terminated employees survive; join through the employee table when you mean the current workforce.

columns.name: leave_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the leave request and the row key.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee on leave; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Which leave type this request draws on. Join xero_payroll_uk_leave_types for the name and the is_paid_leave flag — unpaid leave in a paid-absence total silently inflates cost estimates.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text reason (max 50 chars). Frequently contains health or family details — treat as sensitive PII, never group by it.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First calendar day of the leave. Calendar span (end - start) is NOT time off — weekends and non-working days sit inside it; use period units for quantity.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last calendar day of the leave (inclusive). Future-dated rows are approved bookings, not absence that has happened yet.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change; sync watermark, not the request date.

columns.name: periods
columns.description: The leave period information. The StartDate, EndDate and NumberOfUnits needs to be specified when you do not want to calculate NumberOfUnits automatically. Using incorrect period StartDate and EndDate will result in automatic computation of the NumberOfUnits. Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_periods (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Per-employee fan-out.
Names the leave type and flags paid vs unpaid.
The quantified units per pay period; the only place hours taken exists.

examples.question: Leave requests by type in the last 12 months
examples.sql:
SELECT lt.name, COUNT(*) AS requests
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave l
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = l.leave_type_id
WHERE l.start_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months'
GROUP BY lt.name ORDER BY requests DESC

examples.question: Who is on leave today?
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, lt.name AS leave_type
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave l
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = l.employee_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_leave_types lt ON lt.leave_type_id = l.leave_type_id
WHERE CURRENT_DATE BETWEEN l.start_date AND l.end_date

tables.grain: one current leave balance per employee per leave type
tables.description: The employee's leave balances as of the last sync — a point-in-time snapshot that each sync overwrites. Balances are last-value measures: summing them over time or across syncs double-counts, and there is no history here (trend questions need the periods table plus accrual rules). Units differ per leave type, so cross-type sums are unit soup.
tables.additivityAxis: time — each sync replaces the balance; never sum balances across snapshots or attach one balance to multiple periods
gotchas: Snapshot semantics: this is the balance NOW, overwritten every sync. There is no as-at history — 'balance at year end' is unanswerable from this table unless the sync ran then.
Balances can be negative; flooring them at zero hides leave taken in advance and misstates liability.
Only paid leave types belong in an accrued-liability estimate — filter via the leave-type join before costing balances.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee holding the balance; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type the balance belongs to; join xero_payroll_uk_leave_types for paid/statutory flags.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Denormalized leave-type name carried on the balance row; convenient for display but the join on leave_type_id is authoritative if they ever disagree.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: The CURRENT remaining balance in type_of_units. It can be negative (leave taken ahead of accrual). Multiplying by an hourly rate approximates accrued-leave liability for paid types only.

columns.name: type_of_units
columns.description: Unit of measure for balance (typically Hours). Group or filter by it before any cross-employee aggregation — 'total balance' across mixed units means nothing.

joins.note: Per-employee fan-out.
Paid/unpaid and statutory flags for liability calculations.

examples.question: Largest current leave balances among active staff
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, b.name AS leave_type, b.balance, b.type_of_units
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_balances b
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
ORDER BY b.balance DESC LIMIT 15

tables.grain: one pay-period slice of one leave request
tables.description: How each leave request is carved across payroll periods, with the number of units actually deducted from the balance in each period. This is the additive quantity table for non-statutory leave: SUM(number_of_units) is hours (or the type's unit) of leave taken. Slices follow the employee's PAYROLL calendar, so a calendar-month report must aggregate by the slice dates, not assume slices equal months.
gotchas: Approved and Completed answer different questions: Completed is history, Approved is commitment. Mixing them into one 'leave taken' number overstates actuals.
Units follow the leave type's unit of measure — aggregate per leave_type_id (join through the parent) before comparing or converting.
Slices align to pay periods; bucketing by date_trunc('month', period_start_date) approximates calendar months but weekly calendars straddle month ends.

columns.name: leave_id
columns.description: The leave request this slice belongs to; inherited from the parent record.

columns.name: ordinal
columns.description: Stable position of the slice within the request's periods array; the source has no period id.

columns.name: period_start_date
columns.description: Start of the PAY period the slice falls in — payroll-calendar aligned, not month aligned. Use it (or period_end_date) as the time axis for leave-taken trends.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: End of the pay period this slice was deducted in. Pair it with period_start_date to attribute the units to a payroll period, not to the days actually taken: the leave request's own start_date/end_date can sit anywhere inside or across these boundaries, so a slice dated to a period does not mean the absence happened evenly across it.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave consumed in this period — the only additive leave quantity in the domain. Units are the leave type's typeOfUnits (usually hours); summing across types with different units produces a meaningless number.

columns.name: period_status
columns.description: Approved = scheduled/approved but not yet run through payroll; Completed = processed in a finalised pay run. 'Leave actually taken and paid' filters Completed; forward-looking liability includes Approved.

joins.note: Slices of the parent request; employee and leave type come from the parent.

examples.question: Leave hours taken per month this year (completed only)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', p.period_start_date) AS month, SUM(p.number_of_units) AS units
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_periods p
WHERE p.period_status = 'Completed'
  AND p.period_start_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Top 10 employees by leave units taken in the last 6 months
examples.sql:
SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, SUM(p.number_of_units) AS units
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_periods p
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave l ON l.leave_id = p.leave_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = l.employee_id
WHERE p.period_status = 'Completed' AND p.period_start_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months'
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
ORDER BY units DESC LIMIT 10

tables.grain: one leave-type enrolment (accrual rule) per employee per leave type
tables.description: The per-employee accrual configuration for each leave type the employee is enrolled in: accrual schedule, annual hours, caps and opening balance. This is the RULE; the resulting number lives in xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_balances. Distinct from the org-level catalogue xero_payroll_uk_leave_types, which defines the types themselves — join it for names and paid/statutory flags.
gotchas: hours_accrued_annually = 0 under OnHourWorked is by design — annual entitlement for those employees is rate_accrued_hourly x hours worked, not zero.
This table configures accrual per employee; the org-level xero_payroll_uk_leave_types defines the types. Counting 'leave types' from here counts enrolments, not types.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The enrolled employee; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The org leave type this enrolment configures; join xero_payroll_uk_leave_types for its name.

columns.name: schedule_of_accrual
columns.description: When entitlement is granted. Annual-upfront schedules (BeginningOfCalendarYear, OnAnniversaryDate) make mid-year balances look generous; EachPayPeriod and OnHourWorked accrue gradually. Compare balances only within the same schedule.

columns.name: hours_accrued_annually
columns.description: Annual accrual in hours — but ALWAYS 0 when schedule_of_accrual is OnHourWorked (use rate_accrued_hourly instead). Treating that 0 as 'no entitlement' is the classic wrong answer here.

columns.name: maximum_to_accrue
columns.description: Cap on the accruable balance; null means uncapped. Relevant when projecting future balances.

columns.name: opening_balance
columns.description: Hours granted when the type was first assigned to the employee — a setup constant, not the current balance (that is the balances table).

columns.name: rate_accrued_hourly
columns.description: Hours of leave earned per hour worked; normally 0 except under OnHourWorked (the 12.07% holiday-accrual pattern for casual staff appears here as ~0.1207).

columns.name: schedule_of_accrual_date
columns.description: The anniversary date entitlement lands on; only populated when schedule_of_accrual is OnAnniversaryDate.

joins.note: Per-employee fan-out.
Org-level catalogue with names and paid/statutory flags.

examples.question: How does holiday accrue across the workforce?
examples.sql:
SELECT elt.schedule_of_accrual, COUNT(DISTINCT elt.employee_id) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_types elt
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = elt.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY elt.schedule_of_accrual ORDER BY employees DESC

tables.grain: one effective-dated National Insurance category assignment per employee per array position
tables.description: The employee's NI category letter history, exploded from the employee record. The category letter decides the employer and employee NIC rates (A standard, C over state pension age, M/Z under 21, H apprentice under 25, V veteran, F/I/L/S Freeport, N/E/K/D Investment Zone), so any employer-NIC cost model keys off the CURRENT letter: the row with the latest start_date. Rows are assignments over time, not a point-in-time attribute — joining all rows to payslips multiplies pay.
gotchas: This is a history, not an attribute: an employee with three category rows appears three times. 'Current category' = the row with the greatest start_date; joining the whole table to payslips triples pay for that employee.
The deprecated flat Employee.niCategory can disagree with this list mid-year; this table wins.
Category letters encode reliefs, not just rates — treating V or F rows as standard category A overstates employer NIC cost.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Parent employee; inherited from the record the array was exploded from.

columns.name: ordinal
columns.description: Stable position of this assignment in the employee's niCategories array; part of the key because niCategoryID is optional in the payload.

columns.name: ni_category_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the NI category assignment. Numeric (not a uuid) and optional — prefer (employee_id, ordinal) for row identity.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: When this category letter takes effect. The employee's CURRENT category is the row with MAX(start_date) not after today; historical NIC recalculations need the letter effective on the pay period's payment date.

columns.name: ni_category
columns.description: The NI category letter. This single letter sets both employer and employee NIC rates: X means no NICs at all (e.g. under 16), C exempts the employee but not the employer, V/F/I/L/S/N/E/K/D carry employer reliefs. Costing 'employer NIC at 15%' uniformly across letters is wrong.
columns.enums: A; B; C; F; H; I; J; L; M; S; V; X; Z; D; E; K; N

columns.name: date_first_employed_as_civilian
columns.description: Only meaningful for veteran relief (category V): the 12-month employer-NIC holiday runs from this date, not from start_date. Null for non-veterans.

columns.name: workplace_postcode
columns.description: The WORKPLACE postcode that qualifies Freeport/Investment Zone category letters — not the employee's home postcode (that is on the employee row). Required by HMRC for F/I/L/S and N/E/K/D letters.

joins.note: Explode child of the employee record.

examples.question: Current NI category mix of the active workforce
examples.sql:
SELECT c.ni_category, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (employee_id) employee_id, ni_category
  FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_ni_categories
  WHERE start_date <= CURRENT_DATE
  ORDER BY employee_id, start_date DESC
) c
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = c.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY c.ni_category ORDER BY employees DESC

tables.grain: one migration-time opening balance record per employee
tables.description: Fiscal year-to-date statutory pay amounts the employee had ALREADY received before the organisation started (or re-based) Xero payroll, plus the prior employer's staff number. These carry-in figures exist so statutory pay caps (e.g. 28 weeks SSP) compute correctly mid-year. Any 'statutory pay this tax year' total must be payslip amounts PLUS these openings, or mid-year-migrated orgs under-report.
tables.additivityAxis: time — a one-time migration snapshot per employee; never add it to itself across syncs or treat it as a recurring amount
gotchas: These are pre-Xero carry-ins, not live balances: 'SMP paid this tax year' = opening balance + payslip SMP lines. Using either alone is wrong for orgs that migrated mid-year.
All-zero rows are the norm for employees hired after the org joined Xero — zero is not evidence that statutory pay never happened, only that none predates Xero.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee the opening balances belong to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: statutory_adoption_pay
columns.description: SAP already received this fiscal year before Xero took over. Zero means either none or the org migrated at fiscal year start — check the org's first pay run before concluding 'no adoption pay'.

columns.name: statutory_maternity_pay
columns.description: SMP already received this fiscal year pre-migration; add to payslip SMP for a true fiscal-YTD figure and for testing against the 39-week entitlement.

columns.name: statutory_paternity_pay
columns.description: SPP already received this fiscal year before Xero took over payroll. Ordinary statutory paternity pay runs to a small fixed number of weeks, so a non-zero opening here can mean the entitlement is already spent and no further SPP is due in this employment — a payslip-only view would show none paid and wrongly conclude the leave never happened.

columns.name: statutory_shared_parental_pay
columns.description: Shared parental pay already received this fiscal year before Xero took over payroll. ShPP is carved out of the mother's or primary adopter's maternity/adoption entitlement, so this figure and statutory_maternity_pay/statutory_adoption_pay are competing draws on one pot rather than independent amounts — add them for a fiscal-YTD statutory total, but never read them as separate entitlements when testing remaining weeks.

columns.name: statutory_sick_pay
columns.description: SSP already received this fiscal year pre-migration; without it, weeks-of-SSP-remaining computed from Xero payslips alone overstates remaining entitlement.

columns.name: prior_employee_number
columns.description: The staff number issued by the employee's former employer (or former payroll system). A matching hint for imported HR data, never an analysis key — it is not unique in Xero.

joins.note: At most one opening-balance record per employee.

examples.question: Employees who carried statutory pay balances into Xero
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name,
       ob.statutory_maternity_pay, ob.statutory_sick_pay
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_opening_balances ob
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = ob.employee_id
WHERE COALESCE(ob.statutory_maternity_pay,0) + COALESCE(ob.statutory_paternity_pay,0)
    + COALESCE(ob.statutory_adoption_pay,0) + COALESCE(ob.statutory_shared_parental_pay,0)
    + COALESCE(ob.statutory_sick_pay,0) > 0

tables.grain: one standing earnings line per employee's pay template (payTemplateEarningID)
tables.description: The employee's pay template: standing earnings instructions (regular allowances, fixed amounts, default units) that seed each new pay run. These are TEMPLATES, not actual pay — the payslip earnings lines in the sibling pay-run domain are the actuals, and a run can be edited after seeding. Use this table for 'who has a standing allowance' and expected-pay modelling, never for amounts actually paid.
gotchas: Template amounts are standing instructions, not payments — 'total allowances paid' from this table is a forecast at best; actuals are payslip earnings lines in the pay-run domain.
The upstream spec's description of numberOfUnits is a copy-paste error ('The rate per unit'); trust the field name, not the vendor docstring.
Base salary usually lives in xero_payroll_uk_employee_salary_and_wages, not here — pay templates typically carry the extras (allowances, recurring bonuses).

columns.name: pay_template_earning_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the standing earnings line and the row key.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee whose template this line belongs to — carried on the template record itself.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Which org earnings rate the line applies; join xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates for its name, type and unit semantics.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Employee-specific override of the rate per unit; null falls back to the earnings rate's default or the salary basis. A rate, never summable.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Default units seeded per pay run. The spec mislabels this field's description as 'the rate per unit' — it is the unit count; expected amount is number_of_units x rate_per_unit (or fixed_amount).

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Fixed amount seeded per period for fixed-amount earnings; mutually exclusive in practice with rate x units. Still a template figure, not money paid.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Read-only display name of the earnings line, denormalized from the earnings rate; the join on earnings_rate_id is authoritative.

joins.note: Per-employee fan-out (one template per employee, many lines).
Rate semantics (RatePerUnit vs FixedAmount vs multiplier) come from the earnings rate.

examples.question: Active employees with a standing allowance and its expected per-period value
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, er.name AS earning,
       COALESCE(pt.fixed_amount, pt.number_of_units * pt.rate_per_unit) AS expected_per_period
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_pay_template_earnings pt
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = pt.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates er ON er.earnings_rate_id = pt.earnings_rate_id
WHERE er.earnings_type = 'Allowance'

examples.question: Which earnings rates are used as standing template lines, and by how many current employees?
examples.sql:
SELECT er.name AS earning, er.earnings_type, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.employee_id) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_pay_template_earnings pt
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = pt.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates er ON er.earnings_rate_id = pt.earnings_rate_id
GROUP BY er.name, er.earnings_type
ORDER BY employees DESC

tables.grain: one net-pay payment method configuration per employee
tables.description: How each employee's net pay leaves the business: electronically (BACS file), by cheque, or recorded as paid manually. The destination bank accounts for electronic payment live in the child table xero_payroll_uk_employee_bank_accounts. Operationally load-bearing for 'who is in the bank file' questions; analytically a small but telling dimension of payroll process maturity.
gotchas: Bank account rows can exist while payment_method is Cheque/Manual (leftover config) — the method column, not the presence of accounts, decides how pay actually moves.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee this payment configuration belongs to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: Electronically means Xero generates bank-file lines from the child bank accounts; Cheque and Manual employees are paid outside the file. A payment-run reconciliation that assumes everyone is electronic misses them.

columns.name: bank_accounts
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_bank_accounts (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: One configuration per employee.
Destination accounts; only meaningful when payment_method = 'Electronically'.

examples.question: How are active employees paid?
examples.sql:
SELECT pm.payment_method, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_payment_methods pm
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = pm.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY pm.payment_method

tables.grain: one effective-dated salary or wage basis record per salaryAndWagesID
tables.description: The employee's pay basis history: each row fixes an annual salary or hourly arrangement from an effective date, with exactly one Active row per employee at a time (Pending = future-dated change, History = superseded). This is the table for salary bill, pay-rise and pay-basis questions. annual_salary is a stock, not a flow: it is safe to add ACROSS employees once you have picked one row per employee (status = 'Active', or the latest effective_from at the date in question), and never safe to add across an employee's own rows — summing annual_salary without that filter adds every historical salary the employee ever had.
tables.additivityAxis: effective_from / status — the effective-dated version axis. Each employee has one live basis at a time; SUM is only meaningful over a set that contains at most one row per employee, so collapse to status = 'Active' (or the latest effective_from <= the as-at date) before adding anything up.
gotchas: SUM(annual_salary) without status = 'Active' sums every salary the employee ever had — the single most common wrong number from this table.
annual_salary for Hourly staff is rate x contracted units extrapolated to a year; actual pay follows timesheets. Do not present it as guaranteed cost.
Terminated employees keep their records; join the employee table and require end_date IS NULL for a current salary bill.

columns.name: salary_and_wages_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for this pay-basis record and the row key.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee the pay basis belongs to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The ordinary earnings rate the basis pays through — also the base rate that MultipleOfOrdinaryEarningsRate overtime rates multiply.

columns.name: number_of_units_per_week
columns.description: Contracted units (hours) per week. The FTE denominator for pro-rating: comparing annual_salary across staff without normalizing by this punishes part-timers.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Hourly rate for Hourly payment types; derived for salaried staff. The number to test against National Minimum/Living Wage floors — annual_salary is not.

columns.name: number_of_units_per_day
columns.description: Contracted units per day; used for daily-rate pro-rating of starters, leavers and unpaid leave.

columns.name: effective_from
columns.description: The date this basis takes effect. Point-in-time salary questions pick the record where effective_from <= the date, preferring Active/History over Pending.

columns.name: annual_salary
columns.description: Annual salary in GBP for this basis. For Hourly employees it is an extrapolation from rate x units — real earnings vary with hours worked, so 'salary bill' for hourly staff is an estimate, not a commitment.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Active is the one live basis per employee; Pending is future-dated; History is superseded. Every current-pay aggregate filters Active — including History double-counts, including Pending books unstarted raises.

columns.name: payment_type
columns.description: Salary (fixed per period) vs Hourly (earnings follow hours). Segment cost analyses on this: hourly annual figures are projections while salaried ones are commitments.

joins.note: Full effective-dated history per employee.
The ordinary earnings rate the basis pays through.

examples.question: Current annual salary bill for active employees
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(sw.annual_salary) AS annual_salary_bill
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_salary_and_wages sw
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = sw.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
WHERE sw.status = 'Active'

examples.question: Pay rises that took effect this year
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, prev.annual_salary AS old_salary, cur.annual_salary AS new_salary, cur.effective_from
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_salary_and_wages cur
JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT annual_salary FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_salary_and_wages p
  WHERE p.employee_id = cur.employee_id AND p.effective_from < cur.effective_from
  ORDER BY p.effective_from DESC LIMIT 1
) prev ON true
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = cur.employee_id
WHERE cur.status = 'Active' AND cur.effective_from >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  AND cur.annual_salary > prev.annual_salary
ORDER BY cur.effective_from

tables.grain: one statutory leave balance per employee per statutory leave type per as-of date the scan requested
tables.description: Remaining statutory entitlement (SSP, SMP, SPP, SAP, ShPP, bereavement, neonatal care) per employee, fetched one leave type at a time with an explicit as-of date. The ingester must enumerate LeaveType values per employee, so coverage depends on the scan plan — treat absence of a row as 'not fetched', not 'no entitlement'. Because the endpoint answers a question ('what is left on this date?') rather than returning a stored record, the AsOfDate the scan passed is part of the row's identity: two passes on different dates produce two legitimately different rows for the same employee and type. Balances are expressed in Hours even though statutory entitlements are legally defined in weeks.
tables.additivityAxis: as_of_date — the balance is a snapshot pinned to the AsOfDate the scan used; never sum across as-of dates, and pick MAX(as_of_date) per (employee, leave type) before comparing or ranking
gotchas: Rows exist only for (employee, type) pairs the ingester requested — a missing row means unfetched, not zero entitlement. Answers should say the balance was not synced rather than report 0.

The balance is pinned to as_of_date, not to today. Presenting an old row as 'the balance now' overstates remaining entitlement for anyone who has been off since — always select the row with MAX(as_of_date) per (employee_id, leave_type) and quote that date in the answer.
This endpoint is availability-optional: it multiplies scan volume by employees x leave types and may be skipped by the scan plan.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee whose statutory balance this is; inherited from the fan-out path parameter.

columns.name: leave_type
columns.description: Which statutory entitlement the balance measures. Each type has its own statutory cap (28 weeks SSP, 39 paid weeks SMP...), so compare balances within a type only.
columns.enums: Sick; Adoption; Maternity; Paternity; Sharedparental; Bereavement; NeonatalCare

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.api: synthetic:AsOfDate query parameter of GET /Employees/{EmployeeID}/StatutoryLeaveBalance — the response body carries no date, so the ingester stamps the date it asked about
columns.description: The date the balance was calculated for, stamped from the request. Without it the row is undated and every 'remaining entitlement' answer silently claims to be current: a balance computed six months ago against an ongoing sickness absence is stale by construction, not by sync lag. Part of the key so a backfill that asks about several dates does not overwrite itself. Always report it alongside balance_remaining.

columns.name: balance_remaining
columns.description: Entitlement remaining as of the scan's AsOfDate, in Hours. Converting to statutory weeks requires the employee's working pattern — dividing by 40 is a guess, not a rule.

columns.name: units
columns.description: Always Hours per the spec — kept so unit-checking logic can be uniform across all balance tables.

joins.note: Per-employee fan-out, one row per requested statutory type.

examples.question: Active employees with under 8 weeks (assuming 37.5h weeks) of SSP entitlement left
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, b.balance_remaining, b.as_of_date
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (employee_id, leave_type) employee_id, leave_type, balance_remaining, as_of_date
  FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_statutory_leave_balances
  WHERE leave_type = 'Sick'
  ORDER BY employee_id, leave_type, as_of_date DESC
) b
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = b.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
WHERE b.balance_remaining < 8 * 37.5
ORDER BY b.balance_remaining

tables.grain: one current PAYE tax configuration per employee
tables.description: The employee's live HMRC tax settings: tax code, W1/M1 basis, starter declaration, P45 carry-in figures, student/postgraduate loan flags and director NIC treatment. This is CURRENT STATE ONLY — Xero returns no tax-code history, so questions about what code applied to a past payslip cannot be answered from here; the payslip's own tax lines are the record of what was actually deducted.
gotchas: Current-state only: Xero keeps no tax-code history here. 'What code was used in April' must come from the payslip's tax lines, not this table.
w1_m1 = TRUE breaks cumulative reconciliation on purpose — flagging those employees' YTD tax as anomalous is a false positive.
previous_taxable_pay/previous_tax_paid are P45 carry-ins: fiscal-YTD earnings computed from payslips alone understate income for mid-year joiners.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee this tax record belongs to; inherited from the fan-out path parameter (the payload itself carries no id).

columns.name: starter_type
columns.description: How the employee joined for PAYE purposes (e.g. P45 vs starter checklist). Explains why previous_taxable_pay is or is not populated.

columns.name: starter_declaration
columns.description: The HMRC starter statement (A: first job this year, B: only job now, C: has another job/pension). C-declaration employees are commonly on BR/0T codes — a cluster of them is a second-jobs population, not a payroll error.

columns.name: tax_code
columns.description: The current PAYE code (1257L, BR, 0T, K497...). K-prefixed codes ADD notional pay rather than granting allowance, so 'allowance = code x 10' arithmetic is wrong for them. This is today's code — not necessarily the code any historical payslip used.

columns.name: w1_m1
columns.description: TRUE means the code operates non-cumulatively (week 1/month 1): each period is taxed in isolation and YTD tax will not reconcile to the cumulative code-implied amount. Any 'expected tax vs actual' check must branch on this flag.

columns.name: previous_taxable_pay
columns.description: Taxable pay from the prior employment this tax year (P45 figure). Include it when computing an employee's true fiscal-YTD taxable pay — payslips alone only cover this employment.

columns.name: previous_tax_paid
columns.description: Tax already paid in the prior employment this tax year (P45 figure); the companion to previous_taxable_pay for cumulative-code calculations.

columns.name: student_loan_deduction
columns.description: Which student loan plan is being deducted (Plan 1, 2, 4 and 5 style values); null/empty means no student loan is operating. Each plan has its own repayment threshold and rate, so counting 'has a loan' is safe while comparing or averaging deduction amounts across plans is not. Postgraduate loans are a separate, stacking deduction — see has_post_graduate_loans, not this field.

columns.name: has_post_graduate_loans
columns.description: TRUE when a postgraduate loan is deducted IN ADDITION to any student loan plan — the two stack, they are not alternatives.

columns.name: is_director
columns.description: TRUE for company directors, whose NICs are computed on an annual (or annualised) earnings period. Directors' per-period NIC looks 'wrong' next to regular employees by design — segment them out of NIC-rate sanity checks.

columns.name: directorship_start_date
columns.description: When the directorship began; pro-rates the annual NIC earnings period in the first year.

columns.name: nic_calculation_method
columns.description: For directors: annual vs alternative (per-period with annual true-up) NIC method. Explains large final-period NIC catch-ups under the alternative method.

joins.note: Exactly one tax record per employee.

examples.question: Active employees on a non-cumulative (W1/M1) or BR/0T code
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, t.tax_code, t.w1_m1
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employee_tax t
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id AND e.end_date IS NULL
WHERE t.w1_m1 OR t.tax_code IN ('BR', '0T')
ORDER BY e.last_name

tables.grain: one current or former UK payroll employee per employeeID within the organisation
tables.description: The master roster of everyone the organisation pays through Xero UK Payroll: current staff, leavers, and off-payroll workers. This is the anchor of the whole UK payroll domain — every leave, tax, salary, timesheet and payslip row hangs off employee_id. Headcount questions must filter end_date (null means still employed) AND is_off_payroll_worker, or contractors inflate the number. Note start_date/end_date are the employment dates 'at the time it was requested' — a convenience snapshot; the authoritative employment episode history is xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts. These tables are only populated for tenants running UK payroll; a tenant has AU or UK or NZ payroll, never two, so never union across regions.
gotchas: Payroll is region-exclusive: a tenant has UK OR AU OR NZ payroll. An empty table usually means the tenant does not run UK payroll, not that sync failed — never union with the AU/NZ employee tables.
'Active employees' requires end_date IS NULL; leavers remain in the API forever. Adding is_off_payroll_worker = false removes IR35 contractors from true-employee headcount.

start_date/end_date are documented 'at the time it was requested' — a current-state snapshot. Re-hire and episode history belongs to xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts; tenure across a break in service computed from this table alone is wrong.
ni_category (flat) is deprecated in the spec; effective-dated NI categories live in xero_payroll_uk_employee_ni_categories and only the latest-dated row is the current one.

Deletion shows up as absence, not as a status. Unlike accounting documents there is no VOIDED/DELETED marker on an employee: a leaver stays visible with end_date set, while a record actually removed in Xero simply stops appearing in GET /Employees. Only full-identity reconciliation catches that — an incremental sync driven by updated_date_utc alone leaves phantom employees in staging and overstates every headcount.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the employee and the join key for every other table in this domain, including the sibling pay-run/payslip domain.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Honorific (Mr, Ms, Dr...). Presentation only; never a grouping dimension.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Employee's first name. PII — display only, never aggregate on names (duplicates exist; the key is employee_id).

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Employee's last name. PII — display only; two John Smiths are two rows, so counting names undercounts people.

columns.name: date_of_birth
columns.description: Date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD). Drives NI category eligibility (under-21 M/Z, state-pension-age C) and pension auto-enrolment ages. Sensitive PII.

columns.name: address_address_line1
columns.description: Line 1 of the employee's HOME address (the HMRC-reported address), not a work location. PII.

columns.name: address_address_line2
columns.description: Line 2 of the home address; frequently null — null here does not mean the address is incomplete.

columns.name: address_city
columns.description: City/suburb of the home address. Usable for coarse where-our-people-live analysis, but it is where staff live, not where they work — do not present it as an office dimension.

columns.name: address_post_code
columns.description: Home postcode. Distinct from ni_categories.workplace_postcode, which is the WORKPLACE postcode used for Freeport/Investment Zone NIC relief — mixing them up breaks any NIC-relief analysis.

columns.name: address_country_name
columns.description: Country of the home address. Often null for UK-resident employees; treat null as United Kingdom rather than unknown when profiling.

columns.name: email
columns.description: Employee's email address. PII and an identity-matching hint across systems; not guaranteed unique or present.

columns.name: gender
columns.description: HMRC-reportable gender marker, restricted to M/F by the API. Sensitive personal data — fine for statutory gender pay analysis, but label it as the payroll marker, not self-described identity.

columns.name: phone_number
columns.description: Whatever number the org captured for the employee — mobile or landline, unvalidated free text with no country-code convention and frequently blank. PII, display only, and never an identity or dedup key: it is neither unique (shared household numbers) nor stable, and a blank means nobody typed one in, not that the employee is uncontactable.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Employment start date as of the moment the record was fetched. For point-in-time headcount or tenure use this, but for re-hires and contract changes trust xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts — this field is a snapshot, not a history.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Employment end date; NULL means currently employed. Every 'current headcount' or 'active staff' filter is end_date IS NULL (optionally AND start_date <= CURRENT_DATE) — forgetting it counts every leaver ever paid.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The pay-run calendar this employee is paid on. Join to xero_payroll_uk_pay_run_calendars to split the workforce into weekly vs monthly payroll populations before comparing pay-period figures.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change; the incremental-sync watermark, not a business event date.

columns.name: created_date_utc
columns.description: When the record was created IN XERO — for migrated orgs this is the migration date, not the hire date. Never use it for tenure; use start_date/contracts.

columns.name: ni_category
columns.description: DEPRECATED single NI category letter. Xero now returns the effective-dated list in xero_payroll_uk_employee_ni_categories; this flat field can be stale when a category changed mid-year. Do not build employer-NIC analysis on it.
columns.enums: A; B; C; F; H; I; J; L; M; S; V; X; Z; D; E; K; N

columns.name: national_insurance_number
columns.description: The employee's NI number — a government identifier and the strongest cross-system person-matching key. Highly sensitive PII; never surface in answers unless explicitly requested.

columns.name: is_off_payroll_worker
columns.description: TRUE marks an IR35 off-payroll worker (deemed employee paid via an intermediary). They sit in this table and get payslips, but they are not employees for headcount, pension auto-enrolment or statutory-leave purposes — most workforce metrics should exclude them explicitly.

columns.name: ni_categories
columns.description: The employee's NI categories Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_ni_categories (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: contracts
columns.description: The employee's contracts Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_contracts (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

columns.name: earning_templates
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_employee_pay_template_earnings (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Which pay frequency population the employee belongs to.
Actual pay lives in the sibling pay-run domain; this table is the who, payslips are the how-much.

examples.question: Current employee headcount (excluding off-payroll workers)
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employees
WHERE end_date IS NULL
  AND (is_off_payroll_worker IS DISTINCT FROM true)
  AND (start_date IS NULL OR start_date <= CURRENT_DATE)

examples.question: Starters and leavers by month this year
examples.sql:
SELECT month, SUM(starters) AS starters, SUM(leavers) AS leavers
FROM (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', start_date) AS month, 1 AS starters, 0 AS leavers
  FROM xero_payroll_uk_employees WHERE start_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date_trunc('month', end_date), 0, 1
  FROM xero_payroll_uk_employees WHERE end_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
) t
GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

tables.grain: one org-level leave type per leaveTypeID
tables.description: The organisation's catalogue of leave types (holiday, sickness, unpaid leave...), with the flags that change how leave costs and displays: paid vs unpaid, statutory vs org-defined, active vs retired. Employee leave requests, balances and per-employee accrual rules all join here for names and flags. Distinct from the per-employee enrolment table xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave_types.
gotchas: Names are org-defined free text — two tenants' 'Holiday' and 'Annual Leave' are the same concept; classify with is_paid_leave/is_statutory_leave flags, not names.
If the scan passed ActiveOnly=true, retired types vanish and old leave rows dangle without a type — the ingester must fetch all types.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the leave type — the key every leave table joins on.

columns.name: leave_id
columns.description: A secondary Xero identifier ('for the leave') that shadows leave_type_id in some payloads; keep for lineage, join on leave_type_id.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name ('Holiday', 'Sickness'...). Org-defined and not standardised across tenants — never string-match names to classify; use the flags.

columns.name: is_paid_leave
columns.description: Whether taking this leave pays the employee. The gate for costing absence: unpaid leave has zero direct wage cost, and paid-absence liability should filter TRUE.

columns.name: show_on_payslip
columns.description: Payslip presentation toggle for the balance; no cost meaning.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: UTC audit stamp of the last edit to the leave-type definition and the incremental-sync watermark for this catalogue. It changes on configuration edits (rename, retirement), not when anyone takes leave — leave activity dates live on requests and periods.

columns.name: is_active
columns.description: FALSE = retired type. The list op's ActiveOnly parameter can hide these at source — the ingester requests all; analysts filter here.

columns.name: is_statutory_leave
columns.description: TRUE marks Xero-managed statutory types (sick, maternity...). Requests against them flow through the statutory leave tables, not ordinary employee leave — a hint for which family answers the question.

joins.note: Requests drawing on this type.
Current balances per employee for this type.

examples.question: Which paid, non-statutory leave types are active?
examples.sql:
SELECT name FROM xero_payroll_uk_leave_types
WHERE is_active AND is_paid_leave AND NOT COALESCE(is_statutory_leave, false)

tables.grain: one payroll calendar (pay frequency schedule) per payrollCalendarID
tables.description: The org's pay schedules: frequency (weekly through annual), the CURRENT period's start/end and its payment date. Employees and timesheets reference a calendar, making this the dimension that splits the workforce into pay-frequency populations. The period dates roll forward as pay runs post — they describe the current period at sync time, not a fixed anchor, so never treat them as the schedule's first-ever period.
gotchas: period_start_date/period_end_date/payment_date describe the current period as of the last sync — historical period boundaries must come from pay runs, not this table.
FourWeekly is not Monthly: a four-weekly calendar pays 13 times a year, so 'monthly payroll cost' from four-weekly periods needs a 13/12 adjustment.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the calendar; employees, timesheets and pay runs reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The org's label for this pay schedule ('Monthly Salaries', 'Weekly Wages'...). Useful for presenting a calendar to a human, but never for inferring frequency — a calendar named 'Monthly' can be configured Fortnightly. calendar_type is the only trustworthy frequency; an org can also run several calendars of the same type (separate sites or entities), so names are not unique either.

columns.name: calendar_type
columns.description: Pay frequency. Comparing per-period figures across calendars of different types compares a week of pay to a month of pay — normalise to annual or monthly first.
columns.enums: Weekly; Fortnightly; FourWeekly; Monthly; Annual; Quarterly

columns.name: period_start_date
columns.description: Start of the CURRENT (next unposted) period at sync time; rolls forward with each pay run. Not the calendar's inception date.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: End of the current period at sync time; rolls forward like period_start_date.

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: When the current period pays out — the payday. For 'when is the next payroll' questions, this is the answer, freshness permitting.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: UTC audit stamp of the last change to the calendar record and this table's incremental-sync watermark. Because the period dates roll forward each time a pay run posts, this timestamp moves with routine payroll activity — a recent value means the schedule is in use, not that anyone redesigned it. Never present it as a business event date; paydays come from payment_date.

joins.note: The pay-frequency population on this calendar.

examples.question: How many active employees are on each pay frequency?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.calendar_type, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM xero_payroll_uk_employees e
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_run_calendars c ON c.payroll_calendar_id = e.payroll_calendar_id
WHERE e.end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY c.calendar_type ORDER BY employees DESC

tables.grain: one UK payroll pay run: one processing of one payroll calendar over one pay period
tables.description: The processing container for UK payroll. Each row is one run of one payroll calendar, carrying run-level totals: total_cost is what the employer spent (gross pay plus employer NI and other on-costs), total_pay is what employees actually took home (net). Draft runs are provisional and mutate freely until posted; only Posted runs represent money that moved and RTI submissions that happened. EarlierYearUpdate runs are HMRC corrections to a PREVIOUS tax year and must never be counted as current-period cost. A payroll calendar period can hold more than one run (an Unscheduled run alongside the Scheduled one), so never assume period dates uniquely identify a run.
gotchas: Draft runs are returned by the API with live provisional totals. Any sum that does not filter pay_run_status = 'Posted' counts money that was never paid.
EarlierYearUpdate runs restate a PRIOR tax year. Including them in current-period cost double-counts corrections in the wrong year.
UK payroll reporting runs on the tax year (6 April to 5 April) keyed by payment_date. Calendar-year sums will not reconcile to P60s, P32s or HMRC figures.
PayRun has no modified watermark; Draft runs mutate silently between scans. Treat Draft rows as volatile until pay_run_status flips to Posted.
One calendar period can contain multiple runs (Scheduled + Unscheduled). Grouping by period dates without pay_run_id merges distinct runs.

UK payroll is region-exclusive: a tenant runs UK or AU or NZ payroll, never two. An empty table here means the tenant is not on UK payroll, not that payroll is missing — and these tables must never be unioned with xero_payroll_au_* or xero_payroll_nz_* to build a 'group payroll' figure, because the objects are not the same shape.

Joining pay runs to payslips and then summing total_cost or total_pay multiplies the run-level total by the number of payslips on the run. Take run totals from this table alone, or pre-aggregate payslips to pay_run_id before joining.

There is no currency field anywhere in UK payroll — every amount is GBP by construction. Never apply an accounting-side CurrencyRate to these figures, and convert the other side before comparing them with foreign-currency invoice or bank amounts.

payRunStatus carries no deleted or voided value: the enum is Draft and Posted only. A Draft run deleted in Xero simply stops being returned, leaving no tombstone, so disappearances must be caught by a full identity scan of PayRunIDs — a status filter will never find them.

columns.name: pay_run_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable pay run identifier and the row key; the fan-out handle for fetching this run's payslips.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The pay frequency calendar this run was processed under. Orgs commonly run several calendars at once (weekly wages plus monthly salaries), so 'the March payroll' is usually two or more runs — group by this id before comparing periods. This domain's ground truth contains no PayRunCalendar object, so there is no calendar dimension here and calendar_type carries the frequency inline; the id stays a stable join key if a payroll-config domain later lands one.

columns.name: period_start_date
columns.description: First day of the earnings period this run pays for. Use the period dates for accrual-style cost attribution (which month the work happened), not for when cash left the bank — that is payment_date.

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: Last day of the earnings period. periodStart/End come from the payroll calendar and can be identical across a Scheduled and an Unscheduled run — they are not a key.

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: The date employees are paid — the date that decides which UK tax period the run falls into for PAYE/RTI purposes. Cash-basis payroll cost and tax-year reporting bucket by this date, not by the period dates; mixing the two shifts runs across month and tax-year boundaries.

columns.name: total_cost
columns.description: The employer's all-in spend for the run: gross earnings plus employer taxes (employer NI, Apprenticeship Levy) and employer-borne items. This is the number for 'what does payroll cost us' — total_pay is not (that is net take-home). Draft runs carry provisional values that change on every recalculation.

columns.name: total_pay
