columns.description: Total NET pay for the run — the sum actually transferred to employees after tax, NI, deductions and court orders. Despite the name it is neither gross nor cost; treating it as either understates payroll spend materially.

columns.name: pay_run_status
columns.description: Draft runs are work-in-progress: totals move, payslips get added and removed, nothing has been paid or reported to HMRC. Every financial aggregate must filter payRunStatus = 'Posted' or draft noise contaminates real history.

columns.name: pay_run_type
columns.description: Scheduled is the regular calendar run; Unscheduled is an off-cycle run (corrections, bonuses, leavers) that shares the same period; EarlierYearUpdate is an HMRC correction to a prior tax year. Period-cost questions include Scheduled + Unscheduled and EXCLUDE EarlierYearUpdate — EYU amounts belong to the year they amend, not the year they were posted.

columns.name: calendar_type
columns.description: Pay frequency of the underlying calendar, and the reason run-level totals are not comparable row to row: a Weekly run covers roughly a quarter of what a Monthly one does (52 weeks against 12 months — not exactly four weeks per month, which is why 'weekly x4' reconciliations drift). Annualize with the factor for the VALUE, not for its position in the enum: Weekly x52, Fortnightly x26, FourWeekly x13, Monthly x12, Quarterly x4, Annual x1. An 'average pay per run' computed across mixed frequencies is a number about nothing.
columns.enums: Weekly; Fortnightly; FourWeekly; Monthly; Annual; Quarterly

columns.name: posted_date_time
columns.description: When the run was posted (finalized). Null/absent for Draft runs. This is an audit stamp — the business date for reporting is payment_date; the two can straddle a month end.

joins.note: Per-employee detail. Payslips inherit no status of their own — this join is how payslip-level aggregates filter to Posted runs.

examples.question: Monthly employer payroll cost this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', payment_date) AS month, SUM(total_cost) AS employer_cost
FROM xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs
WHERE pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND pay_run_type IN ('Scheduled', 'Unscheduled')
  AND payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: How much of payroll spend never reaches employees as take-home pay?
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(total_cost) AS employer_cost,
       SUM(total_pay) AS net_paid,
       SUM(total_cost - total_pay) AS cost_less_take_home
FROM xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs
WHERE pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one benefit line per payslip per position in its benefitLines array
tables.description: Non-earnings compensation applied on the payslip — the spec's own framing is fringe benefits and perks provided in addition to normal earnings. These amounts sit outside the gross-to-net bridge entirely: not in gross_earnings, not in total_pay, so no benefit line is cash the employee received. The analytically dangerous part is that one array carries two different economic things — an employer contribution that IS new spend, and a payrolled benefit value that is only tax bookkeeping on something already paid for — and the spec gives no flag to tell them apart. Only benefit_type_id and display_name, interpreted against how this org configured its benefit types, can separate them, so treat any sum over this table as unclassified until that mapping is known.
gotchas: Employer-side contributions land in this family while the employee's own contributions are deduction lines, so a pension figure taken from either table alone reports one payer and calls it the total. Build it as employer benefit lines plus employee deduction lines, reported separately by payer — and verify via benefit_type_id which lines are contributions at all before adding them.

Benefit amounts are outside gross and net. Blindly adding total_benefits to total_cost-style figures can double-count (pension may already be in the run's totalCost) or count BIK tax bookkeeping as spend — classify first.
Filter to Posted runs through the payslip join; draft benefit lines track live scheme edits.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the reconciliation handle: lines under one payslip_id sum to that slip's total_benefits. Benefit lines carry no employee or date, so this is also the only path to who received the benefit and in which run.

columns.name: benefit_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's benefitLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

columns.name: benefit_type_id
columns.description: The configured benefit type — the stable classifier that decides what a benefit line actually means, and therefore whether its amount is employer spend or only a taxable value being payrolled. This domain's ground truth contains no BenefitType object, so nothing here names the type: pair with display_name for readability, group by this id for stability, and get the org to confirm the mapping before any of it feeds a cost number.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: Benefit name as shown on the slip ('NEST Pension', 'Private Medical'). Org-controlled free text, and the only human-readable classifier this domain carries, so pattern-matching it is the usual first pass at finding pension lines — but it is a heuristic, not a taxonomy: a scheme named after its provider will not match '%pension%', and a renamed benefit silently changes which rows a saved query returns. Confirm any name-matched set against the distinct benefit_type_id values it covers before publishing the number.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The benefit value applied on this line; sums over a payslip reconcile to its total_benefits. It is not part of net pay and not part of gross, so it never belongs in a take-home or gross figure. Whether it belongs in employment cost depends on what the benefit type is — a contribution the employer funds is spend, a payrolled benefit value is not — so classify by benefit_type_id first and never sum this column into a cost number blind.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: The configured flat amount for fixed benefits; an input echoed from setup, already reflected in amount. Never add the two.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: The configured rate for percentage benefits (e.g. 3% employer pension); a rate, never summed — amount carries the resulting money.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Which benefit types look like pension schemes, and what did they cost by month? (name heuristic — check the type ids it caught)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month,
       COUNT(DISTINCT bl.benefit_type_id) AS type_ids_matched,
       SUM(bl.amount) AS matched_benefit_value
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_benefit_lines bl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = bl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
  AND bl.display_name ILIKE '%pension%'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Benefit spend by benefit type this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT bl.benefit_type_id, MIN(bl.display_name) AS name, SUM(bl.amount) AS value
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_benefit_lines bl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = bl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY value DESC

tables.grain: one court order line per payslip per position in its courtOrderLines array
tables.description: Statutory attachments the employer must divert from the employee's pay under a court or agency order — attachment of earnings orders (AEOs), child maintenance DEOs and similar. Deducted after tax on the way to net; the money is the employee's, redirected — never an employer cost and never a voluntary deduction. Sensitive by nature: rows reveal that an employee is under a court order, so aggregate rather than list employees wherever possible.
gotchas: Court orders are separate from deductions in Xero's model (own total, own lines). Adding them into 'deductions' double-counts against total_deductions-based figures.
The existence of a row is sensitive personal information about the employee. Prefer counts and totals to per-employee listings unless the question demands it.
Filter to Posted runs through the payslip join — a draft-run order line may never have been enforced.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. It identifies whose pay was attached and in which run — court order lines carry neither — which is exactly why joining out through it turns an aggregate into named personal data; do that deliberately, not by habit.

columns.name: court_order_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's courtOrderLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

columns.name: court_order_type_id
columns.description: The configured court order type — the distinction between an attachment of earnings order, a child-maintenance deduction order and a council tax attachment, which differ in priority and in who receives the money. This domain's ground truth contains no CourtOrderType object, so the raw id is the only classifier: without carrying it, every order collapses into one undifferentiated bucket.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Amount diverted under the order this run. Sums reconcile to the payslip's total_court_orders. Part of the gross-to-net bridge; excluded from total_deductions — counting it in both places double-deducts.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Total diverted under court orders by quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', pr.payment_date) AS quarter, SUM(col.amount) AS diverted
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_court_order_lines col
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = col.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: How many employees currently have court order deductions?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ps.employee_id) AS employees_with_orders
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_court_order_lines col
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = col.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  AND pr.payment_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 months'

tables.grain: one deduction line per payslip per position in its deductionLines array
tables.description: Configured deductions taken from the employee's own pay on the way from gross to net — typically employee pension contributions, salary sacrifice, union fees and loan repayments, though what a given org actually configures here is visible only through deduction_type_id. Every amount on this table is the employee's money being redirected, never employer cost. subject_to_tax is the one semantic hinge the spec does give: it states whether the deducted amount remains subject to tax, which separates deductions that shrink taxable pay from those taken after tax has been calculated. Statutory tax and court orders are deliberately NOT here — Xero keeps them in their own arrays and their own payslip totals.
gotchas: This table is the EMPLOYEE side only. An employer contribution never appears as a deduction line, so a 'total pension cost' built from this table alone reports only what staff paid — the employer's share sits outside it (commonly on the benefit lines, but confirm against the org's configured types) and must be added by payer, not netted.
Deductions are not statutory tax (employee_tax_lines) and not court orders (court_order_lines); the three families partition the gross-to-net bridge and must not be mixed or double-counted.
percentage is a configured rate; only amount is money. Filter to Posted runs via the payslip join before any total.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. Deduction lines carry no employee and no date, so this id is how a deduction gets attributed to a person and a pay period — and how it reaches the Posted filter that separates enforced deductions from draft ones.

columns.name: deduction_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's deductionLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (deduction lines carry no natural id).

columns.name: deduction_type_id
columns.description: The configured deduction type applied. This domain's ground truth contains no DeductionType object and this family carries no display name, so the raw id is the only thing separating a pension contribution from union fees or a season-ticket loan — drop it from a breakdown and every deduction collapses into one unreadable bucket. Resolving these ids to names requires the payroll-config domain.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Money withheld from the employee on this line. Sums (within Posted runs) reconcile to the payslip's total_deductions. It is the employee's own money redirected — never add it to employer cost.

columns.name: subject_to_tax
columns.description: Whether the deducted amount is still subject to tax, per the spec — in practice the pre-tax versus post-tax split of the deduction. It matters because deductions taken before tax shrink the pay that tax is calculated on, so an employee sacrificing salary looks like a lower earner on gross-based comparisons while their employer's cost is unchanged. Beware nulls: on a three-way FILTER split, rows where the flag is unset fall into neither bucket and silently vanish from the total.

columns.name: percentage
columns.description: The configured rate for percentage-based deductions (e.g. 5% employee pension); null for flat deductions. A rate, never summed — the resulting money is amount.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Employee pension-style (pre-tax) deductions by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(dl.amount) FILTER (WHERE dl.subject_to_tax IS FALSE) AS pre_tax_deductions,
       SUM(dl.amount) FILTER (WHERE dl.subject_to_tax IS TRUE) AS post_tax_deductions,
       SUM(dl.amount) FILTER (WHERE dl.subject_to_tax IS NULL) AS unclassified,
       SUM(dl.amount) AS total_deductions
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_deduction_lines dl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = dl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Deduction totals by deduction type this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT dl.deduction_type_id, COUNT(*) AS lines, SUM(dl.amount) AS deducted
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_deduction_lines dl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = dl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY deducted DESC

tables.grain: one regular earnings line per payslip per position in its earningsLines array
tables.description: Regular (non-leave, non-timesheet) earnings detail: salary, hourly wages, bonuses, overtime and other configured earnings rates, one row per rate application on a payslip. This family is only PART of gross pay — leave-paid earnings and timesheet-driven earnings live in their own sibling tables, so summing amount here alone understates gross for any org using leave or timesheets. amount is the settled value (ratePerUnit x numberOfUnits, or fixedAmount for Fixed-rate types); the rate and unit columns are inputs and must never be summed.
gotchas: This table is one of THREE earnings families. Gross pay = earnings + leave earnings + timesheet earnings; summing only this table understates gross for orgs using leave or timesheets.
rate_per_unit and fixed_amount are inputs; amount is the value. Summing anything but amount produces nonsense money.
Lines inherit Draft/Posted from the pay run two joins away. Unfiltered sums include provisional draft payroll.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the only way out of this table: an earnings line carries no employee, no date and no status of its own, so every filter that decides whether a number is real (Posted, payment_date, employee) arrives through this id.

columns.name: earnings_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position of this row in the payslip's earningsLines array — the provenance of this table's rows. Forms the key with payslip_id because the spec does not guarantee earningsLineID is present; also preserves Xero's display order.

columns.name: earnings_line_id
columns.description: Xero's own id for this earnings line, and the only line family in this domain that has one. Use it to tell a genuinely amended line from a reordered one when a Draft run is re-scanned — line_index shifts when lines are inserted, this does not. It is deliberately not the key: the spec marks it optional, so it can be absent and cannot be relied on to be unique across a null-heavy load.

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The configured earnings rate (pay item) applied — salary, overtime, bonus and so on. This domain's ground truth contains no EarningsRate object, so there is no rate dimension to join here and display_name is the only human handle; group by this id whenever the org has renamed pay items, because names are edited in place and rewrite history in any name-keyed breakdown.

columns.name: display_name
columns.description: The earnings rate's name as shown on the payslip ('Regular Hours', 'Bonus', ...). Free text controlled by the org — filtering on it ('Overtime') works only as well as the org's naming discipline; earnings_rate_id is the stable key.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Price per unit (hour, day...) for this line — an input, not a value. Never SUM it; averaging across lines without weighting by number_of_units gives a meaningless 'average rate'. Null for Fixed-rate lines, which carry fixed_amount instead.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units paid on this line. Units are whatever the earnings rate defines (hours, days) — summing units across lines with different rate definitions mixes hours with days.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: The set amount for lines whose earnings rate is Fixed type (e.g. a flat bonus); null otherwise. Do not add it to amount — amount already equals it for fixed lines.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: The settled value of this line — the only column to SUM. Sum across this table plus the leave and timesheet earnings tables to rebuild the payslip's gross_earnings; this family alone is not gross.

columns.name: is_linked_to_timesheet
columns.description: Spec-declared false in this family: timesheet-sourced pay is materialized separately in xero_payroll_uk_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines. A true here is vendor drift — trust the family (table) membership over the flag.

columns.name: is_average_daily_pay_rate
columns.description: True when the line was priced from an average daily pay rate rather than a directly configured rate. It is the warning label on rate_per_unit: on these rows the rate is a computed average over prior pay, so reading it as the employee's contracted rate — or benchmarking rates across employees without excluding them — compares a derived figure with a real one.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for the Posted filter and payment_date — lines have no dates or status of their own.

examples.question: Which earnings rates drive gross pay this tax year?
examples.sql:
SELECT el.display_name, SUM(el.amount) AS paid
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_earnings_lines el
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = el.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
  AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY paid DESC

examples.question: Gross pay split across the three earnings families last quarter
examples.sql:
SELECT family, SUM(amount) AS paid FROM (
  SELECT el.pay_slip_id, 'regular' AS family, el.amount FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_earnings_lines el
  UNION ALL SELECT ll.pay_slip_id, 'leave', ll.amount FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_earnings_lines ll
  UNION ALL SELECT tl.pay_slip_id, 'timesheet', tl.amount FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines tl
) x
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = x.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
  AND pr.payment_date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '3 months'
  AND pr.payment_date < date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1

tables.grain: one employee tax line per payslip per position in its employeeTaxLines array
tables.description: Statutory tax withheld FROM the employee: PAYE income tax and employee (primary Class 1) National Insurance, one row per tax component. These amounts are inside gross_earnings and reduce it to net — they are not employer cost. The description text ('PAYE', 'Employee NIC'...) is the practical PAYE-vs-NI splitter; global_tax_type_id is the stable code. This table and xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employer_tax_lines materialize two different Payslip arrays of the same TaxLine object — never union them without labeling the payer.
gotchas: Employee tax is withheld from gross, not a cost on top of it. Adding these amounts to employer cost double-counts them — they are already inside gross_earnings.
Negative amounts are legitimate tax refunds. Excluding or ABS()-ing them corrupts withheld-tax totals.
Employee and employer tax tables carry the same TaxLine shape from different arrays. Union them only with an explicit payer label, or PAYE and employer NI blur into one meaningless 'tax' number.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. Tax lines have no date, so the HMRC tax period a withholding belongs to comes from the parent run's payment_date two joins away — bucketing employee tax by anything else misfiles it across month and tax-year boundaries.

columns.name: employee_tax_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's employeeTaxLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (taxLineID is not spec-required).

columns.name: tax_line_id
columns.description: Xero's own id for this tax line, present when supplied. Deliberately not the key — the spec marks it optional, so it cannot be relied on to identify every row — but it is what distinguishes a genuinely amended tax component from a reordered one when a run is re-scanned and line_index shifts underneath it.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Human label of the tax component ('PAYE', 'Employee NIC'). The practical way to split income tax from National Insurance — but it is display text; use global_tax_type_id when exact typing matters.

columns.name: is_employer_tax
columns.description: True when the employer pays this tax. Expected false throughout this table — collection membership (employeeTaxLines) is the authoritative payer signal; a true here is drift to investigate, not a row to silently reclassify.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Tax withheld on this component. Sums reconcile to the payslip's total_employee_taxes. Can be NEGATIVE for refunds (PAYE rebates after a tax code change) — do not filter negatives out or withheld totals overstate.

columns.name: global_tax_type_id
columns.description: Xero's tax type code for this component — the stable classifier behind the display description; group by it for typing that survives label edits.

columns.name: manual_adjustment
columns.description: True when a payroll admin overrode the calculated tax. Flag these when auditing effective tax rates — they are corrections, and outliers usually trace here.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date (which fixes the HMRC tax period).

examples.question: PAYE vs employee NI withheld by month this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month, tl.description, SUM(tl.amount) AS withheld
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employee_tax_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = tl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Payslips with manual tax adjustments to review
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.pay_slip_id, ps.employee_id, tl.description, tl.amount
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employee_tax_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = tl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND tl.manual_adjustment
ORDER BY ABS(tl.amount) DESC

tables.grain: one employer tax line per payslip per position in its employerTaxLines array
tables.description: Tax the EMPLOYER owes on top of gross pay: employer (secondary Class 1) National Insurance and Apprenticeship Levy, one row per component. This is the on-cost wedge — add it to gross_earnings for true employment cost; it never touches the employee's pay. Same TaxLine shape as the employee table but a different Payslip array; the split by array is what keeps 'tax burden on staff' and 'tax cost to the business' from contaminating each other. Note that run-level reliefs like Employment Allowance are settled with HMRC and may not be visible per payslip.
gotchas: Employer tax is ON TOP of gross — it belongs in employment cost and never in the employee's gross-to-net bridge. Mixing it with employee tax lines fabricates a payer-less 'total tax'.
Run-level reliefs (Employment Allowance) reduce what is actually remitted to HMRC but may not appear per payslip — per-slip employer NI sums can exceed the true remittance.
Filter to Posted runs via the payslip join; draft employer tax recalculates on every payslip edit.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time — the only route to employee, run status and payment date, none of which an employer tax line carries. It is also what attributes an on-cost to a head: employer NI per employee only exists by grouping these lines through the slip.

columns.name: employer_tax_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's employerTaxLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (taxLineID is not spec-required).

columns.name: tax_line_id
columns.description: Xero's own id for this tax line, present when supplied. Deliberately not the key — the spec marks it optional, so it cannot be relied on to identify every row — but it is what distinguishes a genuinely amended tax component from a reordered one when a run is re-scanned and line_index shifts underneath it.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Component label ('Employer NIC', 'Apprenticeship Levy'). Display text — the readable splitter of employer NI from levy; use global_tax_type_id for stable typing.

columns.name: is_employer_tax
columns.description: Expected true throughout this table; the employerTaxLines array membership is authoritative. A false here is drift to investigate, not grounds to move the row.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Employer tax owed on this component — pure on-cost, additional to gross. Sums reconcile to the payslip's total_employer_taxes. Negative amounts are corrections; keep them in totals.

columns.name: global_tax_type_id
columns.description: Xero's tax type code for this component — group by it rather than the editable description when typing matters.

columns.name: manual_adjustment
columns.description: True when the calculated employer tax was overridden by an admin — the first place to look when employer NI ratios spike or dip for one slip.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Employer NI and levy cost by month this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month, tl.description, SUM(tl.amount) AS employer_tax
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employer_tax_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = tl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Employer tax as a percentage of gross, by employee
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id,
       SUM(ps.total_employer_taxes) / NULLIF(SUM(ps.gross_earnings), 0) * 100 AS employer_tax_pct
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY employer_tax_pct DESC

tables.grain: one leave accrual line per payslip per position in its leaveAccrualLines array
tables.description: Leave entitlement EARNED in this pay run, in units (hours or days per the leave type) — no money on this table at all. It is a flow, not a balance: summing number_of_units gives cumulative accrual over a window, but remaining entitlement also needs leave taken, which this table does not carry. Paid leave consumption is recorded in the leave earnings lines table (amount plus its own numberOfUnits), but those units are defined by the pricing earnings rate, not by this table's leave type — the two unit systems need not match, so netting accruals against leave-earnings units without confirming both definitions is unsafe. Presenting a sum of accruals as 'leave balance' is the wrong-answer mode to avoid.
gotchas: This is accrual (entitlement earned), not balance. A 'current leave balance' cannot be computed from this table alone — leave taken lives in leave earnings lines, keyed by earnings rate rather than leave type and with rate-defined units, so accruals and consumption cannot be netted without reconciling both the classifier and the unit.
Units are per leave type (hours vs days). Summing number_of_units across leave_type_id values mixes incompatible units.
Draft-run accruals are provisional; filter to Posted through the payslip join.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. An accrual row has no date of its own: what puts entitlement in a period is the parent run's payment_date, two joins away, so accrual-over-time series are only as correct as this join.

columns.name: leave_accrual_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's leaveAccrualLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: The leave type the entitlement accrued under. This domain's ground truth contains no LeaveType object, so the id is the only classifier available here and it is load-bearing twice over: it separates annual leave from sick or parental schemes, and it is the boundary within which number_of_units is comparable, since different leave types are measured in different units.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Entitlement units earned this run. Additive across runs per leave type, but it is accrual only — not net of leave taken, and not comparable across leave types with different units.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Leave units accrued per employee per leave type this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id, la.leave_type_id, SUM(la.number_of_units) AS units_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_accrual_lines la
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = la.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

examples.question: Monthly accrual trend, one series per leave type
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month, la.leave_type_id,
       SUM(la.number_of_units) AS units_accrued
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_accrual_lines la
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = la.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 2, 1

tables.grain: one leave earnings line per payslip per position in its leaveEarningsLines array
tables.description: Pay for leave actually taken in the period — holiday pay, statutory sick/parental pay priced through leave-linked earnings rates. These amounts are INSIDE gross_earnings (they are earnings, paid instead of worked time), so 'cost of leave' from this table must not be added on top of gross. Distinguish from xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_accrual_lines, which records entitlement units earned, not money paid.
gotchas: Leave pay is already inside gross_earnings. Adding this table's amounts on top of gross double-counts every holiday.

This is pay for leave TAKEN; entitlement earned lives in the leave accrual table. Both carry a numberOfUnits, but here units follow the pricing earnings rate while accrual units follow the leave type — netting one against the other without confirming both unit definitions fabricates a balance.
Draft-run lines are provisional — filter through the payslip to pay_run_status = 'Posted'.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. Leave earnings lines are dateless — the leave was paid in the parent run, so 'when did this leave cost us' is the run's payment_date reached through this id, never a leave-taken date (there isn't one here).

columns.name: leave_earnings_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's leaveEarningsLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (leave earnings lines carry no natural id).

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The leave-linked earnings rate that priced this leave — which is also all you get: unlike the regular earnings family, this one carries no displayName, so there is no readable label for what kind of leave was paid. Note this is a rate id, not a leave type id: it does not join to the accrual table's leave_type_id, so 'holiday pay versus sick pay' cannot be answered from this column alone without the org's rate configuration.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Price per unit of leave. Input, never summed; for statutory leave this is the statutory rate, not the employee's ordinary pay.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units of leave paid on this line, in whatever unit the rate defines (hours or days). The paid-leave-volume measure — but confirm the unit before summing across rates.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Set amount when the underlying earnings rate is Fixed type; null otherwise. Already reflected in amount — never add the two.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Money paid for this leave line. Part of gross_earnings — the 'cost of leave taken' measure, not an addition to payroll cost.

columns.name: is_linked_to_timesheet
columns.description: Spec-declared false for leave earnings lines; family membership is the authoritative signal. Treat a true as vendor drift, not a reclassification.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Cost of paid leave by month this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month, SUM(ll.amount) AS leave_pay
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_earnings_lines ll
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = ll.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Share of gross pay that was leave pay, by employee
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id,
       SUM(ps.gross_earnings) AS gross,
       COALESCE(SUM(lv.leave_amount), 0) AS leave_pay,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(lv.leave_amount), 0) / NULLIF(SUM(ps.gross_earnings), 0) * 100, 1) AS leave_pct
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT pay_slip_id, SUM(amount) AS leave_amount
           FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_leave_earnings_lines GROUP BY 1) lv
  ON lv.pay_slip_id = ps.pay_slip_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY leave_pct DESC

tables.grain: one payment line per payslip per position in its paymentLines array
tables.description: How the payslip's NET pay is disbursed: one row per destination bank account, carrying employee bank details (account number, sort code, account name — all PII). Employees can split pay across accounts, so SUM(amount) per payslip — not any single row — should equal the slip's total_pay for electronically paid slips. This is a disbursement instruction, not compensation: never use it for pay analysis, only for payment reconciliation and split-payment questions.
gotchas: One payslip can have several payment lines (split pay). Joining payslips to payment lines and summing payslip columns fans out and double-counts — aggregate payment lines to the payslip first.
Cheque and Manual slips settle outside the BACS flow; their payment lines may be absent or not reconcile. Bank-file checks must filter the parent slip's payment_method.
account_number, sort_code and account_name are sensitive PII — exclude them from any output that does not strictly need them.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the grain you must collapse to before comparing anything with the payslip: the lines under one payslip_id are the split of a single net payment, so they sum to that slip's total_pay rather than each matching it.

columns.name: payment_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's paymentLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (paymentLineID is not spec-required).

columns.name: payment_line_id
columns.description: Xero's own id for this payment line, present when supplied. Not the key (the spec marks it optional), but it is the stable handle on a specific bank destination: when an employee changes the split of their net pay, this id is how you tell an edited routing instruction from a newly added one.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Net pay routed to this bank account. Per payslip these sum to total_pay for Electronically paid slips — a residual is a reconciliation flag, not rounding to ignore. Never treat as earnings: it is cash routing.

columns.name: account_number
columns.description: Employee bank account number receiving the funds. Sensitive PII — surface only in payment-operations contexts, never in analytical output.

columns.name: sort_code
columns.description: UK sort code of the destination account. PII; keep leading zeros — it is a code, not a number.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Destination account holder name. PII; may differ from the employee's payroll name (joint accounts) — not an identity field.

joins.note: Compare SUM(amount) to the slip's total_pay; scope reconciliation to payment_method = 'Electronically'.

examples.question: Payslips whose payment lines do not reconcile to net pay
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.pay_slip_id, ps.total_pay, pl.paid
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
JOIN (SELECT pay_slip_id, SUM(amount) AS paid
      FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_payment_lines GROUP BY 1) pl
  ON pl.pay_slip_id = ps.pay_slip_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND ps.payment_method = 'Electronically'
  AND ABS(pl.paid - ps.total_pay) > 0.005

examples.question: How many employees split net pay across multiple accounts?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.employee_id) AS employees_splitting FROM (
  SELECT ps.employee_id, pl.pay_slip_id
  FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_payment_lines pl
  JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = pl.pay_slip_id
  JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
  WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
  GROUP BY ps.employee_id, pl.pay_slip_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) s

tables.grain: one reimbursement line per payslip per position in its reimbursementLines array
tables.description: Non-taxable repayments of out-of-pocket expenses settled through payroll. Reimbursements are ADDED to net pay but are not earnings: they sit outside gross_earnings and outside tax. The two classic mistakes are counting them as compensation (inflates wage analysis) and forgetting them in the gross-to-net bridge (net looks too high). description is free text from the payroll admin — useful for eyeballing, unreliable for classification.
gotchas: Reimbursements are inside total_pay (net) but outside gross_earnings. Any bridge or ratio between gross and net that ignores them is off by the reimbursed amount.
This is expense repayment through payroll, not the org's whole expense picture — expenses paid via Xero accounting (expense claims, bills) never appear here.
Filter to Posted runs via the payslip join; draft reimbursements are routinely edited away.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time, and the reconciliation handle: the lines sharing one payslip_id sum to that slip's total_reimbursements. Also the only route to employee and payment date, which this family does not carry.

columns.name: reimbursement_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's reimbursementLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

columns.name: reimbursement_type_id
columns.description: The configured reimbursement type — mileage, subsistence, equipment and so on as the org set them up. This domain's ground truth contains no ReimbursementType object, so nothing here resolves the id to a name, but it is still the only stable classifier: group by it and label from description, never the reverse, because per-line descriptions are typed fresh each run.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text note entered per line ('Mileage March', 'Laptop charger'). Human context only; it is not normalized and the same expense category is spelled a dozen ways.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Money repaid to the employee on this line — added to net pay, excluded from gross and tax. Sums reconcile to the payslip's total_reimbursements. Not compensation: exclude it from wage benchmarking.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Reimbursements paid through payroll by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month, SUM(rl.amount) AS reimbursed
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_reimbursement_lines rl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = rl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Employees with the highest payroll-reimbursed expenses this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id, SUM(rl.amount) AS reimbursed
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_reimbursement_lines rl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = rl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY reimbursed DESC LIMIT 20

tables.grain: one timesheet earnings line per payslip per position in its timesheetEarningsLines array
tables.description: Earnings sourced from approved timesheets: hours captured on timesheets, priced at an earnings rate and settled on the payslip. Inside gross_earnings like its sibling families. This domain's ground truth contains no Timesheet object, so within these tables this family is the only record of paid worked time — number_of_units is the paid-hours measure and amount the paid value — but it is the payroll settlement of timesheets, not the timesheets themselves, and a timesheets domain elsewhere in the connector would be the authority on hours worked. What is here is time PAID, which can lag or aggregate the time actually worked when a timesheet spans periods.
gotchas: Rows exist only for orgs that use Xero timesheets. An empty table means 'no timesheet pay', not missing data — regular earnings carry everything for salaried orgs.
Hours here are hours PAID in the run, attributed to payment_date — not a work-date time log. Do not present them as when the work happened.
Timesheet pay is inside gross_earnings; adding it on top of gross double-counts hourly wages.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Parent payslip key, inherited at explode time. The hours on this row belong to whatever period the parent run paid, so this id is the only route to a date at all — and to the Posted filter that decides whether the hours were actually paid.

columns.name: timesheet_earnings_lines
columns.description: Zero-based position in the payslip's timesheetEarningsLines array — the row's provenance and, with payslip_id, its key (no natural line id exists).

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: The earnings rate pricing these timesheet hours. Same rate ids as the other earnings families — usable to compare timesheet vs regular pay for the same rate.

columns.name: rate_per_unit
columns.description: Price per timesheet unit. Input, never summed; weight by number_of_units for a true average rate.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Timesheet units paid — the paid-hours measure for hourly workforces. Units are defined by the earnings rate; confirm before cross-rate sums.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Set amount for Fixed-type rates; null otherwise and already reflected in amount.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Value of the timesheet-driven pay on this line. Part of gross_earnings; the third leg of the gross reconciliation with regular and leave earnings.

columns.name: is_linked_to_timesheet
columns.description: Do not filter on this. The spec documents it here with the leave family's sentence ('False for leave earnings line'), which is plainly a copy-paste into the timesheet object, so neither true nor false can be trusted as a classification. Membership of the timesheetEarningsLines array — that is, being a row in this table — is what makes pay timesheet-sourced; the column is carried for fidelity only.

joins.note: Then to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs for status and payment_date.

examples.question: Paid timesheet hours and value by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.payment_date) AS month,
       SUM(tl.number_of_units) AS units_paid, SUM(tl.amount) AS value_paid
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = tl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Effective hourly rate by employee from timesheet pay
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id,
       SUM(tl.amount) / NULLIF(SUM(tl.number_of_units), 0) AS effective_rate
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslip_timesheet_earnings_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps ON ps.pay_slip_id = tl.pay_slip_id
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY effective_rate DESC

tables.grain: one payslip per employee per pay run
tables.description: The per-employee settlement of a pay run: header totals for gross, net, taxes, deductions, reimbursements, court orders and benefits, with the line-level detail exploded into eleven child tables. The critical trap is total_pay: it is NET take-home, not gross — employment cost per head is gross_earnings + total_employer_taxes. Payslips carry no status of their own; whether the money is real is decided by the parent run's pay_run_status, so almost every query joins xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs. Names are denormalized snapshots at pay time — identity questions must key on employee_id.
gotchas: total_pay is NET, not gross. Compensation and cost questions use gross_earnings (+ total_employer_taxes for all-in cost); SUM(total_pay) is only 'cash paid to employees'.
Payslips on Draft runs are provisional and mutate. Every aggregate needs the join to xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs with pay_run_status = 'Posted'.
total_earnings and gross_earnings are spec-identical for UK. Summing both double-counts gross.
An employee can have multiple payslips in one period (Unscheduled runs, corrections). 'Pay per employee per month' must sum slips, not pick one.

Joining a payslip to any of the eleven line-family tables fans the header out to one row per line, so SUM(gross_earnings) or SUM(total_pay) after that join multiplies the header by the line count. Pre-aggregate the child table to payslip_id, then join.

Payslips are added to and removed from Draft runs as they are edited, and a removed slip disappears from the API with no deleted flag. last_edited only moves on slips that still exist — reconciling a run's roster requires re-reading that run, not trusting the watermark.

Payslips arrive per pay run (the PayRunID parameter), so a full historical backfill costs at least one request per run against Xero's per-org call budget. Backfills should walk runs oldest-first and be resumable rather than re-scanning every run each cycle.

The gross-to-net bridge is gross_earnings - total_employee_taxes - total_deductions - total_court_orders + total_reimbursements = total_pay; benefits sit outside it. Rounding of a penny or two per slip is normal — do not treat tiny residuals as data corruption.

columns.name: pay_slip_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable payslip identifier and the row key; every line-family child table hangs off it. Named payslip_id (matching the PayslipID path parameter) rather than pay_slip_id — joiners take note.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee this slip pays — the only reliable identity key. Join to xero_payroll_uk_employees for demographics; never group by the embedded first/last name, which is a point-in-time snapshot and collides across namesakes.

columns.name: pay_run_id
columns.description: The containing run. Join it on every aggregate: it is the only route to pay_run_status (Draft vs Posted), pay_run_type (to exclude EarlierYearUpdate) and payment_date (the tax-period business date).

columns.name: last_edited
columns.description: When this payslip last changed. GET /Payslips accepts only page and PayRunID — there is no modified-since filter and no If-Modified-Since contract — so this is a client-side change detector, not a server-side incremental filter: rows still have to be fetched before the watermark can be compared. Slips on Draft runs move constantly; a fresh value on a slip whose run is already Posted means a post-posting correction, and its eleven line families must be re-exploded.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Employee first name as printed on the slip — a display snapshot, not identity. It goes stale when the employee record is renamed; use employee_id for anything that counts people.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Employee last name snapshot at pay time. Same caveat as first_name: display only, key on employee_id.

columns.name: total_earnings
columns.description: Gross earnings before any deduction. For UK payroll the spec declares this IDENTICAL to gross_earnings (the pair exists for cross-region API symmetry). Use exactly one of the two — adding them doubles gross.

columns.name: gross_earnings
columns.description: Gross pay: the sum of the regular, leave and timesheet earnings families before tax and deductions. This is the base for employment cost (add total_employer_taxes) and the denominator for effective tax rate. Equals total_earnings for UK by definition.

columns.name: total_pay
columns.description: NET take-home pay — gross minus employee taxes, deductions and court orders, plus reimbursements. The name reads like gross; it is not. 'Payroll cost' questions answered with SUM(total_pay) understate spend by the entire tax and on-cost wedge.

columns.name: total_employer_taxes
columns.description: The employer's own tax on top of gross — employer (secondary Class 1) National Insurance and Apprenticeship Levy. It never reduces the employee's pay; it is pure employer cost. Per-head employment cost = gross_earnings + total_employer_taxes. Detail in xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employer_tax_lines.

columns.name: total_employee_taxes
columns.description: Tax withheld FROM the employee: PAYE income tax plus employee (primary Class 1) NI. Withheld, not employer cost — do not add it to total_cost-style figures, it is already inside gross. Detail in xero_payroll_uk_payslip_employee_tax_lines.

columns.name: total_deductions
columns.description: Sum of the deductionLines family — employee pension contributions and other configured deductions subtracted from gross to reach net. Excludes statutory tax (that is total_employee_taxes) and court orders (their own total). Pre-tax vs post-tax character lives on the lines via subject_to_tax.

columns.name: total_reimbursements
columns.description: Non-taxable repayments of out-of-pocket expenses, ADDED to net pay. They are not earnings: including them in gross-pay or compensation analysis inflates wages with expense repayments.

columns.name: total_court_orders
columns.description: Statutory attachment-of-earnings amounts (AEOs, child maintenance DEOs) the employer must divert from the employee's pay. Deducted after tax; part of the gross-to-net bridge but not an employer cost and not a voluntary deduction.

columns.name: total_benefits
columns.description: Value of the benefitLines family — employer-side, non-earnings compensation, per the spec's own definition (fringe benefits and perks provided in addition to normal earnings). It is outside the gross-to-net bridge: it is not in gross_earnings and not in total_pay, so it is never cash the employee received. Whether a given line is real employer spend (an employer contribution) or only a taxable value being payrolled depends entirely on how the org configured its benefit types — resolve that from xero_payroll_uk_payslip_benefit_lines before this total enters any cost figure.

columns.name: bacs_hash
columns.description: Documented by the spec as the BACS Service User Number despite the field being named 'hash' — treat it as an opaque employer-level banking identifier either way, useful only for tying slips back to a submitted BACS file. It identifies the employer's service user, not the employee, so it is not a per-person attribute and never a grouping key for people.

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: How the net pay leaves the business. Only Electronically slips are expected to reconcile against paymentLines bank splits; Cheque and Manual slips settle outside the BACS file, so 'net pay vs bank file' checks must scope to Electronically.

joins.note: Mandatory on aggregates: payslips have no status of their own — Draft/Posted, run type and payment_date all live on the run.

Cross-domain join into the payroll_uk employees domain, which owns that table — not defined by this domain's ground truth. The names embedded on the slip are pay-time snapshots; the employee row is current truth.

examples.question: Take-home pay by employee for July 2026
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id, SUM(ps.total_pay) AS net_pay
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
  AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-07-01' AND pr.payment_date < DATE '2026-08-01'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY net_pay DESC

examples.question: All-in employment cost per employee this tax year
examples.sql:
SELECT ps.employee_id,
       SUM(ps.gross_earnings) AS gross,
       SUM(ps.total_employer_taxes) AS employer_taxes,
       SUM(ps.gross_earnings + ps.total_employer_taxes) AS employment_cost
FROM xero_payroll_uk_payslips ps
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_pay_runs pr ON pr.pay_run_id = ps.pay_run_id
WHERE pr.pay_run_status = 'Posted' AND pr.pay_run_type <> 'EarlierYearUpdate'
  AND pr.payment_date >= DATE '2026-04-06'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY employment_cost DESC

tables.grain: one reimbursement pay item per reimbursementID
tables.description: Org-level reimbursement definitions — non-taxable repayments of employee expenses routed through payroll (mileage, tools, expenses). Rows are the catalogue; amounts actually reimbursed are payslip reimbursement lines in the pay-run domain. Reimbursements are not earnings: they sit outside gross pay, tax and NIC, so including them in wage-cost or gross-pay metrics inflates both.
gotchas: Reimbursements are outside gross pay — any 'total pay' metric that includes payslip reimbursement lines overstates wages and every tax base.

columns.name: reimbursement_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the reimbursement pay item; payslip reimbursement lines reference it.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The label the org gave this reimbursement item, as it appears on payslips ('Mileage', 'Expenses'...). Org-defined free text with no standard vocabulary, so it disambiguates items within a tenant but never classifies across tenants — there is no category field on Reimbursement, so if a question needs 'mileage vs everything else' the only honest handles are this name and the GL account it posts to.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: GL account the reimbursement posts to; join xero_accounts — usually an expense account, which is how these amounts reach the P&L without touching wages.

columns.name: current_record
columns.description: FALSE = retired item; filter TRUE for the active menu, keep FALSE rows to decode history.

joins.note: Where reimbursed amounts post in the GL.

examples.question: Active reimbursement items and their GL accounts
examples.sql:
SELECT r.name, a.name AS gl_account
FROM xero_payroll_uk_reimbursements r
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.account_id = r.account_id
WHERE r.current_record

tables.grain: one payroll GL account mapping per payroll account role (type) for the organisation
tables.description: The payroll settings' GL account map: which general-ledger accounts UK payroll posts wages expense, wages payable, PAYE and NIC liabilities and the payment bank account to. The row's type is the payroll ROLE and the true row key — the settings payload carries one entry per role, and nothing stops an org pointing two roles (say PAYELIABILITY and NICLIABILITY) at the same GL account, so accountID can repeat. The accountID is the same id as xero_accounts, so this table is the bridge between payroll amounts and where they appear in the P&L and balance sheet.
gotchas: type here is the payroll role, not the accounting account class — 'wages expense account' means type = 'WAGESEXPENSE' in THIS table, then join xero_accounts for the ledger view.
This mapping is why payroll cost questions can be answered from journals: filter journal lines to the WAGESEXPENSE/EMPLOYERSNIC account ids found here.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: The GL account's identifier — the same AccountID as xero_accounts, which is the whole point: it links payroll roles to ledger accounts. (The spec's docstring calls it 'the identifier for Settings'; it is the account id.) Deliberately NOT the row key: nothing stops an org pointing two payroll roles at one GL account, so this value repeats and COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) undercounts the mapping.

columns.name: type
columns.description: The payroll ROLE this account plays and the true row key — the settings payload carries at most one entry per role. WAGESEXPENSE is where gross pay hits the P&L, WAGESPAYABLE/PAYELIABILITY/NICLIABILITY are balance-sheet liabilities, BANK is the paying account, EMPLOYERSNIC the employer NIC expense, PAYEECONTRIBUTION employee contributions. Not the accounting AccountType — do not confuse with xero_accounts.type.
columns.enums: BANK; EMPLOYERSNIC; NICLIABILITY; PAYEECONTRIBUTION; PAYELIABILITY; WAGESPAYABLE; WAGESEXPENSE

columns.name: code
columns.description: The GL account's short code (text — codes can have leading zeros); matches xero_accounts.code.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The GL account's display name, denormalized from the chart of accounts.

joins.note: The full chart-of-accounts record; use it to follow payroll journals into P&L/balance-sheet classes. Many-to-one, not one-to-one: several payroll roles may map onto the same GL account, so joining from xero_accounts back to here can multiply account rows.

examples.question: Which GL accounts does payroll post to?
examples.sql:
SELECT sa.type AS payroll_role, sa.code, sa.name
FROM xero_payroll_uk_settings_accounts sa
ORDER BY sa.type

tables.grain: one statutory leave episode per statutoryLeaveID
tables.description: Every statutory leave episode (maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental, bereavement, neonatal care, sickness) recorded for each employee, with its date span, entitlement verdict and lifecycle status. This is the discovery index for statutory absence: sick episodes fan further out to xero_payroll_uk_statutory_sick_leaves for SSP detail. Note the endpoint requires payroll.settings scope — not payroll.employees — so this family can be absent while ordinary employee data synced fine.
gotchas: Statutory episodes do NOT appear in xero_payroll_uk_employee_leave — total-absence questions must union both families or they miss maternity and long-term sickness entirely. The union needs de-duplication on employee plus overlapping date range, because leave booked against a statutory-flagged leave type can appear on both sides and a naive UNION ALL double-counts it.
The op's activeOnly parameter hides Completed episodes when true; the ingester must pass activeOnly=false or history silently disappears.
The leave TYPE itself is health/family information about a person (pregnancy, bereavement) — treat type + employee combinations as sensitive when surfacing individuals.
The In-Progress status value contains a hyphen ('In-Progress'); an equality filter on 'InProgress' matches nothing.

columns.name: statutory_leave_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the statutory leave episode; also the fan-out key into the SSP detail table for Sick episodes.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee on statutory leave — carried on the record itself here, unlike most fan-out payloads.

columns.name: type
columns.description: The statutory leave category. BereavementNire is the Northern Ireland bereavement variant — group it with Bereavement for UK-wide reporting unless the question is jurisdiction-specific.
columns.enums: Sick; Adoption; Maternity; Paternity; Sharedparental; Bereavement; NeonatalCare; BereavementNire

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day of the statutory leave episode, and the only date on this row that never moves — it is what 'maternity leave started in Q2' must be measured on. Do not use it as the first PAID day: entitlement and payment windows start on their own rules per type (SSP waiting days, the maternity pay period), which is why cost questions resolve on payslip statutory earnings lines rather than on this span.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day of the episode; for In-Progress episodes this is the planned end, which can move.

columns.name: is_entitled
columns.description: Whether the episode qualified for statutory PAYMENT. FALSE episodes are still absence — excluding them from absence analysis is wrong, but including them in statutory-pay cost is equally wrong.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Episode lifecycle. Pending has not started paying, In-Progress is live, Completed is history. 'Currently on maternity leave' = type filter + status = 'In-Progress'.

joins.note: Per-employee fan-out.
SSP entitlement detail; exists only for type = 'Sick' episodes when the optional detail scan ran.

examples.question: Who is currently on statutory family leave?
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, s.type, s.start_date, s.end_date
FROM xero_payroll_uk_statutory_leave_summaries s
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = s.employee_id
WHERE s.status = 'In-Progress' AND s.type <> 'Sick'
ORDER BY s.start_date

examples.question: Statutory leave episodes started per quarter, by type
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', start_date) AS quarter, type, COUNT(*) AS episodes
FROM xero_payroll_uk_statutory_leave_summaries
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

tables.grain: one statutory sick pay (SSP) episode per statutoryLeaveID
tables.description: Full SSP detail for sick episodes discovered in the summaries table: entitlement weeks requested/qualified/remaining, work pattern, pregnancy linkage, notice compliance and failure reasons. The weeks fields are entitlement arithmetic, not time worked — they answer 'how much SSP runway is left', never 'how many hours were missed'. Fetched per StatutorySickLeaveID, so it exists only where the optional detail scan ran.
gotchas: Weeks fields are entitlement arithmetic in WEEKS while every other leave quantity in the domain is hours — never add them to number_of_units figures.
Availability is optional (per-episode fan-out): missing rows mean the detail scan did not run for that episode, not that SSP data does not exist.
Linked sick episodes within 8 weeks share one SSP entitlement — summing entitlement_weeks_remaining across an employee's episodes overstates runway.

columns.name: statutory_leave_id
columns.description: The SSP episode identifier; equals the summaries row's key, making the join one-to-one.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee on sick leave; join xero_payroll_uk_employees for the name and current-employment status. Episodes survive termination, so a per-employee SSP history includes leavers — filter through the employee row's end_date when the question means current staff. Also the grouping key for the shared-entitlement rule: linked episodes of the SAME employee share one 28-week SSP entitlement.

columns.name: leave_type_id
columns.description: Points at the 'Statutory Sick Leave (non-pensionable)' pay item used to pay the episode — a pay-item linkage, not an org leave-type classification.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day of the sickness absence — not the first PAID day. SSP has historically been payable only from the fourth qualifying day (three unpaid waiting days), and the waiting-day and lower-earnings rules have been subject to legislative change, so the paid window inside start_date..end_date is narrower than the calendar span by an amount that depends on the rules in force for that period and on work_pattern. Never derive SSP cost by multiplying this span by a daily rate; the payslip SSP earnings lines in the pay-run domain are what was actually paid.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day of the sickness absence (planned end while the episode is open).

columns.name: type
columns.description: Statutory leave category of this record — always the sick variant here; kept for symmetry with the summaries table.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Episode lifecycle status (the spec's own description is a copy-paste of type; treat values like the summaries statuses).

columns.name: work_pattern
columns.description: Ordered list of weekdays the employee was scheduled to work when the leave was taken — qualifying-day logic depends on the order and content, so the array is kept verbatim. A plain string array, no nested objects.

columns.name: is_pregnancy_related
columns.description: Pregnancy-related sickness has special SSP rules (no disqualification near the due date, can trigger SMP instead). This is health data about a person — sensitive; aggregate, do not list individuals unless asked.

columns.name: sufficient_notice
columns.description: Whether the employee gave the notice/evidence the employer requires; FALSE can lawfully withhold SSP for late-notified days.

columns.name: is_entitled
columns.description: Whether the episode qualifies for SSP payment; FALSE rows still represent real absence with zero SSP cost.

columns.name: entitlement_weeks_requested
columns.description: Weeks of SSP the episode requested — demand, not what was granted.

columns.name: entitlement_weeks_qualified
columns.description: Weeks of the 28-week SSP maximum still available when the leave was requested — a point-in-time entitlement figure, not a balance that updates.

columns.name: entitlement_weeks_remaining
columns.description: Calculated weeks left in the SSP period. The one field here that behaves like a balance — do not sum it across episodes of the same employee, linked episodes share one entitlement.

columns.name: overlaps_with_other_leave
columns.description: TRUE when paternity/shared-parental leave overlaps the sick period — allowed, but payment amounts interact; flag such episodes in cost analyses.

columns.name: entitlement_failure_reasons
columns.description: Why a not-entitled episode failed (string array, verbatim). Populated only when is_entitled is false — the explanatory companion, not an extra filter dimension.

joins.note: Detail record for a Sick summary row; discovered from the summaries scan.
The employee on sick leave.

examples.question: Open SSP episodes with less than 4 weeks of entitlement remaining
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, s.start_date, s.entitlement_weeks_remaining
FROM xero_payroll_uk_statutory_sick_leaves s
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = s.employee_id
WHERE s.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE AND s.entitlement_weeks_remaining < 4
ORDER BY s.entitlement_weeks_remaining

examples.question: How many sick episodes failed SSP entitlement, and were any pregnancy-related?
examples.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_entitled) AS not_entitled,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_entitled AND is_pregnancy_related) AS pregnancy_related
FROM xero_payroll_uk_statutory_sick_leaves

tables.grain: one timesheet line per timesheetLineID: one employee's units for one date and one earnings rate
tables.description: The daily detail behind each timesheet: units (per the earnings rate's unit type, normally hours) worked on a specific date under a specific earnings rate, optionally tagged to a tracking option. This is the workforce time-entry fact of the UK payroll domain — hours by day, by overtime vs regular, by department all resolve here. The payability filter lives on the PARENT: always join the timesheet header and filter its status.
gotchas: Lines carry no status — an unfiltered SUM includes Draft hours. Join the parent and filter its status for every hours metric.
tracking_item_id points at an accounting tracking OPTION (xero_tracking_options), not a payroll or category id — joining it to xero_tracking_categories silently matches nothing.
Units are whatever the earnings rate's typeOfUnits says; summing across rates with different unit types adds hours to days.

columns.name: timesheet_line_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the line and the row key.

columns.name: timesheet_id
columns.description: Parent timesheet; inherited from the record the lines were exploded from. The approval status filter lives on the parent.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The working day the units belong to — the correct time axis for daily/weekly hours analysis (the parent's start_date is the whole period).

columns.name: earnings_rate_id
columns.description: Which earnings rate the units are worked under; join xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates to split regular vs overtime and to read the unit type.

columns.name: tracking_item_id
columns.description: The accounting tracking OPTION (e.g. a specific department) tagged on the line — an option under the timesheet tracking category configured in xero_payroll_uk_tracking_categories. Join xero_tracking_options, not xero_tracking_categories.

columns.name: number_of_units
columns.description: Units worked on the line — additive, in the earnings rate's typeOfUnits (normally hours). The number payroll pays hourly staff from once the parent completes.

joins.note: Employee, period and approval status come from the header.
Regular vs overtime classification and unit semantics.
Resolves the department/region label; the option belongs to the org's timesheet tracking category.

examples.question: Completed hours by earnings rate in the last 4 weeks
examples.sql:
SELECT er.name, SUM(tl.number_of_units) AS units
FROM xero_payroll_uk_timesheet_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_timesheets t ON t.timesheet_id = tl.timesheet_id AND t.status = 'Completed'
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_earnings_rates er ON er.earnings_rate_id = tl.earnings_rate_id
WHERE tl.date >= CURRENT_DATE - 28
GROUP BY er.name ORDER BY units DESC

examples.question: Hours by department (tracking option) this month
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(o.name, 'Untagged') AS department, SUM(tl.number_of_units) AS hours
FROM xero_payroll_uk_timesheet_lines tl
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_timesheets t ON t.timesheet_id = tl.timesheet_id AND t.status IN ('Approved','Completed')
LEFT JOIN xero_tracking_options o ON o.tracking_option_id = tl.tracking_item_id
WHERE tl.date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY hours DESC

tables.grain: one timesheet per timesheetID: one employee's submitted hours for one payroll-calendar period
tables.description: Timesheet headers, each covering one employee for one payroll-calendar period and carrying the total hours plus the approval lifecycle. Hours become payable only as the timesheet moves Draft → Approved → Completed (processed in a pay run); Draft hours are unvetted data entry. The key is timesheetID alone — (employee_id, start_date) is NOT a key, because an employee can hold more than one timesheet for the same period. total_hours duplicates the sum of the line units — use header OR lines in one query, never both.
gotchas: Draft timesheets are data entry, not worked hours — most 'hours worked' questions filter status IN ('Approved','Completed'), and payroll-cost questions filter Completed.
total_hours already equals the sum of the lines; joining lines and summing both double-counts.
Only timesheet-paid (typically hourly) employees file timesheets — salaried staff are absent, so timesheet hours are NOT total org hours.

An employee can have more than one timesheet covering the same period (a rejected sheet re-entered, or hours split across submissions), so (employee_id, start_date) does not identify a row. Deduplicating on employee-and-period drops real hours; joining lines through employee-and-period fans them out.

columns.name: timesheet_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the timesheet and the row key.

columns.name: payroll_calendar_id
columns.description: The pay calendar whose period this timesheet covers; join xero_payroll_uk_pay_run_calendars to translate periods to pay frequency.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: The employee who worked (or at least entered) these hours; join xero_payroll_uk_employees to filter to current staff, because leavers' timesheets persist forever. Only timesheet-paid (typically hourly) employees ever appear here — COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id) is the timesheet population, not headcount.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day of the timesheet's payroll period — payroll-calendar aligned, not month aligned.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day of the timesheet's payroll period (inclusive). Use it to place a timesheet in a period, not to place the WORK: individual lines carry their own date, so hours can fall anywhere in the span and a period straddling a month end will attribute the whole sheet to one month if you bucket on the header instead of on timesheet_lines.date.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Draft is unapproved entry, Approved is signed off and awaiting payroll, Completed is processed in a pay run. Paid-hours analyses filter Completed (or Approved+Completed for committed hours); including Draft counts unvetted numbers.

columns.name: total_hours
columns.description: Header total of the line units. Equal to SUM(timesheet_lines.number_of_units) — adding both in a joined query doubles hours.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change; the incremental-sync watermark.

columns.name: timesheet_lines
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_payroll_uk_timesheet_lines (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Whose hours.
The period definition the timesheet fills.
Daily per-earnings-rate detail.

examples.question: Approved or completed hours by month this year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', start_date) AS month, SUM(total_hours) AS hours
FROM xero_payroll_uk_timesheets
WHERE status IN ('Approved','Completed')
  AND start_date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Draft timesheets awaiting approval, oldest first
examples.sql:
SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, t.start_date, t.end_date, t.total_hours
FROM xero_payroll_uk_timesheets t
JOIN xero_payroll_uk_employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id
WHERE t.status = 'Draft'
ORDER BY t.start_date

tables.grain: one payroll tracking configuration record per organisation
tables.description: A single-row pointer table: which two ACCOUNTING tracking categories UK payroll uses — one for employee groups (org-structure reporting on pay runs) and one for timesheet lines (department/cost-centre tagging of hours). It contains ids only; the categories' names and options live in xero_tracking_categories / xero_tracking_options. This is NOT a payroll copy of the accounting tracking tables — it is the glue that says which of them payroll uses.
gotchas: These are ACCOUNTING tracking category ids — the payroll API reuses the accounting dimension; do not look for payroll-specific category tables.
Exactly one row per org, possibly with both ids null; a query that joins through a null id and returns nothing should report 'tracking not configured', not 'no hours'.

columns.name: record_key
columns.api: synthetic:constant 'payroll_uk' — the endpoint returns exactly one configuration record per organisation, which has no natural key
columns.description: Singleton key so the one-row-per-org grain has a declared primary key.

columns.name: employee_groups_tracking_category_id
columns.description: The accounting tracking category used to group EMPLOYEES (e.g. by team). Null means the org has not enabled employee-group tracking — group-level payroll splits are then impossible, not merely empty.
