columns.name: timesheet_tracking_category_id
columns.description: The accounting tracking category whose options timesheet lines are tagged with (tracking_item_id on lines is one of ITS options). Resolve line tags through this category's options in xero_tracking_options.

joins.note: Name and options of the employee-groups category.
Name and options of the timesheet category.

examples.question: What are the payroll tracking dimensions called?
examples.sql:
SELECT eg.name AS employee_groups_category, ts.name AS timesheet_category
FROM xero_payroll_uk_tracking_categories ptc
LEFT JOIN xero_tracking_categories eg ON eg.tracking_category_id = ptc.employee_groups_tracking_category_id
LEFT JOIN xero_tracking_categories ts ON ts.tracking_category_id = ptc.timesheet_tracking_category_id

tables.grain: one application of prepayment credit to one invoice, keyed by parent prepayment and array position
tables.description: The settlement edge between a prepayment and the invoices it pays down: each row moves a slice of held credit onto exactly one invoice on a given date. Allocations are how invoices get PAID WITHOUT CASH MOVING — treating allocation amounts as receipts double-counts the cash that already arrived when the prepayment was created. Rows are exploded from the parent document's Allocations array and re-land whenever the parent changes; they have no independent watermark.
gotchas: Allocation amount is settlement, not cash: the money moved when the prepayment was created (a bank transaction). Adding allocations to payment-based collections double-counts.
Rows re-land wholesale with the parent and have no watermark of their own; deleted allocations just disappear from the array. Compare sets between syncs rather than looking for tombstones.

Direction and currency live on the PARENT: filter xero_prepayments.type for customer vs supplier credit, exclude VOIDED parents, and convert with the parent's currency_rate before summing across documents.

columns.name: prepayment_prepayment_id
columns.description: Parent prepayment whose credit this row consumes. Populated by the ingester from the parent scan context; provenance is the Allocation shape's source-document echo slot, which the API rarely materializes inline.

columns.name: allocation_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position in the parent Prepayment.Allocations array
columns.description: Array position within the parent payload, minted because older payloads omit AllocationID. Stable only within one parent version — when the parent re-syncs, the whole allocation set for that prepayment_id is replaced, so never diff ordinals across syncs.

columns.name: allocation_id
columns.description: Xero's allocation identifier when the API returns it (it exists to address allocation deletes upstream). Not the row key because legacy payloads omit it — prefer it for entity resolution when present, fall back to the composite key.

columns.name: invoice_invoice_id
columns.description: The invoice this slice of credit paid down — AR credit lands on ACCREC invoices, AP credit on ACCPAY bills; direction comes from the parent prepayment's type, not from this row. Join xero_invoices to see what the credit settled.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Credit applied to the invoice, in the DOCUMENT currency, up to 4dp. This is settlement, not revenue and not new cash: the cash event was the prepayment's source bank transaction. It reduces the invoice's AmountDue and the parent's remaining_credit by the same figure.

columns.name: date
columns.description: When the credit was applied — the settlement date for invoices paid by credit, and the axis for time-series application analysis. Distinct from (and often much later than) the parent prepayment's own date.

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.description: The spec's delete-acknowledgement flag, seen on delete responses. On ordinary reads a removed allocation simply VANISHES from the parent's array — detect unwound applications by rows disappearing on re-sync, not by this flag turning true.

columns.name: credit_note_credit_note_id
columns.description: Always null in the prepayment context: the spec reuses one Allocation shape across credit notes, prepayments and overpayments, and this echo slot only fills on credit-note allocations (invoicing's xero_credit_note_allocations). Mapped so the shared shape is fully accounted — never filter on it here.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-response artefact indicating payload status. Ignore for analytics.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation messages retained verbatim; empty on healthy reads.

joins.note: Parent credit document; carries direction (type), currency and status.
The invoice settled by this application.

examples.question: Which invoices were settled with prepayment credit last quarter?
examples.sql:
SELECT i.invoice_number, a.amount, a.date
FROM xero_prepayment_allocations a
JOIN xero_prepayments pp ON pp.prepayment_prepayment_id = a.prepayment_prepayment_id AND pp.status <> 'VOIDED'
JOIN xero_invoices i ON i.invoice_invoice_id = a.invoice_invoice_id
WHERE a.date >= date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - interval '3 months'
  AND a.date < date_trunc('quarter', CURRENT_DATE)
ORDER BY a.amount DESC

examples.question: How long does customer prepayment credit sit before it is used?
examples.sql:
SELECT AVG(a.date - pp.date) AS avg_days_to_application
FROM xero_prepayment_allocations a
JOIN xero_prepayments pp ON pp.prepayment_prepayment_id = a.prepayment_prepayment_id
WHERE pp.type IN ('RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT', 'ARPREPAYMENT') AND pp.status <> 'VOIDED'

tables.grain: one prepayment credit document per PrepaymentID
tables.description: Money received (or paid) BEFORE any invoice exists: a prepayment is created from a bank transaction and sits as credit against the contact until allocated to invoices or refunded. It is never revenue or expense by itself — recognition happens on the invoice lines it eventually offsets, so counting prepayment totals as sales double-counts the later invoice. Direction is carried by type (RECEIVE-*/AR* = customer credit you hold, SPEND-*/AP* = credit you hold with a supplier), mirroring the ACCREC/ACCPAY split that runs through the whole connector. remaining_credit and applied_amount are current-state balances restated on every sync, not history.
gotchas: A prepayment is not revenue and not expense — it is credit held until invoices exist. Adding prepayment totals to invoice-based sales double-counts the sale when the invoice lands.
VOIDED prepayments keep returning from the API. Exclude them from every total, and remember type mixes customer-side (RECEIVE-*/AR*) and supplier-side (SPEND-*/AP*) documents in one column.

remaining_credit and applied_amount are TODAY's balances, overwritten each sync: they support point-in-time questions only. Reconstruct history from xero_prepayment_allocations dates plus refund payments.
The cash receipt behind a prepayment is a bank transaction (banking domain), and refunds are payment rows. Counting the prepayment document as cash movement double-counts both ends.

columns.name: prepayment_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the prepayment and the row key; the value allocations and refund payments point back to.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Direction of the credit. RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT/ARPREPAYMENT: a customer paid you in advance (you owe them goods or a refund). SPEND-PREPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENT: you paid a supplier in advance. Every prepayment question must pick a side — summing both directions nets customer liabilities against supplier assets. The hyphenated values come from the source bank transaction; the AR*/AP* values are the same documents as typed on the payments surface.

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The counterparty whose credit this is, from the embedded Contact stub. Join xero_contacts; remember merged contacts point at a survivor via MergedToContactID there.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date the prepayment was created — when the cash actually arrived or left via its source bank transaction. Use it for cash timing; allocation dates on the child table are when the credit was consumed, which can be much later.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AUTHORISED still carries credit; PAID means fully applied or refunded; VOIDED is cancelled but STILL RETURNED by the API. Exclude VOIDED from every total or credit is overstated; note there is no DRAFT state — prepayments are born posted.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Declares whether amounts inside line_items include tax (Inclusive), exclude it (Exclusive) or have none (NoTax). It ONLY changes how the jsonb lines read — sub_total, total_tax and total on this row are already normalized (sub_total is always ex-tax).

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Verbatim ordered line array of the credit document — the account/tax/tracking coding, auto-generated from the source bank transaction. Kept as payload because document-level totals answer prepayment questions; interpret raw LineAmount values only together with line_amount_types. If line-level prepayment analysis becomes load-bearing, promote to an explode table in a schema revision rather than parsing ad hoc.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Tax-exclusive total of the document in currency_code — always ex-tax regardless of line_amount_types.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Total tax on the prepayment. Prepayments can carry tax at creation depending on org settings — do not assume zero.

columns.name: total
columns.description: sub_total + total_tax in currency_code: the full size of the credit when created. Compare with applied_amount and remaining_credit for its lifecycle; total never changes as credit is consumed.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Spec quirk, read-only: for prepayments this slot returns the document's invoice-number ('Reference field isn't available'). Do not treat it as user-entered reference text.

columns.name: invoice_number
columns.description: The prepayment's OWN document number, returned for receive prepayments only. It is NOT a pointer to any invoice it later offsets — that linkage lives in xero_prepayment_allocations.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: Document currency for every monetary column on this row. The extracted spec enum truncates mid-alphabet (ends at HRK) — treat the value set as open ISO-4217 (USD, NZD, SGD and others occur constantly); never validate against the enum list. Summing across currencies without converting via currency_rate is meaningless.
columns.enums: AED; AFN; ALL; AMD; ANG; AOA; ARS; AUD; AWG; AZN; BAM; BBD; BDT; BGN; BHD; BIF; BMD; BND; BOB; BRL; BSD; BTN; BWP; BYN; BYR; BZD; CAD; CDF; CHF; CLF; CLP; CNY; COP; CRC; CUC; CUP; CVE; CZK; DJF; DKK; DOP; DZD; EEK; EGP; ERN; ETB; EUR; FJD; FKP; GBP; GEL; GHS; GIP; GMD; GNF; GTQ; GYD; HKD; HNL; HRK

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Branding template applied to a receive prepayment's printable document. Join xero_branding_themes; presentation metadata, no effect on amounts.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Rate to the org's base currency at creation; the XE.com day rate when none was specified. Base-currency reporting multiplies monetary columns by this. A rate — never SUM it, and treat null as base currency (rate 1.0).

columns.name: remaining_credit
columns.description: Unapplied credit RIGHT NOW — a current-state balance restated on every sync, not a historical measure. SUM across rows gives today's outstanding prepayment credit; never trend it over time from this table, and never expect total - applied_amount to equal it once cash refunds exist (refunds reduce credit via xero_payments, not allocations).

columns.name: applied_amount
columns.description: Credit consumed against invoices so far — the current-state sum of this document's allocations. Per-invoice, per-date detail is in xero_prepayment_allocations; use that table for time-series application analysis.

columns.name: allocations
columns.description: Verbatim allocation array kept for payload-level audit (reconciling remaining_credit = total - applications - refunds). The analytic surface is xero_prepayment_allocations, exploded one row per application — query that, not this.

columns.name: payments
columns.description: Refund-payment stubs returned inline on the document. Canonical refund rows live in xero_payments with prepayment_id set and payment_type ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT — use that join; this payload is for audit only.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when files are attached. Cheap existence filter; the attachment rows themselves come from org_meta's xero_attachments fan-out (rate-budgeted).

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Attachment stubs if the API includes them inline (usually absent on list reads). The governed attachment surface is org_meta's xero_attachments; treat this as raw payload, not a catalogue.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit watermark for incremental sync; also moves when allocations change, which is how the child table stays fresh. Not a business date.

columns.name: updated_date_utc_string
columns.description: ISO-8601 string twin of updated_date_utc. Redundant — read the timestamp column.

joins.note: The counterparty holding or owed the credit.
Presentation template of receive prepayments; often null.
Applications of this credit to invoices.
Cash refunds of this credit (payment_type ARPREPAYMENTPAYMENT/APPREPAYMENTPAYMENT).

examples.question: Outstanding customer prepayment credit by contact
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name, SUM(pp.remaining_credit) AS credit_outstanding
FROM xero_prepayments pp
JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_contact_id = pp.contact_contact_id
WHERE pp.status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND pp.type IN ('RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT', 'ARPREPAYMENT')
GROUP BY 1
HAVING SUM(pp.remaining_credit) > 0
ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Prepayment credit raised this year: how much is already applied vs still outstanding?
examples.sql:
SELECT SUM(total) AS raised, SUM(applied_amount) AS applied, SUM(remaining_credit) AS still_outstanding
FROM xero_prepayments
WHERE status <> 'VOIDED'
  AND type IN ('RECEIVE-PREPAYMENT', 'ARPREPAYMENT')
  AND date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)

tables.grain: one task (a billable or non-billable work item) on one project per taskId
tables.description: The work-item and billing-line level of a project: each task carries its charge model (charge_type plus the rate Amount pair) and Xero-maintained to-date rollups of minutes and value split by invoiced state. Chargeability is decided HERE — time entries have no value of their own and inherit everything from the task they are logged against. The rollups are balances that already summarize xero_project_time_entries; add task totals to time-entry sums and every hour counts twice. Deleted tasks vanish from the API rather than gaining a status.
tables.additivityAxis: sync snapshot time — every minute and money column is a to-date balance each sync overwrites, so summing a task across snapshots, or adding these rollups to xero_project_time_entries, double-counts
gotchas: charge_type decides what every number means: for FIXED tasks total_amount is the fee regardless of minutes (rate times minutes is wrong), for TIME it is priced time, for NON_CHARGEABLE it is zero however much was logged. CASE or filter on charge_type before pricing anything.

status = 'INVOICED' can only ever appear on FIXED tasks; TIME tasks never reach it no matter how much has been billed. 'What is not yet billed' must use amount_to_be_invoiced / minutes_to_be_invoiced, not status.
Rollup, not fact: total_minutes already sums this task's time entries — join to xero_project_time_entries and sum both, and utilization doubles.

rate and all amount columns are in the parent project's currency (rate_currency is the pair's own currency half, not an independent denomination): cross-project task sums need the same GROUP BY currency_code discipline as the project table.

This table is a per-project fan-out — one GET /Projects/{projectId}/Tasks call per project per sync, against Xero's 60 calls/minute and roughly 5,000 calls/day org budget. Two consequences for answers: a tenant with thousands of projects cannot refresh every project inside one window, so task rollups can be staler than the project header they are compared against; and any project the /Projects scan did not return (a states-filtered scan, or an org mid-backfill) contributes no task rows at all, silently shrinking every task-level total rather than erroring.

Project name is not unique — two clients can each run a 'Website redesign'. Grouping task aggregates by p.name alone merges unrelated projects into one row; always carry p.project_id in the GROUP BY and use the name for display only.

columns.name: task_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the task and the row key; time entries reference it as task_id.

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Owning project, present on the payload itself (the ingester's per-project fan-out confirms it). Join key to xero_projects — which also supplies the currency_code every monetary column here is denominated in.

columns.name: name
columns.description: What the work is called ('Design', 'Site visit') and what appears on the invoice line when the task is billed through Projects. Not unique across projects — 'Consulting' exists everywhere — so aggregate by task_id and qualify displays with the project name.

columns.name: charge_type
columns.description: How this task turns effort into money, and the column every value question must respect: TIME bills logged minutes at rate, FIXED bills the fee in total_amount regardless of minutes, NON_CHARGEABLE bills nothing ever. Utilization counts all three; revenue counts only the first two. Pricing time without filtering on this column invents revenue from free work.

columns.name: rate_value
columns.description: Charge rate flattened from the rate Amount pair, in the project's currency: the per-hour price for TIME tasks, the fixed price for FIXED tasks, meaningless for NON_CHARGEABLE. Only multiply it by hours for TIME tasks — rate times minutes on a FIXED task manufactures revenue that will never be billed.

columns.name: rate_currency
columns.description: Currency half of the rate Amount pair, kept verbatim so the pair survives flattening. The spec asserts no link to the parent project's currencyCode: expect agreement, treat a mismatch as a payload anomaly worth chasing rather than a signal that this task is priced in another currency, and group or convert on the project's currency_code — this API publishes no rate to base currency.

columns.name: estimate_minutes
columns.description: Estimated effort for the task in minutes. Overrun detection is total_minutes > estimate_minutes; null or zero means nobody estimated, not that no work was expected — exclude those rows from overrun ratios or they divide by zero.

columns.name: total_minutes
columns.description: To-date balance of minutes logged against the task via time entries — it already equals the sum of this task's rows in xero_project_time_entries, so never add the two. Divide by 60.0 for hours; integer division floors.

columns.name: minutes_invoiced
columns.description: Minutes on this task that have already been billed. With minutes_to_be_invoiced it splits chargeable logged time by billing state — the project header's minutes_to_be_invoiced is documented as covering chargeable tasks only, so do not expect NON_CHARGEABLE effort (which lands in non_chargeable_minutes) to appear in either half. On a FIXED task the fee, not the minutes, is what gets invoiced, so reconcile this pair against fixed_minutes before treating it as a billed-hours measure.

columns.name: minutes_to_be_invoiced
columns.description: Chargeable minutes logged but not yet billed — the task-level WIP clock. The project header's minutes_to_be_invoiced is this summed across the project's chargeable tasks.

columns.name: fixed_minutes
columns.description: Minutes logged against the task when its charge type is FIXED. These measure the effort spent delivering the fee, not billable value — cost-of-delivery and margin-on-fixed-fee questions live here, and pricing these minutes at rate double-charges the fee.

columns.name: non_chargeable_minutes
columns.description: Minutes logged when the charge type is NON_CHARGEABLE — where internal, goodwill and rework time accumulates. The chargeable-share utilization ratio uses this as the free component of the denominator; it carries zero billable value by definition.

columns.name: total_amount_value
columns.description: Current chargeable value of the task in the project's currency: minutes times rate for TIME, the fee for FIXED, zero for NON_CHARGEABLE. The task-level analog of the project's total_task_amount — a Xero-maintained balance, not a transaction total.

columns.name: amount_to_be_invoiced_value
columns.description: Chargeable value not yet billed for this task, in the project's currency. Sums (per project) to the header's task_amount_to_be_invoiced; 'what can we invoice' filters charge_type <> 'NON_CHARGEABLE' and sums this.

columns.name: amount_invoiced_value
columns.description: Value of this task already billed, in the project's currency. No invoice ids accompany it — billing state in this API is a rollup, never a link to xero_invoices rows.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Task lifecycle with a trap the spec spells out: only a FIXED task whose rate amount has been invoiced reaches INVOICED (after which it cannot be modified), and a TIME or NON_CHARGEABLE task can never hold that value — it stays ACTIVE (or transiently LOCKED) however much of it has been billed. 'Uninvoiced tasks' must therefore be answered from amount_to_be_invoiced or minutes_to_be_invoiced, never from status, or every hourly task looks perpetually unbilled. LOCKED means the task is mid-state-change and unmodifiable, not deleted — deleted tasks carry no status at all because they stop being returned.

joins.note: Parent project — supplies currency_code for every monetary column here and status for open/closed filtering.

examples.question: Chargeable value still to invoice, by project
examples.sql:
SELECT p.name AS project, p.currency_code, SUM(t.amount_to_be_invoiced_value) AS to_invoice
FROM xero_project_tasks t
JOIN xero_projects p ON p.project_id = t.project_id
WHERE t.charge_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'NON_CHARGEABLE'
GROUP BY p.project_id, p.name, p.currency_code
HAVING SUM(t.amount_to_be_invoiced_value) > 0
ORDER BY to_invoice DESC

examples.question: Which tasks have overrun their estimated hours?
examples.sql:
SELECT p.name AS project, t.name AS task,
       t.estimate_minutes / 60.0 AS estimated_hours,
       t.total_minutes / 60.0 AS logged_hours
FROM xero_project_tasks t
JOIN xero_projects p ON p.project_id = t.project_id
WHERE t.estimate_minutes IS NOT NULL AND t.estimate_minutes > 0
  AND t.total_minutes > t.estimate_minutes
ORDER BY t.total_minutes - t.estimate_minutes DESC

tables.grain: one logged block of minutes by one user against one task per timeEntryId
tables.description: The only transaction-grain fact in the projects domain: one row per block of minutes a user logged against a task, fully additive across every dimension. duration is integer minutes — divide by 60.0 for hours or Postgres integer division floors the answer. The row itself carries no value and no chargeability: join xero_project_tasks for charge_type and rate, and price duration/60.0 times rate for TIME tasks only. date_utc is the day the work was done (the business axis); date_entered_utc is when it was keyed in (the audit axis) — aggregate on the former.
gotchas: duration is INTEGER minutes: duration/60 is Postgres integer division and silently floors each row — write duration/60.0, or SUM minutes first and divide once, or hour totals shrink.

The row carries no value and no chargeability: pricing requires the task join, and duration/60.0 times rate is correct for TIME tasks only — FIXED-task hours add no incremental revenue (the fee is fixed) and NON_CHARGEABLE hours are worth zero by definition.
date_utc (work date, backdatable) versus date_entered_utc (creation stamp): weekly hours grouped on date_entered_utc misplace every late-logged entry. Always aggregate on date_utc.

Unbilled time is status = 'ACTIVE'; INVOICED entries remain valid worked hours for utilization; LOCKED is transient mid-invoicing state. Hard deletions vanish from the API entirely — only a full rescan reconciles them, and there is no invoice id on the row to say WHICH invoice billed an INVOICED entry.

Time lives on closed work too. Joining to xero_projects and filtering status = 'INPROGRESS' is right for pipeline questions and wrong for history: every hour logged on a since-CLOSED project disappears, so year-to-date hours and utilization collapse. Filter project status only when the question is about open work.

Both the joins that give these rows meaning are per-project fan-outs (GET /Projects/{projectId}/Time and .../Tasks, one call each per project per sync, inside Xero's 60/minute and ~5,000/day org budget). A project the /Projects scan missed contributes no time rows and no task rows, and a rate-limited sync leaves the two partially refreshed — an inner join to tasks then quietly drops hours rather than failing. LEFT JOIN and count the unmatched before trusting a total.

This table feeds the canonical workforce_time_entry alongside payroll timesheets, and the same person's day can legitimately exist in both: Projects records billable client time, payroll records paid time. Canonical 'hours worked' must pick one source per question — unioning them double-counts the workday.

columns.name: time_entry_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the logged block of time and the row key.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: The Xero user who logged the time, and the grouping key for every utilization and capacity answer. Join to xero_project_users for name and email — but LEFT JOIN: the roster is current-state, so hours logged by someone since removed from Projects carry a user_id that resolves to nothing, and an inner join deletes those hours instead of showing them as unattributed.

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Project the time belongs to (the task's parent), present on the payload directly — grouping here skips the task join when chargeability doesn't matter.

columns.name: task_id
columns.description: Task the minutes were logged against, and the join that gives the row its economics: charge_type and rate live on xero_project_tasks, so without it a time entry has duration and no value. Misrouting it — pricing hours against the wrong task, or dropping rows whose task is missing from a partially refreshed fan-out — changes the money answer, not just the label.

columns.name: date_utc
columns.description: The date the time is logged ON — the work date, and the business axis for hours-by-week, WIP aging and utilization. The spec pairs it against dateEnteredUtc ('the date time that time entry is created'), so this one is user-supplied and freely backdated: expect it to sit earlier than date_entered_utc and never treat it as an arrival stamp. It is also the field the Time op's dateAfterUtc/dateBeforeUtc filters cut on, which makes them safe for sharding a backfill and unsafe as an incremental watermark.

columns.name: date_entered_utc
columns.description: When the entry was CREATED — set to server time by default per the spec, so an audit stamp in practice, not a work date. Aggregating hours on it shifts every late-logged entry into the wrong period; its legitimate use is bookkeeping hygiene, e.g. how far in arrears the team logs time (date_entered_utc - date_utc).

columns.name: duration
columns.description: Minutes logged — integer, and the domain's one additive measure. Postgres integer division floors: duration/60 loses up to 59 minutes per row, so write duration/60.0, or SUM the minutes first and divide once.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Free-text note of what was done. Handy for keyword slicing ('meeting', 'travel') but optional and null-heavy — never a reliable filter on its own.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ACTIVE is unbilled, INVOICED is billed, LOCKED is transiently mid-invoicing (treat as about-to-be-INVOICED, not missing). All three are real worked time — utilization sums them all; 'unbilled time' filters ACTIVE only. Deleted entries never get a status: they vanish from the API, and only a full rescan clears them from staging.

joins.note: The value-bearing join: charge_type and rate are what turn minutes into money. Both tables fan out per project independently, so a rate-limited or partial sync can leave time entries whose task row has not landed — LEFT JOIN whenever the question is about hours, and reserve the inner join for money, where a missing task means the value genuinely cannot be computed.
Direct project grouping without going through tasks; also supplies currency_code when pricing.
Names the person. LEFT JOIN from the roster instead when zero-hour users must still appear.

examples.question: Value of unbilled time by project, priced at task rates
examples.sql:
SELECT p.name AS project, p.currency_code,
       ROUND(SUM(te.duration / 60.0 * t.rate), 2) AS unbilled_value
FROM xero_project_time_entries te
JOIN xero_project_tasks t ON t.task_id = te.task_id
JOIN xero_projects p ON p.project_id = te.project_id
WHERE te.status = 'ACTIVE' AND t.charge_type = 'TIME'
GROUP BY p.project_id, p.name, p.currency_code
ORDER BY unbilled_value DESC

examples.question: Chargeable versus total hours by person over the last 30 days
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(u.name, '(user no longer on the Projects roster)') AS person,
       SUM(te.duration) / 60.0 AS total_hours,
       COALESCE(SUM(te.duration) FILTER (WHERE t.charge_type IN ('TIME', 'FIXED')), 0) / 60.0 AS chargeable_hours
FROM xero_project_time_entries te
LEFT JOIN xero_project_tasks t ON t.task_id = te.task_id
LEFT JOIN xero_project_users u ON u.user_id = te.user_id
WHERE te.date_utc >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY te.user_id, u.name
ORDER BY total_hours DESC

tables.grain: one Xero user with access to Xero Projects in the org per userId
tables.description: Roster dimension of everyone who can appear in Xero Projects time data — the join target that turns a time entry's user_id into a person. Presence here means access, not activity: utilization answers must LEFT JOIN from this roster or zero-hour people silently disappear. The roster is also current-state only, so it can be narrower than history — someone removed from Projects stops being returned while their logged hours remain, which makes an inner join in the other direction lose real time. It carries personal name and email, the only PII in the projects domain.
gotchas: This is an access roster, not an activity log: users appear whether or not they ever logged time. 'Hours by everyone' needs a LEFT JOIN from this table, or people with zero hours drop out and look like they don't exist.

The gap runs the other way too. The roster reflects who has access NOW, so a user_id on an old time entry may have no row here — INNER JOIN from xero_project_time_entries to this table then deletes that person's hours from the total. LEFT JOIN and label the unresolved ids rather than dropping them.

Deletion is hard and unwatermarked: a removed user vanishes from GET /ProjectsUsers with no status field and no tombstone, and there is no modifiedField to detect it, so only a full identity rescan retires the staging row. Until then the roster overstates current headcount.
name and email are PII. Email is also the only cross-system identity hint here — user_id only resolves inside Xero.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: Xero user UUID and the row key — the identity xero_project_time_entries.user_id points at. The spec calls it 'the xero user identifier', i.e. the org-level user rather than a Projects-local id, so it lines up with the org's Users collection wherever that scope was granted. It means nothing outside Xero: cross-system people matching has to go through email.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The person's full name — the display label for utilization and capacity answers. Personal data: handle under PII rules.

columns.name: email
columns.description: The person's email address. PII — and the practical key for matching this person to identities outside Xero, since user_id means nothing beyond Xero's walls.

joins.note: Same org-level Xero user id, so this lines up with org_meta's user dimension — but only when the accounting users scope was granted and that domain actually scanned, and a Projects user is not guaranteed a row there. LEFT JOIN, and keep using THIS table for time-entry joins: it is the scope-local roster and needs no extra OAuth scope.

examples.question: Hours logged per person this month, including people with none
examples.sql:
SELECT u.name, COALESCE(SUM(te.duration), 0) / 60.0 AS hours
FROM xero_project_users u
LEFT JOIN xero_project_time_entries te
  ON te.user_id = u.user_id
 AND te.date_utc >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
ORDER BY hours DESC

tables.grain: one Xero Projects project (a client job) per projectId
tables.description: The client-job dimension of Xero Projects and the fastest place to answer job-profitability questions: every monetary column is a Xero-maintained to-date rollup — a balance, not a transaction stream — denominated in the project's own currency_code. The rollups already contain everything in xero_project_tasks and xero_project_time_entries, so they must never be added to aggregates built from those child tables. Expenses have no child endpoint in this API version, which makes the expense rollups here the ONLY view of project expenses. CLOSED projects keep returning with full financial history: lifetime questions keep them, WIP and pipeline questions filter status = 'INPROGRESS'. Deletion is hard: a removed project stops being returned rather than gaining a DELETED status, and no field on this object carries a modified watermark, so staging only sheds it on a full identity rescan.
tables.additivityAxis: sync snapshot time — every money and minute column is a to-date balance that each sync replaces, so summing one project across snapshots (or adding a rollup to task/time-entry sums) double-counts
gotchas: Every monetary rollup is in currency_code and the API provides no rate to the org's base currency: SUM(total_invoiced) across mixed-currency projects is a number in no currency. GROUP BY currency_code or convert externally before comparing portfolios.

Rollups double-count when mixed with child tables: minutes_logged already contains every row of xero_project_time_entries and total_task_amount already prices them. Never add a project rollup to an aggregate built from tasks or time entries.
CLOSED projects are returned with full financials. WIP and pipeline questions must filter status = 'INPROGRESS'; lifetime questions must not, or completed work vanishes.

total_invoiced does not equal task_amount_invoiced + expense_amount_invoiced on projects that used deposits or credit notes — the deposit, deposit_applied and credit_note_amount columns explain the gap. Reconcile with them before declaring an invoicing error.

Nothing here links to xero_invoices: the Projects payload carries no invoice ids anywhere (the Time op accepts an invoiceId filter but never returns one), so project revenue reconciles to the invoicing domain only at rollup level.

Zero rows does not mean zero projects. Xero Projects is a paid add-on and an org without it returns nothing on every op in this domain — confirm the domain actually scanned before answering 'the business runs no projects', or an unsubscribed tenant reads as an idle one.

estimate and estimate_amount are two spellings of the same budget and the spec documents neither. Summing both doubles every project's budget; report estimate and treat a mismatch between them as a data-quality flag.

Deletion is hard and there is no modified watermark anywhere in this domain: a deleted project simply stops being returned instead of turning DELETED, so a stale staging row keeps answering as a live project until a full identity rescan tombstones it. Incremental, date-bounded refreshes cannot detect it.

minutes_logged counts non-chargeable and fixed-fee effort as well as billable time, so it is a capacity measure, not a billable one. Using it as the numerator of a utilization ratio reports every hour as chargeable — the chargeable numerator lives on the task table (minutes_invoiced + minutes_to_be_invoiced), not here.

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable UUID for the project and the row key; xero_project_tasks and xero_project_time_entries carry it as their foreign key.

columns.name: contact_id
columns.description: The client the job is delivered for — at most one per project, and nullable: name is the only field the schema requires, so internal and unassigned jobs land here with no contact. It is the org-wide Xero contact identifier, so it resolves against xero_contacts and, through it, the same client's invoices. Grouping the rollups by this id is the fastest 'value by client' in the domain — but LEFT JOIN, because an inner join silently deletes every client-less project from the total.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The human name of the job and the only label the API offers — there is no project code or number field, so answers should display this. Uniqueness is not enforced: two clients (or one) can each have a 'Website redesign', so aggregate by project_id and only ever use name for display.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Project lifecycle. INPROGRESS is open work; CLOSED projects are finished but are STILL RETURNED by the API with all their rollups intact. Pipeline, WIP and utilization-target questions must filter INPROGRESS; lifetime-revenue and history questions must NOT, or finished work disappears.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency the project is quoted, tracked and invoiced in (Xero's CurrencyCode enum). Every monetary column on this row — and every rate and amount on the project's tasks — is denominated in it, and the Projects API supplies no exchange rate to the org's base currency. Any sum that crosses projects must GROUP BY this column or convert externally first; a raw cross-currency SUM is a number in no currency.

columns.name: deadline_utc
columns.description: When the job is due (UTC), null when no deadline was set. The overdue book is deadline_utc < now() AND status = 'INPROGRESS' — a CLOSED project past its deadline finished late, it is not overdue.

columns.name: minutes_logged
columns.description: To-date balance of ALL minutes logged across the project's tasks — chargeable, fixed-fee and non-chargeable alike. It already contains every row of xero_project_time_entries, so adding the two double-counts every hour. Divide by 60.0 for hours: Postgres integer division by 60 silently floors.

columns.name: minutes_to_be_invoiced
columns.description: Chargeable minutes not yet invoiced across the project's tasks — the time-side WIP counter. Non-chargeable minutes never enter it, so on mixed projects this is NOT minutes_logged minus invoiced minutes.

columns.name: total_task_amount_value
columns.description: Current chargeable value of all the project's tasks in currency_code: logged time priced at task rates for TIME tasks plus the fees of FIXED tasks; NON_CHARGEABLE work contributes zero however many hours it burned. A balance Xero recomputes as time is logged — not a transaction total, and not addable to sums built from the task or time-entry tables.

columns.name: total_expense_amount_value
columns.description: Current value of expenses recorded on the project, in currency_code. The public Projects API exposes no expense endpoint, so this rollup and its invoiced/uninvoiced split are the ONLY view of project expenses — there is no child table to reconcile against and no expense-level detail to drill into.

columns.name: estimate_value
columns.description: The project's budget, flattened from the estimate Amount pair, in currency_code. Budget-vs-actual compares it against total_task_amount + total_expense_amount. Null means nobody set a budget — treat as 'no estimate', never as zero, or every unestimated project looks catastrophically over budget. The spec publishes no description for this field or for estimateAmount and offers no formula relating them: read the two as one budget, report this one, and never sum both.

columns.name: estimate_currency
columns.description: Currency half of the estimate Amount pair, kept verbatim so the pair survives flattening intact. Xero documents no relationship between it and the project's currencyCode, so do not assume one: expect them to agree, and treat a disagreement as a payload anomaly to investigate, never as an instruction to convert — this API exposes no exchange rate to convert with. Filter and group on currency_code.

columns.name: estimate_amount_value
columns.description: The second budget field the spec carries next to estimate; Xero publishes a description for neither, and nothing in the spec makes them different quantities. Report the budget from estimate and keep this as the cross-check: adding the two doubles every project's budget, and a row where they disagree is a data-quality flag to chase, not a second business figure.

columns.name: task_amount_to_be_invoiced_value
columns.description: Chargeable task value not yet invoiced, in currency_code; with task_amount_invoiced it splits total_task_amount by billing state. Use it for the task-only slice of WIP and quote total_to_be_invoiced as the headline billable figure — the spec documents no formula linking them, so reconcile the pair on a real tenant rather than assuming one is the other minus expenses.

columns.name: task_amount_invoiced_value
columns.description: Task value already billed, in currency_code. Billing state in this API is only ever a rollup — the payload carries no invoice ids, so this cannot be decomposed into rows of xero_invoices.

columns.name: expense_amount_to_be_invoiced_value
columns.description: Billable expense value not yet invoiced, in currency_code. With no expense child endpoint, this rollup is as granular as expense WIP gets.

columns.name: expense_amount_invoiced_value
columns.description: Expense value already billed to the client, in currency_code. Pairs with expense_amount_to_be_invoiced to split total_expense_amount's billable portion by billing state.

columns.name: project_amount_invoiced_value
columns.description: Invoiced value carried against the project to date, in currency_code. The spec documents neither this field nor total_invoiced, and the two can disagree on projects that used deposits or credit notes — quote total_invoiced as the billed-to-date headline, and use deposit, deposit_applied and credit_note_amount to account for any gap. Reporting the difference between the two as a business quantity, without that reconciliation, invents a number nothing in the API defines.

columns.name: deposit_value
columns.description: Deposit taken up-front on the project, flattened from the deposit Amount pair, in currency_code. A deposit is money billed ahead of delivery, so on deposit-heavy projects billed-to-date runs ahead of work performed and earned-value questions must net it against deposit_applied. Xero documents no formula, so do not assert whether total_invoiced already contains it — reconcile the two on the tenant's own data before mixing them in one answer.

columns.name: deposit_currency
columns.description: Currency half of the deposit Amount pair, kept verbatim so the pair survives flattening. As with estimate_currency, the spec ties it to nothing: expect it to agree with the project's currency_code and treat a mismatch as a payload anomaly rather than a conversion cue — no rate to base currency exists anywhere in this API. Query on currency_code.

columns.name: deposit_applied_value
columns.description: Portion of the deposit already drawn down against later invoicing, in currency_code. deposit minus deposit_applied is the deposit still to be offset — money the client has paid for that has not yet been matched to delivered work, and the reason a project's billed total can move without any new task or expense being invoiced. Undocumented in the spec like the rest of the deposit mechanics, so use it to explain gaps, not to derive other columns.

columns.name: credit_note_amount_value
columns.description: Value credited back against the project's invoicing — corrections, write-offs and refunded billing — in currency_code. It is why a project can legitimately show less invoiced than the sum of its invoiced tasks and expenses, so check it (with the deposit pair) before reporting an invoicing discrepancy. A to-date balance, not a list: no credit-note ids travel with it, so it cannot be tied back to rows in the accounting domain.

columns.name: total_invoiced_value
columns.description: Headline billed-to-date balance in currency_code and the number to quote for 'how much has this project billed'. Xero publishes no formula for it: it will not reliably equal task_amount_invoiced + expense_amount_invoiced wherever deposits or credit notes are in play, so explain the difference through deposit, deposit_applied and credit_note_amount instead of reverse-engineering the column. It is a rollup, not a ledger — the payload carries no invoice ids, so it can never be tied to specific xero_invoices rows. Cross-project sums must respect currency_code.

columns.name: total_to_be_invoiced_value
columns.description: Headline uninvoiced-value balance — Xero's own answer to 'what could this project bill now', in currency_code, and the right single number for unbilled WIP by project or client. The spec documents no composition, so take it as given rather than deriving it as task_amount_to_be_invoiced + expense_amount_to_be_invoiced; the two part company wherever a deposit is still to be applied. Filter status = 'INPROGRESS' or long-closed projects carrying residual balances distort the pipeline.

joins.note: The client the job is delivered for. contact_id is not schema-required, so LEFT JOIN or client-less projects drop out of the answer.

examples.question: How much unbilled work is sitting on open projects, by client and currency?
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(c.name, '(no client)') AS client, p.currency_code, SUM(p.total_to_be_invoiced_value) AS unbilled
FROM xero_projects p
LEFT JOIN xero_contacts c ON c.contact_id = p.contact_id
WHERE p.status = 'INPROGRESS'
GROUP BY p.contact_id, c.name, p.currency_code
HAVING SUM(p.total_to_be_invoiced_value) > 0
ORDER BY unbilled DESC

examples.question: Which in-progress projects have blown their estimate?
examples.sql:
SELECT p.name, p.currency_code, p.estimate_value,
       COALESCE(p.total_task_amount_value, 0) + COALESCE(p.total_expense_amount_value, 0) AS actual_value
FROM xero_projects p
WHERE p.status = 'INPROGRESS'
  AND p.estimate_value IS NOT NULL
  AND COALESCE(p.total_task_amount_value, 0) + COALESCE(p.total_expense_amount_value, 0) > p.estimate_value
ORDER BY (COALESCE(p.total_task_amount_value, 0) + COALESCE(p.total_expense_amount_value, 0)) - p.estimate_value DESC

tables.grain: one line item on one purchase order
tables.description: The queryable grain of committed procurement: what is being ordered, from which GL account and catalog item, at what price, carrying the order's tracking dimensions. Lines have no status of their own — every aggregate must join xero_purchase_orders and filter the parent's status, or DELETED and DRAFT orders pollute committed spend. Whether line_amount includes tax depends on the parent's line_amount_types, so tax-safe rollups need a CASE on that flag.
gotchas: Lines carry no status: every query must join xero_purchase_orders and filter status (usually AUTHORISED, sometimes AUTHORISED+BILLED) or deleted and draft orders inflate committed spend.

Once an order is BILLED the same lines exist again as ACCPAY invoice lines in xero_invoice_line_items. UNIONing the two populations for 'spend by GL account' double-counts every billed order, and it also mixes ACCPAY (bills) with the ACCREC lines that sit in the same invoice-line table — the bill side must be filtered by the parent invoice's Type.
line_amount is tax-inclusive only on Inclusive-mode orders. Tax-safe rollup: SUM(CASE WHEN po.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN line_amount - COALESCE(tax_amount, 0) ELSE line_amount END).
Amounts are in the parent order's currency — group by or convert via the parent's currency_code/currency_rate before cross-order sums.
item_code is a user-editable text key: joins to xero_items silently drop lines whose item was renamed or hard-deleted. LEFT JOIN and treat null matches as 'catalog drift', not missing data.
Tracking lives in the jsonb `tracking` array (max 2 entries) — department/region cuts require jsonb_array_elements, not a column filter.

columns.name: line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's uuid for this line, useful for matching a line to itself between two snapshots — but deliberately NOT the row key: an edit that rewrites the LineItems array reissues these ids, so keying on it would strand the pre-edit rows and double the order's committed value. The grain key is (purchase_order_id, line_ordinal).

columns.name: purchase_order_id
columns.description: Owning purchase order and half the row key. Every aggregate must join through it to filter the parent's status — lines carry no lifecycle state of their own.

columns.name: line_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of the line in PurchaseOrder.LineItems
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line within its order's LineItems array. The other half of the row key, and the only identity that survives an edit intact, since Xero reissues LineItemIDs when the array is replaced; it also preserves document order for rendering.

columns.name: description
columns.description: What is being ordered, in the buyer's words. On free-text lines (item_code null) this is the only evidence of what was bought, so spend-by-product analysis that keys solely on item_code silently ignores it. Description-only lines with no quantity or amounts are legal — filter quantity IS NOT NULL before computing unit economics.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Units ordered; null on description-only lines. Xero records no goods-receipt event or received quantity anywhere in the accounting API — ordered-vs-received gaps are unanswerable from this connector, and this column must never be read as 'delivered'.

columns.name: unit_amount
columns.description: Per-unit price in the order's currency. GET /PurchaseOrders exposes no unitdp parameter, so unlike Items and Receipts this arrives at Xero's default 2dp and cannot be requested at 4dp — quantity * unit_amount can therefore differ from line_amount by rounding, and line_amount is the authoritative extended value. A rate, never a total: average unit prices only when weighted by quantity.

columns.name: item_code
columns.description: User-defined code of the catalog item this line references; null for free-text lines. Joins xero_items.code — a text, user-editable key, so renamed or deleted items orphan historical lines.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: GL account code this committed spend would post to once billed — the category axis for procurement analysis. Null when the org leaves categorization to item defaults until billing.

columns.name: account_id
columns.description: Uuid of the same GL account when the API returns it. Prefer joining xero_accounts on this; fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code on older documents where it is null.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate key applied to this line (joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type); drives tax_amount and the Inclusive/Exclusive arithmetic.

columns.name: tax_amount
columns.description: Tax for the line in the document currency, auto-calculated from the tax rate but overridable — do not recompute it from tax_type and assume equality.

columns.name: line_amount
columns.description: Extended line value after discounts, in the document currency. Includes tax only when the parent's line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' — tax-exclusive rollups need CASE WHEN Inclusive THEN line_amount - tax_amount ELSE line_amount END, or mixed-mode sums double-count tax.

columns.name: discount_rate
columns.description: Percentage discount on the line, already reflected in line_amount — applying it again understates committed spend. A ratio: never summed.

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.description: Absolute discount on the line, already reflected in line_amount; the header's total_discount is the document-level sum of these.

columns.name: tracking
columns.description: Array (max 2 elements) of tracking category assignments — the org's analysis dimensions (department, region). Each element carries TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option. Cut committed spend by dimension via CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(tracking) and match Name/Option, or the ids against xero_tracking_categories / xero_tracking_options.

joins.note: Obligatory for status, currency, line_amount_types and dates — lines are meaningless unfiltered.
Text-code join; expect orphans where items were renamed or hard-deleted after the order was raised.
Preferred id join; fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code when account_id is null on older documents.
Tax rate dimension for effective-rate and jurisdiction analysis.

examples.question: Committed spend by GL account on open purchase orders (base currency, tax-exclusive)
examples.sql:
SELECT li.account_code,
       SUM(CASE WHEN po.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN li.line_amount - COALESCE(li.tax_amount, 0) ELSE li.line_amount END
           * COALESCE(po.currency_rate, 1)) AS committed_ex_tax_base
FROM xero_purchase_order_line_items li
JOIN xero_purchase_orders po ON po.purchase_order_id = li.purchase_order_id
WHERE po.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Open committed spend by tracking category option (e.g. department)
examples.sql:
SELECT tr->>'Name' AS tracking_category, tr->>'Option' AS tracking_option,
       SUM(CASE WHEN po.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN li.line_amount - COALESCE(li.tax_amount, 0) ELSE li.line_amount END
           * COALESCE(po.currency_rate, 1)) AS committed_ex_tax_base
FROM xero_purchase_order_line_items li
JOIN xero_purchase_orders po ON po.purchase_order_id = li.purchase_order_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(li.tracking) AS tr
WHERE po.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY committed_ex_tax_base DESC

examples.question: Most-ordered catalog items this year
examples.sql:
SELECT li.item_code, SUM(li.quantity) AS units_ordered
FROM xero_purchase_order_line_items li
JOIN xero_purchase_orders po ON po.purchase_order_id = li.purchase_order_id
WHERE po.status IN ('AUTHORISED', 'BILLED')
  AND po.date >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE)
  AND li.item_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC
LIMIT 20

tables.grain: one purchase order document raised against one supplier contact
tables.description: The commitment ledger of procurement: each row is an order placed (or drafted) with a supplier, with tax-normalized header totals in the document's own currency. Nothing here is actual expenditure — when a purchase order reaches status BILLED the same value re-materializes as an ACCPAY invoice in xero_invoices, so adding PO totals to bill totals double-counts procurement. Open commitment is status AUTHORISED; DRAFT/SUBMITTED are unapproved intent; DELETED orders keep arriving from the API and must be excluded from every aggregate. Line-level detail (GL accounts, items, tracking) lives in xero_purchase_order_line_items.
gotchas: A purchase order is never spend. BILLED means the money now lives on an ACCPAY invoice — adding PO totals to bill totals double-counts procurement, and treating AUTHORISED totals as expenditure books money that may never be spent.
DELETED orders keep arriving from the API (soft delete via Status). Every aggregate must exclude them or withdrawn commitments resurrect.

Totals are in the document's currency_code. Either GROUP BY currency_code or convert with SUM(total * currency_rate) for a base-currency figure — a raw SUM(total) across a multi-currency org is a number in no currency, and dividing by currency_rate instead of multiplying inverts the conversion.

Purchase orders never post to the general ledger: no journal exists for a PO at any status, so committed spend can never be reconciled against xero_journal_lines or a P&L expense account. Actual expense appears only after billing, as the ACCPAY invoice.
GET /PurchaseOrders accepts no `where` parameter — server-side narrowing is only Status/DateFrom/DateTo (DateFrom/DateTo filter on the issue date). Anything finer is client-side.

columns.name: purchase_order_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the purchase order and the row key; the join key for line items, attachments and history.

columns.name: purchase_order_number
columns.description: Human-facing alphanumeric code, auto-generated from the org's invoice settings when omitted. Unique within an org in practice but user-editable — join on purchase_order_id, display this.

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The supplier the order is raised against; joins xero_contacts. Xero does not require the contact to be flagged IsSupplier — raising ACCPAY documents is what makes a contact a supplier.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized supplier display name as embedded on the document — convenient for reporting, but xero_contacts is authoritative after renames or contact merges.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Lifecycle gate for every number in this table. DRAFT/SUBMITTED are unapproved intent, AUTHORISED is an open commitment, BILLED means an ACCPAY bill now carries the real spend, DELETED rows are still returned by the API. Committed-spend questions filter AUTHORISED; there is no VOIDED state for purchase orders — DELETED covers withdrawal at every stage.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Issue date of the order (org-timezone business date, defaulted to today when omitted at creation). The DateFrom/DateTo server-side filters and all period reporting key off this, not the audit stamp.

columns.name: delivery_date
columns.description: Date the goods are contractually to be delivered; null when never specified. Distinct from expected_arrival_date, which is the forecast rather than the ask.

columns.name: expected_arrival_date
columns.description: Forecast arrival date of the goods. Overdue-delivery reporting is AUTHORISED orders whose expected_arrival_date (or delivery_date) has passed — Xero records no goods-receipt event to close the loop.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text secondary reference (supplier quote number, project code). Not unique and not the PO number — never use as a key.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Declares whether line_amount on this order's lines includes tax. Line-level rollups across mixed modes double-count tax; the header sub_total/total_tax/total are already normalized and immune.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency of every monetary field on this order. The spec enumerates the full ISO list (the extract truncates it, so it is deliberately not carried as a closed enum here). Summing totals across currency codes yields a number in no currency — group by this or convert via currency_rate first.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Rate from this order's currency_code to the org's base currency, fixed at the document date (Xero falls back to the XE.com day rate when the user does not supply one). Base-currency value is total * currency_rate — dividing inverts the conversion and silently produces the wrong magnitude. It is a rate: SUM or AVG over this column is meaningless, and it is 1 on orders already in the base currency.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Order total excluding tax, always normalized regardless of line_amount_types — the safe tax-exclusive measure for committed spend in the document currency.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Tax component of the order in the document currency, normalized so that sub_total + total_tax = total whatever line_amount_types says. It is not a tax asset: a purchase order posts nothing to the ledger, so nothing here is reclaimable input VAT/GST — that exists only once the order is billed and the ACCPAY invoice's tax reaches the journals.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive order value in the document currency. This is commitment, not expenditure: a BILLED order's value lives on in an ACCPAY invoice, so PO totals and bill totals must never be added together.

columns.name: total_discount
columns.description: Sum of line-level discounts already reflected in the line amounts and header totals — do not subtract it again from sub_total or total.

columns.name: sent_to_contact
columns.description: True when the order was marked as sent to the supplier. Settable only on approved or billed orders, so drafts always read false — not evidence a draft was never emailed manually.

columns.name: delivery_address
columns.description: Free-text ship-to address for the goods. Usually the org's own site, but treated as PII because it can carry a person's home address.

columns.name: attention_to
columns.description: Named person receiving the delivery — personal data; keep out of aggregates and shared outputs.

columns.name: telephone
columns.description: Phone number of the person accepting the delivery — personal data, presentation-only for documents.

columns.name: delivery_instructions
columns.description: Free-text delivery instructions (max 500 chars). Operational text that occasionally embeds names or phone numbers — treat with care even though it is not flagged PII.

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Document template applied when sending; joins xero_branding_themes. Presentation only — no analytical meaning.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when at least one file is attached. The files themselves are in xero_attachments via the rate-budgeted per-order fan-out endpoint — use this flag to decide whether that call is worth spending.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Write-response validation indicator from batch upserts (e.g. ERROR), not part of the document lifecycle — status is the real state. Ignore for analytics.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Server-side modification stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (If-Modified-Since). An audit timestamp — never a business date for period reporting.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-time validation messages echoed by the API, kept verbatim for payload fidelity. Empty on clean reads — never analytical.

columns.name: warnings
columns.description: Write-time warning messages — the same transport artifact as validation_errors, retained only for payload fidelity.

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Embedded attachment descriptors (id, filename, mime type, url, size, online-invoice flag) when the API includes them. The governed home for files is xero_attachments — prefer it over parsing this payload.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: See LineItems Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_purchase_order_line_items (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Supplier dimension; contact_name here is a point-in-time copy that goes stale after renames/merges.
Presentation template; join only for document-rendering questions.
Currency descriptions only — conversion uses this order's own currency_rate, not the currency table.

examples.question: Open committed spend by supplier and currency
examples.sql:
SELECT contact_name, currency_code, SUM(total) AS committed
FROM xero_purchase_orders
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY committed DESC

examples.question: Approved purchase orders overdue for delivery
examples.sql:
SELECT purchase_order_number, contact_name, COALESCE(expected_arrival_date, delivery_date) AS eta, total, currency_code
FROM xero_purchase_orders
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND COALESCE(expected_arrival_date, delivery_date) < CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY eta

tables.grain: one line item on one quote per LineItemID
tables.description: Proposed-value lines exploded from Quote.LineItems: what was offered, at what price, before anything was billed. Nothing here is revenue — quotes only become revenue when invoiced (parent status INVOICED and a real invoice exists). Currency and LineAmountTypes come from the parent xero_quotes row, and the quote enum spells LineAmountTypes in UPPERCASE unlike invoices.
gotchas: Quoted value is not revenue: only the invoice raised from an accepted quote bills anything, and there is no QuoteID on invoices — conversion is tracked by quote status (INVOICED), not by a hard key.
Parent status gates meaning: DRAFT/SENT lines are open pipeline, DECLINED/DELETED are dead, ACCEPTED/INVOICED are won. Summing all lines regardless of parent status invents pipeline.
The quote LineAmountTypes enum is UPPERCASE (EXCLUSIVE/INCLUSIVE/NOTAX) — a filter written with invoice casing ('Inclusive') silently matches nothing.

columns.name: line_items_line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the quoted line; the row key.

columns.name: quote_id
columns.description: Parent quote key. Join xero_quotes for status, currency and line_amount_types — quoted value only counts as pipeline under the right parent status.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Zero-based position within the parent's LineItems array (provenance: the array itself). Presentation order; renumbered on edit.

columns.name: line_items_description
columns.description: Free-text description of the offered line; description-only lines (null amounts) carry narrative, not value.

columns.name: line_items_quantity
columns.description: Units offered; null on description-only lines.

columns.name: line_items_unit_amount
columns.description: Per-unit offered price before discount, quote currency. A rate — never summed. Compare against invoice unit_amount to measure quote-to-invoice price erosion.

columns.name: line_items_line_amount
columns.description: Offered value of the line net of discounts, quote currency. Tax-inclusive only when the parent's line_amount_types is INCLUSIVE (note the uppercase quote enum). Pipeline value, never revenue.

columns.name: line_items_tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate key proposed for the line; join xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

columns.name: line_items_tax_amount
columns.description: Tax computed on the offered line, quote currency; indicative until invoiced.

columns.name: line_items_account_code
columns.description: GL account code the line would post to if invoiced; join xero_accounts.code. Often blank on quotes — sales users defer coding.

columns.name: line_items_account_id
columns.description: Immutable GL account id for the prospective posting; join xero_accounts.

columns.name: line_items_item_code
columns.description: Catalogue item code being offered; null on free-typed quote lines.

columns.name: line_items_item_item_id
columns.description: Resolved catalogue item id from the embedded Item echo; durable join to xero_items.

columns.name: line_items_item
columns.description: Verbatim item stub ({Code, Name, ItemID}) as quoted; prefer scalar item_id/item_code for joins.

columns.name: line_items_tracking
columns.description: Up to 2 tracking assignments on the quoted line ({TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}); expand with jsonb_array_elements to attribute pipeline to departments/regions.

columns.name: line_items_discount_rate
columns.description: Percentage discount offered on the line; line_amount is already net of it.

columns.name: line_items_discount_amount
columns.description: Absolute discount offered (supported on quotes per the spec); line_amount is already net of it — subtracting again understates offered value.

columns.name: line_items_repeating_invoice_id
columns.description: Repeating-template lineage on the shared line schema; effectively always null on quotes.

columns.name: line_items_taxability
columns.description: US automated sales tax classification; null outside US orgs.

columns.name: line_items_sales_tax_code_id
columns.description: Internal id of the US sales tax code on the line; US orgs only.

columns.name: line_items_tax_breakdown
columns.description: Per-jurisdiction US sales tax components estimated for the offered line, kept verbatim.

joins.note: Mandatory: status, currency and (uppercase) LineAmountTypes live on the parent.
Null on free-typed lines — use LEFT JOIN.
Often null on quotes; coding happens at invoicing.

examples.question: Open pipeline value by product
examples.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(qli.line_items_item_code, '(no item)') AS line_items_item_code,
       SUM((qli.line_items_line_amount - CASE WHEN q.line_amount_types = 'INCLUSIVE' THEN COALESCE(qli.line_items_tax_amount, 0) ELSE 0 END) * COALESCE(q.currency_rate, 1)) AS open_pipeline_base
FROM xero_quote_line_items qli
JOIN xero_quotes q ON q.quote_id = qli.quote_id
WHERE q.status IN ('DRAFT', 'SENT')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY open_pipeline_base DESC

examples.question: Most frequently quoted items in the last 90 days
examples.sql:
SELECT qli.line_items_item_code, COUNT(DISTINCT q.quote_id) AS quotes,
       SUM(qli.line_items_line_amount * COALESCE(q.currency_rate, 1)) AS quoted_value_base
FROM xero_quote_line_items qli
JOIN xero_quotes q ON q.quote_id = qli.quote_id
WHERE q.date >= CURRENT_DATE - 90 AND q.status <> 'DELETED'
  AND qli.line_items_item_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY quotes DESC

tables.grain: one quote document per QuoteID
tables.description: Pre-revenue sales pipeline: quotes are offers, always customer-facing (no ACCREC/ACCPAY split here), and none of their value is billed until an invoice is raised. Status is the whole story — DRAFT/SENT are open pipeline, ACCEPTED is won-but-unbilled, INVOICED is converted, DECLINED/DELETED are dead. There is no key linking a quote to the invoice it became; conversion analysis works off status and matching by contact/date/amount.
gotchas: Quotes are never revenue: ACCEPTED and even INVOICED quote totals are offer values; billed reality lives on xero_invoices. Adding quote totals to invoice totals double-counts every converted deal.
There is no QuoteID on invoices — conversion has no hard join. Measure conversion via status transitions (SENT → ACCEPTED/INVOICED), not by joining documents.
DELETED quotes are still returned; expired quotes stay SENT. Live pipeline = status IN ('DRAFT','SENT') AND (expiry_date IS NULL OR expiry_date >= CURRENT_DATE).

GET /Quotes has no where parameter — server-side filtering is limited to DateFrom/DateTo, ExpiryDateFrom/ExpiryDateTo, Status, ContactID and QuoteNumber (plus If-Modified-Since); everything else is client-side.

columns.name: quote_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the quote and the row key.

columns.name: quote_number
columns.description: Human-facing quote number (max 255), auto-generated from org settings; display and lookup, not a join key.

columns.name: status
columns.description: The pipeline stage and the mandatory filter on every quote metric: DRAFT/SENT = open, DECLINED = lost, ACCEPTED = won awaiting billing, INVOICED = converted, DELETED = removed but still returned by the API. 'Pipeline value' that ignores status counts dead and already-billed offers.
columns.enums: DRAFT; SENT; DECLINED; ACCEPTED; INVOICED; DELETED

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The prospect/customer quoted; join xero_contacts.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized contact display name at sync time; governed name lives on xero_contacts via contact_id.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference on the quote (customer RFQ number etc.).

columns.name: terms
columns.description: Terms text printed on the quote; presentation only.

columns.name: title
columns.description: Title text printed on the quote; presentation only.

columns.name: summary
columns.description: Summary text printed on the quote; presentation only.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Issue date of the quote (org-timezone business date); the axis for quoting-activity and win-rate cohorts.

columns.name: date_string
columns.description: String twin of date as returned by the API; prefer the typed date column.

columns.name: expiry_date
columns.description: Date the offer lapses. Expired-but-still-SENT quotes remain status SENT — 'live pipeline' should also require expiry_date >= CURRENT_DATE (or null).

columns.name: expiry_date_string
columns.description: String twin of expiry_date; prefer the typed date column.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency of the quote's monetary fields (spec CurrencyCode enum; extraction truncates the full list). Convert before summing across currencies.

columns.name: currency_rate
columns.description: Rate to the org's base currency for a multicurrency quote; multiply monetary fields by it for base-currency pipeline.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Whether quote line amounts include tax — NOTE the quote enum is UPPERCASE (EXCLUSIVE/INCLUSIVE/NOTAX) unlike the invoice enum (Exclusive/...). String filters written with invoice casing silently match nothing.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Tax-exclusive offered total in quote currency — the cleanest pipeline measure at header grain.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Tax estimated on the offer, quote currency.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive offered total (sub_total + total_tax), quote currency. Offered value only — nothing is billed until an invoice exists.

columns.name: total_discount
columns.description: Sum of line discounts offered; already reflected in totals — do not subtract again.

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Template/branding used for the quote; join xero_branding_themes.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Last-modified audit stamp and incremental watermark (If-Modified-Since); not a business date.

columns.name: status_attribute_string
columns.description: Batch-response status indicator accompanying validation messages; ignore for analytics.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: API validation error messages carried verbatim ({Message} objects); data-quality triage only.

joins.note: The prospect/customer quoted.
Null when the default theme applies.

examples.question: Pipeline value by stage right now, base currency
examples.sql:
SELECT status, SUM(sub_total * COALESCE(currency_rate, 1)) AS pipeline_base
FROM xero_quotes
WHERE status <> 'DELETED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY pipeline_base DESC

examples.question: Quote win rate by month sent (won = ACCEPTED or INVOICED)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('ACCEPTED', 'INVOICED'))::numeric
         / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('ACCEPTED', 'INVOICED', 'DECLINED')), 0) AS win_rate
FROM xero_quotes
WHERE status <> 'DELETED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

tables.grain: one line item on one expense receipt
tables.description: The GL-categorized grain of employee out-of-pocket spend: each row says which account (and optionally which catalog item and tracking dimensions) a slice of a receipt hits. Lines carry no status — join xero_receipts and filter the parent's status or declined/voided spend pollutes every sum. Amounts are org base currency; whether line_amount includes tax follows the parent's line_amount_types. These are categorizations awaiting the claims workflow, not ledger postings — the statutory record is journal lines once the claim is processed.
gotchas: Lines from DECLINED and VOIDED receipts are fully populated — every sum must join xero_receipts and filter status = 'AUTHORISED' or rejected spend counts as company spend.

line_amount is tax-inclusive only on Inclusive-mode receipts: use CASE WHEN r.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN line_amount - COALESCE(tax_amount, 0) ELSE line_amount END for tax-exclusive rollups.
account_code here is a categorization awaiting the claims workflow — the statutory P&L number comes from journal lines; small timing differences between the two are normal, not corruption.

Receipt lines are out-of-pocket spend, not bill lines. UNIONing them with xero_invoice_line_items (even correctly filtered to ACCPAY) or with bank-transaction lines to build one 'spend by account' figure counts the same money twice, and adding the matching xero_expense_claim_payments row counts it a third time — that row is the cash leg of this spend, not additional expense.

columns.name: line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's uuid for this line, kept for matching a line to itself between snapshots — deliberately not the row key, because an edit that rewrites the receipt's LineItems array reissues these ids and keying on them would leave the pre-edit rows behind, doubling the receipt's spend. The grain key is (receipt_id, line_ordinal).

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.description: Owning receipt and half the row key. Every aggregate must join through it for status, spend date and the capturing employee — lines have no lifecycle of their own.

columns.name: line_ordinal
columns.api: synthetic:zero-based position of the line in Receipt.LineItems
columns.description: Zero-based position of the line within its receipt's LineItems array — the other half of the row key and the only identity that survives an edit, since Xero reissues LineItemIDs when the array is replaced. Also preserves the order the employee keyed the lines in.

columns.name: description
columns.description: What the employee bought, in their own words — the only textual evidence on hand-keyed receipts; description-only lines with no amounts are legal.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Units purchased, up to 4dp; often 1 or null on expense receipts — filter nulls before unit-economics math.

columns.name: unit_amount
columns.description: Per-unit price in org base currency (unitdp=4). A rate — sum line_amount, never this.

columns.name: item_code
columns.description: Catalog item code when the employee coded the line to an item; usually null on expense receipts. Joins xero_items.code.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: The GL expense account this spend is coded to — the category axis for employee-spend analysis. This is a categorization, not a posting: the ledger truth materializes as journal lines when the claim is processed.

columns.name: account_id
