columns.description: Uuid of the same GL account when returned; prefer it for joins to xero_accounts, falling back to account_code = xero_accounts.code.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate key applied to the line (joins xero_tax_rates.tax_type) — the basis for reclaimable-tax analysis on employee spend.

columns.name: tax_amount
columns.description: Tax on the line in org base currency. Xero derives it from tax_type but it is overridable on write, so recomputing it from the rate and asserting equality manufactures false mismatches; it is also the term subtracted from line_amount when the parent receipt is Inclusive.

columns.name: line_amount
columns.description: Extended line value in org base currency. Includes tax only when the parent's line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' — apply the standard CASE before mixed-mode sums or tax double-counts.

columns.name: tracking
columns.description: Array (max 2 elements) of tracking category assignments carrying TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option — cut employee spend by department/region via CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(tracking), matching ids to xero_tracking_categories / xero_tracking_options.

joins.note: Obligatory for status (AUTHORISED only), spend date and employee.
Preferred id join; fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code when null.
Rarely populated on expense receipts; LEFT JOIN and expect nulls.
For reclaimable-tax and effective-rate questions on employee spend.

examples.question: Approved employee spend by GL account
examples.sql:
SELECT li.account_code, SUM(CASE WHEN r.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN li.line_amount - COALESCE(li.tax_amount, 0) ELSE li.line_amount END) AS spend_ex_tax
FROM xero_receipt_line_items li
JOIN xero_receipts r ON r.receipt_id = li.receipt_id
WHERE r.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

examples.question: Approved employee spend by tracking option
examples.sql:
SELECT tr->>'Name' AS tracking_category, tr->>'Option' AS tracking_option,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.line_amount_types = 'Inclusive' THEN li.line_amount - COALESCE(li.tax_amount, 0) ELSE li.line_amount END) AS spend_ex_tax
FROM xero_receipt_line_items li
JOIN xero_receipts r ON r.receipt_id = li.receipt_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(li.tracking) AS tr
WHERE r.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY spend_ex_tax DESC

tables.grain: one expense receipt captured by one org user in the classic expense-claims workflow
tables.description: Employee out-of-pocket spend documents: who spent, at which merchant, on what date, with tax-normalized totals in org base currency (receipts carry no currency fields). This is the spend-evidence side of the claims workflow — the reimbursement liability lives on the claim, and cash leaves via xero_expense_claim_payments. Receipts are neither bills nor bank transactions: once reimbursed, the same economic spend also surfaces as a payment against the claim, so mixing receipts with ACCPAY invoices or the bank feed double-counts employee spend. Approved company spend is status AUTHORISED only.
gotchas: DECLINED is a live, fully-populated state unique to receipts — a manager rejected the spend. Approved company spend is status = 'AUTHORISED' only; including SUBMITTED counts money that may yet be declined.

Receipts are not bills and not bank transactions: after reimbursement the same spend exists as a claim payment, so summing receipts alongside ACCPAY invoices or xero_bank_transactions double-counts employee spend.
This is the legacy claims workflow — tenants on the newer Xero Expenses product return an empty Receipts collection; emptiness is a product signal, not a sync failure.
receipt_number restarts per user and claim; it is a display sequence, and joining or deduplicating on it corrupts results.

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the receipt and the row key; the join key for line items and the claim link table.

columns.name: receipt_number
columns.description: Xero-generated sequence number scoped to the capturing user's current claim — NOT unique across the org. Display only; never a join key.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date the employee spent the money — the spend-period axis. Reimbursement timing lives on the claim and its payments, not here.

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The merchant/supplier the employee paid; joins xero_contacts. Frequently an ad-hoc, loosely-managed contact created from the receipt itself — expect duplicates of real suppliers.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized merchant name embedded on the receipt; xero_contacts is authoritative after renames or merges.

columns.name: user_user_id
columns.description: The employee (org user) who captured and owns this receipt; joins xero_users — the person axis for employee-spend analysis.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference for the purchase (order number, trip name); matching aid only, no analytical meaning.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Declares whether line_amount on this receipt's lines includes tax; drives the same Inclusive/Exclusive CASE arithmetic as invoices. Header totals here are already normalized.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Receipt total excluding tax, normalized regardless of line_amount_types, in org base currency.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Tax component of the receipt, normalized so sub_total + total_tax = total whatever line_amount_types says. It is the input VAT/GST the org may recover on employee spend — but only for AUTHORISED receipts: summing it over DRAFT, SUBMITTED or DECLINED rows claims tax on spend the business has not accepted.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive amount the employee spent, in org base currency. Company-spend rollups must filter status = 'AUTHORISED' — declined and voided receipts carry fully-populated totals.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Receipt workflow state: DRAFT is captured-not-claimed, SUBMITTED is on a claim awaiting approval, AUTHORISED is approved spend, DECLINED was rejected by the approver (a state unique to receipts), VOIDED is dead. Approved-spend numbers count AUTHORISED only.

columns.name: url
columns.description: Deep link to the source document in a connected app (rendered as 'Go to [appName]' in Xero). Set by API integrations; null for hand-keyed receipts.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when a scanned image or file is attached; the files live in xero_attachments via the rate-budgeted per-receipt fan-out.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Server-side modification stamp and the incremental-sync watermark (If-Modified-Since); audit metadata only.

columns.name: validation_errors
columns.description: Write-time validation messages echoed by the API; kept verbatim for payload fidelity, empty on clean reads.

columns.name: warnings
columns.description: Write-time warning messages; transport artifact retained for fidelity, never analytical.

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Embedded attachment descriptors (id, filename, mime type, url, size, online flag) when included; prefer the governed xero_attachments table over parsing this payload.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Retained verbatim as the raw array Xero returned: the declared element order is part of the document and is lost by flattening. Fully normalised into xero_receipt_line_items (one row per element) — join there for anything you filter or aggregate on, and read this column only when the original ordering or an unflattened payload matters.

joins.note: Merchant dimension; expect ad-hoc duplicate contacts created from receipts.
The spending employee (an org login, not a payroll employee record).
Bridge to the claim; absent for DRAFT (unclaimed) receipts.

examples.question: Approved employee spend by month
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month, SUM(total) AS approved_spend
FROM xero_receipts
WHERE status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Which employees spend the most (approved receipts)?
examples.sql:
SELECT u.first_name || ' ' || u.last_name AS employee, SUM(r.total) AS spend
FROM xero_receipts r
JOIN xero_users u ON u.user_user_id = r.user_user_id
WHERE r.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY spend DESC

tables.grain: one line item on one repeating invoice template per LineItemID
tables.description: The composition of each recurring template: which products/services and GL accounts every generated invoice will carry. Values are per-occurrence template amounts, so like the parent they are non-additive until normalized by the parent's schedule. Realized recurring line detail lives on xero_invoice_line_items of generated invoices, not here.
gotchas: Per-occurrence values: summing line_amount across templates mixes weekly and monthly cadences. Normalize with the parent's schedule before any cross-template total.
Template lines are intent, not billing history — a paused (DRAFT) or DELETED parent means these lines bill nothing; filter parent status = 'AUTHORISED' for live run-rate.
The LineItem schema's RepeatingInvoiceID field is redundant here (it equals the parent key), so this table does not repeat it — lineage is the repeating_invoice_id column.

columns.name: line_items_line_item_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the template line; the row key.

columns.name: repeating_invoice_id
columns.description: Parent template key. Join xero_repeating_invoices for type, status, currency and the schedule needed to normalize any amount on this row.

columns.name: line_items
columns.description: Zero-based position within the template's LineItems array (provenance: the array itself). Presentation order; renumbered on edit.

columns.name: line_items_description
columns.description: Line description copied onto every generated invoice; description-only lines carry narrative, not value.

columns.name: line_items_quantity
columns.description: Units billed per occurrence; null on description-only lines.

columns.name: line_items_unit_amount
columns.description: Per-unit price billed each occurrence, template currency. A rate — never summed.

columns.name: line_items_line_amount
columns.description: Value of the line PER OCCURRENCE, net of discounts, template currency. Non-additive across templates until normalized by the parent's schedule_unit/schedule_period; tax-inclusive only when the parent is Inclusive.

columns.name: line_items_tax_type
columns.description: Tax rate key applied each occurrence; join xero_tax_rates.tax_type.

columns.name: line_items_tax_amount
columns.description: Tax per occurrence on this line, template currency.

columns.name: line_items_account_code
columns.description: GL account code each occurrence posts to; join xero_accounts.code — this is where recurring revenue/spend lands in the P&L.

columns.name: line_items_account_id
columns.description: Immutable GL account id for the recurring posting; durable join to xero_accounts.

columns.name: line_items_item_code
columns.description: Catalogue item code billed each cycle; null on free-typed template lines.

columns.name: line_items_item_item_id
columns.description: Resolved catalogue item id from the embedded Item echo; durable join to xero_items.

columns.name: line_items_item
columns.description: Verbatim item stub ({Code, Name, ItemID}) on the template line; prefer scalar item_id/item_code for joins.

columns.name: line_items_tracking
columns.description: Up to 2 tracking assignments stamped onto every generated invoice line ({TrackingCategoryID, TrackingOptionID, Name, Option}); expand with jsonb_array_elements to see which departments/regions recurring billing is committed to.

columns.name: line_items_discount_rate
columns.description: Percentage discount applied each occurrence (ACCREC templates only); line_amount is already net of it.

columns.name: line_items_discount_amount
columns.description: Absolute discount applied each occurrence (ACCREC templates only); line_amount is already net of it.

columns.name: line_items_taxability
columns.description: US automated sales tax classification; null outside US orgs.

columns.name: line_items_sales_tax_code_id
columns.description: Internal id of the US sales tax code on the template line; US orgs only.

columns.name: line_items_tax_breakdown
columns.description: Per-jurisdiction US sales tax components estimated for the template line, kept verbatim.

joins.note: Mandatory: type, status, currency and the normalizing schedule live on the parent.
Fall back to account_code = xero_accounts.code when account_id is null.
Null on free-typed lines — use LEFT JOIN.

examples.question: Monthly recurring revenue run-rate by GL account
examples.sql:
SELECT a.code, a.name,
       SUM(rli.line_items_line_amount * CASE ri.schedule_unit
             WHEN 'WEEKLY' THEN (52.0 / 12) / ri.schedule_period
             ELSE 1.0 / ri.schedule_period
           END) AS monthly_run_rate
FROM xero_repeating_invoice_line_items rli
JOIN xero_repeating_invoices ri ON ri.repeating_invoice_id = rli.repeating_invoice_id
LEFT JOIN xero_accounts a ON a.line_items_account_id = rli.line_items_account_id
WHERE ri.type = 'ACCREC' AND ri.status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY monthly_run_rate DESC

examples.question: Which products are on recurring billing, and for how many customers?
examples.sql:
SELECT rli.line_items_item_code, COUNT(DISTINCT ri.contact_id) AS customers,
       SUM(rli.line_items_line_amount) AS per_occurrence_value
FROM xero_repeating_invoice_line_items rli
JOIN xero_repeating_invoices ri ON ri.repeating_invoice_id = rli.repeating_invoice_id
WHERE ri.type = 'ACCREC' AND ri.status = 'AUTHORISED' AND rli.line_items_item_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY customers DESC

tables.grain: one repeating invoice template per RepeatingInvoiceID
tables.description: Templates that GENERATE invoices on a schedule — recurring billing (ACCREC) or recurring bills (ACCPAY), with the Schedule object flattened into schedule_* columns. Template totals are per-occurrence values: a $100 weekly template is not comparable to a $100 monthly one until normalized by schedule_unit/schedule_period, which is why this table is non-additive. Realized recurring revenue lives on xero_invoices rows whose repeating_invoice_id points here; only AUTHORISED templates generate anything.
gotchas: Totals are per-occurrence, not per-period: SUM(total) across weekly and monthly templates is meaningless. Normalize to monthly with total * CASE schedule_unit WHEN 'WEEKLY' THEN (52.0/12)/schedule_period ELSE 1.0/schedule_period END.

This is expected billing, not realized revenue — invoices actually generated live in xero_invoices (repeating_invoice_id back-reference), and a template can fail to bill (e.g. deleted contact) without anything changing here.
The endpoint has no If-Modified-Since, no paging and the object has no UpdatedDateUTC: every sync is a full unpaged rescan, and disappearing templates are detected by identity scan, not by watermark.
schedule_start_date resets when the template is edited — do not use it as subscription tenure.

columns.name: repeating_invoice_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the template and the row key; xero_invoices.repeating_invoice_id points here from every generated document.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Verbatim duplicate of the template identifier returned by the API as ID; always equals repeating_invoice_id — kept for payload fidelity, use repeating_invoice_id.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Direction of the recurring flow: ACCREC templates generate sales invoices (recurring revenue), ACCPAY templates generate bills (recurring spend). Recurring-revenue metrics must filter ACCREC or subscription MRR silently absorbs rent and utilities.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Template state: only AUTHORISED templates generate invoices; DRAFT templates are configured but dormant; DELETED templates are removed yet still returned by the API. Run-rate = AUTHORISED only.

columns.name: contact_contact_id
columns.description: The customer billed (ACCREC) or supplier paid (ACCPAY) each cycle; join xero_contacts.

columns.name: contact_name
columns.description: Denormalized contact display name at sync time; governed name lives on xero_contacts.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: Free-text reference stamped onto generated documents; ACCREC only.

columns.name: line_amount_types
columns.description: Whether the template's line amounts include tax (Exclusive/Inclusive/NoTax); inherited by every generated invoice.

columns.name: currency_code
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency the template bills in (spec CurrencyCode enum; extraction truncates the full list). Normalize per-currency before comparing run-rates.

columns.name: sub_total
columns.description: Tax-exclusive value of ONE occurrence of the template. Never sum across templates with different schedules — normalize to a common period (e.g. monthly) via schedule_unit/schedule_period first.

columns.name: total_tax
columns.description: Tax that will be charged on ONE generated occurrence of the template, in the template's currency_code — not a per-month or lifetime figure. Projecting recurring tax liability requires normalizing by schedule_unit/schedule_period first, exactly like sub_total; and a DRAFT-status template accrues nothing, so committed-tax projections must filter status = 'AUTHORISED'. Actual tax charged lives on the generated invoices' total_tax in xero_invoices, which wins whenever the two disagree (users edit generated drafts).

columns.name: total
columns.description: Tax-inclusive value of one occurrence (sub_total + total_tax). Per-occurrence, not per-month — see the schedule columns.

columns.name: schedule_period
columns.description: Multiplier on schedule_unit: 1 + WEEKLY = every week, 2 + MONTHLY = every 2 months. Occurrences per month = (52/12)/period for WEEKLY, 1/period for MONTHLY.

columns.name: schedule_unit
columns.description: Cadence unit of the schedule (WEEKLY or MONTHLY). The other half of run-rate normalization alongside schedule_period.

columns.name: schedule_due_date
columns.description: Integer day used with schedule_due_date_type to derive each generated invoice's due date (e.g. 20 of the following month).

columns.name: schedule_due_date_type
columns.description: Payment-terms rule that interprets schedule_due_date (days after invoice/bill date or month, or a day of the current/following month).
columns.enums: DAYSAFTERBILLDATE; DAYSAFTERBILLMONTH; DAYSAFTERINVOICEDATE; DAYSAFTERINVOICEMONTH; OFCURRENTMONTH; OFFOLLOWINGMONTH

columns.name: schedule_start_date
columns.description: Date the first invoice of the CURRENT version of the schedule was generated — it resets when the template is edited, so it is not the customer's original subscription start.

columns.name: schedule_next_scheduled_date
columns.description: Calendar date the next invoice will be generated; the forward-looking billing calendar.

columns.name: schedule_end_date
columns.description: Date the template stops generating; only returned when an end date is set — null means it runs indefinitely, not that it is ending.

columns.name: branding_theme_id
columns.description: Template/branding applied to generated documents; join xero_branding_themes.

columns.name: approved_for_sending
columns.description: True when generated invoices are auto-approved and emailed to the contact; false means each occurrence lands as a draft for manual handling — a workflow split that shows up as billing lag.

columns.name: send_copy
columns.description: Whether Xero emails the sending user a copy of each generated invoice — an internal-notification preference with no financial meaning; never a proxy for whether the customer was billed.

columns.name: mark_as_sent
columns.description: Whether generated invoices display as 'sent' in Xero regardless of actual delivery.

columns.name: include_pdf
columns.description: Whether the email sent for each occurrence carries the invoice as a PDF attachment — a delivery-format preference only; it says nothing about approval, sending or payment state.

columns.name: has_attachments
columns.description: True when the template carries attachments (copied onto generated invoices); files are catalogued in xero_attachments (org_meta).

columns.name: attachments
columns.description: Attachment stubs occasionally echoed on the template payload; the catalogued inventory is xero_attachments (org_meta).

joins.note: Customer on ACCREC templates, supplier on ACCPAY templates.
Null when the default theme applies.

examples.question: Monthly recurring billing run-rate (base-currency-naive, per currency)
examples.sql:
SELECT currency_code,
       SUM(sub_total * CASE schedule_unit
             WHEN 'WEEKLY' THEN (52.0 / 12) / schedule_period
             ELSE 1.0 / schedule_period
           END) AS monthly_run_rate
FROM xero_repeating_invoices
WHERE type = 'ACCREC' AND status = 'AUTHORISED'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY monthly_run_rate DESC

examples.question: Recurring templates ending in the next 60 days
examples.sql:
SELECT contact_name, reference, total, schedule_end_date
FROM xero_repeating_invoices
WHERE type = 'ACCREC' AND status = 'AUTHORISED'
  AND schedule_end_date IS NOT NULL
  AND schedule_end_date <= CURRENT_DATE + 60
ORDER BY schedule_end_date

tables.grain: one constituent component per (tax rate, zero-based array position)
tables.description: The parts a tax rate is built from — e.g. Canadian GST + PST as two components of one rate. IsCompound marks components calculated on top of tax-inclusive subtotals, which is exactly why the parent's EffectiveRate can exceed the arithmetic sum of component rates. Components have no ids and no watermark; they re-land with each parent rescan.
gotchas: SUM(rate) per tax_type equals the parent's effective rate only when no component has is_compound — reconcile against xero_tax_rates.effective_rate, never against your own addition.
is_non_recoverable only means something for Canadian orgs; do not build recoverability logic on it for other regions.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: The owning tax rate's systemwide code — inherited from the parent scan and the join back to xero_tax_rates. Components have no identity of their own in Xero; this code plus array position IS the row key, so any question about a component starts by resolving the rate through this column, not by matching component names (which repeat across rates, e.g. 'GST').

columns.name: tax_components
columns.description: Zero-based position in the rate's TaxComponents array — the provenance anchor for the exploded container and, with compounding, the application order.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Component label (e.g. 'GST', 'PST') — the granularity tax authorities are remitted at, finer than the parent rate's name.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: This component's percentage (4dp). A rate, never a sum: adding component rates reproduces the parent's effective rate ONLY when no component compounds.

columns.name: is_compound
columns.description: True when this component applies on top of the base PLUS prior components' tax — the mechanism that makes effective_rate exceed the plain sum. Any true value here forbids naive rate addition.

columns.name: is_non_recoverable
columns.description: True when the component cannot be claimed back — applicable to Canadian organisations only; elsewhere expect false/null. Affects whether the tax is a cost or a pass-through.

joins.note: Parent carries the resolved effective_rate; components explain it.

examples.question: Which tax rates are compound, and how do their parts stack?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.tax_type, r.name AS rate_name, c.tax_components, c.name AS component, c.rate, c.is_compound, r.effective_rate
FROM xero_tax_rate_components c
JOIN xero_tax_rates r ON r.tax_type = c.tax_type
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM xero_tax_rate_components x WHERE x.tax_type = c.tax_type AND x.is_compound)
ORDER BY c.tax_type, c.tax_components

examples.question: Multi-component rates where naive rate addition would misstate the effective rate
examples.sql:
SELECT c.tax_type, r.name AS rate_name, COUNT(*) AS components,
       SUM(c.rate) AS naive_sum, r.effective_rate,
       r.effective_rate - SUM(c.rate) AS compounding_uplift
FROM xero_tax_rate_components c
JOIN xero_tax_rates r ON r.tax_type = c.tax_type
GROUP BY c.tax_type, r.name, r.effective_rate
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 AND SUM(c.rate) <> r.effective_rate
ORDER BY compounding_uplift DESC

tables.grain: one org tax rate per TaxType code
tables.description: The org's tax rate definitions, keyed by the TaxType code that journal lines, document lines and account defaults all reference. EffectiveRate is the rate the calculation engine actually applies (compounding included); DisplayTaxRate is the label the UI shows — they diverge exactly when a component compounds. Rates have no uuid and no update watermark: the tiny unpaged set is fully re-scanned each sync, and DELETED/ARCHIVED rates must be kept because historical lines cite them forever.
gotchas: EffectiveRate ≠ DisplayTaxRate whenever any component compounds. Verifying charged tax against display_tax_rate flags correct documents as wrong.
TaxType is the join key everywhere; Name is mutable decoration. Two orgs' 'GST on Income' can be different TaxTypes, and one org can rename a rate without changing its code.

No UpdatedDateUTC exists — the ingester fully re-scans this unpaged set every sync; deleted-in-Xero rates are detected by identity comparison, and rows must be kept (soft) because history references them.

columns.name: tax_type
columns.description: The systemwide tax code (e.g. OUTPUT2, NONE) and the row key — the value every TaxType column elsewhere joins on. Xero addresses rates by this code, not by uuid.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Human label ('20% (VAT on Income)'). Editable and non-unique over time — never join on it; frozen copies on old lines will not match.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ACTIVE rates are offered for new coding; DELETED/ARCHIVED persist on history; PENDING rates are scheduled (e.g. legislated future changes). Do not drop non-ACTIVE rows — historical joins need them.

columns.name: report_tax_type
columns.description: Which box of the regional tax return the rate feeds (INPUT vs OUTPUT sides, EC*, MOSS, flat-rate schemes…). The right slicer for 'tax collected vs tax paid' questions — rate names are too free-form to classify.
columns.enums: AVALARA; BASEXCLUDED; CAPITALSALESOUTPUT; CAPITALEXPENSESINPUT; ECOUTPUT; ECOUTPUTSERVICES; ECINPUT; ECACQUISITIONS; EXEMPTEXPENSES; EXEMPTINPUT; EXEMPTOUTPUT; GSTONIMPORTS; INPUT; INPUTTAXED; MOSSSALES; NONE; NONEOUTPUT; OUTPUT; PURCHASESINPUT; SALESOUTPUT; EXEMPTCAPITAL; EXEMPTEXPORT; CAPITALEXINPUT; GSTONCAPIMPORTS; GSTONCAPITALIMPORTS; REVERSECHARGES; PAYMENTS; INVOICE; CASH; ACCRUAL; FLATRATECASH; FLATRATEACCRUAL; ACCRUALS; TXCA; SRCAS; DSOUTPUT; BLINPUT2; EPINPUT; IMINPUT2; MEINPUT; IGDSINPUT2; ESN33OUTPUT; OPINPUT; OSOUTPUT; TXN33INPUT; TXESSINPUT; TXREINPUT; TXPETINPUT; NRINPUT; ES33OUTPUT; ZERORATEDINPUT; ZERORATEDOUTPUT; DRCHARGESUPPLY; DRCHARGE; CAPINPUT; CAPIMPORTS; IMINPUT; INPUT2; CIUINPUT; SRINPUT

columns.name: can_apply_to_assets
columns.description: Read-only applicability flag: whether asset-class accounts may use this rate. Configuration surface, not usage evidence.

columns.name: can_apply_to_equity
columns.description: Whether equity-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

columns.name: can_apply_to_expenses
columns.description: Whether expense-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

columns.name: can_apply_to_liabilities
columns.description: Whether liability-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

columns.name: can_apply_to_revenue
columns.description: Whether revenue-class accounts may use this rate (read-only).

columns.name: display_tax_rate
columns.description: The advertised headline rate (4dp) shown in the UI. With compound components this is NOT what gets charged — reconciliations against actual tax amounts must use effective_rate.

columns.name: effective_rate
columns.description: The rate the engine actually applies once component compounding is resolved (4dp). expected tax = base × effective_rate/100 — using display_tax_rate on compound rates (classically Canadian PST-on-GST) under-computes.

columns.name: tax_components
columns.description: See TaxComponents Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: The constituent parts; only place compounding is visible.
Actual statutory usage of the rate (Advanced-scope gated).

examples.question: Which active tax rates would apply to expense coding, and at what real rate?
examples.sql:
SELECT tax_type, name, effective_rate, display_tax_rate
FROM xero_tax_rates
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND can_apply_to_expenses
ORDER BY effective_rate DESC

tables.grain: one tracking category (analysis dimension) per TrackingCategoryID
tables.description: The org's self-defined analysis dimensions — 'Department', 'Region', 'Cost Centre' — of which at most two can be ACTIVE at once. These are how Xero users encode structure the chart of accounts does not carry, applied per line via tracking pairs; treat each category as a first-class reporting axis. The ingester passes includeArchived=true, so ARCHIVED categories referenced by history are present; hard-deleted ones are detected only by full identity rescan.
gotchas: At most two ACTIVE categories exist; orgs that 'changed their dimensions' have archived ones whose assignments still sit on history — a segment report by only the active category ignores prior-era coding.
Categories and options can be hard-deleted in Xero; only the full identity rescan notices, so a category disappearing between syncs is deletion, not data loss.

columns.name: tracking_category_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the dimension and the row key — what every tracking assignment (journal, document, budget) joins on.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Current dimension name (max 100, e.g. 'Region'). Renameable — assignments frozen on immutable journals keep the old spelling, so resolve dimensions by id and use this for display.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ACTIVE categories (max two) are assignable today; ARCHIVED/DELETED ones persist on history. 'Current dimensions' questions filter ACTIVE; historical segmentation must not.

columns.name: options
columns.description: See Tracking Options Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: tracking_option_id
columns.description: The Xero identifier for a tracking option e.g. dc54c220-0140-495a-b925-3246adc0075f Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

columns.name: option
columns.description: The option name of the tracking option e.g. East, West (max length = 100) Retained verbatim so the founding canonical mapper keeps reading the column it was written against.

joins.note: The dimension's value list.
Where the dimension is actually applied to the ledger.

examples.question: What analysis dimensions does this org use today, with how many active values?
examples.sql:
SELECT c.name AS category, COUNT(o.tracking_option_id) FILTER (WHERE o.status = 'ACTIVE') AS active_options
FROM xero_tracking_categories c
LEFT JOIN xero_tracking_options o ON o.tracking_category_id = c.tracking_category_id
WHERE c.status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY 1

tables.grain: one selectable option per TrackingOptionID within its tracking category
tables.description: The value list of each tracking category — the 'East', 'West', 'Marketing' a line can be stamped with. Options are the actual segment members reports group by; ARCHIVED options stay bound to historical lines, so segment dimensions must keep them or old segments disappear from breakdowns.
gotchas: Option names repeat across categories ('Other' in Department AND Region) — always qualify by tracking_category_id when filtering by name.
Hard deletion applies here too: an option vanishing from the API means deleted in Xero; its id lives on in historical assignments.

columns.name: tracking_option_id
columns.description: Xero's identifier for the option and the row key — the stable segment key assignments join on.

columns.name: tracking_category_id
columns.description: Owning category — an option name like 'North' is only unique within its category, never globally.

columns.name: options
columns.description: Zero-based position in the category's Options array — provenance anchor for the exploded container; display order in Xero.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Current option label (max 100). Renames leave stale spellings on immutable journal history — group by tracking_option_id, decorate with this.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ACTIVE options are assignable; ARCHIVED/DELETED remain on history. Segment breakdowns over past periods must include non-ACTIVE options.

joins.note: Dimension the option belongs to.
Ledger lines stamped with this segment.

examples.question: All segment values available for the Department dimension
examples.sql:
SELECT o.name AS department, o.status
FROM xero_tracking_options o
JOIN xero_tracking_categories c ON c.tracking_category_id = o.tracking_category_id
WHERE c.name = 'Department'
ORDER BY o.options

tables.grain: one user login with access to the connected organisation
tables.description: Everyone who can act inside the org — staff, external accountants and practice-side logins — with their permission tier. This is the roster history records' free-text actor names resolve against, and the source for access/security questions. It is NOT a headcount table: advisers and managed-client logins inflate it, and the same human appears once per connected org. REMOVED users keep appearing in the payload after losing access.
gotchas: REMOVED users remain in the response after losing access — access reviews and user counts that skip the role filter overstate exposure.
Users are logins, not employees: external advisers appear here and payroll staff may not. Headcount questions belong to the payroll employee tables.
History records name actors by display-name string, not UserID — joining activity to this table is fuzzy name matching, and 'System Generated' events match no user at all.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: Xero's immutable identifier for the user within this org and the row key. Note: document History events reference actors by free-text display name, not by this id, so audit-trail attribution never joins on it; the few accounting payloads that do embed a user (expense-claim Receipts) carry the full User object rather than a bare id.

columns.name: email_address
columns.description: Login email. The only reliable key for recognising the same human across multiple connected orgs — deduplicate people counts on it, never on user_id.

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Given name. Combined with last_name it forms the display string that history records' user_name refers to — the basis for (fuzzy) actor matching.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Family name; see first_name for the history-matching role.

columns.name: updated_date_utc
columns.description: Audit stamp of the last change to the user record (role change, rename) and the incremental-sync watermark. Not a login/activity timestamp — Xero does not expose last-login.

columns.name: is_subscriber
columns.description: True for the person who owns and pays for the Xero subscription — the escalation/billing contact, one per org in practice, and not necessarily an accountant or admin of the books.

columns.name: organisation_role
columns.description: Permission tier controlling what the login can do in Xero and via API. REMOVED marks ex-users that the API keeps returning — every 'how many users / who has access' answer must exclude it. FINANCIALADVISER, MANAGEDCLIENT and CASHBOOKCLIENT flag practice-side or adviser-managed logins rather than the org's own staff.
columns.enums: READONLY; INVOICEONLY; STANDARD; FINANCIALADVISER; MANAGEDCLIENT; CASHBOOKCLIENT; UNKNOWN; REMOVED

examples.question: How many active users does each permission tier have?
examples.sql:
SELECT organisation_role, COUNT(*) AS users
FROM xero_users
WHERE organisation_role <> 'REMOVED'
GROUP BY organisation_role
ORDER BY users DESC

examples.question: Who owns the Xero subscription?
examples.sql:
SELECT first_name, last_name, email_address
FROM xero_users
WHERE is_subscriber
